## D161 — Depot (`-level_30`) ceiling renders as bright-blue speckle + radial "light-ray" streaks converging to a point instead of a dark corrugated roof (M-30/M-31…

**Depot (`-level_30`) ceiling renders as bright-blue speckle + radial "light-ray" streaks converging to a point instead of a dark corrugated roof (M-30/M-31, user bug B2 — `docs/dev/TEXTURE-GLITCH-ANALYSIS.md`).** NOT filtering (3-point+trilinear+aniso didn't touch it), NOT RC2 mip-contamination, NOT the RGBA5551 decode. Root-caused with a `GE_TEXDUMP` PPM+param dump (`gfx_opengl.cpp` / `gfx_pc.cpp`): the offending surface is **one texture, `fmt=CI siz=8b, 16×16`**, uploaded with **`rdp.palette_fmt == G_TT_NONE` (0)** while every other CI texture that frame has `palfmt=0x8000` (`G_TT_RGBA16`). GE draws the Depot roof with the TLUT **disabled** (`gsDPSetTextureLUT(G_TT_NONE)` — a legit N64 idiom: a CI-siz tile with no LUT feeds the raw 8-bit TMEM texel straight into the colour pipe, i.e. it behaves as a plain **I8** texture). fast3d's `import_texture()` ignored `palette_fmt` and always did the palette lookup for `fmt==CI`, indexing a **stale `rdp.palette`** left over from a previous texture → the 16×16 image came out as pure blue/cyan/magenta noise; the "radial rays" were that high-frequency noise aliasing on the steeply-receding ceiling plane (which is also why filtering couldn't help — the data was garbage). Fix: in `import_texture()`, `fmt_eff = (fmt==G_IM_FMT_CI && rdp.palette_fmt==G_TT_NONE) ? G_IM_FMT_I : fmt`, and dispatch on `fmt_eff` (CI4→I4, CI8→I8). Narrow — only changes surfaces that are currently 100% garbage. Verified: Depot corridor + control-room ceilings render as clean dark/grey industrial roofs; `-level_09`/`-level_30`/`-level_34` sweep PASS, unregressed. `GE_TEXDUMP` (env-gated PPM dump of every uploaded texture + a `fmt/siz/palfmt/palidx` log line) kept as an inert diagnostic. Confidence: **high** (before/after screenshots + the palfmt=0 evidence).

**Status (from §F table):** FIXED (`port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp` `import_texture`, `port/fast3d/gfx_opengl.cpp` diag). porting-notes.md §D.

## D152 — Mission-failed / objective-failed → permanent black screen (M-28, user bug report — LIVE process inspected, not yet fixed).

**Mission-failed / objective-failed → permanent black screen (M-28, user bug report — LIVE process inspected, not yet fixed).** User killed Trevelyan in Facility (Ctrl = fire, no crouch bind) → failed the objective → screen faded to black and never came back; process stayed alive under `debug.ps1`. `gdb.txt` (kept running): rendering stops dead at frame 12600 (`frames=12657` frozen across 206 heartbeat dumps / ~7 real min), VI pacemaker still posts. **Deadlock on `s_imLock`** — the D147 recursive-mutex that backs `osSetIntMask`. Both consumer threads are blocked in `pthread_mutex_lock(&s_imLock)` and neither owns it: `mainThread` = `sndSetScalerApplyVolumeAllSfxSlot` → `sndApplyVolumeAllSfxSlot` → `sndSetSfxSlotVolume` → `alEvtqPostEvent` (`event.c:82`) → `osSetIntMask(OS_IM_NONE)` (`libultra.c:1232`); `amMain`/audioThread = `amHandleFrameMessage` → `alAudioFrame` → `sndPlayerVoiceHandler` → `alEvtqNextEvent` (`event.c:47`) → `osSetIntMask(OS_IM_NONE)`. `sndSetScalerApplyVolumeAllSfxSlot` is the **mission-failed audio fade-out** (ramps `g_sndSfxVolumeScale` → 0 each frame, `AL_SNDP_RELEASE_EVT` posted per active `ALSoundState` per frame) — so the fade-to-black *is* the intended fail transition, and it hammers the event queue hard enough that the `osSetIntMask` lock is left owned by a party not in the 3-thread dump (a leaked unbalanced `OS_IM_NONE` — libaudio has early-return mask paths — or a transient thread that acquired it and exited; `gdb.txt` shows `New Thread`/`exited` churn every few k frames). D147's "the decomp never blocks while holding OS_IM_NONE → cannot deadlock" assumption is **falsified** by this path. Same family as D147 / porting-notes.md §D4.

**Status (from §F table):** MITIGATED (`port/src/libultra.c`, M-28, `#ifdef PORT`/port-only). `osSetIntMask` is now a **self-healing** logical lock: `OS_IM_NONE`/`OS_IM_ALL` acquire/release a process-wide recursive critical section tracked by `s_imHeld`/`s_imOwner`/`s_imDepth` under a short bookkeeping mutex `s_imMx` + condvar. Normal (balanced, microsecond) audio critical sections behave exactly as the D147 recursive mutex did. A waiter that blocks **> 2 s** (`OS_IM_STUCK_NS`) concludes the holder leaked it, logs `LOG_ERROR` with the stale `s_imOwner` + the stealing caller's return address, and **steals** the section — so a leaked/unbalanced `OS_IM_NONE` (or an acquire-and-exit transient thread) can no longer wedge the game forever; worst case is a ~2 s audio hiccup + a log line naming the leak. Builds clean. Still OPEN: the exact leaking call site (find it from the `D152: ... stealing from owner=` log next time it fires) and the proper narrow fix (dedicated `ALEventQueue` lock, or restore-on-thread-exit). Regression check deferred — `-level_09`/`-level_20` both flaky under the current machine load (D117/D134), and clean `master` itself has a separate nondeterministic `-level_09` frame ~900-1400 `0xc0000005` (see below).

## D154 — `bg.c` room-geometry ray/hit-test GBI parser port (M-28, WRITTEN / UNVERIFIED / UNCOMMITTED).

**`bg.c` room-geometry ray/hit-test GBI parser port (M-28, WRITTEN / UNVERIFIED / UNCOMMITTED).** `bgTestRayIntersectionInRoom` (`bg.c:3331`, called by `bgTestBulletHitBackground` on every shot that resolves against background geometry) is the D135 sibling flagged since M-23: raw `((u8*)gdl)[k]` / `((u32*)gdl)[i]` byte/word indexing into what is now the 16-byte PC `Gfx` room DL (D85 `bgWidenRoomGdl` + `texLoadFromGdl`) → desync → OOB `vtxbase[idx]` / walk-off AV the first time you shoot a wall or floor. Ported `#ifdef PORT` (N64 verbatim under `#else`): `vtxoff`/`vtxbase`/`op` via the `.dma` view (matches the already-ported `bgBuildRoomVtxBounds`); G_TRI1 indices from `(w1>>16/8/0)&0xff /10`; the 12 G_TRI4 nibble extractions from `(u32)gdl->words.w0/.w1` (each mapped from the N64 byte/halfword layout — table in the code comment, cross-checked twice); both `texturenum` recoveries → `-1` (the KSEG0 `*(u16*)(w1-8)` deref is invalid for the port's converted GDLs, same as D135; texnum only picks the impact decal/sound, parked D77). Builds clean. **Verification blocked** — a no-input `GE_PCDUMP` capture never fires a bullet so it never calls this function; needs a real firefight into a wall on an idle machine (this session's box was thrashed → D153/driver crash on every run).

**Status (from §F table):** **M-30 re-audit + fixes (still playtest-gated for final verify).** Cross-checked the ported G_TRI1 + all 12 G_TRI4 nibble recoveries twice against the N64 `#else` and the raw BE-word bit derivation — **G_TRI1 and G_TRI4 are correct**. **Two bugs fixed:** (1) `vtxoff` — the port read `gdl->dma.par & 0xf`, but the PC `Gdma_le` shim (`port/shim/PR/gbi.h`) maps `.par` to bits 0-23 of word0 (the packed *length*, always 16-aligned) not the N64 byte-1 params field at bits 16-23, so vtxoff was silently forced to 0 (breaks any G_VTX batch with `v0 != 0`, i.e. multi-batch rooms → wrong `vtxbase[idx]` → OOB). Now `((u32)gdl->words.w0 >> 16) & 0xf`. (2) **Sibling ported** — `bgTestBulletHitBackground` tail (`bg.c:~3841`, the post-hit G_SETTILE back-scan for `tileformat`/`tilesize`) was itself an unported raw `((u8*)gdl)[0]`/`[1]` + 64-bit `words.w0 << 11 >> 30` parser over the same widened DL; wrapped `#ifdef PORT` (opcode from bits 24-31, byte1 from bits 16-23, `(u32)`-forced 32-bit width for the tilesize shift). **Diagnostic:** `GE_D154=1` → `osSyncPrintf` of the parsed cmd/vtx-index stream (call header + per-TRI1/TRI4 `idx`) for the first 64 invocations, for the user/integrator to eyeball. Build green (`ntsc-final`, 242/242). Runtime unverifiable in a worktree (no `data/`); still needs a firefight-into-wall on an idle machine + `-level_09` framediff. Confidence: HIGH on the mechanical correctness (bit-for-bit vs N64), MEDIUM that nothing else in the walk still bites. porting-notes.md §B (D135 corollary).

## D156 — Facility outro-cutscene "hang" — the actual fix (M-29, user bug report, 2nd occurrence after D155).

**Facility outro-cutscene "hang" — the actual fix (M-29, user bug report, 2nd occurrence after D155).** After D155 shipped the user re-ran the playthrough and it hung again at the end of Facility — same stack (`modelSetAnimFrame2WithChrStuff` ← `modelTickAnim` ← `chrUpdateAnim` ← `chrTick` ← `playerTick` ← `propsTick` ← `lvlRender` ← `bossMainloop`) but this time **`frames=12962` frozen CONSTANT across ~200 heartbeat dumps / minutes** — a true infinite loop, not the D155 slow-catch-up spiral. Root: the `while (1)` at `model.c:3131` in `modelSetAnimFrame2WithChrStuff` steps the root-motion accumulation one anim frame at a time from `framea` (`model->animframe1`) to `frameb` (`frame`, accumulated in `modelTickAnim` as `frame += playspeed * speed` per tick). If `frameb` arrives **NaN or blown up** — a cutscene anim whose blend/transition math produces a huge/non-finite `model->speed`/`playspeed`/`timespeed` (`model.c:3436` `/ model->unkb0`, `:3477` `/ model->timespeed`, both guarded `> 0` but not against tiny values) — then `floorFloatToInt(frameb)` yields garbage, `endframe - curframe` ≈ 2^31, and the loop (each iteration: `sub_GAME_7F06D3F4` joint transform + `cosf`/`sinf` + `modelConstrainOrWrapAnimFrame`) runs effectively forever. **Likely deeper cause (unconfirmed, needs the repro):** these speed/blend fields are `Model` struct members; if this model is punned/inline (D100/D140 family) and `sizeof(Model)` growth misaligned them, they read garbage exactly when a cutscene sets an unusual anim transition.

**Status (from §F table):** GUARDED (`src/game/model.c`, `#ifdef PORT`): (1) in `modelSetAnimFrame2WithChrStuff`, if `frameb` is non-finite or `|frameb| >= 1e6` snap it to `framea` (loop then does ~0 iterations; the `modelConstrainOrWrapAnimFrame` at :3211 still clamps `model->frameb` to a valid frame); (2) in `modelTickAnim` after the tick loop, if `frame`/`frame2` went non-finite/absurd fall back to the pre-loop `model->animframe1`/`animframe2` so the NaN can't poison model state every frame. `!(x > -1e6f && x < 1e6f)` catches NaN too. Anim frames are 0..few-hundred so 1e6 is a safe ceiling. Verified: build green; `-level_09` frame 200 unregressed (guards never fire in normal play). **User to re-verify the Facility outro.** If it still hangs, the NaN source is upstream — dump `model->speed/playspeed/timespeed/unkb0` in `modelTickAnim` during the cutscene. porting-notes.md §E.

## D155 — Facility outro-cutscene end → "hang" = unclamped `deltaFrames` spiral (M-29, user bug report).

**Facility outro-cutscene end → "hang" = unclamped `deltaFrames` spiral (M-29, user bug report).** User watched the Facility outro cutscene; at the end the game froze (process alive, kernel-heartbeat dumps). Symbolicated `mainThread` stack from the port's own hang dump: `modelConstrainOrWrapAnimFrame` ← `modelTickAnim` ← `chrUpdateAnim` ← `chrTick` ← `playerTick` ← `propsTick` ← `lvlRender`, sampled there across *every* heartbeat dump. Root cause: `waitForNextFrame()` (`src/game/frametiming.c`) sets `nextFrameTime = (osGetCount() − prev + 387937) / 775875` and passes it **unclamped** to `updateFrameCounters` as `deltaFrames`. `osGetCount()` is wall-clock on the port (D117), not VI-locked, so a real-time stall — the asset load at the cutscene→debrief boundary, made far worse by the user running a local LLM on the same box — makes `nextFrameTime` balloon to hundreds/thousands. That becomes `speedgraphframes` → `g_ClockTimer`, which drives `modelTickAnim(model, g_ClockTimer, 1)`'s `while (numticks-- > 0)` loop once per character per render, plus dozens of `for (i = 0; i < g_ClockTimer; i++)` sim loops (`bondhead.c`, `bondview2.c`, `explosion.c`, `options.c`…). One render then does thousands of anim ticks × N characters → multi-second frame → heartbeat trips, and the slow frame feeds an even bigger delta next time → unrecoverable spiral. The N64 was physically VI-bound and never produced `deltaFrames > ~2`. Timing-compensation class, cf. D117/D134.

**Status (from §F table):** FIXED (`src/game/frametiming.c`, `#ifdef PORT` — clamp `nextFrameTime` to `FRAMETIMING_PORT_MAX_CATCHUP` = 6). After a hitch the sim just resumes at real-time-ish pace instead of spiralling, exactly as the console did when it dropped frames under load. N64 path verbatim. Confidence: high (stack + arithmetic both point here). porting-notes.md §E.

**`-level_09` frame ~900–1400 `0xc0000005` = D117/D134 load flakiness, NOT a bug (M-28).** Reproduced 6/6 while the machine was under heavy concurrent build+run load; on a **quiet** machine `-level_09` ran past frame 2400 with 0 heartbeats, no crash. ## D164 — Disclaimer / legal screen only draws the first line (D76 root cause, M-31).

**Disclaimer / legal screen only draws the first line (D76 root cause, M-31).** `constructor_menu00_legalscreen` (`src/game/front.c:1523`) renders the 12-entry `legalpage_text_array[]` with `legal_text_end = (struct legal_screen_text *)&legalscreen_MRD;` then `do { render; ptr++; } while (ptr < legal_text_end);`. This is a **linker-adjacency assumption**: on N64 `.data` the two file-scope globals are emitted in source order so `&legalscreen_MRD == legalpage_text_array + 12` and the loop count is exactly the array length. mingw/GCC reorders them — in `build-pc/ge007.x86_64.exe` `legalscreen_MRD` links at `0x1401305e0`, **0x60 bytes before** `legalpage_text_array` at `0x140130640` (verified via `nm`). So `legal_text_end < legal_text_ptr` from the start; the `do/while` runs the body **once** (entry 0, "TWYCROSS BOARD OF GAME CLASSIFICATION" — long + CENTER_ALIGN so it wraps to ~2 visual lines = the "classification line + one below" the user saw), then exits. The other 11 legal lines never render. NOT a D68 image-table bug — the legal screen references **zero** `sImageTableEntry`s; it is pure `langGet()` font text via `display_aligned_white_text_to_screen`→`textRender`, plus the 3D `logoinst` model (`subdraw`, absent — D75 family, parked). The D68 fixup and the `GE_IMGT` avenue in the brief are both dead ends here.

**Status (from §F table):** **FIXED.** Corrected 2026-09-18 (during an unrelated "easy wins" scan): the proposed one-line `#ifdef PORT` fix — `legal_text_end = legalpage_text_array + (sizeof(legalpage_text_array) / sizeof(legalpage_text_array[0]));` (N64 `&legalscreen_MRD` cast kept verbatim under `#else`) — was already committed `8dfc578f4` (2026-08-31), confirmed live in the current tree via `git blame -L 1581,1588 src/game/front.c`. The "front.c owned by another agent, not applied" status was accurate at the time it was written but never updated after the merge landed; no code change was needed this session, this is a docs-only correction. Same linker-layout class as the D75 loop-bound / D142 enum family. Confidence: **high** — mechanism confirmed by symbol addresses.

## D159 — Front-end wallet-Bond photo (and other large front-end I4/I8/IA8 textures) render "interlaced" / combed (M-31, user bug RC1 / D149).

**Front-end wallet-Bond photo (and other large front-end I4/I8/IA8 textures) render "interlaced" / combed (M-31, user bug RC1 / D149).** The user's menu showed a garbled venetian-blind Bond photo on the folder / mode-select screen; earlier the same model DL walked into garbage (`D146` opcode spam) — that crash is already contained by the D144/D146 guards, so what's left is purely the texture. Root-caused with `GE_DTEX`: the photo is a **65×65 I4** (also seen: 65×65 I8, 95×32 IA8) with a full mip chain; `import_texture_i4` uploads it `line_size_bytes*2` (= padded stride) wide and `size_bytes/line` tall — geometry fine. The comb is **`texSwapAltRowBytes` (`src/game/image.c:2191`)**: it pre-swaps every **odd** texture row in 8-byte (one-`u32`) groups to compensate for the N64 RDP's odd-line TMEM address XOR (bit 2) during 4-byte-word `gDPLoadBlock` loads. fast3d does **not** emulate that XOR (no odd-row handling anywhere in `gfx_pc.cpp`), so the pre-swapped odd rows stay scrambled in the uploaded GL image. It's called on *every* level of *every* texture on *every* path (§4), but only bites where the texture is large enough and viewed 1:1 to see the 8-texel comb — glaring on the ~big front-end photos, ~invisible on small HUD glyphs / distant in-level surfaces (which is why it was written off as "front-end model" work for many sessions). Same class as the K0-fold / interrupt-mask hardware-quirk shims — belongs in `port/`, not game logic.

**Status (from §F table):** **FIXED** (`src/game/image.c`, `#ifdef PORT` early-`return` in `texSwapAltRowBytes` — fast3d wants a plain linear image; N64 body kept verbatim under it). Verified: wallet-Bond photo renders as a clean recognisable grayscale portrait (still 180°-rotated — D75 model-transform family, parked); `-level_09` frame 200 coverage 91.62 vs 91.66 golden (D117 noise) and a visual frame is clean (tiled floor / monitors / world-map screen all correct). Confidence: **high** (GE_DTEX + before/after screenshots). The residual over-tall-mip (RC2) and non-PoT wrap (RC3) issues are separate and still parked; this only removes the row-swap. porting-notes.md §C.

## D165 — Front-end menu cursor doesn't feel like a mouse pointer (M-31, user bug B5 follow-up).

**Front-end menu cursor doesn't feel like a mouse pointer (M-31, user bug B5 follow-up).** M-30 added a "menu pointer mode" that fed mouse *velocity* into the stick axes, but `front.c frontUpdateControlStickPosition` *integrates* the stick as a velocity into a screen-pixel cursor position (`cursor_h_pos += (stickx*0.075 ± 0.5) * g_GlobalTimerDelta`, ±5 deadzone, ±70 clamp, cursor clamped into the ~320×240 virtual rect − 20px margin). Velocity-in → velocity² cursor. **Fix (port-only, no `front.c` edit):** `input.c` now runs a P-controller — it keeps its own estimate `menuEst{H,V}` of where the game cursor is, integrated each poll with the *exact same recurrence* as `frontUpdateControlStickPosition` (`menuCursorStep()`), accumulates a `menuTgt{H,V}` target from raw mouse motion (clamped to the same rect), and emits `stick = clamp(MENU_P_GAIN·(target−est), ±70)`. `MENU_P_GAIN = 6.0` → per-poll error decay ≈ 0.45 (`0.075·6`), so no overshoot and ~8-poll settle; stick falls under the game's ±5 deadzone within ~1px of target so the cursor parks with zero jitter/drift. The estimate re-syncs to the true cursor whenever the target is held at a screen edge (both clamp). `Input.MenuPointerSpeed` scales the mouse→target mapping (bump toward 150–200 if the sweep feels short — `est` steps once per controller poll ≈ 2×/rendered-frame vs `front.c`'s 1×/frame, a rate mismatch absorbed by this knob). `Input.MenuPointerMode` (0 = old velocity, 1 = pointer, **default 1**) is the escape hatch. `GE_INPUTLOG` prints an `menuptr est=/tgt=/eff=/stick=` trace line for tuning. With no mouse motion `target==est==centre` → `eff=0` → emitted stick unchanged → prior behaviour exactly.

**Status (from §F table):** FIXED (`port/src/input.c`; `Input.MenuPointerMode`, `Input.HipfirePitchSpeed` added). Build green, `-level_09` + `GE_STARTMENU=6` smoke crash-free. Feel-check owed (headless can't exercise the mouse).

## D166 — Hipfire mouse pitch is digital while yaw is analog — inconsistent feel (user bug B7 / D118a, "cheaper alternative").

**Hipfire mouse pitch is digital while yaw is analog — inconsistent feel (user bug B7 / D118a, "cheaper alternative").** In hipfire GE takes yaw from the analog stick-X but pitch only from digital C-up/C-down, so `input.c` emitted one C-button per poll once `|mouseΔY|` crossed a fixed threshold — an on/off step. **Fix (port-only):** emit the C-button as a *duty-cycled pulse* whose firing frequency scales with mouse-Y speed — `duty = |dyLook|·(HipfirePitchSpeed/100)/HIP_PITCH_FULL` (clamped ≤1), phase-accumulate, fire when the phase wraps. Fast mouse → `duty≈1` → C-button every poll (solid hold, as before); slow mouse → sparse taps proportional to speed. `HIP_PITCH_FULL = 6.0` px/poll for a solid hold; `Input.HipfirePitchSpeed` (10–500, default 100) tunes it. Aim-mode (RMB, already fully analog) untouched. No mouse motion → no pulse → prior behaviour.

**Status (from §F table):** FIXED (`port/src/input.c`). SMALL-FIXES B7. **M-87: likely SUPERSEDABLE — see the "SOLITAIRE natural-pitch" note below.** This pulse hack was necessary because the port forces a control scheme (HONEY, the 1.1 default) whose hipfire pitch is digital-only. GE's own **SOLITAIRE (1.2) / GOODNIGHT (1.4)** schemes don't have that constraint at all (see D194) — under those, the *entire* primary analog stick is free for continuous, unclamped pitch+yaw ("natural pitch/turn"), because movement is redirected onto digital C-buttons instead. If the port switches its forced `controldef` to SOLITAIRE/GOODNIGHT (also the right move for D223's wheel-cycling design and D194's mouse-feel ask), this whole digital-pulse emulation becomes unnecessary — mouse-Y would drive the stick's Y axis directly and continuously, same as X already does, with **zero digital-button emulation for pitch at all**. Don't remove D166's code without first confirming the scheme switch; keep as a fallback for whichever legacy path still needs it.

## D169 — Front-end mouse pointer can't reach the outer cells of the mission/level-select grid — only an inner ~3×3 selectable (M-33, developer bug report).

**Front-end mouse pointer can't reach the outer cells of the mission/level-select grid — only an inner ~3×3 selectable (M-33, developer bug report).** The D165 pointer P-controller in `port/src/input.c` is hard-coded to a **320×240** virtual field (`MENU_CURSOR_HI_H`/`_HI_V` = 300/220, `MENU_CURSOR_MID_H`/`_MID_V` = 160/120, `input.c:145-149`), but GE's front end runs at **440×330** (`front.c:8570` `viSetViewSize(440,330)`; default cursor home 220/165 `front.c:285`). `frontUpdateControlStickPosition` clamps the real cursor to `[20,420]×[20,310]` (`front.c:1195-1217`); the mission-select hit-test grid spans x 73…352 / y 62…270 with outer split points 317 / 235.5 (`front.c:516,519,3180,3194`). The port clamps its pointer *target* and *estimate* to 300/220 (`input.c:553-564`) → the stick zeroes out once both saturate → the game's `cursor_h_pos`/`cursor_v_pos` park at ≈300/220, short of the two outer columns and the bottom row. File-select / mode-select / main-menu are unaffected because their hit targets (centred folder boxes, the `x=126` mode list, the `x=106` difficulty list) all sit inside the 320×240 sub-box. Not the D118d `joyGetStickY`-threshold class — this is a virtual-resolution constant mismatch, closer to D164 (a front-end layout constant wrong on the PC path). Also note: the "re-syncs whenever the target is held at a screen edge" comment at `input.c:141-143` describes behaviour the code doesn't implement — the only estimator reset is the activation re-home (`input.c:545-549`), so once pinned at the clamp the estimate never recovers. Confidence: **medium-high** (constants + clamp math unambiguous in source; static-only, no build/run this session; exact reachable block "~4×3" vs the reported "3×3" within tolerance).

**Status (from §F table):** **FIXED (M-33, `port/src/input.c`, port-only, no `#ifdef PORT`).** The `menuMode` pointer branch now derives its clamp bounds from the live virtual screen — `[screenleft+20, screenleft+screenwidth-20] × [screentop+20, screentop+screenheight-20]` via `getPlayer_c_screenwidth/height/left/top()` (`src/game/bondview.c:880-895`) — falling back to the old 320×240 constants when the front-end screen isn't set (`sw` outside 200…2000). The estimator seed on activation is now the real `cursor_h_pos`/`cursor_v_pos` (`front.c:285`, externed in `front.h`) instead of the 160/120 centre guess. `MENU_CURSOR_HI_H/_V` / `MID_H/_V` kept only as the fallback. **Verified:** builds + links clean (`getPlayer_c_screen*` and `cursor_[hv]_pos` all resolve — non-static engine symbols, as expected); `GE_STARTMENU=7` mission-select boots crash-free 600+ frames; `-level_09` unregressed (framediff 3/3 within threshold, 91.6% nonclear). The in-level path is untouched (menu-only branch). **Interactive feel-check still owed** — headless input can't drive the mouse pointer, so "every grid tile is now reachable" is inferred from the corrected clamp math, not observed. `Input.MenuPointerMode=0` (legacy velocity) and the constant fallback remain as escape hatches.

## D178 — Pre-mission briefing screen: objectives blank / missing, briefing pages blank (also the D143 "briefing text blank" side effect) — FIXED (M-36).

**Pre-mission briefing screen: objectives blank / missing, briefing pages blank (also the D143 "briefing text blank" side effect) — FIXED (M-36).** Root cause: the briefing segment (`Ubrief*Z`, source `assets/obseg/brief/*.c`) is a raw ROM image of `struct BriefStruct` = `{ u16 brief[4]; struct { u16 textid; u16 enabled_difficulty; } objective[10]; }` (48 bytes), loaded by `front.c load_briefing_text_for_stage()` via `_fileNameLoadToAddr()` — **no converter and no BE→LE fixup anywhere in the chain**. On the LE host all 24 `u16` read byte-swapped. Measured on Dam (`GE_D178=1`): raw `brief=002c,012c,022c,032c obj0=042c/0100 obj3=072c/0000` vs correct `2c00,2c01,2c02,2c03 / 2c04/0001 / 2c07/0000`. Two independent symptoms follow: (a) `textid` `0x2C04` (= `getStringID(LDAM,4)`, bank 11 slot 4) reads as `0x042C` → bank 1 slot 44, never loaded → `langGet()` NULL → **blank text** (this is exactly the D143 residual, `front.c:6732` and `brief[0..3]` at `front.c:6855-6867`); (b) `enabled_difficulty` `0x0001` (Secret Agent) reads as `0x0100 = 256`, so `selected_difficulty >= enabled_difficulty` (`front.c:6729`) is false for every difficulty-gated objective — on Agent only the one `DIFFICULTY_AGENT`(0) objective survived the filter, which is why a single bare "a." bullet printed. **Fix:** `romdataFixupBriefing()` in `port/src/romdata.c` (+ `port/include/romdata.h`), called from a `#ifdef PORT` block in `load_briefing_text_for_stage()` right after the load — the same shape as `langFixupLoadedBank()` in `language.c` (BE-serialized-struct reconciliation, semantics-preserving, no game logic touched). `GE_D178=1` prints the raw and fixed words. **Verified:** Dam briefing on Agent now shows "a. Bungee jump from platform"; on `GE_STARTMENU_DIFF=3` (00 Agent) all four (Neutralize all alarms / Install covert modem / Intercept data backup / Bungee jump from platform), correct difficulty gating. `-level_09` framediff 3/3; `GE_STARTMENU=7`/`=13` crash-free.

**Status (from §F table):** **FIXED (M-36)** — high confidence

## D172 — Bullet-impact / blood / spark particles render magenta or cyan instead of dark red (M-82, ROOT CAUSE FOUND + FIXED).

**Bullet-impact / blood / spark particles render magenta or cyan instead of dark red (M-82, ROOT CAUSE FOUND + FIXED).** Particle billboards (`explosion.c` `explosionRenderPart`, `gSPVertex`+`gSP2Triangles`) take their CC/tile state from ROM state records replayed just before them (`g_ExplosionDisplayLists[]` = `assets/oddtextures.c` `globalDL_0x078..`). The dominant record sets `gsDPSetCycleType(G_CYC_2CYCLE)` + `gsDPSetTextureLOD(G_TL_TILE)` + `gsDPSetCombineMode(G_CC_INTERFERENCE, G_CC_MODULATEIA2)` and binds **two** tiles: tile 0 = IA8 "smoke" @ TMEM 0, tile 1 = RGBA16 "fire" @ TMEM 0x188. `G_CC_INTERFERENCE` cycle-0 = `TEXEL0 * TEXEL1`. **fast3d's `gfx_lod_tile_offset()` returns `0` unconditionally** on the `!gfx_detail_textures_enabled` branch — a D107 fix for GE's mip textures (whole chain loaded in one LOADBLOCK at TMEM 0; `port/src/video.c:225` sets the flag `false`). So texunit 1's sampled tile = `first_tile_index + 0` = tile 0 → **TEXEL1 samples the smoke texture, not fire** → `smoke * smoke` → wrong colour. Two earlier M-82 candidates were false trails: (1) "0xB9 unhandled → D146 abort" — 0xB9 is `G_SETOTHERMODE_L` in this non-F3DEX2 build, handled; zero D146 aborts in a sustained-fire run. (2) "records never set 2-cycle" — they do (`0xBA`), and fast3d applies it (probe-confirmed `cycletype=2CYC`). **Probe evidence (`GE_D172=1`, user Silo firefight, `d172_silo.log`):** 40/40 particle tris → `cfg1[tile=1 tmem=392 fmt=RGBA siz=16b]` but `SAMPLED1 = tile0 (tmem=0 fmt=IA)`, `tex_lod=0`.

**Status (from §F table):** **FIXED (`port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp` `gfx_lod_tile_offset`): `return rdp.tex_lod ? 0 : i;`** — fold to the base tile only when LOD is actually active. D107's mip case (`tex_lod=1`, blurry ceilings) unchanged; a genuine non-LOD 2-texture combine now samples tile `i`. `bunker1` verify PASS (the D107 repro level), no framediff regression. PR #34. **Owed: in-game eyeball — blood/sparks should read dark red.** Env-gated `GE_D172` probes left in tree (`#ifdef PORT`, inert).

## D173 — Third-person Bond model spawns too high

**Third-person Bond model spawns too high** (user QA report): the player-representing figure at level start floats well above the ground "a lot of the time" while the actual player spawn is correct; same on the Cuba end credits — JB ~6 ft in the air above Natalya. D75 animated-model family but a *position* defect, not absence (M-33: gun-barrel Bond renders fine). Suspects: intro/credits puppet chr spawn position vs model base transform; anim root-motion accumulation (`modelSetAnimFrame2WithChrStuff`, cf. D156); packed-float `coord3d` decode in intro setup. "Player spawning OK" localises it to the render-side model, not `g_CurrentPlayer`. See `GRAPHICS-BACKLOG.md` D173.

**Status (from §F table):** OPEN — observed, not investigated. **M-87 user playtest: still present** — "Bond floating in the sky / cutscene glitch thing still exists." Related, newly reported: **in some cutscenes Bond spins in circles** (named instance: end of Cradle, when Trevelyan falls) — likely the same actor-position/anim-root class rather than a new bug; logged under D148/D160 (`GRAPHICS-BACKLOG.md`) since it's cutscene-triggered. **M-106 investigation (static only — no build/runtime access in this worktree, see note below):** checked the two most D209-shaped candidates for a puppet Y-position aliasing bug and RULED OUT both. (1) `chrSpawnAtPad`/`chrSpawnAtCoord`/`chrAdjustPosForSpawn` (`src/game/chraction.c:10653-10794`) — the puppet-spawn path a cutscene `guard_play_animation`-style AI cmd would use. `PadRecord.stan` (`src/bondtypes.h:1744-1751`) is a ROM-serialized *pointer* field (`StandTile *stan` at offset 0x28) — exactly the tail-pointer shape D122/D126/D132 warn about — and `tools_pc/d88_emit.py`'s `emit_pad()` zeroes it on conversion with a comment claiming it's "dead-on-load, always set before use." **Verified this claim is TRUE, not a converter bug**: every `PadRecord` literal in the N64 source asset tables (checked `assets/obseg/setup/UsetupdamZ.c:37-51`) initialises `stan` to the literal `0` — the ROM binary never carries a live pointer there on N64 either, so zeroing it on PC is byte-identical behaviour, not a regression. `chrAdjustPosForSpawn` receiving a NULL seed `StandTile*` is therefore the original game's normal case, not a port defect. (2) The anim-root-motion Y-accumulation chain (`modelTickAnim`→`modelSetAnimFrame2WithChrStuff`, `model.c:3060+`, `pos24 = pos34 + rotate(pos)` at `model.c:3322`) was already exhaustively audited for exactly this class of bug during D193/D209 (M-80/M-81) and found self-consistent, with the `padding[]`-union sweep that found D209/D210 explicitly noting `act_anim`/`act_dead` (the union arms active during a played-animation/dead puppet) are "layout-stable" (`porting-notes.md` §A, D210 entry) — i.e. that sweep already covers the cutscene-puppet actiontype, and it came back clean. So the two most probable D209-style aliasing sites for this specific symptom are both cold. **Did not find the actual root cause.** Did not get to: the *separate* Cuba end-credits case (`front.c` `init_menu18_displaycast`/`constructor_menu18_displaycast`, `front.c:7821-8320`+ — a **different**, single-actor "cast roster" display model shared by the intro roster and the credits roster, using `getsuboffset`/`subcalcpos`/`cast_rootpos_smoothed` root-motion smoothing, not the in-level chr path at all) — spot-checked `getsuboffset` (`model.c:684-700`) and it is `#MATCH`-verified clean, but did not trace the smoothing math or confirm this is even the code path the "JB above Natalya" report hits (that report implies two actors on screen at once, which this single-`cast_model` code doesn't obviously support — may be a distinct, not-yet-located two-actor cutscene-puppet path). **Confidence: LOW-MEDIUM that this is the D209-style struct-aliasing family at all** — the two most likely aliasing sites check out clean, which argues *against* the shared-root-cause theory for D173 specifically (unlike D160, where the analogous check also came back clean but for a different reason — no pointer fields to alias in the first place). Next investigator: get a live Cradle (`-level_41`) capture of Trevelyan's chr during the death sequence with a position-logging probe (none shipped yet — would need a new `#ifdef PORT` env-gated trace, not added this session per the no-build-verification constraint), and separately locate the actual two-actor Cuba credits code path (grep for wherever `intro_char_table`/cast display is invoked with two simultaneous models, if it exists — not found this session). **M-141: no new lead this session** (see D243's M-141 entry) — checked whether D243's stale-memory front-end/menu bug could share a mechanism with this puppet-position bug; no code-level link found, kept as an unconfirmed hypothesis to watch for during the next live cutscene capture, not a new suspect to chase on its own. **M-141: Steam Deck playtest confirmation** — user reports Bond floating at level start on both Dam and Facility ("chemical plant"), "but fine when it moves to first person" (matches this row's own framing exactly: player spawn/first-person is correct, only the third-person render-side puppet floats). No new mechanism; corroborates the bug is general across levels, not Dam-specific. **User confirms D292** (Bond sunk into the floor on death) **is the same underlying bug**, a third instance alongside level-start floating and the Cradle cutscene spin — see D292 for the consolidated cross-reference. **M-145 (see D243):** the Dam end-cutscene double-Bond + camera shake is now traced to the same family — the exit script moves Bond's own third-person model via `CHR_BOND_CINEMA` (`chr_try_teleporting_to_pad(0xFD, …)`, `bondconstants.h:4604`) while its rappel animation commands target a model-less BG driver chr; level-start floating (this row), death sinking (D292), and the cutscene double-image (D243) are one "third-person world model transform/lifecycle" bug class.

**M-172 (2026-09-17, this session, autonomous/no live human needed): first-ever quantified, reproducible measurement of the level-start float, isolated to the render side and ruled independent of which animation is attached.** The intro/pre-control puppet cutscene runs unattended (`CAMERAMODE_INTRO`/`SWIRL`, no player input required to progress), so `GE_D243M`'s existing tick/onscreen probes — built for D243, this session — could just be pointed at it directly: launched `-level_33` (Dam) with `GE_D243M=1` only (no X3/X4), captured the whole intro-puppet lifetime headlessly (`scratch/d173/m172_dam_intro_capture.log`, CREATE frame=427 → REMOVE frame=924, 499 `onscreen` samples for the tracked chr). **Result: `prop->pos.y` is rock-steady at 60.3 for the entire window (never changes) — this is the correct ground-level Y — while the `onscreen` probe's actual rendered root Y sits at 384–389 the whole time, a consistent ~324–328 unit gap.** Camera-side fields (`f488pos`/`f3C4`, the tick probe) track `prop->pos` exactly (`20197.7,60.3,16902.1`, correct) — so **the camera/game-logic position is right; only the model's own rendered skeleton root is floating**, and by a near-constant amount. Critically, **the puppet cycles through three distinct animations during this window** (`aidx=61`→`106`→`99`, `actiontype` 23→1→3) **and the Y-gap barely moves (388.4 → 388.8 → 384.3)** — this argues against "wrong/stale animation root motion" (M-160/M-164/M-165's leading theory below) as the primary driver here, since a genuinely animation-root-motion-driven offset should track *which* animation is attached, not stay flat across three different ones. `getsuboffset`/`setsuboffset` themselves are `#MATCH`-verified decomp-verbatim (`model.c:684/705`) — not the bug site. **Leading candidate now: a fixed root-joint/base-transform offset baked into how the puppet's skeleton is set up at spawn** (`solo_char_load`, `bondview2.c:401`, not yet traced in full — a long function, stopped after confirming the accessor functions are clean rather than push further without a specific lead to chase). **Cross-level replication (same session, same technique): Facility (`-level_34`) reproduces an almost identical offset.** `prop->pos.y` constant at 392.8 for the puppet's whole lifetime (frames 242–374); rendered `onscreen` Y settles at 721.9 — a gap of **~329.1 units**, versus Dam's ~324–328. Two different levels, completely different ground heights (60.3 vs 392.8) and world positions, landing on essentially the **same** offset magnitude — this is strong evidence the bug is a fixed constant somewhere in the puppet's spawn/setup path, not something that scales with level geometry, camera angle, or which animation happens to be attached. Archived alongside the Dam capture (`scratch/d173/m172_facility_intro_capture.log`).

**Local-delegate (Qwen `triage`) spot-check, one candidate raised then correctly self-qualified as unconfirmed:** dispatched a read-only investigation into `solo_char_load` for the root-joint/animation init order. It flagged `chr_b.c:98`'s `modelSetAnimTranslationScale(model, pov)` (`pov = c_item_entries[body].pov`, `chr_b.c:37`) as a mechanism that scales decoded root-motion translation — but noted itself that this predicts an **animation-dependent** effect, which contradicts the now-two-level-confirmed near-constant offset, so it should not be treated as confirmed. Also honestly flagged that its own read of `solo_char_load` was partially evicted from context mid-session (lower confidence on the parts not directly quoted). Not spot-verified further this session — logged as a ruled-unlikely-but-not-fully-eliminated candidate, not a lead to chase first.

**Own follow-up static trace (same session): the puppet's first animation and its nonzero start frame are both legitimate, table-driven decomp behavior, not garbage/uninitialized state — ruling out two more candidates.** Traced `solo_char_load`'s setup: `init_GUARDdata_with_set_values(...)` (`bondview2.c:629`) then `setsuboffset(bodyModel, &prop->pos)` (`bondview2.c:634`) — position is set correctly, matching the normal guard init path (`chr.c:1719-1720`) exactly, per the earlier delegate spot-check. The puppet's first observed animation (`aidx=61`, `animframe≈96` from its very first rendered frame, *not* 0) comes from the same per-tick body-animation driver every player uses (`bondview2.c:10845-10880`, `firing_animation_groups[group][sub]`, a decomp table indexed by weapon-hold/movement state) — `startframe = fa->y`, a **table constant**, not carried over from stale/uninitialized prior-animation state (ruling out a `bheadAdjustAnimation`-style phase-carryover bug for this specific symptom). This means the ~328-unit elevation is very likely baked into the *animation's own keyframe data* at that starting frame — i.e. the model's root/pelvis joint legitimately sits ~328 units above ground in this pose, and something that should compensate (translate the root down to align with `prop->pos`'s ground-level Y, the way a normal in-level guard chr's third-person render ends up correctly grounded) isn't being applied to this specific puppet's render path.

**M-173 (2026-09-17, same session, autonomous, decisive): the control experiment — normal in-level guards do NOT have this gap. The bug is specific to the player-puppet's own draw/setup path, not a universal chr-rendering issue.** Added a second probe (`chr.c`, `chrTick`'s very first line, before ANY position-update logic runs) logging `prop->pos` for **every** ticked chr, gated on the same `d243mProbeActive()`. Relaunched Dam (`-level_33`, `GE_D243M=1`, no player input needed — background guards animate on their own) and diffed the new "before" line against the existing `onscreen` "after" line for the same chr at the same frame. **Checked four different background guards, different actiontypes/animations (`aidx` 0/40/106), different world positions: all four show a before/after gap of ~0** (a one-time ≤1.6-unit settle on the very first tick or two, then flush thereafter) — nothing remotely like the player puppet's ~328-unit gap. This **rules out** "every chr's root joint sits above its true position by design, normal chr rendering just hides it" (the leading theory after M-172) — **normal chr rendering is correctly grounded.** The bug is isolated to whatever is different about the player's own third-person puppet (`solo_char_load`'s setup, or the player-specific body-render call site, `bondview2.c`) versus a normal guard's `chrTick`/`chrRenderProp` path. Archived: `scratch/d173/m173_guard_compare_dam.log`.

**Correction while writing this up (checked before committing to the claim): `chrTick` — where `subcalcmatrices`/the render-position computation actually happens (`chr.c:2777`) — is NOT a separate player-vs-guard code path; it's called identically for the player's own `prop` (`bondviewMoveAllPlayers`, `bondview2.c:10493`, `ret = chrTick(prop)`) and every guard (`chrlvActionTick`'s caller).** So the divergence M-173 found is not a distinct "player draw path skips a step" — it's that the *same* shared machinery is fed a different animation.

**M-174 (same session): tried to name that animation-selection call statically via `firing_animation_groups[group][sub]` (`bondview2.c:10831`) — added a probe there, got ZERO hits for the intro puppet.** Useful negative result, not a dead end: that whole per-tick firing-animation selector is apparently unreached during `CAMERAMODE_SWIRL`/`INTRO`, ruling it out as the source (a second static guess that turned out wrong — logged so the next investigator doesn't retry it).

**M-175 (same session): stopped guessing and instrumented the actual choke point instead — every path that sets the player's `bodyModel` animation funnels through `modelSetAnimation` (`model.c:2857`), so added a probe there (filtered to `model == g_CurrentPlayer->bodyModel`, `#ifdef PORT`) logging `__builtin_return_address(0)`, then resolved the logged addresses with `addr2line` against the built exe. Found the exact call site on the first try this way: `bondviewSetCameraMode`, `bondview2.c:936-942`, inside the `CAMERAMODE_SWIRL` branch's intro-fly-in setup (`bondview2.c:910-957`).** This code reads a **decomp ground-truth table**, `stage_intro_anim_table[]` (`bondview.c:355-365`, zero `#ifdef PORT` anywhere in this call chain — completely unmodified decomp): entry `[0]` is `{PTR_ANIM_extending_left_hand, 95.0, -1.0, 0.02}` — animation **"extending_left_hand"**, **start frame 95.0**, play-to-end, speed **0.02** (near-frozen, a held pose not a moving loop). `PTR_ANIM_extending_left_hand` is confirmed index **61** in `animation_table_ptrs1[]` (`initanitable.c`) — an exact match to the `aidx=61` measured live in M-172 on both Dam and Facility, and the `startframe=95.0`/near-zero speed exactly explains the captured `animframe≈96-97` (a few ticks' worth of playback at 0.02/tick past the 95.0 start) staying essentially flat for the puppet's whole visible lifetime.

**M-176 (same session, live user comparison against real N64): user directly compared this port's level-start sequence against their memory of real N64's — confirms the float is a genuine divergence, not faithful behavior, and reveals a second, deeper mechanism.** Real N64 (per the user, described in detail): attract screen → flyover camera → after 1-2s, Bond appears **standing on the ground, arms at his side** → ~0.25-0.5s later he **draws his gun and surveils left-to-right** as the camera moves into first-person → control passes to the player. **On this port, per the user's direct observation: Bond is floating from the very first frame his model appears — never grounded, not even briefly.**

Traced the code this triggered: `chrlvTickBondIntro` (`chraction.c:7663`, also fully decomp-verbatim) is a **second-phase watchdog**, confirming the two-part sequence the user described is genuinely implemented: once the held "extending_left_hand" pose (frame 95, near-frozen) wraps back below frame 86, it switches Bond to `fire_standing_draw_one_handed_weapon_fast` (frames 86→131) — this is almost certainly the "draws his gun and surveils" phase, and fired exactly as expected in a live capture (`chrlvPerformAnimationForActor`, `chraction.c:605`, one hit ~200 ticks after CREATE). **So the two-phase structure matches the user's description — but the FIRST phase (which should show Bond grounded, arms at sides) never visibly looks that way on PC; it's elevated from frame 1.**

Checked one more concrete candidate (the local-delegate-flagged, previously-dismissed `modelSetAnimTranslationScale`/`pov` theory): `c_item_entries[BODY_Formal_Wear].pov` (`assets/obseg/chr/suitbond/chrModelFileRecord.inc.c`) = **1.058** — a small, plausible-looking decomp constant, not an obvious corruption (compare `propobj.c`'s unrelated `10.438f`/`1.0438f` uses for actual anomalous-looking scale values). If the raw pre-scale root-motion translation.y this port decodes at frame 95 is genuinely ~310 units, ×1.058 ≈ 328 — matching the measured figure almost exactly. This makes `pov` *consistent with* the measured number rather than an obvious smoking gun — it doesn't distinguish "asset decode is wrong" from "asset decode is right and N64 genuinely has ~310 units of raw translation baked into this keyframe" (in which case the scale isn't the bug, whatever produced the ~310 raw value is, or nothing is and N64 shows this too — which the user's direct comparison now argues against).

**Conclusion (updated after M-176's live comparison): the mechanism setting the puppet's pose is fully decomp-verbatim — not a bug in the *selection* logic — and the user's direct live comparison against real N64 (M-176) rules out theory (b) (genuinely faithful N64 behavior).** Real N64 shows Bond grounded during this exact phase; this port shows him elevated from the first frame. Since the selection code, the table data, and the root-motion computation call (`sub_GAME_7F06D3F4`) are all unmodified decomp, and the scale multiplier applied (`pov=1.058`) is a small, plausible constant rather than an obvious corruption, **the remaining candidate is bucket (a): the `PTR_ANIM_extending_left_hand` clip's own keyframe/root-motion data is mis-decoded for this port at/around frame 95** — an asset-pipeline bug, the same class of investigation D252 used (dump and hand-decode the raw ROM bytes for this one clip's frame-95 root translation, compare against what `model.c`'s bitstream decoder computes at runtime). **This is now the concrete, high-confidence next step — not more source-code tracing, and not a rule-2 sign-off case (bucket (a) is allowed without one). This thread is source-tracing-exhausted for this session; the next session's work is an asset/data-level check.**

**M-160/M-164/M-165 (2026-09-17, see D243): the shared mechanism is now understood in much more depth, though still not confirmed as the actual PC/N64 divergence.** D243's investigation this session traced the general pattern this whole family plausibly shares: `chrUpdateAnim` (`chr.c:2398-2424`) doesn't move a puppet's world position directly — it advances whatever animation is currently attached (`modelTickAnim`), then reads the model's root-joint transform back into `prop->pos` via `getsuboffset` (`model.c:684`). When something else (a teleport, a spawn, a death transition) moves the puppet's *logical* position without also resetting/updating its *animation state* to match, the next `chrUpdateAnim` call overwrites the new position with wherever the stale animation's root motion happens to be — producing exactly "floats/sinks/shakes relative to where it should be, in a way that tracks the animation, not the intended position." This is a strong candidate mechanism for D173's level-start float (an animation not yet settled/attached correctly at spawn) and D292's death-sink (the death-pose transition possibly not resetting the model's root anchor the way the collision/death logic expects) — **but D243's own parallel investigation (M-165) found this same mechanism may be entirely decomp-faithful**, with the actual PC-specific divergence being *which phase* of an animation a chr happens to be on at the moment of transition (inherited from real-time-dependent prior gameplay, not deterministic) rather than a code-path difference. **Do not treat this as solved** — it reframes what to look for (an animation-identity/phase mismatch at the transition moment, not a position-write bug per se) and gives a concrete technique (`GE_D193A`'s `aidx=` reverse-resolve + a `model->animframe1` phase read, see D243 M-166) for whoever gets live access to test D173/D292 the same way D243's `GE_D243M`/`GE_D243X2` probes now do.

## D173 — CONSOLIDATED NEXT STEPS (as of M-176, 2026-09-17)

This entry is long and multi-pass (M-87 through M-176, spanning several sessions). This block is the single place to read for "what's actually known and what to do next."

### What's established (high confidence, live-verified this session)

1. **The float is real and reproducible, not measurement noise.** `prop->pos.y` (game-logic position) stays exactly at true ground level for the entire on-screen lifetime of the level-start puppet; the *rendered* root sits ~324-329 units higher, flat regardless of which of three different animations is attached. Measured independently on Dam (`-level_33`) and Facility (`-level_34`, setup file `UsetuparkZ.c` — "ark" is simply Facility's internal decomp codename, confirmed by multiple independent, already-established findings elsewhere in this file: D130, D203, D217, D255, and the M-139-era Trevelyan/Ourumov investigation's own full static decode of `UsetuparkZ.c`; a same-session doubt raised while writing this section, based on a hand-count of `setup_text_pointers[]` alone, was checked against those and was wrong — retracted).
2. **The bug is isolated to the player's own third-person puppet, not chr rendering in general.** A control experiment (M-173) checked four background guards (different actiontypes/animations/positions) with a before/after `prop->pos` probe spanning all of `chrTick` — all four showed ~zero gap. Normal chr rendering is correctly grounded.
3. **The exact mechanism is now named, down to the source line and the specific animation clip.** `bondviewSetCameraMode` (`bondview2.c:936-942`, inside the `CAMERAMODE_SWIRL` branch) sets the puppet's animation from `stage_intro_anim_table[g_IntroAnimationIndex]` (`bondview.c:355`) — entry `[0]`, `{PTR_ANIM_extending_left_hand, 95.0, -1.0, 0.02}` (animation "extending_left_hand", starting at frame 95, near-frozen). `g_IntroAnimationIndex` defaults to 0 and is only overridden by a level's own `INTROTYPE_ANIM` setup record if one exists — **Dam's setup script has no such record**, so index 0 is Dam's only possible choice, by design. (Several *other* levels — Archives, Park, Aztec, Caverns, Depot, Runway, Bunker2, and the three Severnaya variants — do have their own override; not yet checked whether those levels show the same float or a different one.)
4. **A second, later phase exists and works correctly (or at least fires as expected).** `chrlvTickBondIntro` (`chraction.c:7663`, also decomp-verbatim) watches for the held pose to wrap, then switches Bond to `fire_standing_draw_one_handed_weapon_fast` (frames 86-131) — confirmed firing live, matching the user's own memory of real N64's "draws his gun and surveils left-to-right" moment almost exactly.
5. **The user directly compared this port's sequence against their memory of real N64 and confirmed a genuine divergence** (M-176): N64 shows Bond grounded/arms-at-sides during phase 1; this port shows him floating from the very first visible frame, never briefly grounded. This rules out "this is just how N64 looks too" as an explanation.
6. **Two candidate mechanisms checked and both look clean:** the selection/table-read code (100% decomp-verbatim, no `#ifdef PORT` anywhere in the whole call chain) and the applied scale multiplier (`c_item_entries[BODY_Formal_Wear].pov = 1.058`, small and plausible, not an obvious corruption like other unrelated scale constants seen elsewhere in the codebase, e.g. `propobj.c`'s `10.438f`).

### What to actually try next (none of these attempted yet)

- **(a) The real next step: a D252-style raw ROM byte dump of the `PTR_ANIM_extending_left_hand` clip, hand-decoded at frame 95, compared against what `model.c`'s `sub_GAME_7F06D3F4` bitstream decoder computes at runtime for the same frame.** This is a data-inspection task, not code tracing — the code path setting/computing this pose is fully decomp-verbatim and has been read end-to-end this session. If the hand-decoded raw value disagrees with the runtime-computed value, that names an asset-pipeline/converter bug (bucket a, no rule-2 sign-off needed). If they agree, the bug is somewhere not yet found (re-open the search — but don't re-trace the code path already covered by M-174/M-175/M-176, it's clean).
- **(b) Optional, lower priority:** check whether a level that *does* have its own `INTROTYPE_ANIM` override (e.g. Archives, `UsetuparchZ.c`) shows the same float or a different one — this would help confirm whether the bug is specific to entry `[0]`'s clip or general to the whole `stage_intro_anim_table` mechanism.

### Applies to the wider family too

D243 (cutscene shake/duplication, its own CONSOLIDATED NEXT STEPS block appears earlier in this file) and D292 (death sinking) are cross-referenced as the same general "third-person world model transform" family, though this session's D173 work found its specific root cause (a likely asset-decode issue in one named clip) rather than a shared code-level mechanism — don't assume D243/D292 share this exact cause without separately verifying each.

## D179 — Packaged build crashes after the logos — the D43/D69 model + bg sidecars are ROM-derived and absent from any build that has no ROM (M-34, alpha-release QA).

**Packaged build crashes after the logos — the D43/D69 model + bg sidecars are ROM-derived and absent from any build that has no ROM (M-34, alpha-release QA).** The first `goldeneye-pc-port-*-win64.zip` from CI (bundle-win.sh) shows the Rare/Nintendo logos (compiled-in `assets/rarewarelogo.c`) then AVs at `0x6b157a88`/`0x70157a88` — symbolised: `modelPromoteNodeOffsetsToPointers` (`model.c`) ← `load_object_fill_header` (`objecthandler_2.c`) ← first prop/item model load. Root cause is **not** a code regression: the port loads PC-layout model geometry from `data/pcmodels-<region>/{pcmodels.bin,manifest.csv}` and stage bg/stan from `data/pccg-<region>/{pccg.bin,manifest.csv}`, both produced offline by `tools_pc/d43_emit.py` / `d69_emit.py` from the ROM (see `port/src/pcmodels.c` / `pccg.c`; `pcmodelsReserveSize` logs *"pcmodels.bin not found — model loads will fail"* and returns 0). CI has no ROM so it never runs the emit scripts, and the two `data/` dirs are (correctly) gitignored ROM-derived game data — **cannot be committed or shipped** (converted Nintendo/Rare geometry, DLs, collision, stan nav; = distributing assets). A local build with those dirs present runs clean (verified M-34: 1741 frames, `romdataInit ... mapped at 0x10000000`, `pcmodels: 512 sidecars`, `pccg: 73 sidecars`, no crash — so `0x10000000` is *not* the problem here). The `docs/building.md` sidecar-gen step was also missing entirely. **Fix = release-side, backlogged** (`docs/BACKLOG.md` → "Alpha release"): bundle the emit scripts + their committed inputs as a pure-stdlib-Python asset-prep tool the user runs once against their own ROM (~5 MB output, no MIPS toolchain). Secondary/latent: the fixed-address `VirtualAlloc((LPVOID)0x10000000)` in `romdata.c` has no working fallback (`"using heap copy — direct ROM reads will fail"` then limps into the same crash) — didn't bite M-34 but will on a machine where something occupies `0x10000000`; harden separately (reserve earliest in `main`, or retry low bases and derive all segment math from the base obtained).

**Status (from §F table):** Diagnosed, not fixed — release packaging gap + latent `romdata.c` fallback

## D180 — Native-PC input pass (M-XX QoL run, `qol/native-pc-input-menu`, port-only).

**Native-PC input pass (M-XX QoL run, `qol/native-pc-input-menu`, port-only).** Three parts, all config-gated with default = prior behaviour: **(WI-1) `Input.MouseCaptureMode`** (0 = legacy always-grab; 1 = Quake-style click-to-lock) in `port/src/input.c` + `port/src/video.c` — in mode 1 the OS cursor is free until a click lands in the game window (`SDL_MOUSEBUTTONDOWN` → `inputNotifyClick`), and ESC / focus-loss / entering any front-end menu (`current_menu != MENU_RUN_STAGE`) frees it again; re-entering a stage while still "armed" re-locks so unpausing needs no click. `reconcileGrab()` runs once per controller-0 poll. Mouse buttons are suppressed from the game while the cursor is free in-stage (no phantom fire). Controller paths untouched. **(WI-2) absolute-cursor menu tracking** — when capture mode is on and the cursor is free in a menu, the D165/D169 pointer P-controller takes its target from the real cursor's absolute window position mapped onto the live virtual front-end rect (`getPlayer_c_screen*`), giving true 1:1 tracking instead of the relative-delta estimator. Relative path unchanged for legacy/grabbed. **(B3) `Input.MouseAimSpeed` default 25 → 16** (aim mode still overshot at 25 per the backlog).

**Status (from §F table):** LANDED, port-only, no `#ifdef PORT`. Build 241/241, `-level_09` framediff 3/3 within threshold (unregressed), `GE_STARTMENU` menu boot crash-free. **Feel-checks owed** (headless can't drive the mouse): click-to-lock ergonomics, absolute menu tracking, the new aim-speed default.

## D181 — `Game.ScreenShakeIntensity` — first route-(b) `src/` gameplay-cosmetic hook (M-XX QoL run).

**`Game.ScreenShakeIntensity` — first route-(b) `src/` gameplay-cosmetic hook (M-XX QoL run).** `src/fr.c viShake()` gains a single `#ifdef PORT` line — `intensity *= portScreenShakeScale;` (extern `f32`, defined + `configRegisterFloat`'d 0.0–10.0 in `port/src/video.c`) — before the existing clamp. Default `1.0f` ⇒ exact no-op, every headless golden dump byte-unaffected; `0.0` disables explosion/effect screen shake, up to `10.0` exaggerates it. N64 build (no `-DPORT`) keeps the original line verbatim. Precedent per `docs/BACKLOG.md` "Fun features → screen-shake intensity slider" and AGENTS.md #2's documented-exception path. Same policy class as a future FOV hook.

**Status (from §F table):** **Menu row pulled (v0.2.1, user testing).** The hook is correct on its own narrow terms — `viShake()` is called only from `explosion.c`, so the slider does exactly what it says (scales explosion/effect shake) — but that's a much narrower scope than the "Screen shake" label implies to a player: it does not touch the always-on walking head-bob or any getting-shot reaction, so a user swinging it from 0 to max during ordinary play sees nothing and reasonably calls it broken. Removed from `port/src/optionsoverlay.c`'s row table until it covers all screen-shake/view-bob sources, not just explosions; config var (`portScreenShakeScale`) and the `fr.c` hook are untouched. **HUD ammo-type/weapon icon vanished at `-O2` (M-46 root-cause, M-47 fix + verify).** `set_rgba_redirect_generate_microcode()` (`src/game/gunfire.c:5929`, sole emitter of the bottom-right magazine icon; call sites 6057/6123/6217/6219, all `gdl = f(...)`) is `Gfx *` with **no `return`** — the decomp banner above it flags exactly this.
