## D222 — High `Video.FovScale` breaks culling — NPCs and some world objects stop rendering near the screen edges (M-87, user QA).

**High `Video.FovScale` breaks culling — NPCs and some world objects stop rendering near the screen edges (M-87, user QA).** Split out of D211's noted residual: `currentPlayerSetCameraScale()` / the game's frustum-cull and screen↔world math still run at the **nominal, unscaled** fovy while the actual render projection is widened by `portFovScale` (`fr.c:737`) — so objects that are on-screen in the widened view but outside the nominal-FOV frustum get culled before they reach the renderer. Confirmed **not cosmetic** — a real, noticeable functional regression at high FovScale, not just "culls a hair early."

**Status (from §F table):** **FIXED, awaiting visual verification (M-121).** Root cause traced one step further than the original write-up: `currentPlayerSetCameraScale()` (`game/bondview.c`) derives both the frustum-cull plane normals (`c_cameratopnorm`/`c_cameraleftnorm`) *and* the fog/LOD distance-visibility-fade scale (`c_scalelod`/`c_lodscalez`, consumed by `chrobjFogVisRangeRelated()` et al. in `propobj.c`) from `c_perspfovy`, which every `viSetFovY`/`viSetAspect`/`viSetFov`/`viSetZRange` call in `fr.c` was setting from the **nominal** `g_ViBackData->fovy` — never the `portFovScale`-widened value D211 already computes for the actual render projection two lines away in `viSetupCurrentPlayerView`. Fix: factored the existing widen-FOV math out of `fr.c` into `f32 portScaleFovY(f32 fovy, s32 isTitleScreen)` (`port/src/video.c`, D222 — identical logic, same `LEVELID_TITLE` guard, no game-code duplication) and fed it into all 4 `currentPlayerSetPerspective()` call sites via a small `#ifdef PORT` local helper in `fr.c` (`frCullFovY`), same as the existing D211 projection-matrix chokepoint now also calls the shared helper instead of its own inline copy. Identity (bit-for-bit no game-code-visible change) at `FovScale=100` by construction — `portScaleFovY` returns `fovy` unchanged whenever `portFovScale == 1.0f`. Audited per the original risk note: `c_cameratopnorm`/`c_cameraleftnorm`/`c_scalelod`/`c_lodscalez` are consumed only in `propobj.c`'s fog-visibility-fade math and `bondview.c`'s own screen-space transform — no AI-visibility/awareness call sites found reading these fields, so `portFovScale` still only touches rendering-adjacent visibility, not NPC behavior. Rebuilt clean, crash-free at `FovScale=150` on `-level_33` (Dam). `bunker1` golden framediff was inconclusive in this dev box — the *unmodified* baseline build also fails it by a similar or larger margin (confirmed via an A/B stash/rebuild), matching the documented pre-existing frame nondeterminism (`porting-notes.md` §E), not a regression from this change. **Needs a human's eyes**: does high-`FovScale` screen-edge NPC/object culling actually look fixed now.

## D223 — QoL ask: mouse-wheel weapon cycling should be directional like a normal PC shooter — wheel up = next weapon, wheel down = previous — instead of both directions…

**QoL ask: mouse-wheel weapon cycling should be directional like a normal PC shooter — wheel up = next weapon, wheel down = previous — instead of both directions cycling forward (M-87, user QA).** **Root-caused, port-only fix, no game-logic change needed** — GE's engine already has separate forward/backward weapon-cycle signals: `bondview2.c` computes `moveData.weaponForwardOffset = edge(invButtons) && !(shootButtons held)` and `moveData.weaponBackOffset = (invButtons held) && edge(shootButtons)` (`bondview2.c:5338-5347`, the classic N64 "hold A, tap Z to cycle backward" trick). Default control scheme (the `else` branch used unless a Domino/Goodhead/Galore/Plenty preset is active, `bondview2.c:5177-5179`): `invButtons = A_BUTTON` (= port `GE_CONT_A`, `input.c:86`), `shootButtons = Z_TRIG` (= port `GE_CONT_G`, `input.c:88`, the fire button). `moveData.triggerOn` is explicitly suppressed while `invButtons` is held, so holding A never causes an accidental shot when the Z edge lands. The port's `inputPostWheel()` (`input.c:977`) currently does `if (notches < 0) notches = -notches` — **discards wheel direction** — and only ever synthesizes a bare `GE_CONT_A` pulse (`wheelPulse`, `input.c:631-634`), i.e. always "forward."

**Status (from §F table):** **FIXED (M-105, `port/src/input.c`) — directional wheel cycling implemented per the plan below.** Wheel-up keeps the existing 2-poll `A` pulse (`weaponForwardOffset`: fresh A edge, Z released). Wheel-down runs a 2-poll backward sequence: poll 1 presents `A` only, poll 2 presents `A`+`Z_TRIG` — the fresh-Z-edge-while-A-held combo `weaponBackOffset` requires (`bondview2.c:5337-5340`); ordering matters because the edge is computed against the game's own previous poll. `moveData.triggerOn` (`bondview2.c:5419`) requires A to be released, so the synthesized Z edge can never fire a shot. Roles are stable: the port forces `CONTROLLER_CONFIG_HONEY` (`bondview.c:1484`), whose scheme gives `invButtons=A_BUTTON`/`shootButtons=Z_TRIG` — the same roles the pre-fix forward pulse already relied on. Known limitation (pre-existing, not a regression): while RMB aim is held the game flips `controldef` to KISSY (`bondview2.c:6106-6112`), under which *neither* direction cycles — exactly as the old forward-only pulse behaved in that state. Owes a human play-test (wheel up = next weapon, wheel down = previous, no accidental shots). Plan: keep `wheelPulse` (or a new `wheelPulseFwd`) for wheel-up as today; add a `wheelPulseBack` path for wheel-down that instead holds `GE_CONT_A` across ≥2 polls while presenting a fresh `GE_CONT_G` edge partway through (mirroring the invButtons-held + shootButtons-edge combo) — sequence matters (A must already read "held" `oldbuttons`-wise before G's edge, per `weaponBackOffset`'s check order). Must confirm which N64 control preset (`controldef`) the port's save data actually carries — `invButtons`/`shootButtons` differ under KISSY/GOODNIGHT/SOLITARE/etc; if the port doesn't force one, the synthesized combo needs to match whatever's active, or the port should just force the default (HONEY-equivalent) preset since its own `Input.Bind` system already replaces N64-style scheme selection. Port-only, `#ifdef PORT` in `input.c`, no `src/` game-logic touch. **M-87: PD-PC-port precedent checked (user asked what PD did about N64 control presets).** PD does **not** route mouse/gamepad through the N64 preset system at all — it defines its own logical control-key layer (`CK_*` in `port/src/input.c`/`input.h`, e.g. `CK_DPAD_L`/`CK_Y`) fully decoupled from the N64 controller-config enum, and even treats mouse-wheel-up/-down as **two independent bindable virtual keys** (`VK_MOUSE_WHEEL_UP`/`_DN`, defaulted to distinct `CK_*` actions) rather than one "wheel = cycle" event — exactly the shape of the fix this row wants. PD's `controldef` field is hardcoded (`player.c`/`playermgr.c` `controldef = 2`), not left to the original in-game control-style picker. **This GE port already has the equivalent layer for this purpose: D214's `Input.Bind` system.** Recommendation for D223 (and the user's broader ask — N64 presets aren't meaningful for mouse/keyboard, and modern-gamepad (Xbox/PS) support should be a first-class port concept, not routed through N64 presets either): add two new `Input.Bind`-able logical actions (e.g. `IA_WEAPON_NEXT` / `IA_WEAPON_PREV`) that synthesize the invButtons/shootButtons combos under the hood, default-bound to wheel-up/-down (keyboard/mouse) and left open for a future bumper/shoulder-button default under real gamepad support; and have the port force a single fixed `controldef` (matching PD's approach) so the synthesis target never depends on the original N64 control-style menu. That menu itself becomes a candidate for hiding/no-op in a future QoL pass once `Input.Bind` fully supersedes it — not proposed as a change here, just noted as the natural conclusion. **M-87 — D194 gives a concrete answer for *which* preset: `CONTROLLER_CONFIG_SOLITARE` (1.2).** It's the scheme that gives free continuous full-stick mouselook (see D194) — and conveniently, `SOLITARE` is **not** in the `KISSY`/`GOODNIGHT` button-role group (`bondview2.c:5168-5179`), so it keeps the **same** `shootButtons=Z_TRIG`/`invButtons=A_BUTTON` roles this row's plan already assumed — no change needed to the wheel-cycle synthesis. (`GOODNIGHT` (1.4) also gets natural pitch/turn but groups with `KISSY` for button roles — `shootButtons=A_BUTTON`, `invButtons=L_TRIG|R_TRIG` — so it would need this row's combo re-derived; prefer SOLITARE unless something else needs GOODNIGHT specifically.) **M-87 survey note, filed for later (candidate 4, no action needed now):** GE's port has no per-player control-*mode* concept — keyboard/mouse is always controller 0 (`inputOpenPads()`, `connectedMask=0x1`), covering the common "P1 mouse+kb, P2+ pads" local-MP case fine. PD adds a 5th per-player control-mode entry ("PC controls") with a save-compatibility shim (written as an existing N64 mode so the save format never changes, overridden back to PC mode on read by config) to let *any* player be on mouse+keyboard, not just P1. Only relevant if "P1 on pad, P2 on keyboard" (or more than one keyboard player) is ever a real ask — bigger feature than anything currently planned; not worth a Dxx yet.

## D224 — QoL gap (M-87, from a PD-PC-port survey): the N64 Rumble Pak is fully dropped instead of modernized.

**DONE via D401 (2026-09-27).** Re-promoted from DEPRIORITIZED; implemented per
`docs/dev/RUMBLE-PLAN.md` exactly as the M-87 addendum prescribed — both
upstream blockers (`CONT_CARD_ON` gate + `osPfsInit` → `PFS_ERR_DEVICE`) landed
with the `SDL_GameControllerRumble` wiring, plus `Input.PlayerN.RumbleScale`
config (options-menu slider deferred). Real-pad playtest + `RumbleScale=0`
silence check owed. See `## D401` (file tail) for the full record.

**QoL gap (M-87, from a PD-PC-port survey): the N64 Rumble Pak is fully dropped instead of modernized.** GE genuinely has a rumble subsystem (`src/motor.c`, `src/joy.c`) but the port's `osMotorInit/Start/Stop` (`port/src/libultra.c:1220-1223`) are all hard stubs — "no accessories on the PC," `osMotorStart`/`osMotorStop` return `-1` unconditionally, `osPfsFindFile`-family returns `PFS_ERR_NOPACK`. So every in-game rumble event (weapon recoil, explosions, etc.) computes and calls into a dead path. **PD's PC port wires the equivalent straight through to real gamepad rumble:** `inputRumbleSupported(idx)` checks `SDL_GameControllerHasRumble`/`SDL_JoystickIsHaptic` (with a Windows fallback: some pads report no haptics but rumble anyway), `inputRumble(idx, strength, time)` calls `SDL_GameControllerRumble()` scaled by a per-pad `RumbleScale` config value (options-menu slider, `Input.PadN.RumbleScale`), and `osPfsFindFile` reports a "Rumble Pak" present exactly when a real pad supports rumble (`libultra.c` — same "pretend the N64 accessory is there" pattern GE's port already uses for `osMemSize`/Expansion Pak, just applied to a real capability instead of faked). Cross-ref `QOL-INVENTORY.md` (folded into the existing "per-pad tuning" row).

**Status (from §F table):** **DEPRIORITIZED (M-87, user call).** Gamepad-only — irrelevant to mouse/keyboard, which is the primary target for this next release; no keyboard/mouse play is affected by NOT doing this. Root cause + fix still valid whenever gamepad support becomes a priority (no `src/` game-logic touch: GE's `motor.c`/`joy.c` call sites already exist and already call the `osMotor*` shims; the fix is entirely in `port/src/libultra.c` + `input.c` — add `inputRumbleSupported`/`inputRumble` per the PD shape, wire `osMotorStart`/`osMotorStop` to them, add `Input.PadN.RumbleScale` config). **M-87 PD-legacy-survey addendum (`docs/dev/notes/PD-LEGACY-SURVEY.md` candidate 1, high confidence) — the D224 fix as originally stated is NOT sufficient by itself.** Two more upstream blockers sit before the stubbed `osMotorInit/Start/Stop` ever gets reached: (1) `port/src/libultra.c:1096-1098` sets `g_contStatus[i].status = 0` for every pad — `CONT_CARD_ON` is never set, and `src/joy.c:184` gates the *entire* rumble-pak init path on that bit, so `joyRumblePakInit()` never even calls `osPfsInit`. (2) `src/joy.c:186-190` only attempts `osMotorInit` if `osPfsInit`'s return is `PFS_ERR_ID_FATAL` or `PFS_ERR_DEVICE` — but the port's stub (`libultra.c:1214`) returns `PFS_ERR_NOPACK`, so motor init is never attempted even once (1) is fixed. PD's exact trick (`libultra.c:213-227,349-351`): set `CONT_CARD_ON` for connected pads, and make `osPfsInitPak()` return `PFS_ERR_DEVICE` specifically when the pad supports rumble. **Whenever D224 gets implemented, both of these must land alongside the `SDL_GameControllerRumble` wiring** or the game's state machine parks at `RUMBLEPAKINITSTATE_NOT_READY` forever and nothing audibly changes despite looking wired up correctly.

## D225 — Dev-tooling QoL (M-87, user ask): a debug-build/env toggle that unlocks all missions + all cheats, for testing.

**Dev-tooling QoL (M-87, user ask): a debug-build/env toggle that unlocks all missions + all cheats, for testing.** Root-caused a clean single choke point — **both** gates route through the same function: `bool fileGetIsCheatUnlocked(save_data *save, s32 cheat)` (`src/game/file2.c:391`) reads the save's `unlocked_cheats_1/2/3` bitfields and returns whether bit `cheat` is set. Mission-select lock (`src/game/file.c:59`, gates whether a briefing page's mission is selectable) and the cheat-menu availability check (`frontCheckIfCheatIsUnlocked`, `front.c:1009`, itself calling `fileGetIsCheatUnlocked` for the per-level `SP_LEVEL_*` cheat IDs) **both** call it — it's a pure, side-effect-free bitfield read (no save-data mutation), so short-circuiting it to always-true under a debug env var unlocks mission-select *and* the cheat menu in one change, matching exactly what was asked ("those two go a long way"). **Bonus, free once cheats unlock:** the ROM already contains real Rare-era developer cheats that are otherwise unreachable in normal play — `CHEAT_LINEMODE` (wireframe render — would make D222-style culling bugs trivial to see), `CHEAT_BONDPHASE`, `CHEAT_DEBUG_POS`, `CHEAT_DEBUG_UNK5` (`cheat.c` ~L687-707, `CHEAT_MASK_GLOBAL`) — worth trying once this lands, may be useful dev tools in their own right.

**Status (from §F table):** **FIXED (2026-09-18), implementing the plan as proposed.** `fileGetIsCheatUnlocked()` (`src/game/file2.c:391`) now has an `#ifdef PORT` block right after the function's existing D301 NULL-guard: `GE_DEBUG_UNLOCKALL` is read once via the established cached-getenv pattern (`static int s_unlockAll = -1; if (s_unlockAll < 0) s_unlockAll = getenv(...) != NULL;`) and, if set, returns `TRUE` unconditionally before the real bitfield read. Default off ⇒ zero behavior change; when set, purely a query-time override — the save file is never written, so it can't corrupt or leak into a shipped save. **Verified:** clean rebuild; headless boot with `GE_DEBUG_UNLOCKALL=1 GE_STARTMENU=7` reaches mission select crash-free (visual confirmation of "everything shown as unlocked" not captured this session — the mission-select filmstrip's non-selected thumbnails always render dimmed regardless of lock state, so a static frame can't distinguish locked-dim from just-not-hovered; mechanism is correct by code read). The bonus developer-cheat suggestion (`CHEAT_LINEMODE` etc.) from the original write-up is unexplored, not part of this fix.

## D226 — QoL ask: player-adjustable HUD scale for the ammo counter, bottom-left pickup/item status text, and top-of-screen dialogue/subtitle text.

**QoL ask: player-adjustable HUD scale for the ammo counter, bottom-left pickup/item status text, and top-of-screen dialogue/subtitle text.** All three route through the same primitive, `textRenderOutlined()` (`src/game/textrelated.c:688`, doc comment: *"Used for ammo counter, bottom left HUD messages, countdown timers"*), called from two specific in-game (not menu) sites in `bondview2.c`: **ammo + bottom-left pickup/status** at `bondview2.c:10005` (`stringbuffer_lowerleft[...]`, anchored at `view_left`/`view_vert`), and **top-of-screen dialogue** at `bondview2.c:10163`/`10165` (`stringbuffer_top[...]`, anchored at `msg.x`/`msg.y`). `textRenderOutlined` → `textDrawGlyphQuad` (`textrelated.c:615`) emits each glyph as a plain RDP `gSPTextureRectangle` at the glyph's native font-metric pixel size, `dsdx`/`dsdy` = `0x400` (1:1 texel:pixel, no scale factor anywhere in the call chain). Same function is also used by menus/options/multiplayer UI (`front.c`, `options.c`, `mpmenu.c`) — **do not scale generically**, those have their own layout at fixed screen fractions and D211 already established HUD anchors must stay put; scale only the 3 in-game HUD call sites named above, about their existing anchor (so bottom-left stays bottom-left, top stays top — same anchor-preserving principle as D211's HUD-static check).

**Status (from §F table):** **OPEN — root cause / call sites identified, not designed or implemented.** Two viable directions: (a) a `#ifdef PORT` wrapper at just these 2-3 `bondview2.c` call sites that scales the emitted `gSPTextureRectangle` geometry (`xl/yl/xh/yh`) by a new `f32 portHudScale` (default 1.0 ⇒ byte-identical) while inversely scaling `dsdx/dsdy` to keep the same source glyph texels mapped onto the larger/smaller rect, re-anchored so the opposite edge (bottom for the lower-left block, top for dialogue) doesn't move; or (b) thread a scale parameter into `textRenderOutlined`/`textDrawGlyphQuad` itself, defaulted to 1.0 at every other call site. (a) is more surgical (matches the "don't touch shared menu text" constraint) but duplicates a little geometry math; (b) is more central but touches a much more widely shared function. No PD precedent found (PD's port has no equivalent HUD-scale option). F10 overlay slider candidate once implemented, alongside `Video.FovScale`.

**Design refinement (2026-09-23, not implemented).** Per-glyph scaling in `textDrawGlyphQuad` (option a/b above) is insufficient. Both HUD text sites first draw a background box sized to the measured *unscaled* text (lower-left: `draw_blackbox_to_screen`; top dialogue: `microcode_constructor_related_to_menus` over `msg.y..msg.bottom`), NTSC's dialogue path is `textRender`, not `textRenderOutlined`, and the ammo counter pairs text with an icon image (`set_rgba_redirect_generate_microcode`). Scaling glyphs alone would overflow the boxes and split the ammo readout. **Recommended:** a port-side span transform in fast3d, analogous to D335's aspect modes: a new EXT command carrying (scale, anchor x/y) that scales *all* rect and vertex positions (x and y, plus texrect dsdx/dsdy) about the anchor until cleared. The game-side edit is then just a wrap around each HUD call (box + text + icon together), anchored bottom-left for status text, top-centre for dialogue and bottom-right for ammo. The D335 LEFT/RIGHT/CENTER anchoring composes with it. Slider `Game.HudScale` 75–200%, default 100 (no emission, byte-identical).

**IMPLEMENTED (2026-09-24, v0.4.0) as designed above: `Game.HudScale` (F10 "HUD scale %", 75–150, default 100; capped at 150 after the user playtest: "past that not super effective").** fast3d: new extension command `G_HUDSCALE_EXT` (opcode 0x46, free in GE's command space; w0 low 16 = scale×256, w1 = anchor x/y in 10.2): while active, `gfx_dp_texture_rectangle` / `gfx_dp_fill_rectangle` scale rect coordinates about the anchor and divide texrect dsdx/dtdy by the scale (glyphs stay crisp, same texels). Rects clip at the canvas origin (negative rects aren't drawn). The state resets every frame. It composes with the D335 aspect anchors (scaling happens in logical space before the aspect mapping). Game (`#ifdef PORT`, Rule-2 approved presentation, `port/include/hudaspect.h` macros): bottom messages / title card anchored at the view's bottom-left; top dialogue anchored at its text origin (`msg.x` = view left + 0x1e); ammo per hand at the bottom-right / bottom-left. **Width cap:** dialogue and bottom-message line breaks are authored into the text (no runtime wrap), so those two scale only as far as their widest line still fits (`textMeasure` with the renderer's fonts; long lines stay at ~100% instead of clipping). At 100% nothing is emitted (byte-identical; golden 3/3). **Verified (1280×720 captures):** title card and ammo at 150%/200% correctly enlarged about their corners; Archives dialogue no longer clips (an earlier centre-anchor attempt cut off "Guard:", and an origin anchor without the cap overflowed the right edge). Windows + Linux builds clean. Commit `30720354`.

## D230 — In-level music quality: a bass instrument sounds corrupted on PC, correct on N64 reference (M-105, user reports; repro refined M-106).

**In-level music quality: a bass instrument sounds corrupted on PC, correct on N64 reference (M-105, user reports; repro refined M-106).** Filed to give the post-D77 residual its own label — D77 (in-level music *absence*) is RESOLVED (PR #42, missing `return` in `sub_GAME_7F0C0BF0` zeroed the seqp volume on the only in-level trigger path), so "music doesn't play" claims in tracked docs are stale; what actually remains is this quality gap. **M-106 repro, deterministic (not intermittent):** Control's elevator track and its regular in-level track both carry the bad instrument throughout; Cavern's elevator track has it too; Runway's track is otherwise fine but the same instrument enters ~5–7s after the track starts and sounds bad from then on. User confirmed against original N64 reference audio that a bass instrument belongs there on Runway — this is **not** a wrong-instrument/wrong-bank selection (rules out the D77 trigger-path family and the seqp-volume fix's neighborhood); the instrument choice is correct, only its *sound* is wrong on PC. Determinism (same track, same spot, every time) points at a static decode/synthesis bug for this instrument's wavetable/ADPCM data — most likely low-frequency-specific (pitch-shift/downsample artifacting, a wrap/loop-point error, or a clipping/gain issue that only bites bass-range samples) — rather than a live mixing/voice-stealing issue (D147/D152/D202 family), which would be intermittent. The mixer layer and the trigger layer are both proven working by every track that sounds right, so the suspect neighborhood is the seq/instrument-bank decode path (`csplayer.c`/`synthesizer.c`, bank loading), not `port/` audio plumbing.

**Status (from §F table):** **FIXED (M-121, v0.2.0) — see the M-121 paragraph below for the actual root cause and fix; the M-108/M-120 material immediately following this line is superseded investigation history, kept for the record.** Original M-108 static-analysis pass, repro: Control (elevator + regular track, throughout), Cavern (elevator, throughout), Runway (~5–7s in). Traced the suspect neighborhood to the software ADPCM decoder in `port/src/mixer.c` — the PC replacement for the RSP's `aLoadADPCM`/`aADPCMdec` ucode ops (`csplayer.c`/`synthesizer.c` only emit ucode command lists; they don't decode samples themselves). Found two hardcoded assumptions that don't hold for the general ADPCM-book format: (1) `sAdpcmTable` (`mixer.c:174`) is declared `[8][2][8]`, hardcoding predictor `order=2`, but `order`/`npredictors` are per-instrument authored fields (`include/PR/libaudio.h` `ALADPCMBook.order`; `src/libultra/audio/load.c:428-429` computes `bookSize` from them) that the bank-relayout code (`port/src/romdata.c:718-736`) already handles generically — if this bass instrument's authored book uses `order != 2`, the 2-tap recursion at `mixer.c:223-240` would decode it wrong; (2) even at `order=2`, `aLoadADPCMImpl` (`mixer.c:177-192`) silently truncates any book over 256 bytes (`mixer.c:183`, `npredictors > 8`), while the decode loop's 4-bit predictor-select nibble (`mixer.c:219`) can legitimately address up to 16 rows — an instrument with `npredictors > 8` would read truncated/garbage rows for some frames. **Caveat weakening confidence:** N64 SDK ADPCM in practice is conventionally always `order=2` (the RSP ucode's own decode algorithm is essentially fixed to a 2-tap recursion industry-wide), so candidate (1) may not apply to a real N64 title's data; candidate (2) (`npredictors > 8`) is the more plausible of the two absent contrary evidence. Not confirmed against GE's actual ROM-authored book data (no live capture taken this pass). Next: extend the existing `GE_MIXERTRACE=1` trace's `[LOADADPCM]` line (`mixer.c:187`, already logs `count` — `count/16 = order*npredictors`) to flag any book where `count > 256` (proves truncation) during a Control run, and correlate the anomalous book to its channel/instrument via `seqplayer.c:1120`'s program-change. If no anomaly shows, this whole neighborhood is likely a dead end and the next suspect is the resample (`mixer.c:295-341`) or envelope/gain (`mixer.c:379+`) paths for bass-range-specific behavior. **M-120 (local-Qwen triage dispatch): a third hypothesis proposed and CHECKED, RULED OUT.** The dispatched read-only pass proposed that `afFixupBook`'s `port/src/romdata.c:733-737` conversion of the ADPCM book coefficients (BE ROM → LE host, via `afRd16`/`afWr16`) is backwards and should stay big-endian. Verified against the actual code and disproven: (1) that conversion is the identical BE→LE pattern used for every other field in the same function (`order`/`npredictors` two lines above) and in the sibling `afFixupAdpcmLoop`'s ADPCM state array a few lines down — not something special-cased for this one book; (2) `port/src/mixer.c`'s `aLoadADPCMImpl` does a raw `memcpy` of the already-converted book straight into a host-native `s16[8][2][8]` table with no further byte-swap, consistent with the coefficients being intentionally pre-converted to host order; (3) decisively, `afFixupBook` is one shared code path applied uniformly to every ADPCM book in the game — if this conversion were actually backwards, every ADPCM-encoded sound would decode wrong, not one bass instrument on three tracks, and the vast majority of the game's audio is confirmed correct. Do not re-propose this specific byte-order theory without new evidence; the standing M-108 leads above (predictor-count truncation / `order` mismatch) remain the live ones. **FIXED (M-121, v0.2.0 finalization) — root cause was a plain byte-order bug in a corner neither M-108 nor M-120 looked at: RAW16 wavetables.** Offline decode of the local NTSC ROM's instrument bank found exactly two `AL_RAW16_WAVE` (type 1) wavetables — instruments 2 and 51, both sharing base 0x2118 / len 790 in the `_instrumentstbl` segment — which decode as a clean ~110 Hz soft-attack bass synth sample when read as **big-endian** s16. That is the missing bass instrument on Control/Cavern/Runway. On N64 the CPU reads those bytes BE, so it plays fine there; on PC the mixer's resampler (`port/src/mixer.c` `alRaw16Pull` path) consumes host-native (little-endian) s16, so every sample arrives byte-swapped — a deterministic per-instrument corruption, exactly matching the M-106 repro (and explaining why every ADPCM-based instrument in the game sounds right: nibble data is byte-order agnostic). Both M-108 candidates are moot — every ADPCM book in both bank trees (scanned offline from the ROM) is `order=2, npredictors∈{1,4}`, so neither the `[8][2][8]` shape nor the 256-byte truncation can ever bite GE's data. **Fix (port-only, D55 in-place-fixup idiom):** `romdataFinishCartMap()` (`port/src/romdata.c`) now walks both bank trees (SFX + instruments; same ALBankFile layout as `romdataFixupAudioBank`) and bswap16s each RAW16 wavetable's `[tbl+base, +len)` range in place in the cart map — where the sample data lives for the mixer (`alBnkfNew()` points at the tbl segments directly; only the bank structs are re-laid out, D37). Shared ranges are deduped (swapping twice would undo the swap); every read is bounds-checked against the ROM size. Startup log: `romdataInit: D230 byte-swapped 1 RAW16 wavetable range(s) in place` (one range: the two instruments share the sample data). Byte-level verification done (BE decode of the ROM range = clean tone; post-swap LE decode identical by construction); **owes a by-ear pass** on Control (elevator + level track), Cavern elevator, and Runway ~5–7 s in.

## D218 — Wide FOV exposes the per-level draw-distance / fog boundary — "blue artifacting" down long peripheral sightlines (M-84, user QA on the D211 FOV slider).

**Wide FOV exposes the per-level draw-distance / fog boundary — "blue artifacting" down long peripheral sightlines (M-84, user QA on the D211 FOV slider).** BUNKER→**Dam main tunnel** at `FovScale` ~150: geometry / backdrop past the level's fog-end distance shows at the widened frustum edges (blue = Dam's fog tint). Not a render bug — `fogLoadCurrentEnvironment` (`bgfog.c:305`) does `viSetZRange(Visibility.BlendMultiplier, Visibility.FarFog)`, so **`Visibility.FarFog` is both the far clip plane and the fog-saturation distance**; levels tune it for the stock ~60° FOV.

**Status (from §F table):** **Logged (M-84), fix proposed + parked.** Plan: `Video.DrawDistance` (percent, 100–400, default 100 ⇒ no-op) `#ifdef PORT` multiplier on `FarFog` at `bgfog.c:305` (+ the direct `arg0->Visibility.FarFog` reads just below, so fog stays consistent) plus `Video.DrawDistanceAutoFov` (0/1, default 1 — couples draw distance to `FovScale` unless `DrawDistance` is set explicitly). Clamp effective multiplier ≲2.5× (small znear ⇒ far-field z-fighting risk). **M-87: user confirms still occurring** at high FOV, and — reversing the earlier "not implemented by user request" — **now wants `Video.DrawDistance` implemented as a real QoL feature**, plus scope it to cover **LOD/detail-distance in general**, not just the fog/far-clip boundary this row root-caused. Open question for that broader ask: does GE have a *separate* geometry/object LOD-swap or draw-culling distance mechanism (distinct from `Visibility.FarFog`) worth exposing too, or is fog-distance the only meaningful "how far can you see" knob in this engine? Check for a per-object visibility-radius / simple-model-swap system before assuming `FarFog` is the whole story. **FIXED as designed, awaiting visual verification (M-121).** Implemented exactly the parked plan: `f32 portDrawDistanceMultiplier(void)` (`port/src/video.c`) — an explicit `Video.DrawDistance != 100` wins outright, otherwise `Video.DrawDistanceAutoFov` (default on) couples the multiplier 1:1 to `Video.FovScale`, clamped to `[1.0, 2.5]` (never shrinks draw distance; the 2.5x ceiling is the finding's own far-field z-fighting caution). Applied in `fogLoadCurrentEnvironment` (`bgfog.c`) to a new local (`scaledFarFog`) used at *both* the `viSetZRange` far-clip call and the `g_CurFogDetails.scaled_far_fog_dist` fog-blend read just below it, so the clip plane and the fog math stay consistent per the original plan's own note — the level's `EnvironmentRecord` itself is never mutated (it's shared/reloaded, not a per-frame copy). Both new config keys added to the F10 overlay (`Video.DrawDistance` slider, `Video.DrawDistanceAutoFov` toggle) alongside the existing `FovScale` row. Identity at both defaults (`DrawDistance=100`, `FovScale=100` ⇒ `portFovScale==1.0f`) by construction. **Broader LOD-swap question from M-87 ANSWERED — yes, and now exposed too (same session, M-121 continued).** `src/game/model.c` has a real, distinct geometry-LOD system: `MODELNODE_OPCODE_LOD` nodes whose children are shown/hidden per-frame by `modelUpdateDistanceRelations()` testing a view-space `distance` (scaled by `getPlayer_c_lodscalez()`, itself now FOV-consistent per this session's D222 fix) against each node's `MinDistance`/`MaxDistance` — a genuine detail-swap mechanism, separate from the fog-visibility-fade this row already fixed. It even has an existing ground-truth multiplier hook, `g_ModelDistanceScale`, already used transiently by the game itself (`chr.c`'s 0.3125f close-up override, `front.c`/`title.c`'s menu-model `modelSetDistanceDisabled`). Rather than write to that shared global (would fight those existing overrides), added a second, composed multiplier at the same call site: `f32 portLodDistanceMultiplier(void)` (`port/src/video.c`), driven by new `Video.LodDistance` (percent, 25-400, default 100) and `Video.LodDistanceAutoFov` (**default OFF**, unlike `DrawDistanceAutoFov` — this is meant as a standalone performance lever the user can pull *down*, not something that silently adds cost as FovScale widens) — `distance *= portLodDistanceMultiplier()`, inverse-scaled so `LodDistance=200` keeps full detail twice as far (more cost) and `LodDistance=50` drops to the lower LOD twice as soon (less cost). Both new keys in the F10 overlay alongside `DrawDistance`. Identity at `LodDistance=100`. Rebuilt clean, crash-free at `LodDistance=40` (aggressive) on Dam and at defaults on bunker1. **M-121 live playtest, iterated to a working state.** Two real issues found and fixed while testing live on Dam with the user: (1) **regression** — the D222 fix (above) correctly widened `c_lodscalez` for the screen-edge cull planes, but that same value is *also* read directly by `propobj.c`'s `chrobjFogVisRangeRelated()`/`sub_GAME_7F054C58()` (the character/prop fog-visibility-fade cutoff) — uncompensated, this made guards fade/disappear *sooner* at wide FOV than before D222, the opposite of the intent. Fixed by dividing that same `c_lodscalez` reading by `portDrawDistanceMultiplier()` at both call sites (`#ifdef PORT`), so the "how far can you see" question these two share is answered consistently. (2) **tuning** — a straight 1:1 `Video.FovScale` auto-coupling on `portDrawDistanceMultiplier()` was not aggressive enough; live-tested up twice (1x → 2x → 4x `FovScale`, clamp ceiling raised 2.5x → 4.0x → 6.0x each time) before guards held up and the Dam tunnel's blue-glow artifact receded to the user's satisfaction. Re-verified end-to-end that the fog *ramp* itself (not just the far-clip cutoff) scales with the multiplier — `g_ScaledFarFogIntensity`/`scaled_far_fog_dist` both derive from the same scaled far value — so if a similar artifact resurfaces on another level, the multiplier magnitude or a level-specific tunnel-length edge case are the first things to check, not this math. **User confirms this is good for now.** All three (D222 cull fix, D218 draw-distance + fog-visibility-fade fix, D249 LOD-distance) verified crash-free and landing in the same PR.

## D220 — 1P muzzle flash position shifts upward at higher `Video.FovScale` (M-87, user QA, Jungle/M16).

**1P muzzle flash position shifts upward at higher `Video.FovScale` (M-87, user QA, Jungle/M16).** Likely shares D211's noted residual: the viewmodel draws through `c_perspfovy`/unscaled fovy while the world view is FovScale-scaled (`fr.c:737`), so a flash sprite anchored to viewmodel-space vs. screen-space math can drift as the two diverge more at higher scale.

**Status (from §F table):** **ANALYZED (M-91) — the suspected unscaled-viewmodel root does NOT hold; this is correct perspective behavior, likely cosmetic/QoL.** The 1P hand + flash are model nodes in ONE gun DL (`gunfire.c` builds `rwmtx[1..4]` for hammer/flash/billboard nodes) drawn through the single per-frame projection from `viSetupCurrentPlayerView` — which IS FovScale-scaled on PC. So the flash and the muzzle it attaches to share projection and matrix chain: their relative position is geometrically preserved. What moves is the whole camera-anchored viewmodel: under perspective, screen offset from center ∝ 1/tan(fovy/2), so widening the FOV migrates every camera-space point (gun body included) toward screen center — a muzzle sitting slightly below/right of center visibly drifts up-left at FovScale 150. Same family as the M-85 accepted "viewmodel scales down, stays bottom-right anchored". `c_perspfovy`/`currentPlayerSetCameraScale` do stay unscaled (the D211 note) but that feeds frustum-cull/screen↔world math (→ D222), not the flash's render path. **Disposition: human call** — if it bothers at high FovScale, the fix is a QoL viewmodel re-anchor/scale-at-FOV (VIEWMODEL-RESEARCH.md family), not a fidelity bug; no game-logic change either way. Optional headless confirm: Jungle M16 fire at FovScale 100 vs 150, measure flash centroid vs muzzle in PPM pairs (expected: both shift toward center together).

## D235 — Wrong textures load after dying/restarting a level — not Facility-specific, seen on multiple levels (M-106, user QA report; clarified same session).

**Wrong textures load after dying/restarting a level — not Facility-specific, seen on multiple levels (M-106, user QA report; clarified same session).** Original report ("Facility: wrong textures now") read as a build regression; user clarified the actual trigger is **death/restart** (or a similar level-reload path), and it has recurred on other levels too — this is a state-leak on level re-entry, not a one-level texture-decode bug and likely not caused by #47/#49 at all. Prime suspect: the texture pool / CI-cache (D217/D228 neighbourhood) not being fully reset between a level teardown and its reload — a stale arena base, a leftover palette-cache entry keyed by an address that gets reused with different content, or a texpool index not rewound — surfacing as "wrong texture" only after the reload path runs, never on a fresh level boot. Logged in `GRAPHICS-BACKLOG.md`.

**Status (from §F table):** OPEN — needs: does it repro on a *fresh* level boot (rules out reload-state) vs only after death/restart (confirms it); which surfaces; a screenshot. **M-108 static-analysis pass: the leading "stale CI-cache not reset on restart" hypothesis is likely REFUTED, don't re-propose it as-is.** The theory was that `g_TexCacheItems`/`g_TexCacheCount` (`src/game/image.c:38-40`, cleared only in `set_mt_tex_alloc()`, `src/game/initmttex.c:8`) survives a death/restart because the restart path skips `set_mt_tex_alloc`. But tracing the actual call graph: `set_mt_tex_alloc()` runs inside `lvlStageLoad()` (`src/game/lv.c:369`), which has exactly **one** call site (`src/boss.c:485`) inside `bossMainloop`'s outer `while (!done)` loop; that loop re-runs on *every* stage transition, driven by `g_StageNum = g_MainStageNum` (`boss.c:693`) which is set by `bossSetLoadedStage()` (`boss.c:722`) — the same function the front-end's level-select/continue path calls (`front.c:6947`). Nothing in this call graph is level-select-specific vs. restart-specific; both look like they go through the identical full reload (including the `set_mt_tex_alloc` cache reset). Have not yet found the actual death/restart trigger's call site to be 100% certain it doesn't have its own bypass, so this isn't fully closed out — but the single-reload-path structure makes the "cache survives restart" mechanism unlikely as stated. Next: find the actual death-handler call site (search for where a life/continue/retry decision is made, likely `chr.c`/a game-state machine, not yet located) and confirm whether it calls `bossSetLoadedStage`/goes through `bossMainloop`'s reload path same as normal transitions, or has a distinct lighter-weight path — if it's the same path, the real D235 mechanism is still unknown and this CI-cache theory should be dropped.

**M-193 (v0.4.0 Phase 1, 2026-09-21): port-side GL texture cache found — the M-108 refutation stands for the *game-side* CI cache, but the port has its own cache with the exact same structural hazard, and it was never invalidated on stage transitions.** The PC renderer keeps a `TextureCacheMap` (`port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp`) mapping `(source address, palette addrs, fmt, siz, palette_index, size_bytes, palette_hash)` → uploaded GL texture, with **no content check** — a hit trusts the key. Stage textures' source addresses live in the `MEMPOOL_STAGE` arena, which the per-stage `while (!done)` block in `boss.c` resets via `mempResetBank`/`memaReset` on *every* transition (death/restart included — M-108's call-graph trace already established both paths re-run that block). After the reset, any cache entry keyed into that arena is stale; if the texpool places a different image at an address that held another image in the previous run of the level, the lookup hits and returns the old pixels = "wrong textures after dying/restarting", never on a cold boot (empty cache). The N64 has no such cache (the RSP re-reads DRAM every frame), so this is a pure port-side defect — fixable in `port/`-adjacent code with no rule-2 sign-off. **Fix applied:** the orphaned `videoResetTextureCache()` (`port/src/video.c`, zero callers) is now wired into that per-stage block right after `memaReset`/`reset_play_data_ptrs` (`#ifdef PORT`) — a full clear on every stage load. Re-uploads are pixel-identical (same content → same GL upload), cost is one-time during the loading screen; ROM-segment textures (menu/HUD) just re-upload too, harmlessly. `GE_D235=1` logs the purged entry count per transition (cold boot = 0, death/restart > 0) as direct mechanism evidence. **Remaining:** live death/restart confirmation at playtest (wrong textures gone?) + a `GE_D235` capture showing >0 on a restart; if symptoms persist after this, the next suspect is intra-level texpool eviction reusing addresses mid-play (nothing emits `G_INVALTEXCACHE_EXT`, so per-address staleness is possible there too — the handler exists at `gfx_pc.cpp:3624` but has no emitter).

**v0.4.0 verification pass (2026-09-23, native Windows, headless): fix wired and clean on reload; the bug itself did NOT reproduce, even with the fix disabled. Needs the user's original trigger to close.** Harness: `-level_09`, scripted watch Abort → title stage → new TEMP `GE_D235_RELOAD=<frames>` re-enters Bunker 1 via `bossSetLoadedStage()` (the front end's mission-start call) after a front-end dwell; new TEMP `GE_D235_OFF=1` skips the reset for an A/B. Results:
- Fix ON: cold boot purges 0, the abort into the title purges 527–833, and re-entry purges 63 (front-end entries). The reloaded level renders correctly; settled gameplay matches the fix-OFF run 7/9 frames, and the 2 fails are intro-fade/camera timing (D117), not textures.
- Fix OFF, identical load order (intro both times, 300-frame legal-screen dwell): 588–788 stale entries survive into the reload; **all textures correct**.
- Fix OFF, divergent load order (first load skips the intro, so only the shaft is seen; the reload plays the full control-room flyby): 589 stale entries survive; **all textures correct** at full resolution (`scratch/d235_1750.png`).

So on this path, stale keys either miss or hit the same image. Either GE's placement of Bunker 1's bg textures is order-independent here, or the key (`palette_hash`, `size_bytes`, fmt) disambiguates. The fix stays correct by construction: an address-keyed cache with no content check outlives an arena reset, and clearing it at every stage load costs only re-uploads during the loading screen. What's untested is the reported trigger: a real **death → mission failed → mission select → restart** (the front end's image-heavy briefing/folder screens and 3D models go through the stage arena in between) on the level where it was seen (Facility first). **Human test:** reproduce with `GE_D235_OFF=1` (expect wrong textures) and without (expect clean); note the level and surfaces. Confidence that the fix addresses the report: medium, since the mechanism is real but the trigger is not captured.

**2026-09-25 playtest (user, Windows, one ~46-min session Silo → Caverns, `GE_D322=1 GE_D204=1`, build `7baf4900`):** die → mission select → restart did not reproduce wrong textures (fix on). Still unreproduced in every configuration; stays OPEN only because the original trigger was never observed locally.

**Surface 1: 2D billboard trees render as a wall/sheet of tree texture instead of discrete camera-facing tree sprites (M-106, user QA report).** Eight passes so far (D265, D266–D270, D271, D272, D273, D274, D275–D276). Ruled out: IA4/IA8 decode (as originally scoped), the blend pipeline, fog combine (as originally scoped), portal-culling over-draw (D271, real bug, fixed, not the cause), converter/UV-conversion bugs (D272, code-read clean), the CI palette bit-layout (D273/D274, tested twice against real content), "mips absent" (D274, confirmed present/enabled), "identical UV window" *for the CI8 classes* (D272). **Current leading picture (D276, M-134): the actual visible weave at confirmed weave pixels is painted by a different, previously-dismissed class — an IA8 blocky-noise texture (`oml=0xc81049d8`/`fmt=3`) sampled with a fixed, byte-identical 2×-wrapped UV window and low fog, reproducing D265's original "same window" observation exactly (D269's CI8-classes framing had reframed away from that lead prematurely).** A third, unattributed CI8 class (`0x0c184b50`) may be the reference's actual discrete-tree layer and shows an erratic z/w suggesting its own occlusion/billboard bug — D236 may split into two root causes. **Ninth pass (D280, M-135): fog math verified N64-faithful (±2 truncation over 2505 verts), the IA8 noise class visually confirmed as the weave's painter (HF 14.8→2.9 when collapsed), `0xc8102078` ruled out (terrain, 1.4M tris), and the depth-race read inverted — `0x0c184b50` tree cards are IN FRONT of the noise quad (z/w smaller=closer) yet still don't visibly win; under deterministic `-level_36` boot they barely instantiate at all (~4 tris vs 720 in a free run). No quick win: remaining work is CPU-side instantiation/room-streaming, not a port fix.** **Tenth pass (M-155): that CPU-side-instantiation framing itself is REFUTED — three independent deterministic re-runs of the same `-level_36` boot (one with sustained camera rotation) proved the class's per-frame count is byte-identical, not run-to-run dependent; the earlier "~4 vs 720" comparison was an outdoor-vs-indoor room mismatch (the boot's scripted intro walks the camera out of the tree-bearing room at a fixed frame), not nondeterminism. No fix; the original wall-vs-discrete-sprites symptom is unresolved and untouched by this pass.** Distinct from D176(b)'s painted tree-line backdrop. Logged in `GRAPHICS-BACKLOG.md`.

**Status (from §F table):** OPEN — **pass 24 (2026-09-21, static) DECODED THE TREE TEXTURE** (new `tools_pc/texdecode.py` ports image.c's LOOKUP/HUFFLOOKUP/RLELOOKUP codecs). **`tex1198` LOD 0 = 64×17 RGBA5551, 44.2% opaque, and its 1-bit alpha renders as an unmistakable treeline silhouette** — pass 23's identification confirmed by decode, not inference. **Rare authored a six-level LOD pyramid that PRESERVES the silhouette and its alpha coverage (44.2% → 43.1% → 38.8%), each level a separately-authored image with its own compmethod.** Since `XLU_SURF` has no alpha test (pass 22), averaging that 0/1 alpha into fractional mip alpha would smear the minified treeline into exactly the reported band — so 'authored LOD chain replaced by driver-generated mips' is now the leading mechanism, with hard ground truth behind it. Corrects pass 23: only `tex1198` is a treeline (`tex1199` 89.4% opaque denser foliage; `tex1200`/`tex1201` 100% opaque detail textures sharing the class). Two decoder bugs found while porting (missing per-image byte-align, `image.c:1096`; a GUESSED rather than ported RLE fudge) — both produced confident wrong pictures. Next: one `-level_36` run filtered on **`fmt=0 siz=2`**, diffing the live import against this offline reference on (1) 64×17 RGBA5551 dims/format, (2) ~44% alpha transparency, (3) whether all six authored LODs reach GL or only LOD 0.

**Pass 12 (2026-09-18, this session): a genuinely new mechanism found and confirmed real, but the exact visually-bugged view still has too little tree-class geometry to test it against — not a fix, narrows the next pass.**

**New mechanism, not considered by passes 1-11 (all of which reasoned from z/w comparisons):** decoded both classes' full `other_mode_l` words offline — `0xc81049d8` (noise) and `0x0c184b50` (tree cards) are **both `Z_CMP=1`/`Z_UPD=0`/`ZMODE=DEC`** (decal mode, depth-tested but not depth-written). Two non-depth-writing decals never actually depth-test against each other — each tests only against the static background's z-buffer — so on-screen precedence between them is decided by **draw order alone** (whichever is submitted later in the frame wins the color buffer), not by which is geometrically closer. This means the z/w comparisons all 11 prior passes made were measuring something that doesn't determine the visual winner between these two specific classes.

Built `GE_D236ORDER` (`port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp`, `gfx_sp_tri1`, env-gated, zero cost unset) to measure this directly: a per-frame submission-order counter, logging the min/max order index for each class whenever `num_dls` (frame) changes. Also built `GE_D236ZFIX` (same file), a diagnostic-only experiment forcing `depth_update=true` for the tree-card class alone, to test whether giving it real z-write lets it correctly block a later-drawn noise quad — **not proposed as a fix** (decal-mode classes aren't supposed to write depth; this would need its own rule-2 justification if it ever became a real fix candidate).

**Headless repro finally landed on the actual bug, no live session needed this pass.** `GE_PCDUMP=1300-1700:100` on `-level_36` (a snowy corridor level, not literally "Surface 1/2" by debug number but visually and mechanically the same wall-of-static symptom) captured the exact reported look: a solid black-and-white static-noise "wall" on both sides of a snow corridor, `docs/dev/GRAPHICS-BACKLOG.md`-consistent with the user's screenshots. **`GE_D236ORDER` at this exact captured frame range shows `tree_n=0` throughout** — the discrete tree-card class has **zero triangles present at all** in the view that shows the bug, not merely "in the wrong order." A few hundred frames earlier in the same deterministic run (dl≈609-634), 2 tree triangles ARE present and (in that window) drawn **after** the noise class — the theoretically-correct order for them to win — but 2 triangles is nowhere near enough geometry to visually register against a whole wall of noise texture, and a screenshot at that exact frame (`scratch/ppm_620/frame_000620.png`) confirms it looks identical to the bugged view (no visible trees).

**Conclusion: the draw-order/decal mechanism is real and worth keeping as a documented candidate, but it isn't provably the active cause of the specific reported visual** — the deterministic boot simply never has enough tree-class geometry present at the bugged camera position to test the theory against, the same wall every pass since D280 has hit. This is unchanged from pass 9-11's own conclusion despite the new mechanism: **the real blocker is still CPU-side tree-prop instantiation/room-streaming at this exact camera position**, not (as far as this pass can tell) a port-side rendering bug. Confidence: HIGH that the decal-mode draw-order mechanism is real and correctly understood; LOW-to-none that it's the dominant cause of the reported symptom, since the necessary competing geometry isn't present to observe it losing or winning.

**Next pass, concrete (supersedes the "correlate against D280" step above, still valid but now sharper):** a live human session, `GE_D236ORDER=1` set, walking directly toward the tree line from inside the level (not the deterministic boot's opening corridor) is now the single most informative next capture — it would show, in one run: (a) does the tree-card count reach anything near D280's ~720 figure at this camera position, and if so (b) is `GE_D236ORDER`'s per-frame order relationship consistently noise-after-tree (bad) or tree-after-noise (fine) once real geometry is present. That single data point would finally either confirm or rule out the decal draw-order mechanism as the actual fix target, something no headless capture has been able to test in three sessions running. **Not v0.3.0-blocking, per standing user priority** — recommend parking again rather than rushing an unverified fix under release-timeline pressure. `GE_D236ORDER`/`GE_D236ZFIX` left in tree, env-gated, zero behavior change when unset.

**Pass 13 (2026-09-18, same session): the requested live capture landed, and it demotes the draw-order mechanism rather than confirming it — the more promising remaining lead is the tree class's own fog, not draw order.**

User played live with `GE_D236ORDER=1` set, walked toward Surface1's tree line, and confirmed the wall bug still reproduces (`scratch/d236_live_capture.log`, 2024 `D236ORDER` lines). Real data at last: tree-card count reached up to **121 triangles** (still short of D280's old ~720, but far beyond the deterministic boot's 2-4 — confirms the boot genuinely undersamples this class, not that it's absent from the level). More importantly: **the draw-order relationship is distance-dependent** — at low tree counts (6-12 tris, farther away) the noise class is consistently drawn *after* the tree class (bad order, matches pass 12's theory); at high tree counts (100+, closer) this **flips** — the tree class is consistently drawn *after* the noise class (good order, trees should win the color buffer).

**The decisive fact: the user still saw the wall bug while walking through the zone where tree count was high AND draw order favored the trees.** If pass 12's decal-ordering mechanism were the dominant cause, the bug should have resolved (or visibly improved) exactly in that zone — it didn't. **Conclusion: draw order is real (confirmed twice now, in two different measurement contexts) but is NOT the dominant cause of the reported symptom** — something else is preventing the tree cards from reading as discrete trees even when they have substantial triangle count and favorable draw order.

**Redirects the investigation to a lead D280 flagged but never closed: the tree class's own fog computation, not the noise class's.** D280's fog-math verification (`## D280` above, step 1) proved the *noise* class (`0xc81049d8`)'s fog is N64-faithful — it never checked the *tree* class (`0x0c184b50`)'s own fog, which D280's own census separately found to be a strange bimodal 25/255 split per vertex (`gfog=0`, CPU-baked, not RSP-computed). A tree card drawn correctly on top of the noise (as the live data now shows happens at close range) but rendered with fog=255 (fully white-washed) would look exactly like a blank/hazy patch of "wall," not a tree — consistent with the reported symptom persisting despite correct geometry and order.

**Not attempted this pass — genuinely the next step, not a rehash:** trace `0x0c184b50`'s own per-vertex fog computation (where it's set, CPU-side vs RSP, and against what reference distance) and compare it to what N64 would compute for the same vertex positions. This is a different code path than D280's already-verified noise-class fog check and hasn't been looked at directly. Given the depth of this investigation (13 passes) and the release timeline, **recommend keeping this parked for v0.3.0** — the mechanism is narrowed further than ever, but not yet a safe, confident fix. `GE_D236ORDER`/`GE_D236ZFIX` remain in tree, env-gated, zero cost when unset; the live capture log is preserved at `scratch/d236_live_capture.log` for whoever picks this up next.

**Pass 14 (2026-09-18, later session, no timeline pressure — user asked to keep going): sharpened pass 13's fog lead into a falsifiable mechanism and built the probe to test it; not yet live-captured.**

**Two things checked by source review before touching code, both clean:** (1) `port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp`'s `gfx_sp_vertex` fog fallback (`if (rsp.geometry_mode & G_FOG) {...} else { d->fog = rdp.fog_color.a; } d->color.a = vcn->a;`) is **byte-identical to the local Perfect Dark PC port reference** (`pd_port/port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp:1177-1194`) — this exact branch is not a GE-specific bug, it's shared, more-battle-tested fast3d ground truth. (2) `rsp/graphics/gmain.s` (GE's own RSP ucode, the AGENTS.md ground truth for GBI semantics) has **zero fog-related code** — GE's ucode doesn't customize fog generation at all, so there's nothing GE-specific to cross-check there either. Both rule out "our RSP fog emulation is wrong" as the mechanism.

**Decoded the tree class's actual render mode/blend equation** (`0x0c184b50`, matched against `include/PR/gbi.h`'s `RM_AA_ZB_XLU_DECAL(clk)` macro: `AA_EN|Z_CMP|IM_RD|CVG_DST_WRAP|CLR_ON_CVG|FORCE_BL|ZMODE_DEC`, blend `GBL_c(G_BL_CLR_IN, G_BL_A_IN, G_BL_CLR_MEM, G_BL_1MA)` — exactly matches D280/D272's Z_CMP=1/Z_UPD=0/ZMODE=DEC finding). This is an ordinary **alpha-blend decal**: `out = src_color*src_alpha + dst_color*(1-src_alpha)`. Critically, the blend equation does **not** reference `G_BL_CLR_FOG`/`G_BL_A_FOG` at all — whatever ends up as this triangle's alpha (SHADE alpha, i.e. `vcn->a`, the same raw per-vertex value D280's census found bimodal at 25/255) directly controls how *transparent* the tree card is over whatever was drawn underneath it (the noise class, confirmed drawn first in the close/high-count zone by pass 13's own data).

**New hypothesis, not proposed by passes 1-13:** if a meaningful fraction of a close tree card's vertices carry the low end of that bimodal split (`~25`, i.e. ~10% opacity) rather than the high end (`255`, opaque), the card would blend almost invisibly over the noise texture even when it has correct geometry, correct triangle count, and correct (tree-after-noise) draw order — reproducing exactly the "still looks like a wall" result pass 13 reported in its own favorable zone. This reframes the open question from "is the *fog value* right" (D280's framing, ambiguous — this render mode doesn't consume `d->fog`/RSP fog at all) to the narrower, directly testable one: **is vertex alpha low specifically for the close/high-count trees the live capture walked through, or does it correlate sanely with distance (opaque near, faded far, as a billboard fade LOD would legitimately do)?** Neither this pass nor any prior one has the data to answer that yet — D280's "bimodal 25/255" finding was a class-wide census, not correlated against per-instance camera distance at the specific bugged vantage.

**Built, not yet run live:** `GE_D236ALPHA` (`port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp`, `gfx_sp_tri1`, env-gated, zero cost unset, same pattern as `GE_D236ORDER`/`GE_D236RM`). For every triangle of the `0x0c184b50` class (capped at 4000 hits to bound log size): logs the combine_mode word once whenever it changes (to confirm alpha really is sourced from SHADE and not, say, ENVIRONMENT or a constant, before trusting the hypothesis further), then each triangle's three vertex alphas (`v1/v2/v3->color.a`) alongside `1/w` for each vertex (a cheap camera-distance proxy, smaller w = closer) so alpha can be correlated against distance the same way pass 13's live capture correlated tree count/draw-order against distance. Build verified clean (`./build-pc.sh ntsc-final`, 243/243, only pre-existing unrelated warnings); `tools_pc/verify.sh dam` PASS, crash-free with the probe compiled in and unset.

**Next step, concrete: a live capture identical in method to pass 13's** — `GE_D236ALPHA=1`, walk toward Surface1's tree line from far to close, same as before. Read the resulting log for: (a) does `v->color.a` trend toward 255 as `1/w` grows (closer)? If yes, the port is faithfully reproducing an N64-authored near-opaque/far-faded billboard fade and this hypothesis is refuted, redirecting back to an as-yet-unfound mechanism. If alpha stays low (~25) even at high `1/w` (close range, matching the zone where pass 13's draw order was already favorable), that's a concrete, falsifiable bug signature — the next question after that would be *where* that low value is coming from (baked ROM vertex data being read wrong vs. a legitimate baked-low value that N64's own combiner/blend path compensates for in some other way this port doesn't reproduce). **Not v0.3.0-blocking per standing user priority, but the user asked to keep working it regardless of release timing this session.** `GE_D236ORDER`/`GE_D236ZFIX`/`GE_D236ALPHA` all remain in tree, env-gated, zero cost when unset.

**Pass 15 (2026-09-18, same later session — the requested live capture landed, decisively quantifying the mechanism, but still stops short of a fix): confirmed the tree class's vertex alpha genuinely never reaches anywhere near opaque, and confirmed exactly how it drives the final transparency — but couldn't establish whether the low values are faithful ROM data or a decode bug.**

**Launched the game directly** (`GE_D236ALPHA=1 ./build-pc/ge007.x86_64.exe -level_36`, MSYS2 PATH for the SDL2 runtime dep) so the user could walk the exact same far→close tree-line approach as pass 13 without a separate build step; 1500 `D236ALPHA` lines captured (500 triangles × 3 vertices = 4500 alpha samples), well under the probe's 4000-triangle cap.

**Result 1 — alpha never gets close to opaque, anywhere in the walk.** Across the *entire* session, `v->color.a` ranged **0–36** (out of 255, i.e. ≤14% opacity) — not the 25/255 bimodal split D280's older class-wide census described. Bucketing all 4500 samples into deciles by `1/w` (camera-distance proxy, larger = closer) shows a real, monotonic trend — mean alpha rises from 6.2 in the farthest decile to 27.1 in the closest — but the ceiling never lifts: even the single closest samples captured topped out at 36. Two readings are consistent with this data and neither is ruled out yet: (a) the player never got quite close enough in this session to reach whatever distance a card would need to hit 255 (the closest `1/w` bucket, 0.0011–0.0018, has no calibration reference in this codebase to say whether that's "close" in engine units), or (b) the alpha value is capped/scaled wrong regardless of true distance.

**Result 2 — decoded the actual combine equation, resolving pass 14's open "which alpha slot" question.** The single `combine_mode` word logged this session (`0x00f39e4f1f39e4f1`, unchanged for the whole class) decodes via this file's own shader-synthesis extraction (`gfx_pc.cpp` ~L359-366) to alpha cycle `(a=1,b=7,c=4,d=7)` = `(TEXEL0 − 0) × SHADE + 0` in both cycles — i.e. **final alpha = texture alpha × vertex(SHADE) alpha**, the standard `G_CC_MODULATEIA` idiom. This confirms pass 14's hypothesis outright: whatever the CI8 tree texture's own per-texel alpha is (presumably near-255 for opaque tree pixels, going by the format), the vertex alpha multiplies it back down — so a vertex alpha capped at 36/255 caps *every* tree pixel drawn through that vertex at ≤14% opacity, full stop, regardless of the texture's own content. This is now a settled fact about the render pipeline, not a hypothesis.

**Traced the vertex-color path as far as source review allows this pass, found no swap/decode bug in it, but couldn't identify what actually computes/bakes this specific class's alpha.** `bgLoadRoomVtxData`/`bgSwapRoomVtx` (`bg.c:2353-2369`, room-level static vertex table load) explicitly documents and correctly implements "swap the 6 leading u16 fields (position/flag/uv), **leave the 4 colour bytes alone**" — if this room's tree-card geometry comes through this path, the raw ROM-authored alpha byte passes through completely unmodified, byte-for-byte, and this port has no bug in that specific step. Went looking for a CPU-side per-frame alpha *computation* next (the mechanism that would explain the real, non-flat 1/w correlation the data shows) and found one real candidate, `fogGetPropDistColor`/`chrobjFogVisRangeRelated` (`bgfog.c:695`, `propobj.c:7420+`) — a genuine decomp-verbatim distance-fog alpha blend used for `PropRecord`/`ObjectRecord` instances (doors, tinted glass, damage-decal props) — but confirmed by grep that `bg.c`/`bgapply.c` (the actual room-background-geometry load path this tree class's render-mode signature points to, per D280's census) **never reference** `fogGetPropDistColor` or its `far_fog_dist_scaled`/`near_fog_dist_scaled` fields at all, so that specific function is not this class's mechanism — a dead end, not a fit, ruled out this pass. **Did not find the actual code that determines whether this tree class is static ROM-baked vertex data (in which case N64 would show identical values, and any bug is downstream of the raw bytes, not in reading them) or is computed by some other per-frame CPU path not yet located** (the smooth 1/w correlation in the live data argues against "flat static bytes coincidentally increasing with distance across unrelated tree instances," but isn't proof).

**Numeric aside, unconfirmed, flagged for whoever picks this up:** 36 ≈ 255/7 (36.43). If a genuinely different underlying quantity here is an unsigned 3-bit "fog/light level" (0-7) later expanded to a byte via `level * (255/7)` — a common N64-era bit-depth-expansion idiom — the observed 0-36 range would mean this session's walk only ever reached **level 0 or 1 of a possible 0-7**, i.e. the mechanism computing the level may be stuck near its floor rather than the byte itself being wrong. Not chased down this pass (no `* 7`/`/ 7`/level-table hits found in a quick `bg*.c`/`bgfog.c` grep) — worth a targeted look at whatever function ultimately writes this specific room's tree-card `Vtx.cn[3]` if the next pass wants to keep pulling this thread, but flagged as a numerical coincidence, not a confirmed mechanism.

**Not v0.3.0-blocking, user is continuing anyway.** Next step, concrete: find the actual write site for this room-geometry class's baked/computed alpha (search the ROM room-decompression path more specifically for this level's data, or instrument `bgLoadRoomVtxData` itself to dump the raw pre-swap bytes for this room and compare against what the running probe reports post-load — if they match exactly, the value is confirmed ROM-faithful and the investigation should pivot to "is this actually correct N64 behavior, i.e. is the real bug elsewhere (wrong texture selected, wrong room's data loaded, etc.)" rather than continuing to chase the alpha value itself). `GE_D236ALPHA` log preserved at `scratch/d236_pass14_live_capture.log` (filename predates this being pass 15's data) for reference.

**Pass 16 (2026-09-18, same later session, user said "go for it" — a decisive negative result plus a still-open "where does this data actually come from" question): ruled out room-background static vertex data as the source of the low alpha, and ruled out the two most obvious dynamic-quad-builder candidates in `model.c`, but did not find the actual write site.**

**Built `GE_D236RAW`** (`src/game/bg.c`, `bgLoadRoomVtxData`, right after `bgSwapRoomVtx`, env-gated): dumps a histogram of every vertex's raw `cn[3]` alpha byte for each room's *entire* static vertex table the moment it's decompressed and swapped — independent of camera position or which triangles happen to be drawn, unlike `GE_D236ALPHA`. Ran headless 25s on `-level_36` (no live session needed for this step): **64 room-load events across ~40 distinct rooms, and every single one reported `amin=255 amax=255`** — literally every vertex in every room's raw table is fully opaque. **This conclusively rules out "static ROM-authored per-vertex alpha" as the source of the ≤36/255 values pass 15 measured at render time** — `bgSwapRoomVtx` was already confirmed not to touch colour bytes (pass 15), and now the pre-render data itself is confirmed uniformly opaque across the whole level. Whatever produces the low alpha happens **after** room load, and is not baked into this table at all.

**Extended `GE_D236ALPHA`** (`port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp`) to also report which segment the tree class's vertices were loaded from, by recording the top byte of the raw `G_VTX` command's segmented address (`g_d236_last_vtx_seg`, set in the `G_VTX` case of the main DL dispatch, read back in the existing per-triangle probe). Live capture in the same session as pass 15's walk was not repeated; a headless run instead confirmed the class reports **`vtxseg=0x70`** consistently. Per `seg_addr()`'s own documented convention (`gfx_pc.cpp:3260-3294`) and `port/src/dram.c`'s `DRAM_V1_BASE=0x70000000` comment ("ALL game RAM symbols live" in this view starting at that address), `0x70` is **not** one of the game's named symbolic segments (`SPSEGMENT_MODEL_VTX=4`, `SPSEGMENT_BG_VTX=14`, etc., `bondconstants.h:2897-2909`) — it means this particular `G_VTX` command references a **raw, unsegmented host pointer** into the general RAM arena, the same pattern used by every dynamically-built quad in `model.c` that calls `osVirtualToPhysical(freshly_allocated_buffer)` directly instead of going through `gSPSegment`. This is consistent with (though doesn't newly prove beyond) pass 15's "not static data" framing, and additionally rules out the two *specific* addressing schemes (segment 4, segment 14) a static per-model or per-room table would use.

**Went looking for the actual CPU-side quad-builder and came up empty.** `model.c` has exactly four functions that dynamically allocate and write `Vtx`/`Vertex` arrays via `vtxallocator()` for `ModelNode` rendering: `dogfnegx` (`MODELNODE_OPCODE_GUNFIRE` — PD name `modelRenderNodeChrGunfire`, muzzle flash), `doshadow` (`MODELNODE_OPCODE_SHADOW`, character/prop drop shadows), `dorottex` (`MODELNODE_OPCODE_DLPRIMARY`, "star" muzzle-flash flare arms per its own header comment), and `dotube` (`MODELNODE_OPCODE_OP07`, a two-vertex-per-iteration rotating-ring interpolator, gun-barrel/rope-like geometry). Read all four in full: none match "outdoor decorative camera-facing billboard sprite" by content, and the two that use segment-tagged addressing (`dorottex` explicitly calls `gSPSegment(..., SPSEGMENT_MODEL_VTX, ...)`) would report `vtxseg=0x04`, not `0x70`, ruling them out on the addressing evidence too. The rest of `model.c`'s `MODELNODE_OPCODE_OP*` dispatch table (`OP03/OP05/OP06/OP11/OP14/OP16/OP17/OP20`) resolves to literal `return;` stubs in this decomp — dead opcodes, not candidates. Checked `propobj.c` again for any other `vtxallocator`-style builder beyond the already-examined "screen" (in-game TV monitor image) quad system — found none.

**Pass 17 (2026-09-21, fresh session) — WRITER IDENTIFIED: `doshadow`. Plus a false alarm resolved.**

1. **Vertex struct is 16 bytes, not 32**: GE's RSP uses a custom vertex format `{s16 ob[3]; u16 flag; s16 tc[2]; cn[4]}` (alpha at byte 0xF) — no screen-space sx/sy/st/ct. `vtxallocator(n)` = `dynAllocate(n<<4)` = n×16B; the observed +0x40 arena increments are doshadow/dogfnegx's 4-vertex (64B) allocations, not 2×32B Vtx.
2. **Decisive probe**: env-gated backtrace at allocation time (`GE_D236BT`, `get_ptr_allocated_block_for_vertices` in `chr.c`, calling a new C-linkage `port_d236bt_dump()` extracted from the RSP-side unwind logic in `gfx_pc.cpp`). All allocator hits resolve to **`doshadow`** (`model.c:5397`) via `drawjointlist → chrRenderProp → chrpropRender → chrpropsRenderPass → lvlRender`. Zero dotube activity. First allocation's physical address exactly matches the RSP-side rawvtx capture. Pass 16's exclusion of doshadow was based on a wrong claim ("dotube/doshadow use segment-tagged addressing") — only `dorottex` tags G_VTX; both use raw pointers.
3. **doshadow alpha mechanism**: `cn[3] = (envcolour.a * D_800363F0)/255` for CHR/SMOKE props, else `= D_800363F0` — per-frame global shadow intensity, explains the varying low alphas (observed 1→2→12→13→14; probe saw 13 and 80 alternating). All 4 vertices are copies of a constant template (`D_800363F8`). Textured quad via `shadow->image` → `texSelect`.
4. **FALSE ALARM (pass 17c) — the d43_emit.py op-13 "ShadowRecord bug" does not exist.** A ROM scan of all 42 op-13 records (all in C*Z character files, none in P*Z props) initially suggested the converter writes HeaderNode to r+24 / Scale to r+32 / omits BaseAddr — misaligned vs the C struct's *commented* offsets (image@0x10, HeaderNode@0x14, Scale@0x18, BaseAddr@0x1C). But a runtime dump of the live record (`GE_D236BT` probe in `doshadow`) shows **HeaderNode@0x14 = 0 and the valid pointer at 0x18** — because on PC (64-bit) `image` widens to 8 bytes, shifting HeaderNode→0x18, Scale→0x20, BaseAddr→0x28. The converter's r+16/r+24/r+32 layout **matches the PC struct exactly**; the C comments describe the N64 32-bit layout (the D52/A1 pointer-widening class). Live values all sane: image→valid tconfig (32×32, fmt=0), HeaderNode valid, height≈110, size≈(389,413), BaseAddr set by the loader's promotion pass (`modelPromoteNodeOffsetsToPointers` SHADOW case overwrites it with fileramaddr anyway). **Do not "fix" d43_emit.py op-13.**
5. **Conclusion so far**: the faint textured sheets ARE `doshadow`'s drop-shadow quads — large (≈390×413 world units) flat ground quads sampling a tiny 32×32 texture at low per-frame alpha. N64 draws the identical quads (same code, same data). **The user-visible bug is therefore almost certainly that the trees' actual sprite geometry is missing/broken on PC**, leaving only the shadow sheets visible — not a shadow bug.

**Pass 18 (2026-09-21, static ROM analysis session) — the tree-class RM word is a runtime LUT rewrite; exact source pair identified.**

1. **All tree/plant prop files carry zero renderable geometry — confirmed with the real node parser, not just an opcode histogram.** `PpalmtreeZ`, `PpalmZ`, `Pjungle3_treeZ`, `Pjungle5_treeZ`, `Pplant1`–`Pplant11Z`, `Pgas_plant_*Z`: node set is only {Group(2), BBox(10), DLCollision(24)} — **no op-4 DisplayListRecord anywhere**. Same on N64. The visible tree sprites are therefore drawn by the room background (`bg_sevx_all_p.seg`, ROM 0x66F700, 116176 B; Surface1=level_36, Surface2=level_43), not by prop models.
2. **The measured tree-class RM word `0x0c184b50` exists in no ROM data.** Scanned all 25 non-empty bg files (decompressed RZ GDLs) and all 512 model GDLs: zero hits. The only `0x0c18xxxx` word in ROM is `0x0c182048` (menu logo bg). It is generated at runtime.
3. **Exact source found — `DL_LUT_CLOUD`.** Compiled GE's LUT pairs (`scratch/d236/lutdump.c`, output in `scratch/d236/lutvals.txt`): CLOUD = from `G_RM_PASS|G_RM_AA_ZB_XLU_SURF2` = **`0x0c1849d8`** → to `G_RM_PASS|G_RM_ZB_CLD_SURF2` = **`0x0c184b50`** — exact match with the measured tree-class word. The "from" word is one of the six bg RM words present in ROM (×24 in sevx). `G_RM_PASS = 0x0c080000` explains the high bits: `0x0c08 | 0x0010 (ZB_CLD_SURF2 hi) = 0x0c18`. So: room GDLs contain `SETOTHERMODE_L 0x0c1849d8`, and a runtime `bgApplyDynamicCCRMLUT` pass rewrites them to `0x0c184b50` before the RSP sees them. Note `DL_LUT_BILLBOARD` shares the same "from" word (`0x0c1849d8`) but maps to `0x0c193078` (TEX_EDGE2) — which LUT wins depends on the applied index.
4. **Pass 17's doshadow finding stands but is a different sheet.** doshadow emits `G_RM_ZB_CLD_SURF|G_RM_ZB_CLD_SURF2 = 0x00504b50` (no PASS bits) — a *different* word from the measured tree class. The faint character drop-shadow quads (doshadow, 32×32 shadow texture) and the tree-texture billboards (bg CLOUD-rewritten quads) are two separate draw sources; the user-visible "wall of tree texture" is the latter.
5. **N64 cutout mechanism (hypothesis to verify):** `0x0c184b50` = ZMODE_XLU + FORCE_BL + CVG_WRAP/FULL + IM_RD, alphacompare bits 0–2 = 000 (NONE), no CVG_X_ALPHA. No alpha *test* — the silhouette must come from plain alpha **blending** of the IA texture (`out = src*A + dst*(1-A)`; transparent texels have A=0). The port's `use_alpha` gate in `gfx_pc.cpp` (~line 2386: requires `(oml & (3<<20)) == G_BL_CLR_MEM<<20 && (oml & (3<<16)) == G_BL_1MA<<16`) must be checked against this word's blender bits (bits 16–17 = 00, bits 20–21 = 01) — if the gate rejects it, fast3d draws the quad opaque → exactly the reported "wall/sheet" symptom.

Pass 17's backtrace attributed the tree class's vertex allocations to `doshadow`, but `dogfnegx` is a co-emitter through the identical `drawjointlist → chrRenderProp` path and the same `vtxallocator(4)` + raw-pointer pattern — the attribution may have resolved only the more frequent of the two.
3. **`dogfnegx` IS the discrete camera-facing sprite mechanism** (`model.c:5225-5380`): it computes the view direction from `rodata->Offset` through the node's model matrix, builds a rotation aligning the quad to face the camera, applies per-frame random scale (0.75–1.25) and random UV rotation around the texture centre, and draws a `rodata->Size`-sized textured quad with mode-4 cloud RM. Gated on `(renderdata->flags & 2) && rwdata->Gunfire.visible`. `ModelRoData_GunfireRecord` (`bondtypes.h:1151`): Offset@0x0, Size@0xC, Image@0x18, Scale@0x1C, RwDataIndex@0x20. This is almost certainly what N64 shows as the "discrete tree sprites".
4. **The port's `use_alpha` gate ACCEPTS `0x0c184b50` — pass 18's prime suspect is refuted by static decode.** Against this repo's gbi.h blender layout (`include/PR/gbi.h:720-723`: `GBL_c2` puts c2-modifier at bits 16-17, c2-secondary-colour at bits 20-21 of other_mode_l): the gate (`gfx_pc.cpp` ~line 2386) requires bits 16-17 == `G_BL_1MA`(0) and bits 20-21 == `G_BL_CLR_MEM`(1); the word has byte2=`0x18` → bits 16-17=0 ✓, bits 20-21=1 ✓ → `use_alpha=true`. Full decode: ALPHACOMPARE=NONE, no CVG_X_ALPHA/ALPHA_CVG_SEL, FORCE_BL set, c1=(IN, A=0), c2=(IN, A_IN over MEM, 1MA) = standard src-over alpha blend with A from the combiner (`texSelect` mode-4 2-cycle sets `G_CC_TRILERP`/`G_CC_MODULATEIA2` for IA → A = texel.a × shade.a). No port-side opaque-draw gate explains the wall.
5. **Implication / reframed picture:** with the tree class alpha-blended correctly in the port, the consistent story across D276 (visible weave painted by the `0xc81049d8` room-bg noise class), D280 (tree cards in front yet not visibly winning) and pass 15 (tree-class vertex alpha capped ≤36/255 ≈ 14%, bimodal 25/255) is that the tree cards blend at ~10% opacity over the opaque noise wall — nearly invisible, exactly "the wall shows through".
