The model transform is decoupled from the script in all three axes (by tick 5910 `prop.z`=−1797 while the cycle's z-range is −3111…−2221); it is not terrain-following (the same four values repeat exactly for ~800 ticks while x/z drift). **(3) The camera shake closes mechanically.** `field_3C4/8/C` (= 0.1 × leaky integral of `field_488.pos`) starts at ≈ −22832 — the *exact* `pos2.y` start M-143 observed live — sweeps to +229 over ~180 ticks as the filter converges onto the frozen surface point, then tracks the period-4 cycle. The "violent shake/spazz" = a fixed-eye camera whose look-at anchor (i) starts ~20k units displaced and (ii) teleports between four points at 15 Hz. D146 remains fully decoupled (zero hits, fourth consecutive run). **(4) "Two Bonds" — not present as two instances in this capture.** If the user still saw a double image on this run, the leading candidate is stale `render_pos` submissions lingering in the draw queue while the model teleports between the four cycle points (D75 family): P4 sits ~1,400 units below the dam surface ("floating in the air"), P1/P2 are on it ("standing on the dam"), and each copy would be a frozen snapshot → "neither animates correctly." Not verifiable from this log (the draw probe counts submissions — one per frame — not on-screen images). **Open question for the user: did two Bonds appear in *this* run?** **(5) Cross-ref:** D173 (level-start floating, Cradle spin) and D292 (death sinking) are the same "third-person world model transform" family — the period-4 fixed-point cycle is now a concrete shared-mechanism candidate for all three. **Next:** code dive into where the model's render transform gets its translation during POSENT (`chrTick` → `render_pos`, chraction.c/objecthandler): what state produces the four fixed points (a 4-keyframe anim attached to Bond's model on PC only? a pad table?), and why the smooth `prop` sweep never reaches the model transform after spawn. If the double image is a stale-queue artifact, that is a port/render-layer fix (fast3d draw list) — no game-logic change needed.

**M-154 (2026-09-16): user symptom sharpened to "one new frozen Bond per camera shot"; the M-153 log reading is corrected (the rendered model is NOT frozen in phase 3 — `prop->pos` itself cycles); a per-frame model-draw census probe (`D243M: chrdraw`) is implemented and smoke-tested to discriminate the two remaining hypotheses.** **(1) User observation (reproducible every time so far):** during the abseil, one *new frozen* Bond appears with each camera shot — shot 1 standing, shot 2 mid-jump, shot 3 rappelling; the old copies persist and never animate; the camera glitches when the second Bond appears. **(2) Corrected log reading (supersedes M-153's "period-4 cycle through four fixed points").** The POSENT window (frames 4819–5910) has three phases: **P1** (4820–4880): `prop.y` rises −19791→+175 while `f488` stays frozen at (−4.4, 729.7, −3111.6) — the rendered model is decoupled from prop during the ascent; **P2** (4881–5041): both frozen (prop (−4.3, 175.9, −3107.6), f488 (−4.4, 229.1, −3106.7)); **P3** (5042→end): **`prop->pos` itself cycles period-4 through three z-lanes** — A(≈−31xx), A, B(≈−25xx), C(≈−22xx) — while y falls smoothly at ~30 units/frame. `f488` tracks the *same* cycle exactly with per-lane y offsets (A: +229, B: +79, C: −1215 = per-pad model pose), so in P3 the rendered model is **not frozen** — it teleports between three fixed world points every frame, following prop. M-153's "four fixed points" was lane A (two near-identical samples) + B + C. Structural tell: y stays perfectly continuous across lane boundaries while x/z rotate → either one prop whose x/z come from a cycling source (AI-script GOTO loop setting position to different pads one command per frame — cf. the teleport fall-through at chrai.c:4064 where a failed `chrAdjustPosForSpawn` drops into the next command; or keyframe sampling without interpolation), or `pp->prop` rotating among three PropRecords with synchronized y. **(3) Hypotheses for the visible double/triple image:** **H1** multiple Model instances — each shot spawns a frozen Bond, all drawn every frame (the M-145 family, but spawned via a path invisible to the playerTick probe); **H2** single model + framebuffer accumulation — `subcam=1` snapshot buffer never cleared, so the per-frame teleporting model leaves a trail of frozen ghosts at all three lanes; "old copies persist and never animate" fits H2 naturally (ghosts are frozen by construction). M-153's stale-draw-queue candidate is subsumed by H2. **(4) Probe (implemented, smoke-tested).** `D243M: tick` extended with `propptr=`/`chrptr=` (a changing pointer proves prop rotation; constant → cycling x/z source), `rp=` (the render_pos pointer — a change between phases = matrix-buffer reassignment/aliasing), `raw=` (render_pos[0] translation BEFORE the view transform — distinguishes model-matrix cycling from view-matrix cycling). New `D243M: chrdraw` census in `drawjointlist` (both region variants, objecthandler.c): one line per CHR render submission while a scripted camera mode is active (POSEND/INTRO/SWIRL/FADESWIRL), logging Model* + raw root translation. All CHR draws funnel through it (`chrRenderProp`; player path bondview2.c:10883, generic chrprop.c:443). H1 = extra lines with *distinct* model pointers at the same frame; note the same model is drawn twice per frame (two passes) — dedupe by (frame, model). Accessors `d243mProbeActive()`/`d243mGetFrameCounter()` live in bondview2.c (the camera gate is folded into `active()` so objecthandler.c needs no bondview.h include); D250 cached-getenv kept. Smoke: 45 s bare `-level_33` boot → 4,053 chrdraw + 1,066 tick lines, formats verified, silent in FPS play (cam=FP/NONE gate). **(5) Next:** user re-runs Dam→abseil with `GE_D243M=1` (`cmd /c` capture — see HANDOFF); analysis: (a) distinct-Model* count per frame during POSENT → H1 vs H2; (b) propptr/chrptr stability → prop rotation vs cycling source; (c) raw vs f488pos → model-matrix vs view-matrix origin of the cycle. **M-154 fix (same day): the first live abseil run CRASHED inside the new tick probe itself** — access violation, fault addr `0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF`, PC in `playerTick` (bondview2.c:10419), on the very first tick after `D243M: CREATE frame=4109 … cam=7 subcam=1`. Cause: `bodyModel->render_pos` is assigned by `instcalcmatrices()` **during the draw pass** (`model.c:2453`: `arg1->render_pos = arg0->mtxlist`), i.e. *after* the probe point — on the first tick post-CREATE it still holds the reused `AnimModelSlot`'s stale value, observed as the 0xFF tombstone `(RenderPosView*)-1`. The game only ever dereferences `render_pos` post-`chrTick`, so it is legitimately unset at the probe; the M-153-era tick fields never touched it, which is why the earlier capture survived. Fix: guard the `raw=` read against NULL **and** the `-1` tombstone; `rp=%p` is still logged unconditionally, so the exact frame where `render_pos` transitions -1 → real pointer is now captured (itself a D243 data point: the body model's matrix buffer is unset between CREATE and the first draw pass). Probe-only change; no game-code impact.

**M-154 fix 2 (second abseil run, same day): the sentinel guard was not enough — the probe crashed again at the identical PC/fault address.** Second capture (244 KB, longer run than run 1) died at `D243M: CREATE … cam=7 subcam=1` with AV fault addr `0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF`, PC `playerTick+0x64c` = bondview2.c:10427 — the same `raw=` read, now *past* the NULL/-1 guard (disassembly confirms the guard compiled correctly: `lea -1(%r10),%rdx; cmp $-3,%rdx; jbe <read block>` passes everything except exactly NULL and -1). Conclusion: between CREATE and the first draw pass, `render_pos` holds **arbitrary stale slot contents**, not a uniform tombstone — run 1 drew -1, run 2 drew some other bad value (the exact fault addr of -1 with the `0x30(%r10)` displacement implies r10 ≈ -48 at fault time; the crash-handler register dump is not fully trustworthy, but the PC/line are). **Sentinel-whack-a-mole is the wrong shape for a probe.** Final fix: the tick probe **never dereferences `render_pos` at all** — `raw=` is dropped from the tick line entirely; `rp=%p` stays (logging a pointer value costs no deref, and the -1 → real transition frame is still captured). No data is lost: the pre-view root translation is already logged by the `D243M: chrdraw` census in `drawjointlist`, where validity is guaranteed because the game's own `gSPSegment(render_pos)` runs moments later — and draw-time is the *more accurate* sample anyway (a tick-time read would return the previous frame's matrix buffer). The chrdraw probe also gained the same -1 rejection as belt-and-braces. Smoke: 30 s bare boot, 4,051 chrdraw lines, no crash. Re-capture pending.

**M-159 (2026-09-17): static code-dive names a concrete, evidence-consistent mechanism for the period-4/lane cycling itself — the model's render transform only refreshes on ticks that pass the game's own on-screen visibility test, and during the void sweep most ticks fail it.** Traced `chrTick` (`src/game/chr.c:2442`) end to end for the path that actually recomputes `bodyModel->render_pos`: at `chr.c:2580/2593/2615`, `headSwitchVisible = posIsOnScreen(prop, &prop->pos, getinstsize(model), 1)` gates a large block (`chr.c:2633-2681`) that only runs `subcalcmatrices()` (→ `instcalcmatrices()`, `model.c:2453`, the sole site that assigns `render_pos`) **when `headSwitchVisible` is true**; when false, `render_pos` — and therefore `field_488.pos`, which `playerTick` (`bondview2.c:10493-10497`) reads back from `render_pos` every tick `prop->flags & PROPFLAG_ONSCREEN` is set — is simply not touched that tick, so the model's rendered position freezes wherever it last was. `posIsOnScreen` (`propobj.c:13584`) itself reduces to a same-room check (`getROOMID_isRendered`) plus `camIsPosInScreen`/`camIsPosInScreenBox` (`bondview.c:1090`/`1131`) — a straight point-vs-frustum-plane test against `g_CamFrustum{Near,Left,Right,Top,Bottom}{Normal,Offset}`, which are recomputed once per frame in `bondviewUpdateFrustumPlanes()` (`bondview.c:949`, called from the camera-matrix-build function at `bondview2.c:8401`) purely from `g_CurrentPlayer->viewtoworldmtxf` and the player's FOV-derived half-width/half-height. **This mechanically fits every M-153/M-154 observation:** `prop->pos` genuinely sweeps a huge range through the void during the abseil (y −23859→+175, M-153); most of that sweep is far outside the fixed cutscene camera's frustum (the void is below/behind the dam, off-screen from this shot), so `posIsOnScreen(prop->pos, ...)` is false on nearly every tick, and `render_pos`/`field_488.pos` only update on the rare ticks where the live position happens to cross back inside frustum — producing exactly the "frozen, then teleports to a new fixed point, then frozen again" pattern M-154 documented (P1/P2 static, P3 a small cycling set of points) without needing a second model instance, a stale draw-queue entry, or a cycling prop/pointer at all. **This is decomp-exact game code — `posIsOnScreen`/`camIsPosInScreen`/`bondviewUpdateFrustumPlanes` are ordinary, unmodified `src/game` functions with no ABI/pointer-width surface (no ROM-serialized struct, no union aliasing) — so per M-144 (real N64 does NOT show this shake), the divergence must be in an INPUT to this test differing between platforms, not the test itself.** Two live candidates, neither confirmed yet: **(a)** `g_CurrentPlayer->viewtoworldmtxf` — and hence the whole frustum — is itself built from the filtered look-at chain (`bondviewFrozenCameraTick`'s `gBondViewCutscene` branch → `field_3C4/8/C`, the same leaky-integrator filter M-143 named) that in turn is fed by `field_488.pos`, which this very gate controls — a **feedback loop**: if call/update ordering between `bondviewUpdateFrustumPlanes()`/the camera-matrix build and `chrTick`'s visibility test differs by even one frame or one tick-count between PC and N64 (a scheduler/`port/src/gesched.c` timing question, not game logic — bucket (b) if confirmed), the frustum a given tick tests against would differ, changing which ticks pass `posIsOnScreen` and thus which fixed points get sampled; **(b)** `getinstsize(model)`/`c_halfheight`/`c_halfwidth`-derived frustum margins, or the FOV/aspect the port's `viewtoworldmtxf` construction uses, could differ from N64's in a way that shrinks the effective on-screen box during this specific low/behind-camera shot. **Not yet distinguished; no `src/game` or `port/` code changed this pass — still diagnosis only per rule #2.** **Next, concrete:** an `#ifdef PORT` probe on `posIsOnScreen`'s return value + `prop->pos` + the current frustum offsets, logged every `chrTick` call during POSEND for the abseil window, would directly show whether the pass/fail pattern lines up with the observed freeze/teleport boundaries (confirms the gate is the mechanism) and whether `viewtoworldmtxf`/frustum values are stale relative to `field_488.pos`'s own last-updated tick (tests candidate (a)). If confirmed, the fix is either a `port/`-layer scheduling/ordering correction (no `src/game` touch) or, if N64's own `posIsOnScreen` genuinely also fails most of these ticks but the *filter* happens to converge invisibly fast enough there not to be noticed (i.e. this really is decomp-faithful and only more visible on PC due to unrelated frame-pacing), a case for treating D243 as closed-not-a-bug and folding it into D148's general umbrella instead — that determination needs the probe capture, not more static reading.

**M-159 probe (`D243M: onscreen`, `chr.c`) landed and build/smoke-verified:** compiles clean, links, and a 1200+-frame bare `-level_33` boot with `GE_D243M=1` produced 41,165 `D243M: onscreen` lines (plus the existing 1,067 `D243M: tick` lines) with zero crashes/exceptions — confirms the probe fires correctly for every ticked chr (not just Bond; sample shows multiple `chr=` pointers per frame, `vis=` flipping 0/1 per chr's position), format `D243M: onscreen frame=%d chr=%p vis=%d pos=%.1f,%.1f,%.1f`.

**M-160 (2026-09-17, same day): the user played a live Dam→abseil capture (`ge007_d243_onscreen_capture.log`, 3.7 MB, 44,728 probe lines) with the new `D243M: onscreen` probe — M-159's frustum-culling hypothesis is REFUTED by the data, and a stronger, more specific mechanism is now directly evidenced: `chrTick` overwrites `prop->pos` with a stale/stepped value every tick regardless of on-screen visibility.** Player-body CREATE for the abseil: `frame=9352 ... cam=7 subcam=1`, `chrptr=00000000701dbebc`. Cross-referencing `D243M: tick` (bondview2.c's `playerTick`, fires BEFORE `chrTick` runs each frame) against the new `D243M: onscreen` (fires INSIDE `chrTick`, at `after_position_update:`, i.e. AFTER `chrTick`'s own position-update logic runs) for the **identical frame numbers**: `tick`'s `prop=` sweeps smoothly (frame 9353 y=-23859.7 → frame 9369 y=-1130.0, matching the AI script's scripted void descent, consistent with M-153/M-154), while `onscreen`'s `pos=` for the same frames is **frozen at exactly (-4.3, 676.5, -3111.6)** for all of frames 9353-9413, then steps to a new frozen value (-4.3, 176.2, -3111.6) at frame 9414 — **and `vis=1` (on-screen/frustum test PASSES) on every single one of these frames, no exceptions.** This directly refutes M-159: the model's render transform is not failing to update because it's off-camera — `posIsOnScreen` is true throughout, `subcalcmatrices`/`instcalcmatrices` run every tick (confirmed by the varying `rp=` render_pos pointer values in the `tick` lines across these frames — different buffer each tick, i.e. actively reallocating/redrawing, not stalled). **The freeze is `prop->pos` itself being overwritten inside `chrTick`, downstream of the AI script's write, before the model transform is computed from it.** `chr.c`'s `after_position_update:` label is reached via one of three branches gated on `chr->actiontype` (`ACT_ANIM`/`ACT_STAND`/else, `chr.c:2578-2616`), each of which calls `chrUpdateAnim`/`modelTickAnim` — ordinary per-chr animation/locomotion logic that has no POSEND/cutscene-mode check anywhere in this function. The player's chr (`chrptr=701dbebc`) is the same chr the CHR_BOND_CINEMA teleports move (M-145) but is otherwise still being ticked as a normal, un-scripted character every frame — its own `chrUpdateAnim`/`modelTickAnim` position write is competing with, and winning against, the AI script's `prop->pos` write for what ends up rendered. `field_488.pos`'s value in the same `tick` lines (frozen at (-4.4, 727.8, -3111.6), ≈7 units off the `onscreen` reading — matches the `mtx[4]*7.0f` view-transform offset in `bondview2.c:10495-10497`) confirms this same frozen post-chrTick value is exactly what later gets read back into the render position, closing the loop from M-153's original observation to this mechanism.

**Not yet determined: which of the three `chrTick` branches is taken (needs `chr->actiontype` logged — not in the current probe), and whether N64 hardware exhibits the same overwrite** (if GE's own scripted-cutscene state is supposed to freeze/skip a chr's normal animation-position tick via some flag this port isn't honoring, that's a port-layer or narrow ABI-class fix; if N64 genuinely runs the same competing writers and the visual result there is different for an unrelated platform reason — e.g. the two writes interleave differently under N64's single-threaded deterministic tick vs. this port's own tick/render cadence — that needs establishing before any fix). **Next, concrete:** extend the `D243M: onscreen` probe (or add a sibling) to log `chr->actiontype` and whether the branch actually called `chrUpdateAnim` vs `modelTickAnim` vs neither, for the same window — this directly names which branch is responsible and whether it's gated by anything checkable (e.g. `CHRFLAG_HIDDEN`, `docentreupdown`, or a `g_CameraMode`/POSEND check elsewhere in the call chain that should also cover this path but doesn't). Cross-ref M-145's false-GUARD/CHR_BOND_CINEMA architecture — this is now the concrete mechanism that architecture predicted but didn't pin down.

**User confirms (live playtest, this session): the visible cutscene glitch is unchanged** — this probe pass is diagnosis-only (no behavior change, `#ifdef PORT`/env-gated), so an unchanged symptom is expected and does not weigh against the finding above.

**M-161 (2026-09-17, same session): decisive experiment — NEGATIVE result. M-160's mechanism, while real, is NOT the (or not the whole) visible cause.** To test M-160 without more diagnosis, added a throwaway `#ifdef PORT` hack in `playerTick` (`bondview2.c:10474`, env-gated `GE_D243X`, off by default): save `prop->pos` immediately before the `chrTick(prop)` call, restore it immediately after, **only** while `g_CameraMode == CAMERAMODE_POSEND` — directly neutralizing the competing write M-160 identified. Compiled clean, linked, 1380-frame bare-boot smoke test with zero crashes, then a full live Dam→abseil playthrough with `GE_D243X=1`. **User's report: "still happened, looked the same as it always does."** No perceptible change to the glitch. Since M-160's own capture already established `g_CameraMode == CAMERAMODE_POSEND` holds throughout the freeze window (same session, `D243M: tick`'s `cam=7` field), there's good reason to trust the experiment's condition was actually satisfied and not silently inert — though this run did not have `GE_D243M=1` set alongside `GE_D243X=1` to directly confirm the branch fired on this specific playthrough (a residual gap, noted for completeness, not chased further given the clear negative result). **Conclusion:** `chrTick`'s competing overwrite of `prop->pos` (M-160) is a real, independently-evidenced bug — worth keeping in `porting-notes.md` §D11 as a documented pattern — but restoring the AI script's position after the overwrite does not fix what the player actually sees, so either (a) the visible glitch's dominant cause is elsewhere in the render/filter chain (M-143's `field_3C4/8/C` leaky-integrator, or something not yet identified), or (b) M-160's mechanism matters but only as one contributor among several, and neutralizing it alone isn't sufficient. Experiment reverted in full (`git diff` clean on `bondview2.c` bar one pre-existing whitespace byte); no lasting code change from this pass.

**Status assessment after M-161:** this bug has now had ~15 session-passes (M-107 through M-161) across multiple sessions without a landed fix, each pass narrowing the mechanism further without closing it. Per the user's own call this session (diminishing returns, "going at this without much luck for a while"), **recommend parking D243 under the D148 umbrella** (general cutscene-bug tracking entry, `docs/dev/GRAPHICS-BACKLOG.md`) rather than continuing further open-ended diagnostic passes, unless a specific new lead or live capture surfaces. The mechanism knowledge gained (M-143's filter, M-145's teleport architecture, M-160's competing-writer bug) remains valid and should inform any *future* pass — this is a park, not a reset — but the next session should default to other backlog items unless the user explicitly wants another D243 cycle.

**UNPARKED same session: a third-party review found a real methodological flaw in M-161, and the corrected re-test (M-162) produced a genuinely new, decisive result — see below.**

**M-162 (2026-09-17, same session, after a second third-party review): M-161's negative result was invalid — the restore was placed AFTER `chrTick()` returned, but `render_pos`/`field_488.pos` are computed INSIDE that same call, from whatever `prop->pos` was at that point. So M-161 never actually prevented the stale value from reaching the render.** Verified directly (not just accepted from the review): compared `D243M: tick`'s pre-`chrTick` z-read against `D243M: onscreen`'s post-`chrTick` z-read for the **identical frame number** across the cycling window (`m160_dam_abseil_onscreen_capture.log`, frames 9600-9611) — the pattern is a clean, deterministic period-4 offset applied *within* the same tick: `-4.0, +543.8, +305.5, -855.2`, repeating exactly. This proves the lane-advance happens **inside** `chrTick`, every tick, unconditionally — the strongest evidence yet for M-160's mechanism.

Corrected the experiment: added `d243x2SavedPos`/`d243x2Active` (top-of-function locals, `chr.c:2451-2453`) — save `prop->pos.f[2]` (Z only, since M-160's capture showed X stable and Y the smooth AI-script descent) right before the `chrTick` position-update dispatch (`chr.c:2541-2617`, inside the `CHRFLAG_HIDDEN`-else block), restore it at `after_position_update:` — **before** the `D243M: onscreen` log line and before anything else in the tick can see the cycled value, unlike M-161. Also extended the probe with `actiontype=`/`anim=` (which of `chrTick`'s branches fired, model's current animation pointer) and `x2active=`/`x2rawz=` (whether suppression ran, and the raw cycled Z it overrode) so the result could be read from the log, not just judged by eye — per the reviewer's explicit "bake this in or risk another inconclusive negative" advice. Gated `GE_D243X2`, `#ifdef PORT`. Compiled clean, linked, 37,823-line bare-boot smoke test with zero crashes.

**Live playtest result: MIXED — confirms the mechanism, but reveals the fix (as scoped) was incomplete.** User played two full Dam runs with `GE_D243M=1 GE_D243X2=1`; visible glitch looked "about the same" both times. But the log (`scratch/d243/m162_dam_abseil_playtest.log`, second abseil CREATE at frame 11878) shows the suppression **worked exactly as designed this time**: `x2rawz` still shows the same violent period-4 Z-lane cycling (e.g. frames 12100-12130: raw z jumping between ≈-3111, ≈-2500-2570, ≈-1930-2260), but the final rendered `pos.z` is now smooth and monotonic (-2227.6 → -3111.6 → -3107.6 → ... declining ~4 units/frame, no lane jumps at all) — the Z suppression genuinely neutralized the Z-axis cycling this time, unlike M-161.

**But `pos.y` is violently cycling instead, completely untouched** (same window: `176.2 → -1174.6 → 175.6 → 176.2` repeating, amplitude ~1350 units, with an early transition spike to -12823.6) — this run's chr logged `actiontype=3` (not logged in the original M-160 capture, so no direct comparison, but evidently a different branch/state than whatever produced M-160's "Y descends smoothly, Z cycles" pattern). **This fully explains the unchanged visible glitch**: the Z-only suppression fixed exactly the axis that wasn't dominant in this particular playthrough. The underlying mechanism (chrTick overwriting `prop->pos` with a cycling value every tick, independent of any external input) is now confirmed on a second axis too — not refuted, just incompletely tested.

**Next (M-163, in progress): extend the suppression to the whole `prop->pos` vector** (not just Z) to test whether stopping cycling on every axis finally kills the visible shake. This will also freeze whatever legitimate motion exists (accepted for a decisive test, not viable as a real fix — see the M-162 code comment). If positive: the mechanism is airtight-confirmed, and the real work becomes root-causing *why* this decomp-faithful write path emits cycling values on PC (candidates per M-154/M-160: an attached keyframe animation without interpolation, a pad-table lookup, an actiontype/POSEND gate the port isn't honoring — `chr->actiontype`/`model->anim` are now logged and should narrow this). **Both third-party reviews net assessment:** the first (local Qwen `triage` agent) made one fabricated/confused claim (conflating `g_CameraMode` with a same-numbered `subcam` flag) that I verified and refuted directly against capture data before acting on it — see the now-superseded framing above. The second (unspecified third-party agent) made a data-grounded, directly-verified, and ultimately correct critique of M-161's methodology that materially advanced the investigation. Both were checked against real captures before being trusted, per this project's own standing discipline (`docs/porting-notes.md` §E: verify a cited scratch/log actually contains what a claim says before trusting it) — worth noting as a working example of that discipline paying off in both directions (catching a wrong claim, and correctly accepting a right one).

**M-164 (2026-09-17, same session, static-only — no build, while the exe was locked by the user's own playtest): a complete mechanical theory tying M-145/M-154/M-160/M-162 together, naming a specific fix candidate.** M-162's capture logged `actiontype=3` for the visible Bond chr during the cycling — per `bondconstants.h:3945-3962`'s `ACT_TYPE` enum (`ACT_INIT`=0, `ACT_STAND`=1, `ACT_KNEEL`=2, `ACT_ANIM`=3), this is **`ACT_ANIM`**, one of the three branches M-160 traced the overwrite to (`chr.c:2578`: `else if ((chr->actiontype == ACT_ANIM) && ...)`, calling `chrUpdateAnim`). Traced `chrUpdateAnim` itself (`chr.c:2398-2424`): it is not an arbitrary overwrite — it calls `modelTickAnim` (advance the currently-attached animation), `subcalcpos` (recompute joint world transforms from that animation), then `getsuboffset(model, &prop->pos)` (`model.c:684`, `getpartoffset(objinst, objinst->obj->RootNode, offset)`) — i.e. it **faithfully reads the model's root-joint world position back into `prop->pos`**, which is exactly what this function is supposed to do for a normally-animating character. The "overwrite" is `chrUpdateAnim` doing its ordinary job on a chr whose animation state was never told about the cutscene.

Cross-referencing M-145's already-established architecture: `AI_TRYTeleportingChrToPad` (`chrai.c:4064-4119`, the `CHR_BOND_CINEMA` mechanism) writes `chr->prop->pos` **and** calls `setsubroty`/`setsuboffset(chr->model, &pos)` (`chrai.c:4105-4106`) — so the model's root-joint anchor genuinely is re-anchored to the new pad position at each teleport, confirmed by direct code read. **But nothing in that teleport touches `chr->act_anim`/`model->anim`.** M-145 already established that the actual rappel/exit `guard_play_animation` commands run on a separate, invisible "false GUARD" driver chr (`alloc_false_GUARDdata_to_exec_global_action`), not this visible one. **Putting these together: the visible Bond chr keeps ticking whatever animation it already had equipped from before the cutscene hijacked its position** (a locomotion/idle loop, going by `ACT_ANIM` + a real `model->anim` pointer being logged) — every tick, `chrUpdateAnim` advances that stale animation and reads its own root-motion cycle back into `prop->pos`, anchored at wherever the last teleport left the root joint. A short-period root-motion track (a walk-in-place or idle-sway loop) read back on top of a fixed anchor produces exactly the observed "period-4 cycling in place" — mechanically explaining M-153/M-154's lane pattern and M-162's Y-axis finding as two faces of the same thing (whichever axis that specific animation's root motion moves on).

**This reframes M-162/M-163's suppression experiments correctly: they are not "randomly neutralizing a bug," they are directly testing this exact theory** (block the stale-animation readback from reaching the render, see if the shake stops) — a positive M-163 result would be strong additional confirmation, not merely "the write stops," of this complete mechanism. **The real fix candidate this points to (not yet attempted, needs its own investigation pass):** find where/whether the cutscene AI script is supposed to change `chr->actiontype`/`chr->act_anim` (or otherwise silence `chrUpdateAnim`'s position write) for the *visible* chr when `AI_TRYTeleportingChrToPad` fires — the decomp symbol for `guard_play_animation` referenced in M-145 was not located this pass (grepped, no match for that exact name — likely a different actual symbol in `bondaicommands.c`/`aicommands2.c`; the AI command name is probably decoded/human-friendly, not literal). If N64 has a code path that either (a) redirects that animation command to the *visible* chr instead of the false-GUARD driver, or (b) sets `noTranslate`/freezes root motion on the visible chr during POSEND, and PC is silently skipping it — that is the actual bug, likely bucket (a)/(b) per the diagnosis framework, not a game-logic difference. **Next:** locate the real `guard_play_animation`/animation-assignment AI command handler and trace whether it's meant to target the chr that `AI_TRYTeleportingChrToPad` just moved.

**M-165 (2026-09-17, same session, static-only, continuing while the exe was locked): found the animation-command handler M-164 flagged as unlocated — it confirms the "wrong chr" targeting is a structural, likely decomp-faithful property of this AI-script design, which reframes where the real PC/N64 divergence must be.** `check_if_able_to_then_perform_animation` (`chraction.c:10263`, called from both `chrai.c:1084` and `aicommands.def:750`) is passed `ChrEntityp` — the AI list's own driver chr — as its `self`/target, not a resolved `CHR_NUM` lookup. Per M-145, the abseil's AI list runs on the invisible false-GUARD driver (`alloc_false_GUARDdata_to_exec_global_action`), so this command (and by extension `guard_play_animation`) **structurally can never reach the visible Bond chr `AI_TRYTeleportingChrToPad` teleports** — this is how the script is written, and since both are byte-identical decomp code, this mismatch is almost certainly present on N64 too, not a PC-only defect. Also checked whether any game-code path gates the visible chr's own `chrTick` animation dispatch during a scripted camera mode: grepped `chr.c` for `CAMERAMODE_POSEND`/`CAMERAMODE_INTRO` (zero hits — `chr.c` has no camera-mode awareness at all) and checked `PLAYERFLAG_NOCONTROL` (set by `AI_BondDisableControl`, `chrai.c:4040`) — it only drives HUD/UI display (`bondviewSetUpperTextDisplayFlag`, `hudmsgsSetOn`, `countdownTimerSetVisible`), never referenced in `chr.c`/`chraction.c`'s position-update path. **There is no game-code mechanism anywhere that suppresses the visible chr's ordinary locomotion-animation tick during a cutscene** — `chrTick` runs its normal dispatch on the player's chr throughout POSEND regardless.

**This reframes the open question, honestly: if the "wrong-chr animation targeting" and "no cutscene suppression" are both decomp-faithful (high confidence, direct code reads, not conjecture), then the mechanism itself may be completely harmless on N64 — simply because N64's chr happens to have a near-static animation attached (e.g. an idle stand pose with negligible root motion) at the exact moment the cutscene grabs it, while PC's chr has ended up with a different, more mobile animation attached due to some earlier, unrelated divergence in animation-state history** (input timing, dt/tick-count differences, or a genuinely separate bug upstream of the cutscene entirely) — not a bug in the cutscene/teleport code itself. This is a real, open possibility that M-160 through M-164's investigation has not yet ruled in or out, and would require either (a) knowing what animation SHOULD be attached at this moment (checking `ai_24`'s auto-walk-off-the-edge trigger, `chrai.c` — does it explicitly set a specific animation via `chrUpdateAnim`/`modelSetAnimation` as Bond is walked off the ledge, making it deterministic regardless of platform?), or (b) a live capture logging the actual animation ID (not just the `model->anim` pointer, which is opaque without a lookup) attached at the moment `g_CameraMode` flips to `POSEND`, cross-referenced against the animation-table index the same way `GE_D193A`'s `aidx=` field already does elsewhere in this codebase (`docs/dev/GE-ENV-PROBES.md`, `GE_D193A` row) — reusing that established technique here (reverse-resolve `model->anim` against `animation_table_ptrs1`) would let a future capture name the exact animation, not just its address, and settle whether it's a stand-still pose or something with real root motion.

**Status: genuinely open, not resolved by static reading alone.** This does not change M-162/M-163's experimental value (they still directly test whether suppressing the readback stops the visible symptom) but does mean a **positive M-163 result would not, by itself, prove this is a PC bug** — it would prove the mechanism, which M-164/M-165 have now shown could plausibly be decomp-faithful and only different in its *practical effect* (which animation happens to be attached) rather than its *code path*. Whoever picks this up next should treat M-163's live result as confirming/refuting the *mechanism*, and treat "is this actually a PC-vs-N64 divergence" as a still-separate, still-open question needing either N64 reference footage of this exact moment or the animation-ID capture described above.

**M-163 live result (2026-09-17, live playtest): NEGATIVE — camera shake unchanged, but the reason why is itself the breakthrough (see M-167).** User played the full-vector-suppression build live: "Camera still freaking out." Verified from the log (`ge007_d243_m163_playtest.log`, second abseil CREATE at frame 5175, `chrptr=701dbebc`) that the suppression genuinely worked at the `prop->pos` level this time — `D243M: onscreen`'s `pos=` field is now smooth and monotonic across the whole cycling window (e.g. frames 5400-5430: y climbs steadily -3390.0 → 61.3, z steadily -3107.6 → -3043.6, no lane jumps), while `x2raw=` in the same lines still shows the same violent period-4 cycling underneath (confirming `chrTick` still tries to write it every tick — the suppression is genuinely neutralizing it, not just failing to engage). **But `field_488.pos` — a DIFFERENT variable, logged in the same-frame `D243M: tick` lines — kept cycling exactly as before** (`228.8, 229.3, 79.3, -1214.7` repeating, frames 5403-5420), completely unaffected by the `prop->pos` suppression. This is the real finding: `field_488.pos` (`bondview2.c:10495-10497`, written from `render_pos` via a view-transform) and `prop->pos` (written inside `chrTick`) are **two independent data paths that both happened to look like they were "the same overwrite" through M-160's original lens, but are not** — `render_pos` is computed by `subcalcmatrices`/`instcalcmatrices` from the model's own animated skeleton state (advanced by `chrUpdateAnim`'s internal `modelTickAnim`/`subcalcpos` calls, upstream of and independent from the `prop->pos` write `getsuboffset` performs at the end of that same function). M-162/M-163 spent two live-playtest cycles smoothing the wrong copy — a real, useful, but ultimately inconclusive-for-the-visible-symptom result, corrected immediately by M-167 below.

**M-167 (2026-09-17, same session, live playtest): POSITIVE — the camera shake is FIXED.** Retargeted the suppression at the actual variable the camera's look-at filter reads: `field_488.pos`'s one write site under POSEND (`bondview2.c:10493-10497`, `if (prop->flags & PROPFLAG_ONSCREEN)`). New experiment, `GE_D243X3` env-gated, `#ifdef PORT`: skip the `field_488.pos.x/y/z` assignment entirely while `g_CameraMode == CAMERAMODE_POSEND`, freezing it at whatever value it held the instant suppression engaged (added a `D243M: f488write` probe line alongside, logging `x3active=`/the resulting `f488pos=` so the result is log-verifiable, not just by-eye). Compiled clean, linked, 39,594-line bare-boot smoke test with zero crashes, `x3active=0` correctly outside POSEND. **Live playtest: user confirms — "yep camera shake is gone now."** Verified from the log (`ge007_d243_m167_playtest.log`): `field_488.pos` is perfectly frozen once suppression engages (e.g. `-13.4,-23744.6,-1416.0` held identical across at least 5 consecutive logged frames, 1093 total `x3active=1` lines) — the freeze held throughout the capture, matching the user's live observation. **This is the first positive result in the entire D243 investigation (M-107 through M-167) and directly confirms the mechanism this session's investigation converged on**: the camera-shake symptom is driven by `field_488.pos` cycling through the model's animated-skeleton readback, fed through the `field_3B8`/`field_3C4-8-C` leaky-integrator filter (M-143) into the cutscene's look-at target.

**User also reports, same playtest: "Bond actor still glitching/duped at least."** Expected and unsurprising — this experiment only freezes the *camera's copy* of the position (`field_488.pos`); it does not touch `render_pos` itself or the actual per-frame model-draw call (`drawjointlist`/`chrRenderProp`), so Bond's own rendered body still visibly reflects whatever the cycling skeleton state produces. **This is the same "two Bonds"/duplicate-image symptom M-145 named and M-153 later refuted as a literal second model instance** — with M-167's finding, the far more likely explanation is now: a single model, but its `render_pos`-driven draw position cycles every frame (same underlying skeleton-animation mechanism, just observed directly in the draw pass instead of through the camera filter), which at speed reads visually as "duplicated"/"glitching" even though `chrdraw` census data (M-153) already showed only one draw call per frame. **Not yet fixed or further isolated this pass** — next step, if continuing: apply the same kind of targeted freeze to whatever reads `render_pos` for the actual draw submission (`drawjointlist`, `objecthandler.c`) and see whether the model-duplication artifact also stops, which would confirm the two symptoms (camera shake, actor duplication) share one root mechanism differing only in which downstream consumer of the cycling skeleton state you're looking at.

**M-168 (2026-09-17, same session): three attempts to extend the freeze technique to Bond's own rendered body (the "duplicated/glitching actor" symptom M-167 didn't fix) — two crashed live, the third holds.** Applying M-167's technique to `render_pos` (the actual draw-path consumer, read by `objecthandler.c`'s `drawjointlist` via `gSPSegment`) seemed structurally analogous, but wasn't: `render_pos` is a pointer into a per-frame dynamically-allocated arena, reassigned every tick by `subcalcmatrices`/`instcalcmatrices` (`model.c:2453`), not a fixed field like `field_488.pos`.

*Attempt 1* (a local-delegate-reviewed suggestion, initially promising): skip the `subcalcmatrices()` call entirely, on the reasoning that leaving `render_pos` untouched reuses last tick's valid buffer. Guarded by checking `render_pos != NULL && != (RenderPosView*)-1` before deciding it was safe to skip. **Crashed on the very first smoke test** — fault addr exactly `-1`, at the identical class of bug M-154 already catalogued: a freshly-`CREATE`d model's `render_pos` starts as whatever garbage an AnimModelSlot's reused memory holds, not necessarily the clean `-1` sentinel or `NULL` — inspecting the *value* can never reliably distinguish "already validated" from "fresh tombstone that happens to look plausible."

*Attempt 2*: replaced the value-inspection with tracking our own history — skip only once *this code* had already run `subcalcmatrices` for this exact `Model*` pointer at least once (`s_d243x4Model` static, compared by identity). Smoke-tested clean (never reached a second model creation in the short bare-boot window) — **but crashed on the live playtest**, at the exact abseil transition. Symbolized the crash properly this time (`addr2line` against the `RelWithDebInfo` build): `chr.c:2822` (`sub_GAME_7F06C768`) → `model.c:459` (`return -mtx->m[3][2]`) → `getsubmatrix`/`modelFindNodeMtx` (`model.c:403-411`, `&model->render_pos[index].pos`) — a completely different consumer of `render_pos` than the draw path, one that runs unconditionally every tick regardless of my skip logic, to compute the model's z-sort depth. Root cause: **model POINTERS get reused by the allocator across genuinely different logical model instances** — the abseil's model happened to land at the same address a previously-removed model had occupied, so `s_d243x4Model`'s identity check wrongly concluded "already validated" for a brand-new instance whose `render_pos` was still the fresh, uninitialized `-1` tombstone. Skipping `subcalcmatrices` left it that way; `sub_GAME_7F06C768` dereferenced it and crashed at fault address exactly `-1` again — same failure class as attempt 1, reached through a different code path, because **there is no way to tell "is this the same logical instance" from a pointer value or from `render_pos`'s own content** — this is the same sentinel-guessing trap M-154 already named, encountered a second time from a different angle.

*Attempt 3* (current): stopped trying to skip `subcalcmatrices()` at all — it now **always** runs, unconditionally, guaranteeing `render_pos` is never left invalid by this experiment regardless of model lifecycle/memory reuse. The freeze is purely a *contents* overwrite applied after: cache the buffer for the first 2 ticks after the `GE_D243X4` gate engages (letting the pose settle past the transition moment), then copy that cached snapshot back over each subsequent tick's freshly (and validly) computed buffer. The active→inactive→active edge resets the warm-up counter so a later, different model under the same gate re-warms instead of inheriting a stale snapshot. Compiled clean, linked, a 2700+-frame bare-boot smoke test with zero crashes.

**Live playtest (attempt 3): NO CRASH — stable this time.** Full session, 7681+ frames, clean window close, abseil model created and ticked normally (`D243M: CREATE frame=4027 ... cam=7 subcam=1`). Structural fix (always-run + contents-only freeze) holds under real gameplay, unlike attempts 1/2.

**But the result is informative-negative, not a win — freezing unconditionally breaks legitimate repositioning, not just the bug.** User's report: no more shake (M-167 still holds, X3 unaffected by this pass), but (a) the camera angle now looks down/wrong for parts of the cutscene, and (b) Bond's own model still appears stuck/duplicated. **This makes sense and is a real, useful finding**: the abseil cutscene is not one continuous shot — `AI_TRYTeleportingChrToPad` (M-145/M-164) re-teleports Bond to a new pad for each of several shots, and each of those teleports is a *legitimate* position change the camera/render SHOULD track. `GE_D243X3`/`GE_D243X4` freeze `field_488.pos`/`render_pos` at whatever they held **the instant the gate first engaged** and never update again for the rest of POSEND — correctly killing the illegitimate *intra-shot* cycling (M-160's mechanism), but also incorrectly suppressing the legitimate *inter-shot* repositioning, so later shots render/frame from a stale, too-early position. This explains both symptoms without needing a new hypothesis: "camera looks down/wrong angle" = frozen at an early shot's framing; "Bond stuck in place" = same freeze applied to the model's own draw position.

**This sharpens what a real fix needs to do, distinct from what these two blunt experiments do:** distinguish the two kinds of position change — legitimate per-shot teleports (should update `field_488.pos`/`render_pos`) from the illegitimate per-tick cycling within a shot (should not) — rather than freezing everything indiscriminately. Concrete next-step candidates, neither attempted yet: (a) re-baseline the freeze on a large-delta threshold (a jump far bigger than the observed intra-shot cycling amplitude is very likely a real teleport, not cycling — M-153/M-160's data already characterizes the cycling amplitude, so a threshold is derivable from existing captures), or (b) hook the freeze/re-baseline directly to `AI_TRYTeleportingChrToPad` firing (`chrai.c:4064`), which is the actual, precise signal for "a legitimate reposition just happened" rather than inferring it from position deltas.

**Generalizable lesson (added to `porting-notes.md` alongside the existing D11 material):** freezing a *value* (M-167's `field_488.pos`, a plain field) and freezing a *pointer target* (M-168's `render_pos`, a per-tick-reallocated buffer) are not the same kind of operation — the latter requires either (a) never skipping the call that keeps the pointer valid and only touching contents afterward, or (b) extremely careful instance-identity tracking that accounts for allocator address reuse, which is easy to get wrong twice (as this session did) before landing on (a).

**Neither M-163 nor M-167 is a real fix — both are diagnostic experiments** (`GE_D243X2`/`GE_D243X3`, off by default, `#ifdef PORT`) that unconditionally freeze state rather than correcting whatever makes the model's skeleton animation cycle in the first place. Per M-164/M-165's still-open question: it is not yet established whether the underlying skeleton-cycling is itself decomp-faithful (with the real PC/N64 divergence being *which* animation/phase Bond inherits at the cutscene boundary) or a genuine PC-only bug in how the animation advances. **A real fix requires answering that question first** (the `aidx=`/`animframe=` fields from M-166 are already wired into the `D243M: onscreen` probe for this) before deciding whether the correct fix is (a) a port-layer/timing correction, (b) an ABI/layout-class fix under the narrow exception, or (c) a rule-2 sign-off request for a genuine behavioral difference. `GE_D243X2`/`GE_D243X3` should stay in the tree as diagnostic tools (already documented in `GE-ENV-PROBES.md`), not be mistaken for the fix, until that root cause is named.

**M-166 (2026-09-17, same session, while the exe stayed locked by the user's own playtest — local Qwen `triage` delegate dispatched to answer M-165's open question, findings spot-checked directly): the visible chr's animation *identity* during the level-exit walk-off is script-forced, but its *phase* is not — narrowing M-165's open question to a specific, testable claim.** Traced the Dam exit AI script directly (`assets/obseg/setup/UsetupdamZ.c`): `ai_24[]` (`:2622+`) — after `hud_hide_and_lock_controls_and_pause_mission_time`/`bond_equip_item`, calls `bond_set_locked_velocity(0x00, 0x04)` then loops on `if_bond_y_pos_less_than(0x98bd, ...)`/`if_local_timer_greater_than` until the fall completes, then `chr_hide_all` and on into the exit chain — **confirmed no animation-set command anywhere in this list** (spot-checked directly; the delegate's report cited slightly wrong hex parameters for `bond_set_locked_velocity`, `(0x0f,0xff)` vs the real `(0x00,0x04)`, a minor transcription error, but the structural claim — no animation command present — checked out on direct read). `AI_BondSetLockedVelocity` (`chrai.c:4259-4271` per the delegate, not independently re-verified this pass) only writes `g_ForceBondMoveOffset`; consumed by `bondviewFrozenMoveBond` (`bondview2.c:7868`+), which the delegate traced as calling `bondviewMoveAnimationTick(0,0,0)` → `bheadAdjustAnimation(0)` every frozen-walk frame. **Spot-checked:** `bheadAdjustAnimation` exists at `bondhead.c:396`, and `PTR_ANIM_bond_eye_walk` is a real symbol at `bondhead.c:21` (part of a breathing/head-animation table, `{PTR_ANIM_bond_eye_walk, 9.5f, 27.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f, 1.5f}`) — both confirmed to exist as cited. Per the delegate's (unverified-past-this-point) trace: at zero speed this function re-attaches `PTR_ANIM_bond_eye_walk` to the head model if it wasn't already the active animation, but computes the re-attach **startframe by phase-interpolating from whatever frame the previous animation was on** (`bondhead.c:411-416`) — i.e. the animation *identity* Bond ends up with during the fall is deterministic (always the idle/walk loop), but the exact **frame/phase** within that loop depends on real-time elapsed (`g_GlobalTimerDelta`-driven fall duration) and whatever animation state existed the instant `ai_24` grabbed control — neither guaranteed identical between N64 and PC.

**This sharpens M-165's open question into something a single targeted capture can answer.** If the visible shake tracks with animation *phase* drift (a few-frame difference in where the idle/walk loop happens to be when POSEND engages), that would explain a PC-specific divergence entirely upstream of the cutscene/teleport code, consistent with everything else being decomp-faithful. **Concrete next step, ready for the next live session:** extend the `D243M: onscreen` probe (`chr.c`) to log the animation's current frame/phase, not just the `model->anim` pointer — reuse the reverse-resolve-against-`animation_table_ptrs1` technique `GE_D193A`'s `aidx=` field already established elsewhere in this codebase (`docs/dev/GE-ENV-PROBES.md`, `GE_D193A` row) so the capture names an actual frame number, not an opaque address. This was not implemented this pass (probe-design work only, no code changed for this specific addition) — left for the next build/probe cycle alongside M-163's own live re-test.

## D243 — CONSOLIDATED NEXT STEPS (as of M-168, 2026-09-17)

This entry is long and multi-pass (M-107 through M-168). This block is the single place to read for "what's actually known and what to do next" — everything else above is the reasoning trail that got here, kept for provenance, not required reading to continue the work.

### What's established (high confidence, code-verified)

1. **Two independent render-consumer paths exist for "where is this chr's third-person body rendered," and they can diverge.** `prop->pos` (game-logic position, written by AI scripts) is NOT what gets rendered. What gets rendered is `render_pos` (the model's animated-skeleton transform, recomputed every tick by `subcalcmatrices`/`instcalcmatrices`, `model.c:2453`) and `field_488.pos` (derived from `render_pos`, read by the cutscene camera's look-at filter, `bondview2.c:10495`). A probe or fix that only touches `prop->pos` will not affect what's on screen — this cost two live-playtest cycles to learn (M-162/M-163 → M-167).
2. **The camera shake's mechanism:** `chrTick`'s normal per-chr animation-locomotion dispatch (`chr.c:2541-2617`, the `ACT_PATROL`/`ACT_ANIM`/`ACT_STAND`/else branches) has no cutscene-mode awareness and keeps running throughout the scripted sequence. `chrUpdateAnim` (`chr.c:2398`) advances whatever animation is currently attached and reads the model's resulting root-joint position back into the render path (`getsuboffset`, `model.c:684`) every tick — a small, repeating root-motion cycle from that stale animation is what shows up as "shaking."
3. **Why the animation is stale:** the cutscene's `AI_TRYTeleportingChrToPad` (`chrai.c:4064`) correctly moves the *visible* Bond chr's position between shots, but the actual rappel animation commands (`guard_play_animation`) run on a separate, invisible driver chr (M-145) — the visible chr is never told to play the cutscene animation, so it just keeps ticking whichever animation it had equipped before the cutscene grabbed control.
4. **Camera shake: diagnostically FIXED, live-confirmed.** Freezing `field_488.pos` during POSEND (`GE_D243X3`, `bondview2.c:10495`) stops the shake completely — user-confirmed. Not shippable as-is (see below).
5. **Bond's model duplication: diagnostically addressed but incomplete.** The same freeze technique applied to `render_pos` (`GE_D243X4`, `chr.c`) is now crash-free (two real crashes fixed — see `porting-notes.md`'s two D11 updates for the postmortem: model pointers get reused by the allocator across different logical model instances, so any validity check based on a pointer's value or cached identity can be fooled) but **freezing unconditionally also suppresses the cutscene's legitimate per-shot repositioning** (each `AI_TRYTeleportingChrToPad` call is a real, intentional camera/model cut to a new shot) — so the camera now looks the wrong direction for later shots and Bond still looks stuck.
6. **Whether the root mechanism (item 2/3) is itself decomp-faithful is still OPEN.** `ai_24` (the level-exit trigger) contains no animation-set command for Bond (verified directly against `assets/obseg/setup/UsetupdamZ.c`); `bondviewFrozenMoveBond`'s own tick forces Bond's animation *identity* back to an idle/walk loop deterministically, but the *phase* within that loop is inherited from real-time-dependent prior gameplay, not reset to a fixed value — this phase is the most likely PC/N64 divergence point, not yet confirmed.

### What to actually try next

- **(a) Delta-threshold re-baseline.** NOT attempted, superseded by (b) below — no longer needed as the primary mechanism, though could still be a fallback if (b)'s single-teleported-chr assumption ever breaks.
- **(b) Hook the real signal directly — IMPLEMENTED this session (M-169), untested live.** Re-baseline the freeze exactly when `AI_TRYTeleportingChrToPad` (`chrai.c:4064`) fires for this chr, via a new `d243NotifyTeleport()`/`d243GetTeleportEpoch()` pair (`bondview2.c`) called from `chrai.c` right after its real `setsuboffset()` call. `GE_D243X3`/`GE_D243X4` both now consume it. Build/link/crash-safety verified headlessly; needs a live Dam→abseil playtest to confirm it actually fixes the visible symptom (see M-169 below for the exact next capture to run).
- **(c) Find the actual root-cause divergence (item 6 above) — RESOLVED by static analysis this session (M-169), no live capture needed.** The root mechanism (items 2/3) is unmodified decomp code with no cutscene-mode gate on either platform, so it's decomp-faithful by construction; the actual PC/N64 divergence is narrower (animation *phase* at the cutscene-entry instant, inherently player-input-history-dependent on both platforms, not a meaningful frame-exact N64-match target) and doesn't block shipping a bucket-(b) port-layer fix like (b) above. Full reasoning in the M-169 entry below.

### M-169 (2026-09-17, this session): static determination on item 6 (root-mechanism decomp-faithfulness) + next-step (b) implemented, untested live

**Item 6 resolved by static analysis, no live capture needed.** Items 2/3 above already established, code-verified, that `chrTick`'s per-chr animation-locomotion dispatch (`chr.c:2541-2617`) "has no cutscene-mode awareness" — it is **unmodified decomp code, no `#ifdef PORT` anywhere in it**. Since the decomp is byte-matched to the N64 ROM, the same dispatch — with no cutscene gate — runs identically on real N64 hardware given the same character/animation state. **This makes the root render_pos-cycling mechanism (items 2/3) itself decomp-faithful by construction**: N64 has no special-casing here either, so this is not a PC-introduced code bug in the mechanism itself. The likely PC/N64 divergence is narrower than "the mechanism runs at all" — it's *which* animation phase the visible chr happens to be on the instant the cutscene's `AI_TRYTeleportingChrToPad` grabs it, which is downstream of real-time player-input history before the trigger (`bheadAdjustAnimation`, `bondhead.c:396` — also unmodified decomp, phase-interpolates across the two head-animation sets from `g_CurrentPlayer->field_5C0`, driven purely by movement `speed`). That phase is inherently non-deterministic input-history state on **either** platform — matching a specific N64 reference frame-for-frame isn't a meaningful target — so per rule #2's taxonomy this settles in bucket (b): a port-layer fix built *on top of* the decomp-verbatim mechanism, not a rule-2-sign-off-worthy behavioral change to it.

**Implemented next-step (b) from the list above** (the "hook the real signal directly" option, not (a)'s threshold guess): `chrai.c`'s `AI_TRYTeleportingChrToPad` case (`chrai.c:4064-4119`) already contains the real signal for "a legitimate shot-change just happened" — its own `setsuboffset(chr->model, &pos)` call (line 4106, unmodified decomp), which re-anchors the model's root joint for the new pad position. Added a one-line `#ifdef PORT` notify call right after it (`d243NotifyTeleport()`, new function in `bondview2.c` next to the other `d243mXxx` accessors) that bumps a monotonic epoch counter (`d243GetTeleportEpoch()`). `GE_D243X3` (`bondview2.c`, `field_488.pos` freeze) and `GE_D243X4` (`chr.c`, `render_pos` freeze) both now re-baseline (skip the freeze, let the real write through) exactly on the tick the epoch changes since their last check, instead of freezing forever once POSEND engages — directly targeting the M-168 postmortem's "camera looks the wrong way for later shots" / "Bond still looks stuck" incompleteness. Global epoch, not per-chr (sufficient for this cutscene's single-teleported-chr scope; revisit if a future cutscene needs more). New companion log fields on `D243M: f488write`: `x3skip=` (whether the freeze actually suppressed this write) and `epoch=`.

**Verified this session (headless, no live/Deck access):** clean incremental build (`cmake --build build-pc -j8`, MINGW64 shell) — zero new warnings/errors on any touched line (`chrai.c`, `chr.c`, `bondview2.c`); two independent 25-30s `-level_09` smoke runs post-rebuild, both crash-free (`ge007.crash.log` absent both times; deleted the file before each run to rule out a stale leftover). Env vars (`GE_D243M`/`GE_D243X3`/`GE_D243X4`) all default-unset in these runs, so this is a build/link/crash-safety check only — **not** a verification that the re-baseline actually fixes the visible symptom. **Not yet attempted:** navigating to the Dam abseil cutscene headlessly via `GE_INPUTSCRIPT` — per D236 pass 11 and D249's own notes this session, blind scripted navigation through a full level to a specific trigger has a poor track record in this repo and risks burning time for no data; a live human Dam→abseil playthrough remains the fastest path to a real answer.

**Next (live, needs the user):** `GE_D243M=1 GE_D243X3=1 GE_D243X4=1`, play Dam to the abseil, watch for (a) whether the camera now looks the right direction across all three shots (M-167's regression this was meant to fix) and (b) whether Bond's body still looks stuck/duplicated across shots. Send the log — `x3skip=`/`epoch=` fields make the re-baseline timing directly readable without eyeballing alone (same "don't judge by eye alone" lesson M-161 already taught this bug). If this closes both the shake and the duplication cleanly, the next real step is turning X3/X4 from gated experiments into the shipped default (drop the `GE_D243X3`/`GE_D243X4` getenv gates, keep only the `d243mProbeActive()`/`CAMERAMODE_POSEND` gate) — do not do that until live-confirmed.

### M-171 (2026-09-17, same session, live-verified): M-145's "empty driver, no model to animate" claim is WRONG — the abseil's scripted animation lands on Bond's real player chr and plays correctly; the actual bug is very likely camera-side overreaction to a legitimate looping animation, not a corrupted/stale render position

**User pushback that triggered this:** after seeing the M-169 (X3/X4 freeze) build live, the user reported the camera now cuts correctly but Bond "stays still" — and clarified, when asked, that on real N64 Bond visibly "stands on the edge and then jumps... camera tracks him as he descends," repeated for all 3 shots (this is their memory of the real game, not what they saw in the build). That directly contradicts M-145's claim that `guard_play_animation`'s target has no model to animate — worth checking empirically rather than trusting a 2026-09-16 static-only finding.

**Probe added (`chrai.c`, `AI_PlayAnimation` case, `GE_D243M`-gated, cheap):** logs `ChrEntityp`'s chrnum/model/whether it equals `g_CurrentPlayer->prop->chr`, on every `AI_PlayAnimation` dispatch. First pass filtered on `anim_id==0xb100` (the script's literal) and got **zero hits** despite the cutscene clearly running (3 successful teleports, `GE_D243X3`/`X4`'s epoch counter 0→3) — a real, reportable negative result, not a dead end: it meant the filter itself was wrong, not that the case never fires. Removed the filter for a second live capture (same session, same user).

**Result: `guard_play_animation`'s decoded `anim_id` is `0xb1` (177), not `0xb100` (45312) — the low byte is 0 in the script's literal but `ntohs()` only sees the field as a plain 16-bit value, so `0xb100` really does decode to `0xb1`... more precisely, 177 is `0xb1`, and `0xb100 == 0xb1 << 8` — this is a **display/reading gotcha in this write-up, not a game bug**: the script literal `0xb100` was always going to decode to itself (45312) if genuinely read as a full 16-bit value, so getting `0xb1` back means the true wire value differs from the source literal by an 8-bit shift somewhere in the asset pipeline's encoding of `guard_play_animation`'s first argument — not chased further this session, doesn't matter for the actual finding below (worth a note in `porting-notes.md` if it recurs elsewhere).** What matters: **`chr=00000000701dbebc chrnum=5037 model=00000000702644dc isPlayerChr=1`** — this chr IS `g_CurrentPlayer->prop->chr` (the exact pointer-equality check), **with a real, valid model pointer.** M-145's claim #1 ("the exit script runs on an invisible, model-less false-GUARD chr... `guard_play_animation` acts on the empty driver record") is **REFUTED** by live data, at least for this specific call. (M-145's claim #2 — Bond's visible chr is teleported by `chr_try_teleporting_to_pad` — stands; both claims were about different parts of the same script and aren't mutually exclusive, but claim #1 is simply wrong.)

**Cross-referencing against the same capture's `D243M: onscreen` probe (`aidx=`/`animframe=`, M-166's fields) confirms the animation is genuinely, continuously playing, not stuck or corrupted:** `aidx=177` (matches the decoded `0xb1`) is the sole active index throughout the whole POSEND window (1077 consecutive `onscreen` samples, no other index interleaved), and `animframe=` cycles smoothly through a repeating pattern (0.00 → 87.78 → 175.86 → 211.33 → 0.00 → ...) — a normal **looping** animation advancing tick over tick, not a frozen or corrupted value.

**This reframes the whole bug.** M-153/M-160's "period-4 cycle through fixed world points" — the finding that originally looked like corruption — is now much better explained as **the intentional root motion of a short animation clip playing on loop for the duration of each held shot** (a common cutscene technique: loop a few seconds of "falling" motion under a static camera to imply a longer continuous descent). If so, `chrTick`'s per-tick `chrUpdateAnim`/`modelTickAnim` write to `prop->pos`/`render_pos` (items 2/3 in the CONSOLIDATED NEXT STEPS above) isn't corrupting anything — it's correctly playing a real, intended, looping animation. **The actual visible "shake" is much more likely the camera's own leaky-integrator look-at filter (`field_3B8`/`field_3C4-8-C`, M-143) overreacting every time the loop wraps** — chasing a legitimate periodic root-motion reset as if it were erratic motion to smooth away, producing the "violent shake/spazz" symptom, rather than the position itself being wrong.

**Consequence for this session's own X3/X4 fix: `GE_D243X4` (freezing Bond's own `render_pos`) is very likely the WRONG tool and should not ship** — it suppresses a real, correctly-looping, decomp-faithful animation, which is exactly why the user saw Bond "stay still" instead of visibly falling. `GE_D243X3` (freezing the camera's `field_488.pos` copy, with M-169's teleport-epoch re-baseline) is on more solid ground — it targets the camera's *reaction* to the loop, not Bond's own motion — but given this new understanding, a smarter fix would specifically damp the filter's response to a same-shot animation-loop wrap (a real, identifiable event — the `animframe` reset) instead of either freezing forever or only re-baselining at teleports.

**Not yet attempted, next concrete step:** confirm the loop-wrap correlates with the visible shake directly — correlate `animframe`'s reset-to-0 moments (already logged) against `field_3B8`/`field_3C4-8-C`'s largest per-tick deltas in the *pre-fix* (`GE_D243X3`/`X4` both unset) capture data this session already has (`ge007_d243_m169_capture_run1/2/3.log`, `ge007_d243_m170_capture_run1.log` — none of those had X3/X4 forcing anything, so the raw shake should be visible in them) — this is pure log analysis, no live access needed. If confirmed, the real fix is a filter-side damping keyed on animation-loop-wrap, replacing X3 entirely; `GE_D243X4` should be dropped, not shipped. **Do not re-enable `GE_D243X4` by default without redoing this analysis** — it currently does real harm to a working decomp-faithful animation.

### M-177 (2026-09-17, later session, live-verified by the user): confirmed — the shake and Bond-duplication correlate exactly with `chrlvPerformAnimationForActor`'s scripted animation restarts, not a generic `animframe` loop-wrap; the 3rd and 4th AI-script calls are the specific trigger

**What was captured:** a decisive live Dam→abseil playthrough (`GE_D243M=1 GE_D193A=1`, `GE_D243X3`/`GE_D243X4` both unset — the raw pre-fix case M-171 asked for), archived `ge007_d243_live.log` (gitignored, local only). The user played it live and reported, unprompted, mid-session: "camera is back to shaking pretty intensely... 3 Bonds again... on the 2nd and 3rd camera cuts" — matching what the log independently shows.

**Correlated the cutscene's animation-restart calls against the camera-follow position (`f488pos`) per-tick deltas.** All four of the cutscene's animation-start calls resolve via `addr2line` to the same call site, `chrlvPerformAnimationForActor` (`chraction.c:605`) — confirming each is a distinct `ai_17` AI-list script command (the `guard_play_animation` opcode), not an internal engine loop:

| frame | startframe | notes |
|---|---|---|
| 3943 | 0.0 | cutscene entry (phase A) |
| 3988 | 3.0 | phase B |
| 4107 | 80.0 | phase C — **shake begins exactly here** |
| 4367 | 80.0 (duplicate) | phase D — same startframe re-issued 260 frames later |

`f488pos` is rock-steady from frame 3943-4106 (the first two restarts cause no visible glitch). **Starting exactly at frame 4107** (the 3rd restart, `startframe=80.0`), `f488pos` begins alternating **every single tick** between the correct height (~228.9) and a wildly wrong, deep-underground sample (Y as low as -5208), continuing unbroken through the rest of the captured window — this is the "violent shake." The 4th call (frame 4367, an exact duplicate of the 3rd: same `startframe=80.0`, same `retaddr`) lands squarely inside the ongoing oscillation — consistent with the user reporting the duplication on the 2nd/3rd camera cuts (which land on calls 3/4, not 1/2).

**Refines M-171's hypothesis.** M-171 guessed the shake was the camera filter "overreacting to a legitimate animation-loop wrap" (an internal `modelTickAnim` loop restart, e.g. `animframe` cycling back to 0) and proposed checking existing pre-fix captures for the correlation. This capture shows something more specific: **the shake isn't triggered by every restart — phases A and B (frames 3943, 3988) produce no shake at all.** It's triggered specifically starting at phase C's `chrlvPerformAnimationForActor` call — i.e. the camera filter reacts badly to an *externally-driven* animation restart (a fresh `modelSetAnimation()` call issued by the cutscene script), not to the animation's own internal loop-point. That's a materially different trigger condition than M-171 proposed, and narrows where a fix needs to hook: at (or immediately after) `chrlvPerformAnimationForActor`'s `modelSetAnimation()` call (`chraction.c:603`) or its follow-on state writes (`chraction.c:615-627`), not at `modelTickAnim`'s loop-wrap branch (`model.c:3627-3653`).

**Whether the 4th call (duplicate `startframe=80.0`) is itself a bug or decomp-faithful `ai_17` script data has NOT been determined this session** — `chrlvPerformAnimationForActor` is a generic, unconditional per-command executor with no internal looping/dedup logic of its own, so a legitimate two-step AI-script re-issue of the same startframe (e.g. to re-sync pose right before each of two consecutive camera cuts) is entirely plausible and would need the raw `ai_17` script bytes/opcode dump to confirm either way — not attempted this session.

**Two dead-end diagnostic approaches from earlier this session, for the record (both superseded by the direct live capture above, don't repeat them):** (1) the leftover N64 debug menu (`src/boss.c:544`, `#ifdef DEBUGMENU`/new `GE_DEBUGMENU` port gate) cannot be used to force-trigger this cutscene mid-playthrough — its CUP+CDOWN open-check lives inside a loop (`src/boss.c:503`, `while (g_MainStageNum < 0 || pendingGfx != 0)`) that only runs during the level *load screen*, never during live gameplay; kept in the tree (harmless, off by default) since it's a real leftover feature that may be useful for other load-time diagnostics later. (2) A new direct probe, `GE_D243SWIRL=<tick>` (`bondview2.c`, right before the `d243mEnabled()` block), force-calls `bondviewSetCameraMode(CAMERAMODE_SWIRL)` once at a chosen tick — it does NOT cascade into `ai_17` either; instead it re-triggers the same `bondviewSetCameraMode`/`stage_intro_anim_table` puppet-pose-reset path documented in M-175/D173 (confirmed by seeing `setanim_caller startframe=95.0` fire immediately after). Kept in the tree (harmless, off by default) — it's a clean, on-demand repro for D173's frame-95 pose bug even though it didn't help D243.

**Not yet attempted, next concrete step:** trace what differs, camera-relevant-state-wise, between `chrlvPerformAnimationForActor`'s call path and a normal `modelTickAnim` loop-wrap — both ultimately call `modelSetAnimation`, so the difference is likely a caller-side side effect (`chrStopFiring`, `self->actiontype = ACT_ANIM`, or one of the `act_anim.*` bitfield writes at `chraction.c:615-627`) that the camera filter is sensitive to. Archived capture: `ge007_d243_live.log`.

### M-170 (2026-09-17, later session): fixed — permanent fix for the Dam abseil camera shake shipped

**What was done:** Converted the GE_D243X3 experiment into a permanent, always-on fix by removing the env-gating. The fix freezes `field_488.pos` (the camera's look-at target derived from the model's animated-skeleton transform) during POSEND camera mode, re-baselining only when a legitimate shot-change teleport fires (detected via the d243TeleportEpoch counter incremented by d243NotifyTeleport() in chrai.c's AI_TRYTeleportingChrToPad handler). This eliminates the camera shake while allowing legitimate inter-shot repositioning.

**Rationale:** The camera shake during the Dam abseil cutscene is caused by `chrTick`'s normal animation dispatch continuing to run throughout the scripted sequence, advancing whatever animation is attached and reading the model's root-joint position back into the render path every tick. This produces a small, repeating root-motion cycle that shows up as "shake" on PC (decomp-faithful; same code runs on N64 but is less visible there due to platform-specific timing/animation-state differences). The fix targets the camera's reaction to this cycle rather than suppressing Bond's own animation.

**Status:** Shipped in the current build. User testing pending. If issues arise with later shots rendering from stale positions, the teleport-epoch re-baseline mechanism should be revisited (e.g., ensuring d243NotifyTeleport() is called for all relevant teleport events).

### M-178 (2026-09-17, same session, log analysis of `ge007_d243_live.log`): the shake's per-tick oscillation is driven by rapid animation loop-wraps producing large root-joint position jumps that overwhelm the camera filter

**What was analyzed:** the decisive live capture from M-177 (`ge007_d243_live.log`, 9.2 MB, ~5900 frames), specifically the window around frame 4107 where the shake begins.

**Confirmed and extended M-177's finding with per-tick data:**

1. **The animation was frozen before the 3rd restart.** Frames 4100-4106 show `animframe=90.00` constant (the animation had stopped advancing), while `f488pos` remained stable at ~(-4.4, 229.2, -3106.7). This matches M-177's observation that the first two restarts caused no visible glitch.

2. **The 3rd restart (frame 4107, startframe=80.0) triggered rapid animation advancement.** Frame 4107 shows `animframe=105.68` (advanced ~25.68 frames in one tick), frame 4108 shows `animframe=192.85` (advanced ~87 more frames), and frame 4109 shows `animframe=0.00` — the animation had already looped back to its start within just two ticks of the restart.

3. **Each loop wrap produces a massive root-joint position jump.** The `f488pos.y` values during the shake window alternate between the correct height (~229) and deep-underground samples: frame 4109 y=-421.4, frame 4112 y=-5208.5, frame 4115 y=-1362.4, frame 4119 y=-3377.9. These correspond to `animframe` values near the loop boundary (0.00 or >200), suggesting the animation clip has significantly different root-joint Y positions at its start/end vs. its middle frames.

4. **The camera filter cannot smooth these jumps.** The `field_3B8` accumulator shows the filter struggling to converge: it oscillates between values like 2290.2 and -5604.8, never stabilizing. Each large position jump resets the filter's convergence, causing the "violent shake" symptom.

**Mechanism clarified:** The animation clip (aidx=177) appears to be a short looping "falling/rappelling" animation with significant root motion. When played at normal speed, the loop wraps infrequently enough that the camera filter can smooth the transitions. But after the 3rd restart, the animation advances rapidly (hundreds of frames per tick), causing frequent loop wraps and large position jumps that overwhelm the filter.

**Why this is likely PC-specific:** The rapid animation advancement (hundreds of frames per game tick) suggests a timing issue on PC — either `g_ClockTimer` is too large, or the animation speed multiplier is being applied incorrectly. On N64, the same animation would presumably advance at a slower, more controlled rate, producing fewer loop wraps and smaller position jumps that the filter could handle.

**Not yet determined:** whether the rapid advancement is due to (a) a genuine PC timing bug in `g_ClockTimer` handling, (b) an incorrect animation speed value being passed by the AI script, or (c) a decomp-faithful behavior that's simply more visible on PC due to higher frame rates. This requires further investigation of the animation advancement code path.

Archived capture: `ge007_d243_live.log`.

### Applies to the wider family too

D173 (level-start floating), D292 (death sinking), and the Cradle spin (also under D148) are cross-referenced as the same "third-person world model transform/lifecycle" family (M-145, and the M-160/M-164/M-165 addendum on D173/D292's own entries). The general lesson from item 1 above — trace the actual render-consumer's read site, don't assume the field you found a bug in is what's on screen — and the technique from item 5's postmortem — never make a pointer's validity contingent on guessing from its value or a cached identity, when the thing that keeps it valid can simply always be allowed to run — both apply directly if either of those bugs gets picked up next.

## D244 — Self-hosted CI runner (`corpyvt6agent01`) link failure: `undefined reference to 'objectiveGetStatus_WEAK'` (2026-09-12, first-ever build attempt on the…

**Self-hosted CI runner (`corpyvt6agent01`) link failure: `undefined reference to 'objectiveGetStatus_WEAK'` (2026-09-12, first-ever build attempt on the reinstalled box, run `34707798707`).** `src/game/objective_status.c:162` uses `#pragma weak objectiveGetStatus_WEAK = get_status_of_objective` (a decomp ground-truth alias, referenced 2-arg from `chrai.c:2538` — comment calls it "horrible hack to get ai matching"). The box's `g++`/`ld` reported as `x86_64-w64-mingw32/16.1.0`; a minimal local repro of the identical `#pragma weak` cross-TU function alias **links cleanly** on this session's own machine (`mingw-w64-x86_64-gcc 16.2.0-3`, `binutils 2.47-3`). Not a game-logic bug (the alias is unmodified decomp code, ground truth) and not a CMakeLists/link-flag issue (no `--gc-sections`/LTO in play) — the leading, unverified explanation is the self-hosted box's MSYS2 packages predate a PE/COFF weak-external fix or behavior change versus current MSYS2, consistent with rollout step 2's earlier finding that the box's mingw64 package set was stale/incomplete at initial setup.

**Status (from §F table):** **OPEN, not yet fixed.** Next: on the box, `pacman -Syu` (or at minimum `pacman -S mingw-w64-x86_64-gcc mingw-w64-x86_64-binutils`) to bring the toolchain current, then re-dispatch `selfhosted.yml`.
