## D281 — `Game.AllUnlocked` (D257) still breaks audio, and can also break right-mouse aim, when enabled before any save has ever been written (v0.2.1 user testing…

**`Game.AllUnlocked` (D257) still breaks audio, and can also break right-mouse aim, when enabled before any save has ever been written (v0.2.1 user testing, 2026-09-15) — a distinct regression from D259, which only fixed the all-zero-slot volume case.** User's empirical workaround: complete a level normally first (e.g. Dam on Agent, which writes a real save), THEN enable `All unlocked`; enabling it on a completely fresh install (no save yet) still reproduces both symptoms. Not root-caused this session — D259's `geEepromPatchAllCheats` all-zero-slot seeding was verified against exactly the "fresh eep" case, so either that fix doesn't cover every code path a truly-first-launch toggle can hit (e.g. a race between the F10 toggle taking effect and the very first save-slot creation/read), or there's a second, independent mechanism. The right-mouse-aim symptom is new information with no prior lead — cross-ref D211/D194 (aim-mode sensitivity/mode family) for where a save-state-dependent aim regression could originate.

**Status (from §F table):** OPEN — user-reported regression, not root-caused; mitigation is user-facing guidance only (release notes: don't enable until a save exists, treat as experimental).

**Root cause + fix (2026-09-23, v0.4.0):** D259 emulated only part of the fresh-slot path. Without AllUnlocked, an all-zero slot fails `fileValidateSaves`' CRC → `fileResetSave` → a *free* `BLANKSAVEDATA` slot (DORESET, vol 0xFF, `options = DEFAULT_OPTIONS` 0x3A), and then `fileBuildWriteNewSave` fills the first free slot for each folder without a save. The AllUnlocked read patch re-CRCs every slot, so all-zero slots instead **survived** as five non-free slots all claiming folder 1, with `options = 0` (sight-on-screen OFF = no crosshair when aiming, which is the "RMB aim broken" symptom; auto-aim, look-ahead and ammo display also off). The game then reset/rebuilt the duplicate folder slots mid-validate. **Fix (`port/src/libultra.c` `geEepromPatchAllCheats`, port-only):** all-zero slots take the folders no real slot holds, in order, built exactly as `fileBuildWriteNewSave` does (`BLANKSAVEDATA` + `fileSetSaveFoldernum`/`fileSetSaveFlagDoReset(FALSE)`/`fileSetSelectedBond`, the game's own setters); leftovers become free `BLANKSAVEDATA`. Real saves keep their bytes. **Verified (native Windows, fresh zero eep, `AllUnlocked=1`, `SkipIntro=1`, `GE_SAVELOG=1`):** `fileValidateSaves` now sees `00/21/42/63/80` (folders 1–4 + one free slot, the layout a normal fresh install produces), all CRC OK and no repair writes; the eep on disk stays pristine (read-time patch). Before: five `00` slots. Golden 3/3 (AllUnlocked off by default, so the change is inert there); Windows + Linux builds clean. **Owed:** the audio half of the report was never mechanised. The volumes were already right after D259, and the folder-collision churn this removes is the most plausible remaining cause. User check: fresh install (move `ge007.eep` aside) → enable All unlocked → play a level; audio and RMB-aim crosshair should both work.

## D282 — QoL ask (v0.2.1 user testing, 2026-09-15): front-end menu navigation (main menu, file select, mission-select map) currently requires the RIGHT analog stick —…

**QoL ask (v0.2.1 user testing, 2026-09-15): front-end menu navigation (main menu, file select, mission-select map) currently requires the RIGHT analog stick — matches N64 default control schemes but is unintuitive on a modern controller/Steam Deck, where the left stick is the expected primary-navigation input.** Distinct from the F10 options overlay, which is already left-stick/D-pad navigable (`port/src/optionsoverlay.c`). Scope: front-end menu input in `src/game/front.c` (or wherever N64 stick reads are gated by the active `controldef`) — likely wants a port-layer input remap for these menu contexts specifically, not a general control-scheme change. **M-141: root cause found + fixed, port-only.** `front.c`'s menu-nav code reads `joyGetStickX/Y` — the same emulated N64 "Control Stick" channel (`stick_x`/`stick_y`) that in-level gameplay uses. `port/src/input.c`'s gamepad poll routes that channel to the LEFT physical stick by default, but `naturalPitchMode` (D194/D238's SOLITARE-style scheme, **default-on**) reroutes it to the RIGHT stick for continuous look — and since menus share the channel, they silently inherited that reroute too. The poll already computed an unused `padMenuMode` flag (`current_menu != GE_MENU_RUN_STAGE/GE_MENU_INVALID`, previously only gating shoulder-button weapon-cycle edges); moved it earlier and added a `padMenuMode` branch that always sources `stick_x`/`stick_y` from the left stick outside a running stage, regardless of `naturalPitchMode` — matching the F10 overlay's existing left-stick convention (`optionsoverlay.c`). Zero effect on in-level control feel (the branch is inert whenever `current_menu == GE_MENU_RUN_STAGE`). Verified: build green; `-level_09`/`-level_20` unregressed (1100+ frames each, no crash) — bare `-level_XX` launches skip the front end entirely, so this only proves the gameplay path (unaffected) stays clean. **In-menu feel not interactively verified this session** (no physical gamepad available in this environment) — needs a human playtest with a controller to confirm the menu now navigates on the left stick as expected.

**Status (from §F table):** FIXED (`port/src/input.c`, `#ifdef` not needed — port-layer-only file), feel unconfirmed.

## D283 — Steam Deck first-run preset (D-unnumbered in `port/src/video.c`/`main.c`, `videoApplySteamOSDefaults()`) did not apply for a user who added the game via Steam…

**Steam Deck first-run preset (D-unnumbered in `port/src/video.c`/`main.c`, `videoApplySteamOSDefaults()`) did not apply for a user who added the game via Steam in Desktop Mode and switched to Game Mode afterward — resolution stayed at some non-native value instead of the Deck's native 1280×800 (v0.2.1 user testing, 2026-09-15).** Root mechanism, confirmed by code inspection: the preset only applies when `getenv("STEAMOS")` is truthy AND no `ge007.ini` exists yet (`main.c:126-129`, before `configLoad()`); once any ini exists, it always wins over the preset on every future launch (by design, so user F10 changes persist). **Leading hypothesis (not verified on real hardware in this environment):** SteamOS's Desktop Mode (a normal Plasma/X11 session) likely does not export the same `STEAMOS` env var that the Game Mode/gamescope session does, so a Desktop Mode test-launch (a natural step when adding a non-Steam game via its file browser) creates `ge007.ini` with ordinary Linux defaults *before* the user ever reaches Game Mode — permanently skipping the preset for that install, since the ini already exists on the first real Game Mode launch. This exact caveat was already known internally (`docs/HANDOFF.md`: "a Deck that already has an ini needs `-fresh` or F10 to pick the preset up") but was never surfaced in user-facing docs (README/release notes) — same class of gap as the stale D230 release-notes reference. **Workaround (lighter than `-fresh`, which also wipes the save):** F10 → Resolution → 1280×800 manually; takes seconds, no data lost.

**Status (from §F table):** OPEN — mechanism understood, root cause (Desktop-vs-Game-Mode `STEAMOS` env var difference) unverified on real hardware; user-facing workaround documented in README/release notes.

## D287 — User-confirmed real, non-self-recovering freeze on Windows (M-141, 2026-09-15/16) after ~15-20 minutes with no input, triggered by clicking back into the…

**User-confirmed real, non-self-recovering freeze on Windows (M-141, 2026-09-15/16) after ~15-20 minutes with no input, triggered by clicking back into the window.** Caught live under `tools_pc/debug.ps1` (gdb-attached), evidence preserved at `scratch/d287_freeze_gdb.txt`. Last real `frame N rendered` log line: frame 17616. The heartbeat (`portHeartbeatCheck`) then fired 3 times with a **growing** stall (8001ms → 13017ms → 18021ms, `frames=17616` unchanged all 3 times) and then stopped logging entirely, while the VI-retrace pacemaker (`D51 vi post #N`) kept incrementing at its normal ~60 Hz rate for well over 100 more real seconds until the user closed the window — i.e. the pacemaker/OS-timer side is alive, the sim/render side is genuinely wedged, not the D286 shape (which self-recovered after one dump). **Different from D286**: no explosion/level-streaming context (idle + refocus, not combat), and the growing-then-silent heartbeat pattern (vs. D286's single fire-then-recover) points at a different mechanism. **Leading lead, not yet confirmed:** at freeze time, `gfxFrameMsgQ` (`src/init.c`, the scheduler's 32-slot client completion queue, registered via `osScAddClient`) shows `valid=32/32` — completely full — while the VI-retrace queue (8-slot) is not (`valid=1/8`). A full *client* queue with the producer (scheduler) still ticking implies the **consumer** (the main thread's `osRecvMesg(&gfxFrameMsgQ, ...)` in the frame loop) stopped draining it — consistent with the main/render thread blocking on something else (a lock, a GL call, a Windows message-pump stall) during or after a long-idle refocus, not with the scheduler itself stalling. Not yet identified what that something is. A pre-existing, currently-unused diagnostic (`GE_D60`, `port/src/libultra.c:630+`) already watches `gfxFrameMsgQ` receives and looks like the right next probe to enable. **Next, concrete:** reproduce with `GE_D60=1` (and ideally `GE_INPUTLOG=1`) running under `debug.ps1`, leave the window idle+unfocused 15-20 min, refocus, and once frozen `bt full` the actual game/render thread (not just the auto-dump's generic `WaitForMultipleObjects` frames for `shedThread`/`audioThread`) to find what it's blocked on. Cross-ref D134's superficially-similar-sounding-but-different mechanism (a different, 8-slot queue, already fixed) — do not assume the same fix applies here without confirming the actual blocked call site.

**M-152 correction (2026-09-16, static-only pass — verified directly, don't skip this): `scratch/d287_freeze_gdb.txt` does NOT contain the evidence this entry describes.** Grepped the file on disk for `17616`/`8001ms`/`13017ms`/`18021ms`/`portHeartbeatCheck` — zero hits. What the file actually holds is a **clean normal-exit capture**: boot through `frame 20700 rendered` / `D51 vi post #20821`, then `[INFO] video: window closed`, all threads exiting with code 0, `Inferior 1 exited normally`, and gdb's post-mortem `No stack.`/`The program has no registers now.` under `BACKTRACE`/`REGISTERS` — i.e. the user closed the window normally in whatever run produced this specific file; it is not a freeze capture at all. The frame-17616/heartbeat numbers cited above must come from a different run that was never saved, or got overwritten by this file under the same name. **Practical upshot: no real freeze-time thread state has actually been analyzed yet** — everything upstream in this entry citing `d287_freeze_gdb.txt` as "evidence" is describing a file that no longer supports that claim; treat the freeze mechanism as still fully open, not "narrowed and just needs confirming." Architecture traced (still useful, static-only, no game execution): the sole `OS_MESG_BLOCK` **send** anywhere in mainThread's per-frame path is `osSendMesg(sched_cmdQ, ...)` at `src/game/rsp.c:271` (end of `rspGfxTaskStart`), which per `port/src/libultra.c:605-628` does an unbounded `pthread_cond_wait` if the scheduler's 8-slot `cmdQ` is full; the scheduler thread (`__scMain`, `src/sched.c:245-310`) drains that queue unconditionally every retrace tick (`__scHandleRetrace`, `sched.c:323-325`) and separately stuffs `gfxFrameMsgQ` via NOBLOCK sends every retrace (`sched.c:352`) — consistent with the "queue fills because the consumer stopped receiving" shape, but a missed-wakeup race on the `cmdQ` condvar is a hypothesis, not evidence; no second "idle+refocus"-shaped blocking call was found in mainThread's path (SDL event pumping runs on a separate host thread, `port/src/main.c:243-246`, ruling out message-pump starvation as a mainThread blocker). Also noted: `portHeartbeatCheck` (`port/src/libultra.c:218`) hard-caps at **3 reports total per process lifetime** by design — "heartbeat stopped logging" (cited above as evidence the mechanism differs from D286) is that cap firing, not a signal the hang changed shape; don't read silence from this diagnostic as meaningful without accounting for the cap. `GE_D60` (`port/src/libultra.c:630-642`) only validates `gfxFrameMsgQ` receive *content* isn't clobbered — it does not instrument sends or `sc->cmdQ`, so it alone won't catch a `cmdQ`-side stall. Proposed for the next real capture (not yet added to tree): a `GE_D287` env-gated variant of `portHeartbeatCheck` that keeps reporting (with a full thread/queue dump via the existing `crashDumpThreads`) for the whole stall instead of stopping after 3, run alongside `GE_D60` under `debug.ps1` for the actual 15-20 min idle+refocus repro — this is the only way to get mainThread's real blocked call site.

**Status (from §F table):** OPEN — the `d287_freeze_gdb.txt` file this entry cited as evidence turned out to be a normal-exit capture, not a freeze capture (M-152 correction); no real freeze-time thread state has been analyzed yet. `gfxFrameMsgQ` full remains an architecturally-plausible lead (traced statically: consumer-side stall via an unbounded `pthread_cond_wait` in `rsp.c:271`'s `osSendMesg`, if the scheduler's `cmdQ` fills), not a confirmed cause. Needs a fresh live capture — ideally with a raised/env-gated heartbeat-report cap (see above) plus `GE_D60` — to get mainThread's actual backtrace at freeze time.

**2026-09-25: likely mechanism (code review) + fix applied, pending a re-test.**

- **Queue-deadlock leads ruled out statically.** The only blocking sends are `rsp.c:271` (main → sched `cmdQ`, 8 slots), `sched.c:428` (task-done → `gfxFrameMsgQ`) and PI completions. The main loop caps work in flight at `pendingGfx < 2`, so it can never fill `cmdQ` and block there; a sched↔main circular wait cannot close. The shared-condvar `pthread_cond_signal` pattern in `osSendMesg`/`osRecvMesg` needs two blocking waiters of the same kind on one queue plus an opposite waiter; no queue in the game has that shape. `joyPoll`'s blocking receive (joy.c:438) is balanced by `osContStartReadData`'s immediate completion post.
- **What does fit "idle, then click back into the window":** `port/src/input.c` called `SDL_SetRelativeMouseMode` and `SDL_ShowCursor` from **two threads**. The scheduler thread did so on every controller poll (`osContStartReadData` → `contSnapshotFromKeyboard` → `inputComputePad` → `reconcileGrab`/`applyCursorVisibility`); the host thread, which created the window and pumps its events (`port/src/main.c` loop → `videoPumpEvents`), did so from focus/click handling (`inputSetMouseGrab`, `inputNotifyClick`). SDL's mouse/window API is not thread-safe and belongs on the window's thread. On Windows, relative mode starts/stops SDL 2.30+'s raw-input thread and re-clips the cursor. Refocus + click is precisely when both threads flip the grab state at the same moment. The port already had this rule for F10 window changes (`videoDrainWindowRequests`), but mouse mode was never routed that way.
- **Fix (port-only, `port/src/input.c`, `port/src/video.c`, `port/include/input.h`):** `applyGrab`, `applyCursorVisibility` and `inputSuspendForOverlay` still update the logical state immediately, but only *record* the wanted relative-mode/cursor state (spinlock, last writer wins). `inputApplyMouseRequests()` applies it, deduplicated, on the host thread at the start and end of every `videoPumpEvents()` (and once in `inputInit`, which runs on the host thread). `inputUpdate` skips relative deltas until relative mode is actually on, so the ≤8 ms gap reads no absolute motion.
- **Verified:** Windows + Linux builds clean; golden gate 3/3. **Not verified:** the freeze itself (needs the idle 15–20 min + refocus repro) and mouse feel. **User checks:** click-to-lock, mouse-look, ESC release, alt-tab away/back, F10 overlay cursor, cursor hidden in menus; then leave the window unfocused ~20 min and click back in.

**2026-09-26 (v0.4.0, M-201): user-confirmed FIXED.** Mouse checks (click-to-lock, Esc, alt-tab, F10 cursor, front-end pointer) all fine; the real repro, the game left unfocused with no input past the ~15–20 min window and then clicked back into, resumed normally with no freeze.

**Status: FIXED (user playtest, 2026-09-26).**

## D288 — Silo intro: a huge, flat-shaded, untextured brown/tan triangle sweeps across the frame during the camera pan down the missile shaft (M-141, user report —…

**Silo intro: a huge, flat-shaded, untextured brown/tan triangle sweeps across the frame during the camera pan down the missile shaft (M-141, user report — "weird triangle drawn on silo intro randomly when the camera pans around the rocket"; previously catalogued as `GRAPHICS-BACKLOG.md` D171, "observed, not investigated" since M-34, never given a full findings.md entry until now).** Reproduced headlessly this session: `GE_PCDUMP=1-2000:10 ./build-pc/ge007.x86_64.exe -level_20` (run backgrounded, not foregrounded — see the environment note below), captured to `./ppm/`. Visual sweep (contact-sheet montages, `docs/img/bugs/D288-silo-stray-triangle-sheet.png` covers frames 571-751; `-closeup.png` is a full-res crop of frame 691) shows: **clean at frames 481-561** (no triangle), **first appears between frame ~562-601**, grows continuously in screen size through frame ~711 (by which point it covers roughly a third of the frame), then **shrinks and is gone by ~731-741** as the scene cuts to the first-person shaft-corridor view. Sampled pixel color is **exactly uniform** across the whole triangle (`RGB(83,62,44)` / `#533E2C` at two different sample points) — no gradient, no texture detail — i.e. this is a flat-shaded (no per-vertex color variance, no texture bound) single triangle, not garbage/noisy vertex-color data. **Reading of the evidence:** the grow-then-shrink-then-vanish arc across ~15 real seconds of camera motion is the classic signature of a genuine 3D triangle in world space that the camera flies close to/through during the scripted pan — not a 2D HUD/UI element (which would stay roughly fixed in screen size) and not obviously a `D146`-class freed-memory read (which reads as noisy garbage bytes, not a clean uniform flat color). The flat uniform color argues this is a REAL, correctly-colored asset triangle whose position/transform is wrong, which points at the same neighborhood as D106/D233 (near-plane / w-clip mishandling in `port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp`) rather than a game-code or converter data bug — but this is a read of the visual evidence, not a code-level confirmation; no probe has been run yet. **Not yet identified:** which model/prop this triangle belongs to (nothing in `UsetupsiloZ.c` was grepped for a matching solid-brown material this session), and no `port/fast3d/` tracing was done to catch the actual triangle at draw time. **Environment note (new, useful beyond this bug):** launching `ge007.x86_64.exe` in the **foreground** under this session's Bash tool with `timeout N ...` produced **zero** `ppm/` output despite `GE_PCDUMP` being set and verified exported — the `ppm/` directory was never even created (`GE_MKDIR` never ran or `frames`-gated capture never fired). Backgrounding the same invocation (`... &`, `sleep N`, `kill`) worked immediately and reliably. Not root-caused (didn't block this investigation), but worth remembering for the next session that needs `GE_PCDUMP` from this same tool. **Next, concrete:** (1) grep `assets/obseg/setup/UsetupsiloZ.c` / the missile-shaft model's material table for a solid `RGB(83,62,44)`-ish prim/vertex color to identify the source asset; (2) add a temporary `#ifdef PORT` probe in `gfx_sp_tri1` logging any triangle whose post-transform screen-space bounding box exceeds some fraction of the viewport together with each vertex's `w`, gated to `-level_20` frames ~560-740, to catch the culprit triangle's `w` sign/magnitude at the moment it blows up — same style as the existing `GE_D271`/`GE_D104` probes; (3) cross-check against D233's `w<0` trivial-reject fix and D106/D271's near-plane portal-bound clamp to see if this is a third site with the same underlying class of bug, or a genuinely new mechanism.

**M-152 (2026-09-16, static-only pass, no game execution this session — user was mid-playtest):** read `gfx_sp_tri1` (`port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp:1586-1651`) against D233/D106/D271/D234 to see what's already guarded. **D233's trivial-reject fix is ruled out as the direct cause** — it only ever adds triangles GL's own hardware clipper would legitimately draw from well-formed clip-space geometry (`gfx_opengl.cpp:320` hands GL raw `x,y,z,w` and lets GL clip natively), so a well-formed w<0/straddling triangle can't come out screen-filling from that guard alone. **New unguarded site found, not previously catalogued:** the backface-cull test right below it (`gfx_pc.cpp:1618-1629`) divides raw vertex `w` with no epsilon guard when computing the cull cross-product; a vertex at/near `w≈0` during a near-plane crossing can NaN/Inf the cross product, which silently fails both `<=0`/`>=0` cull branches and lets a triangle through that should have been backface-culled. Asset search (`UsetupsiloZ.c`, `bg_silo_all_p.c` — no `SetPrimColor`/`SetEnvColor`/`SetFillColor` at all, so the flat color must be vertex-RGBA or lighting-derived, not a literal stored triple; a byte-triple grep for `0x53,0x3e,0x2c` ±3 fuzzy across all of `assets/` found zero matches) did not identify the source model — GE's binary-included model blobs aren't literal hex in the `.c` sources, so this needs a runtime probe, not more grepping. **Confidence: LOW-MEDIUM, still not root-caused.** Two live candidates: (1) the new backface-cull NaN/Inf leak above, (2) the D106/D271 portal/room-visibility BFS family in `bg.c` (less likely given the smooth 150-frame grow/shrink arc, which doesn't match that family's usual abrupt full-screen-clamp signature, but not traced through the silo intro's specific camera/portal path so not ruled out). A `GE_D288=1` env-gated probe (cached-getenv, D250-safe) is now in tree at `gfx_pc.cpp` right after the D233 guard (~line 1616): logs any triangle whose clip-space NDC bbox covers >15% of the screen or goes non-finite, together with each vertex's `w` and `any_behind_camera`. **Next:** `GE_D288=1 GE_PCDUMP=560-745:5 ./build-pc/ge007.x86_64.exe -level_20 2> scratch/d288_probe.log` (background it, not foreground — see the environment note above), grep around frames 562-741 for `color≈(83,62,44)`. `any_behind=1` with one `w` very close to (not deeply past) 0 → candidate 1; `any_behind=0` with comfortably-positive `w`s but still a large bbox → a genuine asset/transform bug outside fast3d entirely, rules out both candidates above.

**M-155 (2026-09-16, this session): the M-152 probe run happened, result is inconclusive — the probe itself needs frame-gating before it can disambiguate.** Ran `GE_D288=1 GE_PCDUMP=560-745:5 ./build-pc/ge007.x86_64.exe -level_20 2> scratch/d288_probe.log` (backgrounded, per the environment note above) for a 25s bare boot. **Two problems with the result, not with the underlying bug:**
- The probe fires **116,308 times** in 25s (roughly 1500-2000 frames) — i.e. dozens of times per frame throughout the *entire* run, not bounded to the reported ~562-741 window. `bbox_frac > 0.15` (covering >15% of the screen) turns out to be a common, unremarkable occurrence for ordinary near-camera geometry (walls, floors, large props), not a distinguishing signature of the stray triangle — the threshold alone can't isolate the bug.
- The target signature from M-152's own next-step note, `color≈(83,62,44)`, **never appears** in the log (checked via `color=\([789][0-9],[567][0-9],[34][0-9]\)`, zero matches) — either the boot never actually reached the frame window where the bug fires in this run, or the flat vertex color isn't quantized the way the visual sample suggested. No `GE_PCDUMP` PPM frames were produced either (the `ppm/`-style output dir wasn't created — likely a missing/different output-dir env var beyond just the frame-range spec — so there was no visual cross-check available this pass).
- Of the `any_behind=0` subset (comfortably-positive `w`, ruling out candidate 1 for those specific triangles) with very large bboxes, all sampled instances had ordinary-looking greyscale colors (`(68,68,68)`, `(179,179,179)`, etc.) consistent with normal level geometry, not the flat brown culprit — further evidence the probe is catching routine triangles, not the bug.
- **Confidence: unchanged from M-152 (LOW-MEDIUM), no candidate confirmed or refuted.** This pass is a probe-refinement finding, not a root-cause finding.
- **Next, concrete:** gate the probe to the actual bug window before re-running — extend `GE_D288` with a `num_dls` (frame counter) check bounding it to roughly 560-745 (same pattern `GE_D236RM` already uses for its own frame gating, `gfx_pc.cpp` ~line 1648), and/or tighten the bbox threshold well above the apparent ~0.15 "normal" baseline this run established. Confirm the correct `GE_PCDUMP` output-directory env var (see `docs/dev/GE-ENV-PROBES.md`'s `GE_PCDUMP` row) before relying on visual frame dumps again.
- **Environment note, reinforcing the existing one:** the launched `ge007.x86_64.exe` process does **not** reliably die with `pkill -f ge007.x86_64.exe` from this Bash tool (process shows in `ps aux` as bare `ge007.x86_64`, no `.exe` suffix) — a stray instance ran ~90s longer than intended this session before being caught via `taskkill //F //IM ge007.x86_64.exe`. Use `taskkill //F //IM ge007.x86_64.exe` (not `pkill`) to reliably terminate a backgrounded launch from this shell.

**M-155 follow-up (same session): frame-gated re-run also inconclusive — bbox_frac is not a meaningful signal when `any_behind_camera=1`.** Gated `GE_D288` to `num_dls` 550-755 (matching the reported window) and raised the threshold to `bbox_frac > 0.5`, then re-ran the same 25s bare `-level_20` boot. Volume dropped from 116k to 28,883 hits — still far too many to be the single reported triangle. Root cause of the remaining noise: for `any_behind_camera=1` triangles (a vertex behind the camera plane, `w<0`), the perspective-divide math `x/w` this probe uses to estimate screen coverage is **not meaningful in the first place** — dividing by a near-zero or negative `w` produces arbitrarily large/nonsensical "bbox_frac" values for perfectly ordinary near-camera geometry, which is exactly why the surrounding code already defers to GL's own clipper for these triangles rather than trusting a raw NDC divide (see the D233 comment just above this block). This isn't evidence of the bug; it's the probe's own math breaking down in a case it was never valid for. Restricting to `any_behind_camera=0` (2,128 of the 28,883 hits) still found **no match for the target color** `(83,62,44)`; the largest/most persistent hits (`(82,94,89)`, `(70,70,70)`, repeating identically across every sampled frame in the window) look like static level geometry, not the transient grow/shrink/vanish triangle. **Working theory, unconfirmed:** the bare `-level_20` boot's scripted intro camera may not reach the same in-game state the visual bug report was captured from — the same "deterministic boot flag ≠ deterministic/representative camera path" caveat this session's D236 passes (10/11) independently ran into on a different level. **Confidence: unchanged, LOW-MEDIUM; probe volume is now sane but still hasn't isolated the signal.** **Next, concrete, revised:** (1) restrict the probe to `any_behind_camera==0` only (the `w<0` case needs a different, GL-clip-aware approach or should be dropped entirely as a false lead); (2) get a real `GE_PCDUMP` PPM capture working (confirm the output-dir env var) to visually confirm which `num_dls`/frame the boot's camera is actually at when the bug is visible, rather than assuming the frame-range label transfers directly to `num_dls`; (3) if headless deterministic-boot probing keeps missing it, this may need a live human repro with `GE_PCDUMP`/F12 at the moment the triangle is visible, same as D290's falsifier plan.

**Status (from §F table):** OPEN — visually confirmed and precisely bounded (frames ~562-741 of a bare `-level_20` boot); M-152 narrowed to two live candidates (fast3d backface-cull NaN leak, or the D106/D271 portal-BFS family) via static review; two M-155 probe runs (ungated, then frame-gated) were both inconclusive — the `any_behind_camera=1` case's bbox math is a false lead, and the `any_behind_camera=0` subset found no match for the target color. Root cause still not identified; a live human repro is now the more promising next step over further headless probing. Promoted from the long-parked `GRAPHICS-BACKLOG.md` D171 entry with real evidence.

**v0.4.0 re-check (2026-09-23, native Windows, current `release/v0.4.0` build): does NOT reproduce.** Bare `-level_20` at 640x480 with a defaults ini, `GE_PCDUMP` 400–1200 every 25 frames, then 500–950 every 5 (91 frames covering the whole rocket pan and the cut to first person). A pixel scan for the reported flat `RGB(83,62,44)` ±6 finds only frames 825–840, and those are Bond's own head fading out as the camera pushes into first person (normal GE behaviour, eyeballed). No stray triangle anywhere in the window. **D271 A/B:** temporarily restoring the pre-D271 portal-bounds limit (1e5 instead of 1e38, `bg.c`) gives the identical result, so the D271 portal-culling fix is not what removed it. The M-155 probe runs (2026-09-16) had already missed the colour, so it has not reproduced headlessly since it was written up. Either it was fixed incidentally before 09-16 (not identified), or it is intermittent, which fits the user's "randomly". **Next:** the playtest brief item (play Silo normally, F12 if seen). If it isn't seen, close as not reproducible.

**2026-09-25 playtest (user, Windows, one ~46-min session Silo → Caverns, `GE_D322=1 GE_D204=1`, build `7baf4900`):** user reports the Silo intro clean. Closed; the specific fixing commit was never isolated.

## D290 — Watch's in-game "controller" section shows no control-pad graphic (M-141, Steam Deck user playtest).

**Watch's in-game "controller" section shows no control-pad graphic (M-141, Steam Deck user playtest).** Likely a missing/failed texture or model bind on one of the watch's equipment-display pages — candidate area `src/game/bondview2.c` (watch display) alongside the front-end options/controller-config screens, not yet located precisely.

**M-152 (2026-09-16, static-only pass, no game execution this session — user was mid-playtest):** traced the real render path: `draw_watch_control_options_page()` (`src/game/options.c:3511`) gates `draw_watch_controller()` (`options.c:3336`) on `check_watch_page_transistion_running()` — this gate covers the model draw AND both text labels, so a mis-gate would drop the whole page, not just the graphic; ruled out. `draw_watch_controller()` picks `watchRenderController`/`watchRenderControllerOpaque` (`src/game/gunfire.c:1983`/`:2343`) by `g_WatchBackgroundGreen` fade state — both build a 13-node joystick+buttons model from `g_CurrentPlayer->copy_of_body_obj_header[GUNRIGHT]`, animated from live `joyGetStickX/Y`/`joyGetButtons`, then `subdraw()`. Verified the equip path is correct: `sub_GAME_7F05DA8C(GUNRIGHT, 0x55)` equips `ITEM_JOYPAD` (0x55 confirmed against `bondconstants.h`'s `ITEM_IDS` enum, not an off-by-one), the `GjoypadZ` ROM resource is present in `file_resource_table.inc.c:165`/`obseg.h:162`, and `port/shim/bondconstants.h`'s `GUNFILERECORD`/`GUNSTATS` macros are only token-paste syntax variants of the same decomp macros — no port-shim divergence. **The entire `src/game/` decomp side (item ID, model header wiring, generic equip/on-demand-load pipeline shared by every weapon, page-transition gating) is byte-matched/generic-and-proven-elsewhere — ruled out with HIGH confidence.** Root cause not found. Best-narrowed hypothesis (LOW confidence, pattern-match only, no direct evidence yet): downstream in `port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp`'s rasterization, not game logic — `watchRenderController`'s fading branch draws `PROP_TYPE_PLAYER` with a low `envcolour` alpha (green-6) and `fogcolour` alpha=0, a translucent one-off combiner/blend path that doesn't share code with the common in-level render path; this project has a recurring bug class of fast3d mishandling exactly this kind of one-off blend/CC-mode/texture-format combo while the common path works fine (D172 particle color, D217/D228 CI/IA16 palette, D229 water blend, D233 invisible-through-doors) — matches the "graphic vanishes, surrounding text stays" symptom shape. **Falsifier for next session:** get a live repro (open the watch → controller-config page) with `GE_PCDUMP`/F12 at both `g_WatchBackgroundGreen < 0xe0` (fading, `PROP_TYPE_PLAYER`) and `>= 0xe0` (settled, `PROP_TYPE_OBJ`) — missing in BOTH states kills the blend-mode hypothesis and points back to something structural (e.g. `objheader->Switches[]` never populated for this object); missing ONLY in the fading state confirms it and narrows the fix to `gfx_pc.cpp`'s `PROP_TYPE_PLAYER` + low-alpha handling.

**Status (from §F table):** OPEN — M-152 ruled out the entire `src/game/` decomp side (item ID, resource table, equip pipeline, gating) with high confidence via static trace; root cause not found, best-narrowed hypothesis points at a fast3d translucent-blend edge case, needs a live repro with `GE_PCDUMP` at both watch fade states to confirm/refute (see falsifier above).

**FIXED (2026-09-23, v0.4.0): ABI/layout class, the D264 pattern on a second call site.** Headless repro: `-level_09`, `GE_INPUTSCRIPT="1000:START;1400:RIGHT;1600:RIGHT"` (watch → Inventory → Control Options), `GE_PCDUMP` through the page. Labels drew and the model didn't, in **both** fade states (frames 1650–1700 fading, 1725+ settled), which falsifies M-152's blend-mode hypothesis. Cause: `watchRenderController` (`gunfire.c`) builds its `ModelRenderData` from `*(ModelRenderData *)((u8 *)D_80035D04 + 0x3c)`. On N64 that 64 bytes is D_80035D04's last word (0) followed by `watchControllerButtonBases` `{1, 3, 0…}` (gun.c): the same template D264 documents (basemtx NULL, zbufferenabled TRUE, flags 3). On PC `basemtx` is 8 bytes and the globals aren't at those offsets, so `flags` read 0 and `subdraw()` gated off every node. D264 fixed only `set_enviro_fog_for_items_in_solo_watch_menu`. **Fix (`#ifdef PORT`, same explicit template as D264).** Three more pointer-width/Gfx sites on the same path were fixed because the model now draws: both `matrix_4x4_copy((u32)modelstack.render_pos + i*sizeof(Mtxf), …)` loops (u32 pointer truncation; harmless on this Windows build because the pool sits below 4 GB, fatal under Linux PIE), `watchRenderControllerOpaque(…, (s32) watchTable, …)` in `options.c` (truncated stack pointer), and the dual-controller branch's hand-encoded N64 `G_MTX` word `0x01030040` (B class; now `gSPMatrix`, as the decomp comment says it should be). **Verified:** native Windows capture shows the N64 pad model and the floating button icons (`scratch/d290_after.png`); bunker1 golden 3/3; Windows and Linux builds clean. The dual-controller branch (2.x control styles with a second pad) was not exercised at runtime.
