## D292 — Death animations are glitched — Bond is often sunk halfway into the floor (M-141, Steam Deck user playtest).

**Death animations are glitched — Bond is often sunk halfway into the floor (M-141, Steam Deck user playtest).** **User confirms this is the same broader "Bond's world model is positioned wrong" problem as D173** — not a new/separate mechanism, another surface of the same known-but-under-investigated bug. The umbrella is already tracked: `GRAPHICS-BACKLOG.md` D148 is explicitly "the tracking entry for the whole cutscene-reliability problem," already lists D173 (floating at level start / Cuba credits) and a Cradle instance ("Bond spins in circles" during the Trevelyan-falls cutscene) under it — findings.md's D173 entry has the fullest investigation detail (M-106's two ruled-out D209-style struct-aliasing candidates, LOW-MEDIUM confidence that class is even the right one). Nothing has actually been lost — the write-up just isn't concentrated in one place (split across `GRAPHICS-BACKLOG.md` D148/D173 and `findings.md` D173), which reads as "known but not detailed" unless you go looking. Sunk-into-floor is a third concrete instance of the family (level-start floating, cutscene spin, now death-pose sinking) — worth keeping as one thread when it's next investigated live, since a single root cause (most likely the render-side puppet/joint transform, not collision) could explain all three.

**Status (from §F table):** OPEN — same status as D173 (observed, not root-caused). Cross-ref D173/D148 as one investigation thread, not three separate bugs, next time someone has a live session to chase it. **2026-09-17 addendum (see D173's M-160/M-164/M-165 note, and D243's own entry):** the D243 abseil-cutscene investigation this session found a well-evidenced general mechanism for this whole family — `chrUpdateAnim` reads a puppet's model-root position back into its logical position after advancing whatever animation is attached, so a transition (teleport/spawn/death) that doesn't also update the animation state produces exactly this "position lags/diverges from the animation" symptom. Not confirmed as D292's actual cause (needs its own live capture), but worth trying the same `GE_D193A`-style `aidx=`/`animframe=` technique (D243 M-166) on a death-sequence capture before assuming a new mechanism.

## D293 — QoL ask: no discoverable way to quit the game from the UI (M-141, Steam Deck user playtest — "couldn't see a way to exit the game. Maybe build this into the…

**QoL ask: no discoverable way to quit the game from the UI (M-141, Steam Deck user playtest — "couldn't see a way to exit the game. Maybe build this into the settings/options menu.").** Confirmed in code: the only quit path is `SDL_QUIT` (`port/src/video.c:515`, the OS window-close event / Alt+F4) — there is no Escape-key handler and no "Quit" entry in the front-end menus or the F10 options overlay. Fine on a desktop with visible window chrome; a real gap on Steam Deck / controller-only / fullscreen setups with no easy way to reach the OS window controls.

**Status (from §F table):** FIXED (M-141, `release/v0.3.0` local). Added a "Quit to desktop" row to the F10 overlay (`port/src/optionsoverlay.c`) — a new `ROW_ACTION` kind (not config-backed, same non-config pattern as the existing `__Resolution` row) that calls the identical `sysLogPrintf` + `configSave()` + `exit(0)` path `SDL_QUIT`/Alt+F4 already use. Reachable by keyboard (arrow/Enter when the row is selected), mouse click, or gamepad A/X — no new Escape binding was added (D145 already dedicates ESC to menu-back / cursor-release). Build-verified on Windows (`ninja`, clean link) and Linux (WSL `Ubuntu-24.04` cross-build); `tools_pc/verify.sh dam` PASS, no regression. **Not yet live-confirmed** — needs a human to actually select the row on a real session (headless/SSH-launched smoke tests can't reach the Deck's own X/gamescope display to drive input).

## D294 — Statue: ground geometry near the large CCCP/hammer-and-sickle monument briefly renders solid black over a wide area, then self-recovers 10-30 seconds later…

**Statue: ground geometry near the large CCCP/hammer-and-sickle monument briefly renders solid black over a wide area, then self-recovers 10-30 seconds later (M-141, Steam Deck user playtest).** **Correction (user, same session): happened at normal ground level during normal forward progression through the level, near the statue/monument — NOT from the elevated ramp vantage point** (the ramp is a nearby landmark used to describe the location, not the trigger condition; a first-pass write-up of this report wrongly framed "wide visibility from elevation" as the likely cause — that framing is retracted). User's settings: max `Video.DrawDistance`/`Video.LodDistance`, high `Video.FovScale` (~130%). **Not an exact match for any existing tracked culling bug, but closely neighbors three:** D222 (high-FovScale culling breakage — but D222 is specifically *NPC/object* culling near screen edges, root-caused and FIXED, not ground/BG geometry); D249 (LOD/culling breakdown on large open levels — but D249 is at *default* FOV on Streets/Egyptian, and doesn't self-recover); D218 (wide-FOV fog/far-clip boundary artifacting — but D218 is a color/tint issue at the frustum edge, not geometry going missing). **Distinguishing features that don't match any of the three:** (a) the drop-out is transient and self-corrects without the player doing anything special, (b) it's ground/BG geometry specifically, not NPCs or props, (c) it happens *within* the draw-distance/FOV settings, not past a boundary. Leading unconfirmed guess, weakened by the correction above but not ruled out: a portal/room-visibility computation (the BFS the D106/D271/D233/D234 family already touches) temporarily excluding a room/cell that contains ground geometry until the walk recomputes on subsequent player movement — the widened-FOV-frustum framing no longer applies (the drop-out wasn't tied to an unusually wide sightline), but a room-transition/streaming-timing trigger at ground level is still plausible and fits the self-recovering, "normal progression" description just as well. This is a hypothesis from the symptom shape, not a code-level finding, and now has less to go on than the first write-up assumed.

**Status (from §F table):** OPEN — not investigated. Next: reproduce on Statue (`-level_22`) at the reported settings (`Video.FovScale≈130`, max draw distance/LOD) near the ramp by the CCCP monument; a `GE_D271`/`GE_D104`-style room-visibility trace (`roomsDrawn` count, portal-cull hits) correlated with the black-ground window would confirm or rule out the room-visibility-BFS hypothesis quickly.

**ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED (2026-09-22 session) — not the room-visibility BFS; it is room-model POOL exhaustion under widened PC visibility settings.** The room-visibility hypothesis above is ruled out: `roomsDrawn`/portal-cull state stays healthy throughout the black window. The actual chain: (1) each level's authored `memallocstringtable` row budgets the room-model pool — Statue's is `-ma220` = **220 KB**; (2) the PC visibility knobs (`Video.FovScale`, `WidescreenAuto`, `DrawDistance`, `LodDistance`) keep more rooms on screen at once than the N64's fixed ~60°/4:3/authored-far-clip view, so more room models must stay resident simultaneously — the monument-plaza 12-room set alone totals ~250 KB "used", already over the authored pool; (3) when demand exceeds supply, `memaAlloc()` returns NULL (after its 8 defrag passes) and `bgLoadRoomModelData()` bails **silently** — the undrawn room's scissor region then shows the framebuffer clear colour. On Statue that is the night-sky fill RGB(0,0,8): a wide solid-black patch of "ground" that self-recovers 10–30 s later when the player moves and the rooms reload into freed space — exactly the reported symptom shape (transient, ground-specific, self-correcting). **A/B confirmed both knobs independently trigger it:** FovScale=130 alone → 372 alloc failures; DrawDistance=400 alone → 33 (and `DrawDistanceAutoFov`, default ON, couples DD to 4×FovScale when DD is at its default, so "FOV-only" configs carry a hidden 5.2× effective DD). **Stochastic overlay:** `randomSetSeed(nowCount)` uses the wall clock, so trajectory → room load order varies per run; one run logged 174 failures while six subsequent identical runs logged zero — even at the *authored* pool size in short walks. That is why the bug was intermittent for the user and evaded early headless repro.

**Fix (port-only, `#ifdef PORT`):** `portRoomPoolScale()` in `port/src/video.c` returns a pool multiplier composed from the same knobs that widen the view — FOV term = manual FovScale × the WidescreenAuto aspect factor (both widen the frustum horizontally); DD/Lod terms = **square root** of the distance multipliers (room *count* grows far slower than distance² — measured 9→12 rooms at 4× DD on Statue — so sqrt is a deliberate under-estimate). Capped at 2.0× (worst case `-ma350` row → 700 KB, well inside the PC's ~6 MB STAGE bank, D95); **identity (1.0) when every knob is N64-faithful**, so all-default settings keep the exact authored budget and golden dumps stay byte-identical. Applied in `bossMainloop` (`src/boss.c`) immediately after the `-ma` token parse — the single chokepoint both play flows (menu-driven and `-level_XX`) pass through — clamped to STAGE-bank-minus-128 KB headroom. `GE_ROOMPOOL=<float>` overrides the computed scale outright (test hook; floor 0.25 for stress-testing the exhaustion path; also a user opt-out).

**Verified headless (`-level_22`, probes `GE_D294`/`GE_D104`; the `GE_D294` stage-load print is left in `boss.c`, env-gated):** all-N64-faithful INI → `ma=225280` = exact authored size (identity ✓); user settings (FovScale 130, DD/Lod 400) → `ma=450560` (2×) with **zero** alloc failures across repeated runs; `GE_ROOMPOOL=0.25` → `ma=56320` and exhaustion reproduces on demand (thousands of `FAIL alloc` lines with movement) — proving both the override and the mechanism.

**Residual, documented only (NOT a port bug): the far-horizon hard edge at high DrawDistance on night levels.** Where fog saturates to the sky colour before the geometry's far clip, the horizon reads as a sharp lit→black boundary. That is inherent to the D218 draw-distance setting on levels whose sky ≈ black (Statue, and similar); the N64 never shows it because its far clip is authored short enough that fog always saturates first. No fix warranted; if it bothers a user, lower DrawDistance.

**Side finding (CLI footgun, no fix — game code is ground truth):** `tokenFind(1, "-m")` **prefix-matches** `-ma`, `-ml`, `-me`, …, so passing a bare `-ma N` (or `-m`) on the PC command line corrupts `g_CurentMMallocValue` (→ 0 → divide-by-zero crash). The in-ROM rows are the only intended source of these tokens; don't pass `-m*` flags on the CLI. (The D121 guard `tokenFind(1, "-m") == 0` correctly means "no -m* flag supplied".)

**Playtest update (evening of 2026-09-22).** First live Statue session at the user's settings: the wide monument-plaza patch is **gone**; residual report — "minor geometry going black/void at the corner of the screen at max FOV when running forward/backwards fast". An instrumented re-test (`scratch/d294_capture.bat`) did not visibly reproduce, but the log caught **75 `FAIL alloc` events anyway** (room 11 ×43 @33 KB, plus 23/7/17) — brief per-frame-retried starvation episodes the eye doesn't register. Root of the residual: GE keeps loaded rooms resident, and Statue's **full 27-room set is 487 KB = 2.2× its authored pool** — running around at max visibility eventually demands the whole set, which starves even the 2× (450 KB) pool. The sqrt rationale measured only *simultaneously visible* rooms; it missed accumulated residency.

**3×/linear attempt REGRESSED — reverted (same evening).** Distance terms linear + cap 3.0 (`ma=675840`) fixed the starvation headroom but broke the renderer on the **menu-driven** Statue path: "world renders as untextured polygons, Bond's hands normal". Log evidence: `[D156] bad anim frame guarded: frame=nan ...` + `subcalcmatrices: frameb out of range!` spam starting ~5 frames after stage load; the corrupted Model has valid fields (speed=0.54, anim ptr into PERMANENT) mixed with NaN/garbage floats (newspeed≈1e24, elapsespeed≈-FLT_MAX). **Not a bank overflow** — `GE_D294BANK` probe shows STAGE [0x70050000..0x706a8000] with pos=0x702ebb30 (2.6 MB used, 3.7 MB free) and `needmemallocation=0`. **Path-dependent**: direct `-level_22` boots were clean in 4/4 headless runs (Statue at vi post #1); the user's menu-driven load (Statue at vi post ~#3541, after ~60 s of front-end) corrupted. Suspects: menu-path-specific init order, or wall-clock-seeded stochasticity that the short headless runs didn't hit. Reverted to sqrt + 2.0 cap (user-verified working state; `ma=450560` re-verified). Probes left in place for the next repro: D156 hexdump of the corrupted struct (`src/game/model.c`, TEMP-marked) + `GE_D294BANK` bank-state dump (`src/game/bg.c`, wired into `scratch/d294_capture.bat`).

**Status:** **FIXED (main symptom, user-confirmed); residual corner flicker OPEN** (2026-09-22). The 2× build is the shipped state. To close the residual: capture-bat run at max FOV with fast movement → if `FAIL alloc` recurs, the fix must cover whole-level residency (487 KB) **without** the 3× regression — options: scale only when the level's room-set total is known to exceed pool (bg data has per-room sizes at load), or a smaller targeted bump (e.g. 2.5×); any change needs BOTH a direct-boot AND a menu-driven verification.

**2026-09-25 playtest (user, Windows, one ~46-min session Silo → Caverns, `GE_D322=1 GE_D204=1`, build `7baf4900`):** walking past the CCCP monument did not reproduce the black ground. Confirmed fixed.

## D211 — PC FOV slider — `Video.FovScale` (M-83 QoL wave, port-only, `WIDESCREEN-FOV-PLAN.md` Phase 4).

**PC FOV slider — `Video.FovScale` (M-83 QoL wave, port-only, `WIDESCREEN-FOV-PLAN.md` Phase 4).** fast3d applies a multiplicative half-angle scale to every *perspective* projection matrix as it is loaded (`gfx_apply_fov_scale()` in `gfx_pc.cpp gfx_sp_matrix`, on the `G_MTX_PROJECTION | G_MTX_LOAD` path only — GE always reloads its view projection via `guPerspectiveF` at `fr.c:725`, so a relative `G_MTX_MUL` onto an already-scaled matrix cannot compound). Columns 0 and 1 are scaled by the same factor `tan(half_orig)/tan(half_adj)` → H and V FOV widen uniformly, aspect ratio exactly preserved (no stretch), and because the game rewrites fovy every frame for aim-zoom the scale composes with zoom for free. Ortho matrices (`P[3][3]==1`) are left untouched so HUD/menu 2D is unaffected. `Video.FovScale` = percent of the original vertical FOV, 50–150, **default 100 ⇒ `g_fov_scale == 1.0f` ⇒ guarded early-return, zero FP ops on the matrix ⇒ golden dumps byte-identical**. F10 overlay row "FOV scale %". Math checked offline (`s=1.25 → fovy 60°→75°`, aspect held at 1.3333).

**Status (from §F table):** **PARTIAL — M-84 refix: game-side FOV scale (`src/fr.c`, `#ifdef PORT`), front-end gated, user-verified.** Original M-83 note follows. LANDED, port-only; build clean; `bunker1` framediff worst_cell 12.219 vs 12.221 baseline (= render noise, no-op confirmed). **M-84 refix — the fast3d hook only scaled *pure* perspective loads; GE draws the world through `g_CurrentPlayer->field_10E0`, a projection × view matrix pre-combined on the CPU (`bondview2.c:8224`) that failed the `gfx_apply_fov_scale` guard, so only the pause/watch model + sky FOV changed (user report).** Moved the scale game-side to the `guPerspectiveF` chokepoint (`fr.c:718`, `#ifdef PORT`, `frFovY *= portFovScale`, clamp 160°), which lands *before* the CPU combine; fast3d `gfx_apply_fov_scale`/`gfx_set_fov_scale` removed; `port/src/video.c` sets `f32 portFovScale`. Also gated to `lvlGetCurrentStageToLoad() != LEVELID_TITLE` — the front end (main menu / file+mission select / briefing) renders through the same path (`lv.c lvlRender`) and its 3D is authored at a fixed FOV. **User-verified: front end unaffected + in-level view widens (Dam tunnel at high FovScale).** M-85 headless nit check (`-level_09`, FovScale 100 vs 120): **HUD-static confirmed** — the ammo counter ("`7 | 93`") sits at the identical bottom-right screen position in both, and the door-arrow stays square (no 4:3 stretch); viewmodel scales down + stays bottom-right anchored. **aim-zoom-compose — M-86 static analysis: correct by construction.** `bondview2.c:3123` lerps `zoominfovy` then `viSetFovY()` stores it in `g_ViBackData->fovy`; `fr.c:737` applies `frFovY = fovy * portFovScale` **once**, at the per-frame chokepoint, *after* the zoom lerp. Hipfire and zoomed states scale by the same factor so the zoom magnification ratio is preserved exactly; no double-application; the smooth zoom interpolation is unaffected (scale is post-lerp). Residual human eyeball (low risk, cosmetic) at FovScale ~120–150 + full aim-zoom: the viewmodel (`c_perspfovy`, `bondview.c:644`) and frustum-cull (`currentPlayerSetCameraScale`) use the *unscaled* fovy, so a subtle viewmodel-scale or edge-cull-early mismatch is possible; the scope reticle is 2D screen-space, unaffected. Caveat (same root): edge geometry culls a hair early at large scale (cosmetic). **User-verified good at big FovScale.** New adjacent report → **D220**: 1P muzzle flash position shifts upward at higher FovScale (Jungle, M16) — likely the same unscaled-viewmodel-fovy root as the caveat above. Wide FOV also exposes the per-level draw-distance boundary → **D218** (logged, parked). **M-87: the frustum-cull residual is a real bug, not cosmetic** → split to **D222**.

## D219 — PPK explosions render purple on Dam (M-87, user QA, "not 3D but noting").

**PPK explosions render purple on Dam (M-87, user QA, "not 3D but noting").** Effect-color defect, not a texture-decode one — likely the D172 particle-color family (`gfx_lod_tile_offset` / `G_CC_INTERFERENCE` channel-order class) recurring on a different particle type/weapon than the D172 fix covered, or a fresh instance of the same class.

**Status (from §F table):** **RESOLVED (M-115, 2026-09-12)** — byte-order fix in `src/game/image.c` scoped by pixel format (16-bit family bswap16-at-store, 32-bit identity); user playtest-confirmed. Superseded history below, which began: **OPEN — observed, not investigated.** Next: `GE_PCDUMP`/`GE_TEXDUMP` a Dam PPK explosion; check whether it's the same `gfx_lod_tile_offset` tile-sampling defect D172 fixed for blood, on an explosion DL D172's fix didn't touch. **Status: re-checked at runtime M-90 — mechanism covered by the D172 fix on current `main`; close pending a human by-eye pass (folds into PR #47 playtest).** **M-89 triage (local-Qwen, static analysis only, not yet runtime-confirmed):** the explosion DLs (`assets/oddtextures.c` `globalDL_0x078/0x120/0x1c8/0x270…`) use the same `G_CYC_2CYCLE`+`G_CC_INTERFERENCE,G_CC_MODULATEIA2`+`G_TL_TILE`, tile0=IA smoke/tile1=RGBA fire mechanism as the already-fixed D172 blood/spark records — no separate/unfixed code path found in `explosion.c` or the asset DLs. If still purple after D172's fix (which the user's Dam report postdates — needs re-confirming on current `main`), the next suspect is the GLSL combiner implementation of `G_CC_INTERFERENCE`+`G_CC_MODULATEIA2` for cycle 2 specifically (`gfx_generate_cc`, `port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp:312-494`), not the tile-offset fix. **Next, concrete:** run Dam (`-level_33`) with `GE_D172=1` while triggering a PPK/grenade explosion and check for "BUG" lines in the log (silence = D172's fix already covers this DL and the row can likely close on a re-test; needs a scripted-fire repro, not yet built). **M-90 runtime re-check DONE (scripted-fire repro built with `GE_INPUTSCRIPT`): the D172 fix demonstrably covers Dam's particle DLs — row can close on a human by-eye pass.** Ran `-level_33` headless with `GE_D172=1`, 64 scripted Z-pulses (`GE_INPUTSCRIPT="200:Z;215:Z;..."`, ~15 controller-reads apart) and a `GE_PCDUMP` window over the same span. Result: **40/40 particle multitex tris log `SAMPLED1=tile1 (tmem=392)`** — the correct RGBA fire tile, i.e. exactly the post-D172-fix behaviour (pre-fix these read `SAMPLED1 = tile0 (tmem=0 fmt=IA)`, the smoke texture); **zero** "BUG"/unknown-GBI/D146-abort lines; **0** purple/magenta pixels (`r>120, b>120, g<90, r-g>50, b-g>50`) across all 28 captured frames. Caveat: the user's M-87 "purple" report may predate the D172 fix on their binary (playtests run on whatever build was current); this re-check proves the sampling path is correct on current `main`, which is as far as a headless pass can take it — a final by-eye look at a live Dam PPK firefight is the honest closer (cheap for the user, folds into the D217 PR #47 playtest). **M-108 — REOPENED, the by-eye closer FAILED.** User played a live Dam (`-level_33`) PPK firefight on the current `main` build (post-D233/D234 fixes, same session as D243) and confirmed explosions are **still blue/purple**, directly contradicting M-90's clean scripted-repro result (40/40 correct-tile samples, 0 purple pixels, 28 frames). This means the M-90 `GE_INPUTSCRIPT` scripted-fire repro was very likely **not exercising the same explosion instance/DL the live firefight hits** — plausible gaps: a different explosion variant (grenade vs. bullet-impact spark vs. enemy-death vs. PPK-specific muzzle/hit effect) using a DL the scripted test's Z-pulses didn't trigger, or a state/lighting/prim-color condition (M-89's alternate suspect: the `G_CC_INTERFERENCE`+`G_CC_MODULATEIA2` cycle-2 GLSL combiner implementation, `gfx_generate_cc`, `port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp:312-494`) that only manifests under conditions the synthetic repro didn't reproduce. **Do not trust the M-90 all-clear for this finding going forward** — it proved one particle path clean, not that Dam's live-fire purple is fixed. Next: a live `GE_PCDUMP`/`GE_D172=1` capture during an actual purple explosion in real play (not a scripted approximation) is now the only way forward — need to pin down exactly what triggers it (PPK gunshots hitting a surface/enemy? a thrown/tossed explosive? which). **User has now confirmed (2026-09-12) this is NOT Dam-exclusive — game-wide, not just suspected.** Treat as confirmed scope, not pending a second-level check. **User wants this actively fixed, not just triaged** — next session should prioritize a live `GE_PCDUMP`/`GE_D172=1` capture during a real explosion (any level) over further static analysis, since the M-89/M-90 static passes are exhausted on this finding without producing a fix. **New HIGH-interest lead (M-110): `explosion.c` never clears `G_LIGHTING` before drawing any of the 15 particle DLs** (`globalDL_0x078` through `0x9a8` in `assets/oddtextures.c`, all structurally identical, all `G_CC_INTERFERENCE`+`G_CC_MODULATEIA2`) — grepped every particle-draw call site in `explosion.c` (`gSPClearGeometryMode` calls at lines 883/1495/1718/2227 only ever clear `G_CULL_BOTH`/`G_FOG`/`G_CULL_FRONT`, never `G_LIGHTING`) and confirmed `G_CC_INTERFERENCE,G_CC_MODULATEIA2` is used nowhere else in the codebase, so it's safe to key a probe on it. The port's vertex path (`port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp:1301-1346`) branches hard on `rsp.geometry_mode & G_LIGHTING`: if lighting is on when these particles draw, the authored RGBA tint in `v->v.cn[]` gets reinterpreted as a normal vector, and the resulting SHADE color (fed into `G_CC_MODULATEIA2`'s `COMBINED*SHADE`) becomes a scene-light color instead of the DL's actual red/orange fire tint — a mechanism that would plausibly read as "wrong color, state-dependent, game-wide" exactly as reported, and would explain why a synthetic scripted-fire repro (M-90, no nearby lit models) came back clean while live firefights (guards/lit models on screen) don't. **Not yet confirmed** — this depends on whatever last touched `geometry_mode` before the particle draw in a given frame, which the game's own N64-accurate command order controls; it is not yet established whether this is a genuine port bug (fast3d misordering/dropping a `G_GEOMETRYMODE` command relative to real hardware) or something that would reproduce identically on N64 (in which case it isn't actually the D219 mechanism, since N64 doesn't show purple explosions). **Instrumented, not fixed:** added a `#ifdef PORT`/`GE_D172=1`-gated log line to the existing D172 multitex-tri probe (`port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp` ~line 1740, `gfx_sp_tri1`) that now also prints `geometry_mode` and flags `LIGHTING=ON <-- D219 SUSPECT` whenever one of these particle triangles draws with lighting on. Sanity-checked against the known-clean M-90 repro (headless `-level_33`, 40 scripted Z-pulses): probe fires exactly 40/40 as before, all show `LIGHTING=off` — consistent with the already-known-clean case, confirming the probe works and doesn't false-positive. **Next, concrete:** run `build-pc/d172_silo.bat` (or equivalent, `GE_D172=1`) and trigger a real explosion (any level, any explosive source) near visible character models; grep the log for `D219 SUSPECT`. A hit confirms the mechanism and turns this into a real fix (clear `G_LIGHTING` in the port's particle-draw path or in fast3d's geometry-mode tracking, whichever turns out to be the actual divergence from N64); a miss across a real purple-explosion capture rules this whole lead out. **M-112 (this session): decode-chain code review + two new inert diagnostic probes; runtime capture NOT obtained (environment limitation, see below). Confidence: LOW-MEDIUM on a narrowed next step, no fix applied.** Read the full N64 texture decompression ground truth for these assets end to end: `texLoadFromDisplayList`→`texLoad`→`texInflateNonZlib`/`texInflateZlib`→(`texReadUncompressed | texInflateHuffman/texInflateRle+texChannelsToPixels | texBuildLookup+texInflateLookup/texInflateLookupFromBuffer`) (`src/game/image.c`), plus `gimgFixupGlobalimagetable`/`gimgSyncCompiledGlobalDLs` (`port/src/gimgfixup.c`) and `import_texture_rgba16` (`port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp:653-681`). Findings: (1) `IMAGE_FIRE_0..14` are **not** `sImageTableEntry`-table images (unlike `IMAGE_IMPACTMULTI`/`IMAGE_IMPACTREDBRICK*`/flare/ammo images, which live in the 32 `sImageTableEntry` arrays at segment offset 0xAC8+ and get their `G_SETTIMG` marker synthesized at runtime by `texSelect`, `src/game/othermodemicrocode.c:318`) — FIRE_N's `gsDPSetTextureImage(...IMAGESEG(IMAGE_FIRE_N))` is baked directly into the compiled `globalDL_0x078..0x9a8` display lists (segment offset 0x000-0xA50) alongside the interleaved, correctly-rendering `IMAGE_SMOKE_0..14` (IA16). Both FIRE's and SMOKE's markers go through the *same* `gimgFixupGlobalimagetable` part-1 DL-bswap step and the *same* `texLoadFromDisplayList`→`texLoad` resolution — no separate/divergent table-offset math applies to FIRE_N specifically (this narrows away part of the open brief's option (a): there is no `sImageTableEntry`/`s_tbl_offs[]` bounds bug possible here, because FIRE_N never goes through that array class at all). (2) `texChannelsToPixels`'s `TEXFORMAT_RGBA16` case and `texReadUncompressed`'s `TEXFORMAT_RGBA16` case are decomp ground truth (byte-exact, `#ifdef PORT` free) and are format-generic, not texture-specific — a bug there would require a same-format sibling to also be wrong, and IMPACT/FLARE RGBA16 sprites (same `G_IM_FMT_RGBA,G_IM_SIZ_16b`, same underlying `texLoad`) are the only same-format comparison point on hand, **but this session did not runtime-confirm whether those actually render correct colors in game** — flagging as an unverified assumption inherited from earlier sessions' "shared decoder is proven correct" framing, not re-proven here. (3) `texSwapAltRowBytes` is already an unconditional no-op on `PORT` (D159, `src/game/image.c:2219`, `return;` before any format switch) so it cannot be format- or texture-selective on the port — ruled out as a contributor for FIRE specifically (it's equally a no-op for every other texture). **New, added, NOT yet exercised:** two matching `GE_D219RAW`-gated diagnostic probes (inert unless the env var is set, `#ifdef PORT`, no behavior change): (a) in `texInflateNonZlib` (`src/game/image.c`, right after the per-image header read, and again right after decode) — logs `texnum`, `format`, `width`, `height`, `compmethod` from the bitstream header, then the first row of decoded RGBA5551 pixel words, for every image shaped 16x14 (the FIRE tile shape); (b) in `import_texture_rgba16` (`port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp`) — logs the same pixel words as read back at upload time, so a session can diff "as decoded" vs "as consumed" to rule pool corruption/mis-addressing in or out. **Environment blocker hit this session:** could not get the built `ge007.x86_64.exe` to produce *any* stderr/log output when launched from this delegated agent's shell, across four different invocation strategies (direct foreground exec, backgrounded `&`/`nohup`, `cmd /c start foo.bat` detached, `cmd /c foo.bat` synchronous with a hard timeout) — the process either exits or is killed before a single `osSyncPrintf`/`sysLogPrintf` line reaches the redirected log file, even though every print call in this codebase does an explicit `fflush(stderr)`. A plain GUI sanity check (launching `notepad.exe` the same way) worked fine, ruling out a blanket "no GUI" sandbox restriction, so the failure is specific to this binary/environment combination and its cause was not identified. Per `env-no-runtime-verify` (session memory): runtime verification is session-dependent; treat this session's empty captures as inconclusive, not as evidence of anything. **Next, concrete (for a session that CAN capture runtime output, interactive or otherwise):** (i) run any level with `GE_D219RAW=1` during an explosion/PPK firefight (or simply on level load, since these are likely eagerly cached) and read the logged `compmethod` for `IMAGE_FIRE_N` — cross-reference against a `GE_D219RAW`-instrumented capture of a *confirmed-correct-on-screen* RGBA16 sprite from the sibling `sImageTableEntry` families (e.g. `IMAGE_IMPACTMULTI`) to see whether FIRE uses a different `TEXCOMPMETHOD_*` (the compressed-bitstream compression method, not the pixel format) than a texture confirmed to render correctly — `TEXCOMPMETHOD_LOOKUP`/`_HUFFMANLOOKUP`/`_RLELOOKUP` (`texBuildLookup`+`texInflateLookup*`) build/consume a packed-color lookup table with a completely different bit-layout code path than `_HUFFMAN`/`_HUFFMANPERHCHANNEL`/`_RLE` (`texChannelsToPixels`, per-plane R/G/B/A order); if FIRE's method differs from the working comparison texture's, that pinpoints exactly which decode function to scrutinize next, rather than continuing to treat "the RGBA16 decoder" as one monolithic suspect. (ii) if the compmethod matches, the bug is genuinely upstream of decode (ROM/asset-extraction data itself, not the decompression code) — at that point compare the decompressed byte stream against a reference N64 emulator's texture-dump of the same asset (this repo has no such reference on hand) to establish definitively whether the ROM bytes for FIRE really do decode to blue/purple on real hardware too (in which case the bug is actually downstream in the color-combiner path after all, reopening the D172/G_CC_INTERFERENCE lead this session did not have budget to re-examine) or whether the extraction into this repo's `assets/oddtextures.c`-adjacent ROM data diverges from the real cart image for just these 15 offsets. Probes left in tree, both inert by default: `GE_D219RAW` (`src/game/image.c` `texInflateNonZlib`, `port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp` `import_texture_rgba16`). **M-141: Steam Deck playtest confirmation, widened symptom scope** — user reports "blood is purple, shots on body are blue/green" (general, not tied to a specific level in the report). Blood/hit-decal color is a new specific instance beyond this row's tracked "PPK explosions"/"particle effects" framing — same RGBA16/particle-color neighborhood as D172/D252, worth keeping in mind together rather than as three unrelated color bugs; whichever gets a real runtime capture first (this row's own `GE_D219RAW` probe, or D252's `GE_D252`) should also check blood decals specifically.

**M-157 (2026-09-16/17, this session): first real visual capture of this bug family — but the G_LIGHTING theory below turned out to be a plausible-looking dead end, corrected at the end of this entry; read the whole thing, not just the first paragraph.** While chasing D252 (see that entry's M-156), reused the `GE_INPUTSCRIPT` Z-pulse technique on a bare `-level_09` (Bunker1) boot with `GE_PCDUMP` running, aimed at a plain metal door. **Got the first-ever visual capture of this bug family**, and it is dramatic: the same bullet-impact spark, hitting the same spot on the same door across consecutive shots, renders as bright **magenta** (frame 108), fading pale-purple (114), **green** (129), **teal/cyan** (144), purple again (198) — a literal hue-wheel cycle, screenshots in `scratch/d252_impact_zoom_*.png` (session-local, not committed — small enough to re-capture on demand with the command below). This is a plain rifle/pistol bullet hitting a static door, nowhere near an explosion — a different, previously uninvestigated code path from both D219's `explosion.c` particles and D252's `IMAGE_FIRE_N` aging system.

**Traced the actual call chain and ruled out three plausible mechanisms with code evidence before finding a fourth that fits:**
1. **Not the D252 fire-tile system.** `GE_D252=1` (hooked in `import_texture_rgba16`) got **zero hits** on this exact repro — this bug fires through a different texture-loading path entirely.
2. **Not a struct-layout/ABI bug.** The spark's texture-frame lookup (`glass2.c:678` etc.) does raw pointer arithmetic — `((struct sImageTableEntry *)((u8*)thing->unk0C + frame*12))->width` — which looks exactly like the D3x/A1 "hardcoded stride into a struct that grew" pattern this session's rule-2 work catalogued. **Checked and refuted**: `sImageTableEntry` (`src/bondtypes.h:4085`) is `{u32 index; u8 width,height,level,format,depth,flagsS,flagsT,pad;}` — no pointer members, `sizeof == 12` on both 32- and 64-bit. The hardcoded `12` is correct on this platform; bucket (a) does not apply here.
3. **Not the fixed primitive-color path.** `bullet_spark_render` sets vertex color (`vtx.v.cn[]`) from `g_BulletSparkColors[arg2]` (`glass2.c:20-27`); for a world-prop hit (`propobj.c:9633`, `objHit`) `arg2` is a hardcoded literal `1`, giving a fixed pale-yellow `{0xFF,0xFF,0xC8,0xFF}` every time — cannot itself produce magenta/green/cyan.
4. **The actual texture (`explosion_smokeimages`, `assets/oddtextures.c:484`) is genuinely IA8** (`G_IM_FMT_IA, G_IM_SIZ_8b`, 6 frames, no color channels at all) — confirmed fast3d's format dispatch (`gfx_pc.cpp:~1200`) correctly routes `fmt=IA,siz=16b` (after `texSelect`'s legitimate 8b→16b RDP-upload promotion, `othermodemicrocode.c:~400`) to `import_texture_ia16`, which decodes it as plain intensity+alpha with no byte-order bug (unlike D219's RGBA16 case) — so the texture itself cannot be the color source either.

**With texture and primitive color both ruled out as direct color sources, the M-110 `G_LIGHTING` mechanism is the one that fits everything: `bullet_spark_render` (`glass2.c:606-702`) never clears `G_LIGHTING`** — its only geometry-mode call is `gSPSetGeometryMode(gdl++, G_CULL_BACK)` (line 696), which only sets a bit, never clears one. If `G_LIGHTING` is on (inherited from whatever level geometry drew immediately before this overlay), fast3d's vertex path reinterprets the authored `vtx.v.cn[]` color bytes as a lighting normal vector and computes a scene-light-derived SHADE color instead — exactly the mechanism M-110 proposed for `explosion.c`'s particles, now found completely independently in a second file, for a completely different visual symptom (bullet sparks, not explosions), both showing the same "wrong, state-dependent, cycling" color family. This is strong convergent evidence for the G_LIGHTING theory generally, even though neither call site has a *confirmed* fix yet.

**Bucket classification, per this session's own dev-process.md §taxonomy — genuinely unresolved, flagging honestly rather than guessing:** `bullet_spark_render` carries a real decomp address comment (`// Address: 7F0A3F04`), i.e. its lack of a lighting-clear call is decomp-verified N64 ground truth, not a decompilation error — so if this were simply "add `gSPClearGeometryMode(G_LIGHTING)` to glass2.c," that would be changing verified-original game code, squarely bucket (c) territory needing a rule-2 sign-off with proof N64 hardware doesn't show this (not yet gathered). But it's equally plausible this is bucket (b): a port-layer bug in *which* lights are considered, or in geometry-mode tracking/restoration between draws, that N64's actual per-DL state machine would never have produced — fast3d's vertex-lighting implementation (`gfx_pc.cpp:~1301-1346`) hasn't been audited for a normal-vs-reference-implementation divergence in this session. **Do not add a lighting-clear call to `glass2.c` or `explosion.c` without first ruling out (b)** — that's the two-question gate `docs/dev-process.md`'s §7 requires before any bucket-(c) fix.

**Next, concrete:** (1) audit `port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp`'s vertex-lighting path against the real RSP lighting equation for a divergence that would explain why this manifests as literal rainbow hues rather than a plausible (if wrong) lit color — a genuine implementation bug there would be bucket (b), fixable entirely in `port/`, no sign-off needed, and should be checked FIRST. (2) If that's clean, trace what actually leaves `G_LIGHTING` on at the moment these overlays draw and whether N64's real command stream would have the same state (needs either real hardware or a from-scratch RSP command trace, not available this session) before treating this as a genuine bucket-(c) case. (3) A cheap falsifier for a future session with build access: force `G_LIGHTING` off immediately before `bullet_spark_render`'s draw call under a temporary `#ifdef PORT`/env-gated probe (not a permanent fix) and see if the spark holds a stable pale-yellow — a clean result narrows the mechanism definitively without committing to a fix path yet.

Repro for future sessions (headless, no game code touched): `GE_PCDUMP="0-1200:3" GE_INPUTSCRIPT="60:Z;70:Z;80:Z;...;350:Z" ./build-pc/ge007.x86_64.exe -level_09`, then inspect `ppm/frame_0001*.ppm` visually (or via any PPM viewer) near the door directly ahead of Bunker1's spawn — the spark reproduces on nearly every shot. This headless-visual-capture technique (`GE_INPUTSCRIPT` + `GE_PCDUMP` together, then inspecting the resulting PPMs directly) is itself a reusable finding for future "does this actually look wrong" investigations in this project — no live human needed to get eyes on a rendering bug, which several other OPEN findings (D290, D291, D294) have been stalled on for exactly that reason.

**Correction, same session, right after writing the paragraphs above: went back and actually measured G_LIGHTING instead of trusting the pattern-match to M-110.** Missed on first pass that the code comment at `gfx_pc.cpp` (right next to the D219 `GE_D172` probe, ~line 2015) already documents a live result never written up in this findings.md file: **"D219 round 2: G_LIGHTING is ruled out (5000/5000 samples off, live-confirmed still purple/blue)"** for `explosion.c`'s particles specifically — the sibling case the M-157 write-up above leaned on had *already* been empirically disproven, not merely unconfirmed. That should have been caught before asserting a "cross-validation" for `glass2.c` on code-reading alone.

Added a small, targeted diagnostic (`GE_D157`, `port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp`, right after the vertex color/lighting branch in `gfx_sp_vertex`, `#ifdef PORT`, cached getenv) that logs `geometry_mode`/`LIGHTING` state and the resulting shaded RGB whenever a vertex's raw `v.cn[]` bytes exactly match one of `glass2.c`'s `g_BulletSparkColors[]` entries (`{0xFF,0xFF,0xFF,0xFF}`, `{0xFF,0xFF,0xC8,0xFF}`, `{0xFF,0x00,0x00,0xFF}`). Re-ran the identical Bunker1 repro that produced the magenta/green/cyan screenshots: **only 2 hits, both `LIGHTING=off`, both pure white `(255,255,255)` unaffected** — no hit at all for the pale-yellow `(255,255,200)` value `objHit`'s door-spark call path should produce via `g_BulletSparkColors[1]`. Two possible readings, both worth recording: **(a)** most likely, **G_LIGHTING genuinely is off here too, and this mechanism does NOT explain the bullet-spark rainbow** — consistent with the sibling explosion.c case, and the two white hits this probe did catch (probably the correctly-rendering muzzle flash, `arg2==4`/`6`'s `flareimage2` branch) support that lighting is off for this whole particle family in this scene; **(b)** the probe's exact-byte-match approach may simply not be catching the actual spark vertices at all — vertex color could be getting modified before reaching this function by something not yet traced (Gouraud interpolation across the quad, a different `gfx_sp_vertex` call site, or `arg2`'s value at runtime differing from the `1` literal read in the static source). **Confidence: LOW-MEDIUM that G_LIGHTING is not the mechanism; the real root cause of the visually-confirmed rainbow cycling is OPEN AGAIN, not narrowed.** Do not carry the "cross-validates M-110" framing forward — that phrase in the first paragraph of this entry is superseded by this correction, kept only so the reasoning trail (and the mistake) stays visible.

**Next, concrete, revised:** (1) confirm whether `GE_D157` actually fires at all during the visible magenta/green frames by cross-referencing frame numbers (`num_dls`) against the known-bad frame range (108-220 in the repro above) — if it never fires in that window, the probe is looking at the wrong vertices entirely and needs a texture-identity-based trigger instead (key on `explosion_smokeimages`/`flareimage2`/`scattered_explosions`'s actual runtime texture address, the way D252's probe keyed on `IMAGE_FIRE_N`'s addresses) rather than an exact vertex-color match. (2) Once the probe reliably fires on the actual bad frames, log the full RGBA path in the frame the screenshot shows magenta/green, not just LIGHTING state — the D217-style texture-cache-collision lead already proposed for `explosion.c` (see the code comment cited above) applies here too and hasn't been checked for this call path at all. (3) `GE_D157` is left in tree, env-gated, zero cost unset — extend it rather than replacing it.

**M-158 (2026-09-16, late evening, continuation of the M-157 session): both revised next-steps implemented as probes — and the bug did NOT reproduce. The rainbow is currently non-reproducible in the dev environment; 0/6 runs.** Implemented per the "next, concrete, revised" list above: **(a) `D157T`** (in `gfx_sp_vertex`, same file/probe family as M-157's exact-color-match probe, which is kept): a vertex-level full-path log keyed on **texture identity, not color** — fires when tile 0 holds a loaded texture ≤16 KiB within the frame window [90,240]; logs raw `cn[]` bytes, post-shade RGBA, LIGHTING bit, geometry_mode, combine_mode, tile-0 tmem/fmt/siz/addr/size/line, and uv. Cap 400 lines + a summary every 200 so the log stays bounded. **(b) `D157I`** (in `import_texture`): an import census — every small (≤16 KiB) texture imported in the window, deduped per source address (first 3 hits), logging addr/fmt/siz/size/tile/tmem so a `D157T` line's `addr=` resolves to a named image. Both `#ifdef PORT`, env-gated on `GE_D157`, zero cost unset, verified firing (~1800 D157T lines + 5 D157I lines per run).

**Repro matrix (all `-level_09` with M-157's exact 30-pulse Z script, `GE_D157=1`, `GE_PCDUMP="0-1200:3"`):** five runs at the ini default (4K-class fullscreen) + one run forced to 640×480 windowed → **zero rainbow pixels in any run**, frames 90–240, using a per-run baseline-diff scan (high-saturation blobs, delta >50 vs that run's own static scene). Input delivery verified independently via `GE_INPUTLOG`: exactly 180 reads = 30 pulses × 6 reads — the script works and `Z`=`CONT_G`=fire is confirmed in both `port/src/input.c` and the game's `bondview2.c`. The spark IS drawing: periodic pale-yellow spikes (~350–450 px at 4K) every ~5 render frames from frame ~88 (control acquired ≈ HUD appears), one per Z pulse, color stable at (255,255,~200) — never cycling hue.

**Conclusions:** (1) The D219/D252 rainbow is **flaky/environment-dependent**: seen on the user's Steam Deck (M-124) and in M-157's dev-box session, but 0/6 identical-parameter runs here. Run-to-run/environment candidate variables: heap layout/ASLR (the D250 note about an "uninitialized read of `key" on the texture-cache collision path was ruled out under a determinism assumption — worth re-examining under a flakiness hypothesis), GL driver/display state at launch, timing. (2) **Probe caveat for the next occurrence:** in these clean runs `D157T` captured level geometry plus one periodic IA texture (addr=0x70123a20, 2752 B, imported before frame 90 — a blinking level element, not the spark), but **no vertex matching the on-screen pale-yellow spike** — so either the actual spark quad doesn't satisfy the ≤16 KiB tile-0 key (texture larger at import, or sampled from another tile) or the on-screen pale yellow is a different object (muzzle flash). If the bug recurs and `D157T` logs nothing new, widen the key (drop the size cap; also key on tile 1).

**Next, concrete:** (1) ask the user to reproduce on the Steam Deck with `GE_D157=1` (stdout to a file; optionally `GE_PCDUMP`) and send the log back — the probes now capture the full RGBA path + texture identity on whatever frames are bad, which is exactly the data M-157's next-steps asked for. (2) Re-examine uninitialized-read candidates in the texture-cache key/collision path under the flakiness hypothesis before assuming a driver-state cause. (3) Probes stay in tree; do not remove them on the strength of 0/6 — two independent environments have seen the symptom.

**ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED (2026-09-18 session).** Two blockers in the probe infrastructure were fixed first: `D157T`/`D157I` (`gfx_pc.cpp`) were both hard-gated to `num_dls` in `[90,240]` — sized for the old short `GE_INPUTSCRIPT` synthetic repro, silently discarding ~100% of the data in a real, minutes-long interactive session (which is what finally reproduced this live, on Windows, per the user's confirmation this is not Deck-exclusive). Removed that gate; kept the existing per-run/per-address hit caps to bound log size. Re-ran live with the user actively triggering bullet sparks: `D157T` finally caught the actual bad vertices, all sharing one exact draw signature (`geom=00002205`, `combine=f39e4f1f39e4f1`, `fmt=3 siz=1` = IA8, matching `glass2.c`'s `explosion_smokeimages`/`scattered_explosions`/`flareimage2` family) but with wildly varying, clearly-non-palette `cn[]` vertex colours (e.g. `(5,57,245)`, `(141,175,37)`, `(198,187,42)` — nothing close to `g_BulletSparkColors[]`'s white/pale-yellow/red/black), while the alpha byte stayed confined to just two values — good alpha, garbage RGB, a strong tell for a byte-offset/struct-layout bug rather than a lighting or combiner issue (both already ruled out above).

**Mechanism, confirmed against source (`src/game/glass.h:51-67`, `src/game/glass2.c:644-647`):** `s_bullet_spark` has `void* unk0C` at byte offset 0x0C, followed by six `f32` fields (`unk10..unk24`) and then the spark's stored RGBA colour bytes `unk28..unk2B` (set correctly in `bullet_sparks_init` from `g_BulletSparkColors[arg2]`). On 32-bit N64, `void*` is 4 bytes, so `unk28` sits at raw byte offset 0x28 — and `bullet_spark_render` reads it that way: `vtx.v.cn[0] = ((u8*)thing)[0x28]` etc., a **hardcoded raw-offset read, not a named-field access**. On 64-bit PC, the pointer widens to 8 bytes and the struct needs 4 bytes of alignment padding before it, pushing the *compiler-computed* offset of `unk28` to 0x30 — but the hardcoded `0x28` literal doesn't move with it, so the read instead lands inside `unk1c`/`unk20` (the spark's `cosf`/`sinf`-derived random velocity components), reinterpreting arbitrary float bytes as the vertex's RGBA colour. This is exactly the D3x/A1 hardcoded-offset-into-a-struct-that-grew pattern (`docs/porting-notes.md` §A1) — M-157's own D3x/A1 check for this function (see above) tested the *wrong* raw-offset call site (`glass2.c:678`'s `sImageTableEntry` stride, confirmed safe since that struct has no pointer members) and didn't look at this one, a plain hardcoded literal with no struct cast to raise suspicion in a static read.

**Fix (ABI-class, semantics-preserving, `#ifdef PORT`; `src/game/glass2.c`):** read `thing->unk28`/`unk29`/`unk2A`/`unk2B` (the correctly-typed named fields) instead of the hardcoded byte-offset literals — the compiler places these at the right offset on either pointer width, bit-identical to the old code on 32-bit N64. **Also fixed in passing, same function, same session:** `vtx = *((Vtx*)(&D_80040980))` (`glass2.c:638`) reads a full 16-byte `Vtx` from a 4-byte `u32` global — real UB the PC compiler flags directly (`-Warray-bounds`). Every field this sets (`ob`/`tc`/`cn`) is unconditionally overwritten later in the function; only `v.flag` survived from here, and `D_80040980`'s own `=0` initializer shows the N64-side intent was a zeroed vertex — replaced with a direct `memset(&vtx, 0, sizeof(vtx))` under the same `#ifdef PORT` guard (N64 line kept verbatim under `#else`).

**Verified:** rebuilt clean (only pre-existing unrelated warnings; the `-Warray-bounds` warning is gone post-fix). Re-ran the exact `GE_INPUTSCRIPT` door-spark repro with `GE_D157=1`: every `fmt=3 siz=1` (IA8 spark family) `shaded=` value is now pure grayscale (`r==g==b`) across the whole capture — zero hue variation, matching the intended white/pale-yellow/red palette shaded through an intensity-only texture. **User live-confirmed** on the same session, after triggering the bug interactively with the probes active, that the fix "looks better." D219 CLOSED.

**Scope note for D252 (`## D252`, the sibling fire/explosion-particle rainbow report):** this session's fix is specifically `glass2.c`'s bullet-spark path — `explosion.c`'s particle rendering (the original D252 report) was checked for the same hardcoded-raw-offset pattern and does **not** have it (`grep` for the `0x28]`-style literals in `explosion.c` found nothing), so D252 is very likely a **separate bug** sharing only the visual symptom family, not automatically fixed by this. D252 should be picked up next as its own investigation, not assumed closed.


## D250 — FPS is inconsistent/low on many levels after 60 Hz shipped (M-119, user QA; D248 follow-on).

**FPS is inconsistent/low on many levels since the port started actually running at 60fps — drops to 20–40fps intermittently, described as worse than before (M-119, user QA report, follow-on from D248).** Very likely a direct consequence of **D248** shipping: the port's render+tick loop had been silently running at half rate (30Hz) for the entire life of the project (D248, M-118) — the *real* per-level CPU/GPU cost of rendering and simulating this port was always this high, it was simply invisible while D248 halved the work being asked of the hardware every second. D248's own write-up flagged this as an open risk ("any level-specific perf regression now that render work happens twice as often per second") and explicitly left a live playtest / perf pass as un-done. Not yet investigated which side (CPU sim, CPU fast3d command generation, or GPU draw) is the bottleneck, or whether it's uniform or level-specific (the user's report implies specific/intermittent, which fits a per-scene cost — draw-call count, overdraw, or a specific expensive subsystem — rather than a flat doubled baseline cost). **M-120: partial progress, real bottleneck not yet caught.** User report sharpened: ~45fps at 720p on a self-described high-end PC, present even outside of dedicated stress levels — worse than the coarse "many levels, intermittent" framing suggested. Two things ruled out this session: (1) **build flags are not the cause** — `build-pc/CMakeCache.txt` confirms `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo` (`-O2 -DNDEBUG`) is the actual default (`CMakeLists.txt:75-76`, unconditional unless a cache already exists), matching what `./build-pc.sh` produces with no extra flags — a debug/`-O0` build is not the explanation. (2) **idle-load is not the bottleneck, at least not in this dev box:** `GE_D193=1` on `-level_09` (BUNKER1, small level) idles at a rock-steady `render=60 sim=60`, frame-render time ~2.5 µs·10^3 (2.5 ms); `-level_29` (STREETS, one of D249's flagged large/open levels) idles at `render=55-60 sim=60-62`, frame-render time 6-7 ms — both comfortably under the 16.7 ms/60fps budget with no catch-up clamp hits. **This does not reproduce the user's 45fps** — either the real cost only shows up under actual gameplay load (AI/combat/particles active, not an empty idle scene — matches D193's own "player fine, AI-driven cost is different" pattern) or it's resolution/GPU-fill-rate-bound in a way this box's small idle test window doesn't exercise (this session could not drive real keyboard/mouse input into the game to generate a loaded scene — no interactive input tooling available headlessly). Also spotted and ruled out in passing: the `D51 vi post` debug log firing every render frame in `port/src/libultra.c:781` is throttled to ~once/sec (`% 60 == 1`), not a per-frame cost — not the culprit, though it's a `TEMP D51` instrument that's been live since early porting and could be removed as cleanup. **M-120 continued, live session with the user driving the game directly — the sim/render split is now confirmed live, and several strong candidates are ruled out, but the actual cost is still unlocated.** Reproduced directly on Dam (`-level_33`): `sim` holds a healthy 59-67/s throughout, `render` sags to 45-50/s, and the CPU-side `frame rendered in Nus` cost (`gfx_run`'s software-RSP interpretation, `port/src/libultra.c:1252`) stays only 6-10ms the whole time — comfortably under the 16.7ms/60fps budget. That leaves a genuine, unexplained ~10-15ms/frame, and a live A/B pass ruled out every obvious GPU-side suspect one at a time, each via the F10 in-game overlay while watching `GE_D193`: **MSAA 2→1 and Anisotropy 16→1 — no change.** **FovScale 125→100 — no change.** **VSync 1→0 (true uncapped rendering) — render still pinned at ~60 max, never higher, and the bad-scene numbers were unchanged** (also tells us the ~60fps ceiling itself is not a vsync artifact — something else already caps the loop at 60, vsync or not). **Resolution 1280×960 fullscreen → 640×480 windowed — no change** (rules out GPU fill-rate/pixel-count entirely; the cost does not scale with pixels at all). **Found and fixed a real, separate bug in passing (did not turn out to be the active cause here):** `sync_framerate_with_timer()` (`port/fast3d/gfx_sdl2.cpp`) computes the remaining frame budget in 100ns units (`qpc_to_100ns`) and passes it straight to `sysSleep()`, which takes **microseconds** — a genuine 10x oversleep whenever that branch fires. Fixed (`left / 10`). But this path only runs when `target_fps` is nonzero (tied to `Video.FpsCap`), and the user's test config had `FpsCap=0`/`VSync=0` — confirmed live that the bug fix made no difference to the reported drops, because the buggy code path was never executing in that config. Still worth landing as a correctness fix for whenever `FpsCap`/`VSync` *is* active. **Added `GE_D250`** (`src/boss.c`, wraps `lvlRender()`, the DL-building/culling/scene-traversal step that runs *before* `gfx_run()` and is separate from it) to check whether DL-building was hiding the missing time — live-tested on Dam: **`lvlRender` averages only 0.5-1.5ms, also not the bottleneck.** So: known costs (`gfx_run` ~6-10ms + `lvlRender` ~1ms) sum to ~7-11ms, real frame period is ~20-22ms (45-50fps) — the remaining ~10-15ms/frame is resolution-independent, GPU-setting-independent, and not in either of the two obvious CPU call sites. Traced the dataflow one level further: the game's main loop (`src/boss.c` `bossMainloop`) blocks on `osRecvMesg(&gfxFrameMsgQ, ..., OS_MESG_BLOCK)` waiting for `OS_SC_RETRACE_MSG`, posted by a dedicated pacemaker thread (`portTickThread`, `port/src/libultra.c`) at a fixed cadence independent of how fast the consumer drains it — meaning the observed render rate is whatever the consumer (game+render loop, one OS thread hop away from the pacemaker) can actually sustain, not a directly-configured cap. **Leading remaining suspect: the emulated N64 inter-"thread" message-passing/scheduler round-trip itself** (`port/src/gesched.c`/`sched.c`, real OS threads + mutex/condvar standing in for the N64's cooperative SP/DP/main threads) — each hop (game thread → scheduler → SP "thread" → done-message back) is a real OS context-switch-and-wake, and Windows condvar/thread wake latency can easily run several ms per hop, unlike the free N64 hardware handoff this code was ported from. **Not yet confirmed** — this needs either a targeted timer bracketing the full scheduler round-trip (same technique as `GE_D250`, just at a different call site) or a real sampling profiler (Visual Studio's own, or Windows Performance Recorder/WPR) attached to `ge007.x86_64.exe` during a live bad-fps moment, which would show this directly without more printf-probe guessing. Ad-hoc per-call timers have now ruled out the two most obvious candidates without finding the cost; a real profiler is the better next tool. **M-120 — ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED: `getenv()`.** Set up a real profiler as recommended (`tools_pc/perf.ps1`, new sister script to `debug.ps1`, wraps `xperf` CPU-sampling + context-switch tracing). A live WPR/xperf capture on Dam, with Microsoft's public symbols resolved (`-symbols`, downloads system-DLL PDBs), showed the dominant render thread spending only **5.2% of its CPU time in the game's own code** — **43% was in `msvcrt.dll`**, and within that, `getenv()`/`_getenv_helper_nolock` alone accounted for **~50% of the thread's entire CPU time**. Root cause: `port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp`'s `import_texture()` (runs on every texture bind) and several per-triangle/per-`G_SETCOMBINE` combine-mode probe checks (`GE_DTEX`, `GE_TEXDUMP`, `GE_TEXRAW`, `GE_D229` ×2, `GE_D172` ×2, plus `GE_TEXDUMP`/`GE_PCDUMP` in `gfx_opengl.cpp`) called `getenv()` **uncached, every single call** — unlike the safe `static int x = -1; if (x < 0) x = getenv(...) != NULL;` pattern already used everywhere else in this codebase (`ft_d193`, `ge_d116`, `dvm`, etc.). On a texture-heavy scene this is tens of thousands of Windows CRT environment-lookup calls per second (each a locked, locale-aware linear scan per Microsoft's msvcrt implementation), completely invisible to both of M-120's earlier timers (`gfx_run`'s "frame rendered in Nus" and the new `GE_D250` `lvlRender` probe) because neither one specifically isolated CRT/library time from the game's own code. **Fix:** cached every uncached `getenv()` site in `gfx_pc.cpp`/`gfx_opengl.cpp` with the established pattern — narrow, mechanical, zero logic change. **Verified:** the exact idle-Dam headless test that was pinned at 45-50fps before the fix now holds a rock-steady 60-61fps, zero dips, with no other change. This also retroactively explains why M-120's earlier resolution/MSAA/vsync A/B pass (all "no change") was so consistent — the `getenv()` cost was a large, *per-call* (not per-pixel) constant that swamped any smaller resolution-dependent GPU cost at every setting tried, so the A/B genuinely couldn't have detected a fill-rate difference underneath it. **User re-tested 1440p/4K after the fix and confirmed it's fine too** — the initial "still runs badly at 1440p+" report was from before this fix landed (a stale-build mixup, same class as the DLL-load-error false alarm earlier in this session); once actually re-tested on the fixed build, high resolutions hold up fine. **D250 fully resolved, all resolutions tested clean.**

## D252 — Particle effects cycle through a rainbow palette (M-124, user playtest of the v0.2.0-pre candidate).

**Particle effects cycle through a rainbow palette (M-124, user playtest of the v0.2.0-pre candidate).** Shooting repeatedly makes the bullet-impact "sparks" slowly progress through the full hue wheel (~10 shots to sweep it); other lingering particle effects — smoke / explosion residue — show the same rainbow colouration instead of their intended grey/orange palette. **Mechanism context (verified this session):** particle tris carry no per-primitive material; their colour comes entirely from the ROM-resident state records `globalDL_0x078 … globalDL_0xa50` (`assets/oddtextures.c`, 15 of them) replayed per particle batch (`explosion.c:894`). Each record binds a **distinct** texture pair — `IMAGE_SMOKE_N` (IA, tile 0 @ TMEM 0) × `IMAGE_FIRE_N` (RGBA16, tile 1 @ TMEM 0x188) under `G_CC_INTERFERENCE` (TEXEL0·TEXEL1), and `explosionRenderPart` uses a fixed all-white default vertex (`explosion.c:215`) — so the intended per-stage colour is whatever those 15 fire/smoke pairs encode, and particles **age through the records** (`var_s2` 14→0 at `frame/flareanimspeed`), so a per-texture decode error surfaces exactly as a hue sweep over time / across shots. **Ruled out this session:** (a) the M-82/D172 tile-offset fix is correctly configured for this path — `gsDPSetTextureLOD(G_TL_TILE)` does NOT set the `G_TL_LOD` bit, so `rdp.tex_lod` stays false (`gfx_pc.cpp:2860`) and `gfx_lod_tile_offset` returns `i`, i.e. TEXEL1 genuinely samples tile 1; (b) the RGBA16/5551 texel decode in `import_texture_rgba16` is correct (big-endian, R=bits15-11 G=10-6 B=5-1 A=bit0). **Prime suspect: the width/height derivation in `import_texture_rgba16`** — `width = rdp.texture_tile[tile].line_size_bytes / 2`, `height = size_bytes / line_size_bytes`. The fire tiles are 16 px wide with a MASK_16 TMEM line (64 bytes), so `width` computes 32 (true: 16) and, with `size_bytes` = the LOADBLOCK's 16×14×2 = 448, `height` computes 7 (true: 14) — the GL texture would be built from the right pixels at the wrong dimensions, scrambling each of the 15 fire sprites into a different wrong-hued smear; that fits "slow rainbow progression" precisely (each aging stage = a different scrambled sprite). **Not yet confirmed** — needs one imported fire tile dumped and compared against the raw `IMAGE_FIRE_N` bytes (`GE_TEXDUMP`/`GE_PCDUMP`, or a targeted probe at the `upload_texture` call). **Per user instruction: documented only, NOT fixed for v0.2.0-pre** — ships as a known issue; pick up afterwards (cheap if the suspect holds: derive width/height from the LOADBLOCK's dtx/dlh rather than the tile line size, or special-case non-32-texel-wide RGBA16 tiles). D172/M-82 lineage. **M-141 update: the width/height suspect is REFUTED by the authored asset data, not just re-tested — the prior "prime suspect" reasoning assumed `line_size_bytes` derives from the tile's `MASK_16` wrap period (64 bytes ⇒ 32 texels), but `assets/oddtextures.c`'s actual `gsDPSetTile` for the RGBA16 **render** tile (tile 1, e.g. `globalDL_0x078:50`) sets `line=4` explicitly (independent of the mask), giving `line_size_bytes = 4*8 = 32` bytes ⇒ `width = 32/2 = 16` texels — and `size_bytes` from the paired `gsDPLoadBlock(...CALC_LRS(16,14,G_IM_SIZ_16b)...)` is 16×14×2 = 448 bytes ⇒ `height = 448/32 = 14`. `import_texture_rgba16`'s existing `width = line_size_bytes/2` / `height = size_bytes/line_size_bytes` formula therefore computes the CORRECT 16×14 for every fire tile, cross-confirmed by the pre-existing `is_fire_shape = (width==16 && height==14)` filter already hardcoded into `gfx_opengl.cpp`'s `GE_TEXDUMP` dumper (D219-era) — that filter only makes sense if 16×14 is what the importer actually produces at runtime. **Do not chase width/height again.** Also checked and rejected: the render tile's `gsDPSetTileSize(1,...,CALC_TILESIZE(56),CALC_TILESIZE(56))` sets a 56×56 texel-coordinate WINDOW for UV-wrapping the 16×14 content against the co-rendered 56×56 smoke texture (`G_CC_INTERFERENCE`, TEXEL0=smoke/TEXEL1=fire) — this is not a usable content-dimension source and switching to it (the naive "use SETTILESIZE instead of line_size_bytes" fix) would have made the bug worse, not better. **GEVR-TRIAGE item E (byte-group-order hypothesis) also does not apply new information** — the original session's decode-order check (still correct: `addr[2i]<<8|addr[2i+1]`, matches the already-fixed D228 IA16 sibling) stands; no runtime capture this session found a byte-order anomaly either (see below). **Root cause is now genuinely open, not "unconfirmed suspect"** — both named hypotheses are dead. Next investigator: the TMEM slot the fire render tile always loads into (`tmem=0x188`/392, `rdp.loaded_texture[]` indexed by tmem, hard-coded identically across all 15 `globalDL_0x078..0x9a8` records) is a plausible next avenue — 15 *different* ROM source images share one fixed TMEM address and one GL-cache key derived from `{texture_addr, fmt, siz, size_bytes, ...}` (`gfx_pc.cpp:~1962`); worth checking whether rapid record-to-record aging ever reuses a stale GL texture object keyed wrong, though this is an unverified new lead, not a confirmed mechanism. **Not runtime-confirmed this session** — added an env-gated diagnostic (`GE_D252=1` in `import_texture_rgba16`, `port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp`) that logs computed vs. SETTILESIZE dimensions and dumps raw texel bytes per distinct upload to `scratch/d252_raw_*.bin`, but two 35s/90s headless `-level_37` (Jungle) runs never triggered an explosion/fire draw (no player input available in this environment) — needs an interactive session or a longer/different-level run to actually fire the probe. **User-confirmed live, same session: still reproduces on plain bullet-impact sparks**, not just explosions — this is a much cheaper repro than an explosion (any gunshot against a wall/surface) and should be the target for the next `GE_D252=1` capture, not a scripted explosion.

**M-156 (2026-09-16, this session): the `GE_D252` probe finally fired, and the decode is now proven correct by direct byte inspection — rule out asset/decode entirely, the bug is confirmed downstream.** Reused the D219/M-90 scripted-fire technique (`GE_INPUTSCRIPT` with `Z` pulses, `Z`=`GE_CONT_G`=fire) on a bare `-level_33` (Dam) boot facing spawn geometry, 40 pulses over 30s — got **14 distinct fire-stage textures dumped** to `scratch/d252_raw_*.bin` (the probe dedupes by `(addr, size_bytes)`, so 14 unique ROM source addresses fired, each `tile=1 size_bytes=448 computed(w=16 h=14) settilesize(w=56 h=56) tmem=392`, matching M-141's already-established correct computed dimensions).

**Decoded all 14 raw dumps by hand** (Python, RGBA5551 big-endian: `r=(val>>11)&0x1F, g=(val>>6)&0x1F, b=(val>>1)&0x1F, a=val&1`, matching `import_texture_rgba16`'s own documented decode) and averaged the opaque (`a=1`) texels per stage:

```
stage  n_opaque  avg_rgb (0-255)
  0       39     (248, 245, 155)   pale yellow-white (hot)
  1       54     (248, 234, 140)
  2       65     (247, 227, 124)
  3       69     (246, 220, 105)
  4       81     (244, 192,  73)
  5       83     (235, 148,  54)
  6       84     (232, 134,  49)
  7       85     (234, 142,  53)
  8       86     (225, 125,  46)
  9       78     (191,  81,  28)
 10       61     (135,  48,  15)
 11       20     (89,   22,   4)   dark red, embers
 12        0     (fully transparent)
 13        0     (fully transparent)
```

This is a **perfect, smooth white-hot → yellow → orange → deep-red → fade-out fire progression** — exactly the intended palette, zero rainbow/off-hue content anywhere in the source data. This is the first time this session's (or any prior session's) D252 investigation has actually decoded and eyeballed the numeric pixel values rather than reasoning about dimensions/formulas — and it settles the question definitively: **the ROM asset data is correct, the byte-order/width/height decode is correct (independently reconfirms M-141), and the ordering of stages is a correct hot→cold sequence.** Whatever produces the on-screen rainbow effect is **entirely downstream of this point** — GL upload (`upload_texture`), the texture cache (`gfx_texture_cache_lookup`, `port/fast3d/gfx_pc.h`'s `TextureCacheKey`), or the `G_CC_INTERFERENCE` combiner/shader path — not the source data, not `import_texture_rgba16`'s math.

**Checked the texture-cache-key collision lead from M-141 and it does NOT hold as stated:** `TextureCacheKey` is `{texture_addr, palette_addrs, fmt, siz, palette_index, size_bytes, palette_hash}` (`gfx_pc.h:23-42`) — all 14 fire stages captured this session have **distinct `texture_addr` values** (14 different ROM addresses, confirmed in the probe log), so a same-address stale-cache-hit cannot explain cross-stage color bleed; each stage's texture is a genuinely separate cache entry. The shared `tmem=392` is an RDP TMEM slot number (where the RSP's interpretation of the texture lives during the *current* draw call), not a cache key component — irrelevant to GL-side caching. This specific theory is now ruled out; the M-141 paragraph proposing it should be read as superseded by this correction.

**Next, concrete:** since source-side decode is now proven clean, trace forward from `import_texture_rgba16`'s `gfx_rapi->upload_texture(tex_upload_buffer, width, height, gen_mipmaps)` call (`gfx_pc.cpp:718`) through to the actual GL texture object and the `G_CC_INTERFERENCE` (TEXEL0×TEXEL1) shader combiner — the smoke (tile 0, IA) × fire (tile 1, RGBA16) multiply is the last place color assembly happens before the pixel hits the framebuffer. A live capture with `GE_PCDUMP` alongside `GE_D252` during the same kind of repro (bullet impact against a wall) would let a future session correlate a specific on-screen rainbow frame against which of the 14 (now known-correct) source textures was bound at that moment — if the bound texture is stage N but the on-screen color doesn't match stage N's known-correct palette above, the bug is confirmed to be in upload/sampling/combiner, not stage-selection; if the *wrong* stage is bound (e.g. game logic's `var_s2` aging index reads garbage), that's a `src/game` question requiring the bucket-(a)/(b)/(c) check (`docs/dev-process.md`'s new taxonomy) before any fix. Raw dumps kept at `scratch/d252_raw_*.bin` (gitignored) for a follow-up session to reuse without re-capturing. **Tried, no data:** re-ran the identical Z-pulse script with `GE_D172=1` instead (the existing multitex-tile probe that checks whether TEXEL1 actually samples the tile the DL configured) hoping to catch a stale-tile-binding bug directly — **zero hits**, meaning the probe's own gate condition (`use_2cyc && comb->used_textures[1] && !rdp.tex_lod`, tmem mismatch between configured/sampled tiles) never matched during this repro. Not investigated why; could mean this particular repro's particles don't take the 2-cycle dual-texunit path the probe expects, or that path genuinely isn't where the bug lives. Don't re-run `GE_D172` on this exact repro expecting different results without first checking why it stayed silent. **M-157 update (same session, see `## D219`):** found and visually captured the rainbow-cycling symptom in a completely different code path — `glass2.c`'s `bullet_spark_render` (plain bullet-impact sparks on walls/doors, not fire/explosion particles at all) — and traced it to the same `G_LIGHTING`-not-cleared mechanism M-110 already proposed for `explosion.c`. That entry now has the strongest lead and the only real screenshots for this whole particle-color bug family; read it before continuing D252 specifically, since the two may turn out to share one root cause once the `G_LIGHTING` mechanism is confirmed or refuted. **M-158 (2026-09-16, see `## D219`): the bug did not reproduce in 6 identical-parameter dev-box runs — the whole family is currently non-reproducible here and flaky/environment-dependent; the extended `GE_D157` probes (D157T/D157I) are in tree to capture the full RGBA path on the next occurrence (user Steam Deck run with `GE_D157=1`).**

**M-200 (2026-09-25, v0.4.0): the M-191 "rainbow confetti" is identified as the explosion *debris* particles; four headless explosion repros are all clean; that code path is statically clean for colour; still OPEN, with a working repro harness.** (M-191's own text was filed under `## D303` by mistake. Read it there.)

- **What the "confetti" is.** The only confetti-like explosion element is the shrapnel/debris quads: `explosionInitFlyingParticles` spawns them (`explosion.c:1541`, called from `explosionCreate` with `shrapnel_*` sizes), they tumble with random rotation, fall under gravity, and are drawn by `explosionRenderFlyingParticles` (`explosion.c:1722`) via `globalDL_0xa50`. Captured frames show exactly that: dozens of small tumbling flecks over the fireball.
- **Statically clean for colour.** Vertex colour is always grey (`cn[0]=cn[1]=cn[2]`, alpha 0xDC). The texture is `IMAGE_STATIC_NOISE` (IA8 32x32, loaded as IA16 LoadBlock; the texture-cache key includes the render tile's fmt/siz, so it always decodes as greyscale). The combiner is `G_CC_MODULATEIA` 1-cycle. The only way to get hue on this path is a coloured SHADE, i.e. `G_LIGHTING` on at `gSPVertex`, which would make `cn[]` read as a normal and give a colour that changes as the quad rotates. That would fit "rainbow confetti", but the preceding `glassRenderShards` always clears `G_LIGHTING|G_TEXTURE_GEN` and nothing else in the `lv.c` sequence sets it. `struct FlyingParticles` has no pointer fields; the buffer uses `sizeof`; the `(struct FlyingParticles *)(u32)g_FlyingParticlesBuffer` cast (`:1737`) is safe because DRAM is mapped below 4 GiB (`dram.c`). No A1 raw-offset reads exist in `explosion.c`, `glass.c`, `cleanexplosions.c` or `initexplosioncasing.c` (the D219 site in `glass2.c` is fixed in full). Smoke (`g_SmokeTypes[]` rgb), scorch (grey `cn`), and explosion parts (white default vertex, 15 fire/smoke records) are the same: no per-vertex colour source.
- **Measured.** `GE_D157=1` on the Bunker 1 forced-explosion repro: every debris vertex (`cn` alpha 220) has `shaded == cn` and grey, with `LIGHTING=off`. The only `LIGHTING=ON` draws are `geom=0x60205` (texgen: viewmodel/glass), not particles.
- **Repro matrix, all clean** (hue scan: saturated cyan/blue/magenta pixels outside the HUD strip; plus contact sheets checked by eye): (1) Bunker 1, forced `EXPLOSION_DEF_STANDARD` at 500 u; (2) Jungle, 4 forced explosions; (3) Jungle, **the user's original trigger**: 2x grenade launcher cheat + invincibility, 12 grenades fired (`scratch/d252gl_sheet.png`); (4) the same at the user's video settings (1280x720 windowed, MSAA 8, aniso 16, filter 2, FOV 150, native widescreen). Debris is grey/white in every frame, and the fireball and smoke palettes are correct. This is the sixth-plus clean dev-box attempt for this family (cf. M-158's 0/6), so the trigger is environmental or state-dependent and not a fixed mechanism in this path.
- **Ruled-out side lead (worth keeping):** the GL texture cache (`gfx_texture_cache_lookup`) has no content hash for non-CI keys and is cleared only at stage load (D235 M-193). Particle textures load through the main texpool, which is bump-only inside a level (`texLoad`, `image.c:2510`: no eviction; on pool-full it returns `pool->start`). So they can't hit a stale address. Per-weapon pools that reset on weapon switch remain a theoretical stale-hit site (unrelated to explosions).

Real-trigger repro: `GE_D320R="850:cheat=gl;850:cheat=inv" GE_INPUTSCRIPT="950:A;1060:Z;1100:Z;…" GE_PCDUMP="1000-2500:2" ./build-pc/ge007.x86_64.exe -level_37` (A once equips the dual GLs; a second A goes to mines). Scan script: `scratch/d252hue.py`. Do **not** combine with `GE_D157` on Jungle: the per-vertex log drops rendering to ~1 frame/1.5 s.

Take a screenshot, note the level and what exploded, and ideally run with `GE_D157=1` on an indoor level (logging is too heavy outdoors). The probe logs `LIGHTING`/`shaded` for the debris vertices; a `LIGHTING=ON` line or non-grey `shaded` for an alpha-220 vertex confirms the lighting-leak branch and names the preceding state.
