**Status: OPEN (PARTIAL) — unchanged; not reproducible headless across 4 configurations including the user's own trigger; debris-particle path statically clean for colour.**

**M-201 (2026-09-26, v0.4.0): ROOT CAUSE FOUND + FIXED — port-side, `port/src/gimgfixup.c` (the D68 shim). Explosion display lists kept the *first stage's* (title screen's) texture pointers for the rest of the session.**

- **User trigger that cracked it:** Facility explosions are fine at first and go rainbow for *every* weapon once the player reaches the middle (by the lockers), and stay broken. So it is state-dependent, not per-explosion-type (the tank = `EXPLOSION_MEDIUM` vs grenade `EXPLOSION_DEF_STANDARD` split was a red herring).
- **Refuted on the way:** stage texpool exhaustion. `GE_D252POOL` (TEMP, `image.c` texLoad) logged 0 pool-full events; Facility's 650 KB pool is 85% full at spawn and still had ≥61 KB free at the lockers.
- **Evidence:** the F12 burst capture (`GE_D157`) showed the debris/smoke/fire textures being read from `0x700ae2e8…0x700bb5d8`, while Facility's texpool was `[0x70102ae0..)`. `0x700ae2e8` is exactly the *title stage's* texpool start + the 8-byte texnum header. The debris quad state itself was clean (grey `cn`, LIGHTING off, MODULATEIA, IA8), so the colour came from the texture bytes.
- **Mechanism:** `texReset()` (`image_bank.c`, called from `lv.c` on **every** stage load, after `set_mt_tex_alloc()`) re-copies the global image table from ROM and `texLoadFromDisplayList()` resolves the `globalDL_0x078…0xa50` IMAGESEG words into the new stage's pool. On N64 those ROM-copy DLs are what executes. On PC `explosion.c` executes the *compiled* shadows (`g_ExplosionDisplayLists[]`), and `gimgSyncCompiledGlobalDLs()` copied resolved words into them **only for slots still holding the `0xABCDxxxx` marker**, i.e. only on the first call (the title stage). Every later stage kept pointers into the title's freed pool region. That memory is reused by the new stage's own allocations, so explosions look right until the stage overwrites it (Facility: rooms streamed in around the lockers), then every smoke/fire/debris texture samples garbage.
- **Why ~10 headless repros were clean:** `-level_XX` boots straight into the level (its own first stage, so its pointers are correct), and even a harnessed `level → title → level` reload lands both pools at the same address with the same load order, so stale pointers hit identical bytes. Only a real boot → title → level sequence moves the pool.
- **Fix:** learn which compiled `G_SETTIMG` slots are IMAGESEG references on the first sync (marker still present), store them in `s_imgslot[][]`, and re-copy those slots on every call. Semantics now match N64 (fresh pointers per stage). Port-only; no game code touched.
- **Verified:** user playtest, boot → title → Facility → past the lockers, grenades/mines/tanks all correct ("yeah that fixed it"). `D252SYNC` (TEMP, `GE_D252POOL`) logged `32 texture slots re-synced, 32 changed` at the Facility load, i.e. all 32 were stale before the fix. Golden gate 3/3.
- **Scope:** covers every D252-family report that goes through these 17 global DLs (explosion parts, smoke, debris; `globalDL_0x000` too). The M-124/M-157 bullet-impact spark sightings are likely the same stale-pointer effect but were not separately re-tested.
- **TEMP probes to remove when the release settles:** `GE_D252POOL` (`image.c`, `initmttex.c`, `D252SYNC` in `gimgfixup.c`); `GE_D157` F12 burst (`gfx_pc.cpp`, `video.c`); `GE_D320R explode=/cheat=`.

**Status: FIXED (M-201, user-verified 2026-09-26).**

## D255 — Facility firefight SIGSEGV on Steam Deck (v0.2.0-pre CI bundle; D253 fix confirmed working).

**Facility firefight SIGSEGV on Steam Deck (v0.2.0-pre CI bundle, D253 fix confirmed working — user got past the opening crouch tile).** Crash during gunplay; abort-unwind backtrace points at `sub_GAME_7F09BAC4` (`vtxstore.c:158`) ← `sub_GAME_7F09BBBC` (`:220`) ← `lvlManageMpGame` (`lv.c:1302`) ← `bossMainloop` (`boss.c:567`). Disassembling the exact CI binary at the fault PC (`0x200db135`) gives `mov 0x14(%rax),%edi; mov 0x10(%rdi),%rax`: the function walks the active PropRecord list keeping `type == 1` — which is **PROP_TYPE_OBJ, not CHR** (the decompiler cast to the union's first member and misnamed the field `ChrRecord.chrflags`; it is actually `ObjectRecord.model` at `0x14`) — then dereferences `model->obj`. Two port-relevant wrinkles: (a) the load is **32-bit zero-extended** because the decomp types the field through the `CHRFLAG` enum, so a model pointer ≥ 4 GB would truncate to garbage; (b) the loop skips records whose `model->obj` is NULL but *dereferences* `model` unconditionally, so an active object with a NULL/freed `model` faults — plausible in a firefight where destructibles (crates etc.) die. Not reproduced on WSL after equivalent play. **Register capture (D254 format, 2026-09-13):** two more Deck crashes — Bunker mid-firefight, then Frigate with ~3 NPCs alive; log: `SIGNAL: 11 / FAULT ADDR: 0x10 / Rax=0x701e5f54 Rdi=(nil) / PC 0x200db135`. `Rdi` = the record's model value = **exactly NULL** → case (b) confirmed: an active PROP_TYPE_OBJ record with a NULL `model`, dereferenced by the unconditional `mov 0x10(%rdi),%rax`; truncation (a) and stale/garbage pointers are ruled out. Faulting PC matches the recorded disassembly (`sub_GAME_7F09BAC4` = `vtxstore_fix_refs`). Grep-verified: nothing in game code ever writes NULL into `ObjectRecord.model` — `clear_model_obj()` nulls `model->obj` only, and `objInit`/spawn paths only activate a record once model ≠ NULL — so the NULL comes from either a fresh/uninitialized record slot being activated or a destroy-path ordering race (model freed/nulled while the record is still active this tick). **Fix constraint:** any guard lands in game code (`vtxstore.c`) → needs rule-#2 sign-off; `port/` cannot intercept this dereference. Next: (1) decision on whether a NULL-model skip in `vtxstore_fix_refs` qualifies as an ABI-class exception (semantics-preserving defensive guard, PD analogue check); (2) if yes, add it plus a `#ifdef PORT` trace at the deactivation/model-free sites to name the path that leaves the record model-less. **Corrected, deterministic repro (v0.2.1 user testing, 2026-09-15, superseding the initial report): the trigger is Facility's computer terminals — the ones you ACTIVATE (interact with, not shoot/destroy) to open a door for level progression.** User confirms this is consistent/reliably reproducible on those specific terminals, on Steam Deck **and** Linux generally (not Deck-hardware-specific). This is a much stronger lead than the original "sometimes during firefights" — a terminal activation deactivating/freeing its associated object model while the record briefly stays active this tick is fully consistent with the destroy-path-ordering theory above, just via a scripted trigger instead of combat destruction, and gives a deterministic repro instead of a probabilistic one. **Next session should reproduce via terminal activation specifically**, not generic combat — much cheaper to instrument. **M-140: added a diagnostic probe (`GE_D255`, off by default, `#ifdef PORT`) — `vtxstore.c`'s `sub_GAME_7F09BAC4` now skips-and-logs instead of dereferencing when it finds a NULL model on an active OBJ record (identity + state fields), and `propobj.c`'s `objFree` logs every free call for correlation. Attempted a live Windows repro this session (5 terminal activations across 3 Facility launches, one direct `-level_34` boot each time): zero probe hits, zero crashes — Windows does not reproduce this, consistent with the existing WSL-negative result. Two negatives (WSL, native Windows) against one positive (Linux/Steam Deck) points at something genuinely platform-specific (allocator/timing), not a Windows-reachable path — don't spend further Windows session time chasing a live repro.** The probes are harmless (env-gated, zero behavior change when unset) and committed so a Linux/Deck session can set `GE_D255=1` and get the trace directly. **User report, 2026-09-15 (same day, later, real Steam Deck hardware on the published v0.2.1 release — unverified by this session, logging as reported, not re-asserting the activation theory as wrong):** Facility crashes **consistently on terminals being destroyed** (shot), not (only) on activation. Frigate crashed once during this same testing pass, specifics not recorded. Shooting terminals elsewhere/other attempts did not reliably reproduce. This is closer to the *original* pre-M-139 framing (combat/destructibles triggering the NULL-model race) than the M-139 "corrected, activation-only" theory — both are plausible triggers of the same underlying destroy-path-ordering race (any code path that frees/nulls an active OBJ record's model mid-tick), not necessarily contradictory. **Not yet reconciled or verified by a session with hands on the repo** — next Linux/Deck session should test both triggers (activation AND destruction-by-gunfire) with `GE_D255=1` set before revising the "reliable repro" framing again. **Reconciled, same day, further real-Deck testing (v0.2.1 published release): destruction is the trigger, not activation — confirmed across four levels.** Facility: **every** terminal crashes consistently when destroyed (not merely activated). Caverns: terminals near the radio objective crash when they explode — same mechanism, different level, rules out a Facility-specific asset/state bug. Archives: a **similar** crash when a guard's grenade detonates — same destroy-via-explosion mechanism, no terminal involved at all, which narrows the real trigger to "an object dying via explosion damage" in general, not anything terminal-specific. **Negative control:** shooting an entire room of terminals on Frigate did not reproduce it — so it isn't simply "any destructible OBJ record exploding" either; something about the specific object/scene state still gates it. Release notes updated to match (`.github/release-notes.md`, D255 bullet: "consistently crash the game when destroyed"). **Static lead for next session (untested, from this session's code read):** `objFree`'s destroy path (`propobj.c:1017-1039`, entered via `RUNTIMEBITFLAG_REMOVE` from explosion damage, `sub_GAME_7F04424C`/`sub_GAME_7F0442DC`) never explicitly nulls `ObjectRecord.model` — `clear_model_obj()` only nulls `model->obj`. The NULL therefore can't come from that assignment; it must come from either (a) `chrpropFree`'s freed slot being reused by `chrpropAllocate` for a *different*, not-yet-`objInit`'d record before `vtxstore_fix_refs`'s later same-frame pass reaches it (a stale-pointer/reuse race, not a field write), or (b) the active-list unlink (`chrpropDelist`) happening while some other code is mid-iteration over the same list (a modify-during-iterate bug) — explosion damage plausibly spawns new effect props (sparks/debris/smoke) in the same tick that immediately reuse the just-freed slot, which would explain why it's tied to *explosions specifically* and not simple destruction. **Next, concrete:** with `GE_D255=1` set (probes already in tree from this session, ship in any build off `release/v0.3.0` including the local Linux package built this session), reproduce on Facility from the Deck itself (Desktop Mode, launch from a terminal, redirect stdout to a file) and send the log back — the probe already logs the dying record's identity plus every `objFree` call, which should show whether the crashing record's `prop`/`obj` pointer address was recently freed-and-reused this same session.

**ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED, same day, live Deck session over SSH (M-140).** The `objFree`/destroy-path-race theory above was a red herring — set up a real Deck test (SSH access, key-based auth, WSL-cross-compiled local Linux build deployed and run live against the user's own prepared ROM assets), reproduced the crash directly, and symbolized it on-device against the build's own debug info. **First capture with the `GE_D255` probe active:** the probe's `ObjectRecord.model == NULL` guard did NOT fire, yet the game crashed anyway at `vtxstore.c:199` (`var_v1->RootNode`), `FAULT ADDR: 0x10`, `Rdi=(nil)` — a *different* pointer than the one the probe was checking. **Actual bug:** `sub_GAME_7F09BAC4` (`vtxstore_fix_refs`) reads the record's `Model*` through `((Model*)((ChrRecord*)prop->chr)->chrflags)` — a union pun onto `ChrRecord.chrflags`, which is typed `CHRFLAG`, a **4-byte enum**. On 32-bit N64 this is bit-exact; on 64-bit PC the cast reads just the pointer's low 32 bits and zero-extends it, discarding the real high bits — the exact D3x pointer-width ABI class. `(nil)` is exactly what that truncation produces whenever the real pointer's low 32 bits happen to be zero, which is what pointed two prior sessions at the wrong (NULL-model/destroy-race) theory. **Proof it was the field, not the object:** reading the same record through the correctly-typed `ObjectRecord.model` field showed it was **always a valid, non-NULL pointer**. **Fix (ABI-class, semantics-preserving, `#ifdef PORT`; `src/game/vtxstore.c`):** read the pointer through `ObjectRecord.model` instead of the mistyped `ChrRecord.chrflags` alias, at both use sites. The earlier `GE_D255` diagnostic guard (which checked the wrong field) is removed as unneeded. **Verified live:** held through the entire Facility level (multiple terminal destructions) and Caverns' radio-objective terminals with zero crashes, on the user's own Steam Deck hardware; Windows rebuild + full 21-level `verify.sh sweep` also clean. The separate audio-thread crash (D285) is untouched by this fix.

**Status (from §F table):** FIXED (M-140) — root-caused as a D3x-class 32-bit pointer truncation (not a destroy-path race) and verified live on real Steam Deck hardware across both confirmed-repro levels (Facility, Caverns).

## D152+ — D152 addendum — static audit + narrow fix (M-31).

**D152 addendum — static audit + narrow fix (M-31).** Audited every `osSetIntMask(OS_IM_NONE)` in the *compiled* audio code (`event.c` `alEvtqNextEvent`/`alEvtqPostEvent`/`alEvtqFlush`/`alEvtqFlushType`, `csplayer.c` `__CSPRepostEvent`, `synaddplayer.c` `alSynAddPlayer`, `snd.c` `sndRemoveEvents`/`sndSetupSound`/`sndDeactivateAllSfxByFlag`): **all balanced on every path** — `alEvtqPostEvent`'s lone early `return` (`event.c:86`, freeList empty) restores the mask first. The §F D152 guess "libaudio has unbalanced early-return mask paths" is **not** borne out. Two real defects found + fixed `#ifdef PORT` (N64 verbatim `#else`): **(1)** `sndSetSfxSlotVolume` (`snd.c`) walks the live `ALSoundState` list and posts `AL_SNDP_RELEASE_EVT` to the shared `ALEventQueue` **without holding `OS_IM_NONE`** — unlike its structural twin `sndDeactivateAllSfxByFlag`, which wraps its identical walk. On PC that's an unguarded walk racing `amMain` *and* one lock acquire/release per matching sound; the mission-failed fade (`sndSetScalerApplyVolumeAllSfxSlot`→`sndApplyVolumeAllSfxSlot`→ this, every frame, every active sound) turns it into a per-frame lock-acquire storm on `mainThread` = exactly the §F dump's "hammers the event queue hard enough that the lock is left owned." Fix: hold `OS_IM_NONE` once across the whole walk (nested `alEvtqPostEvent` hits the recursive depth++ fast path, no new contention window); also wrap `sndApplyVolumeAllSfxSlot`'s slot loop so the whole volume update is one recursive hold (1 real acquire/frame instead of `SFX_SLOT_COUNT × active-sounds`). **(2)** The actual leak matches the §F dump's *other* hypothesis — "a transient thread acquired `OS_IM_NONE` and exited" (`gdb.txt` shows `New Thread`/`exited` churn). `port/src/libultra.c` `portThreadWrapper` now calls new `imThreadExitRelease()` after the thread entry returns: if that thread still owns `s_imHeld`, release the orphan immediately (+ `LOG_ERROR` naming it). This removes the wedge *and* the ~2 s steal hitch, and stops the **re-wedge** that occurs when a new host thread reuses the dead thread's pthread id and `imAcquire` mis-detects recursion (`s_imOwner == self`). The M-28 steal-lock stays as the last-resort backstop for a genuinely unbalanced *same-thread* path (none found, but cheap insurance). Build green (240/240); `-level_09` frame 300 renders 91.7% non-clear, crash-free; `-level_20` boots crash-free (frame-count flaky under load per D117/D134, no `D152:` log). Fade-out repro is **playtest-gated** — not reproducible headless, so not end-to-end verified; user should replay the mission-fail and confirm no black screen + no `D152:` steal/orphan log lines.

**Status (from §F table):** FIXED (`src/snd.c`, `port/src/libultra.c`, `#ifdef PORT`). porting-notes.md §D4.

## D233 — All levels (intermittent): indoor level geometry invisible near doors — you can see through walls/floors into rooms you can't see into, while world objects…

**All levels (intermittent): indoor level geometry invisible near doors — you can see through walls/floors into rooms you can't see into, while world objects (terminals, furniture) in that space still draw (M-106, user QA report; screenshots `docs/img/bugs/20260912-cullingbug-bugged.png` vs `-notbugged.png`).** Root-caused M-107 (session-016TaKy6, port/fast3d only): **fast3d's CPU-side "trivial reject" AND-test in `gfx_sp_tri1` (`port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp:1455-1460`) has a latent w-sign bug independent of D222/D106.** The per-vertex outcode bits computed in `gfx_sp_vertex` (`x<-w`/`x>w`/`y<-w`/`y>w`/`z>w`, `gfx_pc.cpp:1372-1386`) are only valid half-space tests when `w>0`; for a vertex that has crossed behind the camera plane (`w<0` — common when the camera is close to large room-structure polygons, e.g. walls/ceiling trusses near a doorway) the comparison sense is flipped, so its outcode can come out wrong. If that spurious bit happens to match the other two (genuinely correct) vertices' bits, `v1->clip_rej & v2->clip_rej & v3->clip_rej` fires and the whole triangle is dropped before it ever reaches OpenGL — even though GL's own homogeneous clipper (which *does* handle `w<0` correctly) would have rendered the visible part of it. Confirmed against the two screenshots: same room/camera/ammo-HUD, one frame is missing the room's ceiling trusses/walls (replaced by flat sky) while the console/terminal props in the same room still draw fully — exactly the "big background polys vanish, small prop models don't" split you'd expect, since large near-camera polygons are far more likely to have a vertex cross behind the eye than small self-contained prop meshes. The backface-cull code 6 lines below (`gfx_pc.cpp:1462-1495`) already special-cases this exact `w<0` hazard for its own cross-product sign (`(v1->w<0)^(v2->w<0)^(v3->w<0)`) — the trivial-reject block above it never got the same treatment. **Independent of D222** (D222 is a game-logic frustum-cull bug in `src/game/fr.c`/`bondview2.c` that only manifests at non-default `Video.FovScale`; this is a GPU-pipeline clip-rejection bug in `port/fast3d/` that fires at any FovScale, including the default 100, whenever the camera gets close to a large polygon — matching the report's "all levels, near doors" framing with no FovScale mentioned). Also independent of D106 (D106 fixed the *game-side* portal-visibility bbox computation for a different z==0 edge case in `bg.c`; this is the *renderer-side* per-triangle clip decision, a different stage of the pipeline entirely) — same neighbourhood/symptom vocabulary ("things vanish near a portal-adjacent boundary"), different bug.

**Status (from §F table):** **FIXED (port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp, `gfx_sp_tri1`) — high confidence on mechanism, UNVERIFIED visually.** Fix: skip the trivial-reject AND-test entirely whenever any of the triangle's 3 vertices has `w<0`, deferring to GL's clipper instead (mirrors the cull code's existing w-sign handling one block below). Change only ever *adds* triangles that were previously dropped — cannot make anything newly invisible, so it's a safe, narrowly-targeted fix with no game-logic touch (fast3d is PC-only code, no N64 build parity to preserve, no `#ifdef PORT` needed). **Build verified green** (`./build-pc.sh` equivalent — MSYS2 mingw64 cmake+ninja, full `ge007.x86_64.exe` link succeeds, only one pre-existing unrelated `-Wformat` warning in the same file). **VISUALLY VERIFIED (M-108):** user played `-level_26` (Frigate — corrected level id, the old `-level_02` note above predates the `bondconstants.h` numbering check) and confirmed the doorway/ship-corridor geometry no longer flickers or vanishes near room boundaries. Closed.

> Earlier triage pass, merged 2026-09-15 (ctx-opt Bucket B): "The geometry-vs-object split localises it to room/portal background visibility or frustum culling in fast3d, not textures/models. Logged in `GRAPHICS-BACKLOG.md`." — status then: FIXED + VISUALLY VERIFIED (M-107 fix, M-108 verify).

Could equally be a per-instance object/prop transform or cull-volume bug in `src/game/propobj.c`/`chrprop.c` (out of this task's `port/fast3d/` scope, and out of the `src/game/*` model/anim exclusion in the brief regardless). **No fix attempted — do not have enough evidence to touch code.**

**Status (from §F table):** **VISUALLY VERIFIED FIXED (M-108) — mechanism still unexplained.** User confirmed on a live Dam playthrough (post-D233 fix, correct `-level_26`/Frigate session's build) that all guard towers along the dam now render, not just the first. No code change was made specifically for D234, and the M-107 investigation's own reasoning argued D233's mechanism doesn't fit this symptom (towers viewed from a distance, not a close-camera w<0 case) — so either that reasoning was wrong, D233's fix had a broader effect than analyzed, or the original symptom was intermittent/state-dependent rather than deterministic. ## D120 — Blood-decal `PointUsage[]` chain — converter now emits it (M-30).

**Blood-decal `PointUsage[]` chain — converter now emits it (M-30).** `d43_emit.py` reserved the opcode-0x18 `PointUsage` region in the layout pass (`add_region(puo, 2*nv)`) but the **emit pass never wrote it** — every entry stayed zero. `chr.c`'s decal walk `index = PointUsage[index]` then cycled 0→PointUsage[0]→0 forever (capped by the `#ifdef PORT` guard at `chr.c:3328`, so decals were missing/wrong rather than a true hang). Fix: `op24_pointusage[puo] = nv` in layout + a byteswap loop (`put_s16(remap(puo)+2k, be16(src, puo+2k))` for `nv` = `numVertices` entries — a negative-terminated `s16` index chain, no remap) in the emit pass. Full regen chain re-run, round-trip validation passes. The `chr.c` guard stays as a safety net (SMALL-FIXES B3).

**Status (from §F table):** FIXED (`tools_pc/d43_emit.py`). Interactive verify pending — blood decals on a BUNKER1 firefight should now appear + no hang.

## D228 — FIXED: `palette_to_rgba32` G_TT_IA16 byte order (fix write-up from the §F row, appended 2026-09-15 ctx-opt)

**FIXED (`port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp`, `palette_to_rgba32`) — a real byte-order bug, not a texpool/decode-never-ran issue as originally guessed.** `GE_TEXDUMP` on Facility (`-level_34`) found ~14% of LOD-textured uploads (fmt=CI, `palette_fmt=G_TT_IA16`) rendering solid near-white; a `GE_D228` correlation probe ruled out the texpool/RC2-clip hypothesis (the decoded size exactly matched the tile's base image every time — the data reaches `import_texture` fine, sized correctly). The actual bug: `palette_to_rgba32`'s `G_TT_IA16` branch read `intensity = palentry & 0xff` (low byte) and `alpha = palentry >> 8` (high byte) — backwards relative to the already-correct direct-IA16 decode two functions above it in the same file (`import_texture_ia16`: `intensity = addr[2*i]` (first/high byte after `gfx_dp_load_tlut`'s `PD_BE16` swap), `alpha = addr[2*i+1]`). A dim, fully-opaque palette entry (e.g. intensity=0x58, alpha=0xff) decoded backwards as bright and mostly-transparent (intensity=0xff, alpha=0x58) — exactly the white-patch symptom, on any CI-format material whose TLUT happens to be IA16 rather than RGBA16 (weapon metal/grip materials commonly are, since IA is a natural fit for grayscale metal with a separate opacity channel). Fix: swap the two lines to match the working convention. **User-verified live:** AK47 and other metallic guns render correctly (no more white patches). Verified crash-free with a `-level_34` headless run before the live check; a full 21-level sweep is still owed (not run this session — the user was using their own game instance concurrently, `verify.sh`/`taskkill` would have killed it). D217 · D161 lineage — same general "CI/LUT format-assumption" bug class, distinct specific bug.

It is called unconditionally — **not gated by `j_text_trigger` or the actual selected language** — from `textRenderGlyph`'s string-draw loop (`src/game/textrelated.c:475-499`) for *any* character byte with the high bit set (`*text >= 0x80`). So any rendered string containing a stray high-bit byte null-derefs immediately, on any region build, regardless of language setting. This is the same general shape as the already-documented `D50.5` "Legal-screen UB exposure" nearby in this file (a read that's harmless-by-luck on N64 hardware, fatal on PC) — a good candidate for the same style of minimal `#ifdef PORT` defensive guard, not a game-logic change.

- **Next steps, in order:** (1) add a temporary `#ifdef PORT` probe at `language.c:319` logging `codepoint`/`i` plus the 8–16 bytes around the source string pointer whenever `g_JpnCacheCacheItems == NULL`, then replay the v0.2.1 repro (or try harder to trigger it on HEAD — a longer soak, or navigating to the specific folder/mission-select row that displays this save's Control Center/Caverns stats, since our 90 s window only proved the *default* landing screen doesn't trigger it) to catch the actual string content live; (2) once the upstream OOB read is identified, the real fix is there, not just a defensive NULL guard in `language.c` (though that guard is also cheap, safe, and worth adding regardless, matching the `D50.5` precedent, since a malformed/third-party-corrupted save should degap gracefully rather than crash even if the deeper cause isn't found yet); (3) do NOT close this finding as "fixed by v0.2.2" — that was this session's own wrong first guess, corrected here.

**M-148 (2026-09-16, independent re-verification session): FULLY ROOT-CAUSED end-to-end; verdict OPEN — the bug is live on `release/v0.3.0` HEAD, reproduced there from scratch. The M-147 "upstream OOB/garbage read" guess is retracted: no OOB exists.** Every claim below was re-derived from primary evidence (crash logs, both binaries under gdb, the user's actual `ge007.eep`, compiled-C CRC reproduction) rather than trusted from prior write-ups.

- **The user's save is NOT corrupted — it is a valid *pre-D284* save.** `fileValidateSaves` (`file2.c:544`) CRCs each slot over `&save->completion_bitflags .. save+1` (slot bytes [8..96), 88 bytes) via `fileGenerateCRC` (`src/game/crc.c`), which runs `randomGetNextFrom` off a **local constant seed `0x8F809F473108B3C1`** — *not* `g_randomSeed`. Reproduced that function in compiled C from both the pre-fix (`git show 0de99b4d^:port/src/random.c`) and current-HEAD `random.c`: **the pre-D284 (v0.2.x-shipped) PRNG reproduces all five stored slot CRCs bit-exact; the fixed PRNG matches zero.** (Pure-Python model `tools_pc/d295_crc.py` — gdb scripts/outputs in `scratch/d295/` — now matches the compiled C exactly — two transcription bugs found and fixed along the way: the seed is updated *in place* by `randomGetNextFrom(&polynormal)` each step, and `a2 = a2 >> 0x1f` / `a3 = a2 >> 0x14` are plain `dsrl`, not the `*32` helpers.) Consequence: on any post-fix build, first launch with this save wipes all five slots (confirmed live, `GE_SAVELOG=1`: every slot `BAD -> RESET (progress wiped)`), so **the reported crash does not reproduce on HEAD with the unmodified artifact — but that is a side effect of the wipe, not a fix.**

- **The crash mechanism (M-147) is confirmed end-to-end and is the whole story; there is no upstream OOB.** `front.c:2616` declares `char difficultytext[4]`; the file-select folder panel does `strcpy(difficultytext, "00 Agent")` (9 bytes incl. NUL) + `strcat("\n")`. gdb on **both** the v0.2.1 artifact and a HEAD debug build confirms the stack layout: `&textpos.p[0] == &difficultytext + 8`, so the `\n` lands on the y-coordinate's low byte and the NUL one past it; the subsequent `textpos.p[0] = floor(folderpos2d.f[1]) + 0x15` store then clobbers `\n` with y. Observed y values across window geometries: **128 and 143 — both ≥ 0x80**, i.e. the fatal case is the *normal* one here. `textRender` (`textrelated.c`, `-funsigned-char`) then scans a byte ≥ 0x80 → JPN glyph path → `langGetJpnCharPixels` (`language.c:320`) dereferences `g_JpnCacheCacheItems`, which is NULL outside Japanese mode on PC. Note: on N64 **non-JP builds this pointer is likewise unallocated** (`langInit` allocates it only when `j_text_trigger`, i.e. JP) — so the crash potential is decomp-native, not a port artifact; the reason it (apparently) never manifested on N64 is that at native geometry `y = floor(folderpos2d.f[1]) + 0x15` presumably stayed < 0x80 (unverified from here), whereas PC window geometry puts y at 128/143 in the observed cases. The overflow itself is decomp-faithful original behavior. `"007"` (4 bytes) and `"Agent"` (6) fit or stop before offset 8 → safe; only `"00 Agent"`/`"Secret Agent"` as a folder's highest completed difficulty reach the fatal byte. (`missiontext[18]` one line above has the same class: `"Mission Cuba.Control Center\n"` is 29 bytes — flagged for review, not separately instrumented.)
- **The M-147 "OOB read of save-derived stat text" guess is retracted — verified against source:** `fileGetSaveStageDifficultyTime` (`file2.c:230`) special-cases `DIFFICULTY_007` *before* any bit math — it returns constant `0x3FF` if `fileIs007ModeUnlocked(folder)` (the slot's `flag_007` bit, or all 20 levels completed on 00 Agent) else 0; the high bit region (offsets 600–790 of a 608-bit `times[]`) is **never read**, and the setter (`fileSetDifficultyStageTime`) excludes 007 (`difficulty < DIFFICULTY_007`), so it's never written either. No OOB, no build-layout sensitivity in the game code. The v0.2.1-vs-HEAD difference was entirely the CRC wipe above: v0.2.1 accepted the save (old PRNG) → folder 1's highest = 00 Agent (`flag_007`=0, 00-Agent 16/20 levels → not 007-unlocked) → `"00 Agent"` rendered → crash; HEAD wiped the save → nothing rendered → no crash.
- **DECISIVE HEAD REPRO (bug is live on v0.3.0):** recomputed the user's five slot CRCs with the *fixed* PRNG (`d295_crc.py`, data-only patch of the artifact — no code probes), placed it in `data/`, ran HEAD unattended 80 s: `GE_SAVELOG` shows all five slots **OK** (progress retained), then `EXCEPTION: 0xc0000005`, `FAULT ADDR: 0x0`, register state byte-identical to the user's v0.2.1 log (`Rax=2 Rcx=0 Rdx=1 Rsi=0xffffffff Rdi=0`); `addr2line` on the HEAD binary → **`langGetJpnCharPixels` at `src/game/language.c:320`**. Repro log saved as `ge007.crash.log.head-repro-M148` in the issue-artifacts folder. `data/ge007.eep` restored to the user's original artifact afterwards (md5 `76e18aa4…`).
- **M-149 (fix landed + verified):** both signed-off items applied and verified on `release/v0.3.0`: (a) `port/src/main.c` seeds `g_JpnCacheCacheItems`/`g_JpnCharCachePixels` from static port buffers before `osStartThread` (exact `langInit` construction, `#include "game/language.h"`, `_Static_assert` on the pixel-stub size; reviewer-caught bugs fixed pre-apply: the `0xC000` bitfield sentinel was wrong — eliminated in favour of field assignment — and a stale `sizeof(jpnItems)==0x100` assert would have hard-failed the build, dropped); (b) `src/game/front.c` widens `difficultytext[4]`→`[32]`, `missiontext[18]`→`[32]` under `#ifdef PORT` (D8 class; N64 build keeps decomp sizes — the decomp author's own comment at front.c:2549-2550 already flagged this buffer as "likely incorrect"). Verification: clean rebuild; **the exact previously-crashing input** (user's save re-stamped with post-fix CRCs via `tools_pc/d295_crc.py`) now runs 80 s unattended with all five slots OK, no crash log — vs the byte-identical register-state NULL deref before the fix; user's original artifact still boots cleanly (takes the D297 wipe path, no crash); 21/21-level `tools_pc/level_sweep.sh` PASS. `data/ge007.eep` restored to the original artifact (md5 `76e18aa4…`) — **note: every game launch rewrites `data/ge007.eep`, so the sweep clobbered the restoration that preceded it; the restore+hash check was re-run after the sweep and again at review time.**
- **Verdict: FIXED (M-149)** for the crash itself; the companion save-wipe regression is tracked separately as **D297** (release-blocker, migration shim pending). History — pre-fix, any v0.3.0 player who completed an 00-Agent (or Secret-Agent) level — their save then validates fine on the post-fix PRNG — would crash at file-select on next launch in any window geometry where the folder y ≥ 0x80 (the common case observed here). Fix plan, **signed off by user 2026-09-16** (both items go; review order: crash-fix bundle first, migration shim separately): (a) *port-side defense-in-depth, rule-2-clean:* seed `g_JpnCacheCacheItems`/`g_JpnCharCachePixels` from static port buffers before `mainproc` starts (non-JP mode only) so a stray high-bit byte takes the normal cache-miss path (romCopy from the JP font segment → garbage glyph) instead of NULL-deref — design validated: `langTick` is `j_text_trigger`-guarded, `langInit` non-JP never touches these, no race; (b) *game-side, D8-class layout correction:* enlarge `difficultytext[4]` → `[16]`, `missiontext[18]` → `[32]` under `#ifdef PORT`. Both are small. Scope note for the migration shim: `fileValidateSaves`'s block-0 `smallSave` CRC (file2.c:512-535) needs **no** migration — `SAVEFLAGS_SET(FOLDER3, SAVESLOT1, BOND_CONNERY, FALSE)` = 0x42 and any in-use save has a different header byte (user's: 0x57), so it takes the "customised file" branch and is factory-reset on every load by design (N64-faithful); only the 5 slots carry user data. The separate v0.3.0 save-wipe regression (D284 side effect, above) is a second, independent release-blocker candidate and should be filed/decided on its own.

## D297 - v0.3.0 silently wipes ALL pre-fix player saves on first launch (D284 side effect; release-blocker, found during D295/M-148).

**What:** every save written by a v0.2.x build fails `fileValidateSaves` CRC on any post-D284 build and is reset to factory (`BAD -> RESET (progress wiped)`, confirmed live via `GE_SAVELOG=1` on the user's #87 artifact — all five slots). Players upgrading to v0.3.0 lose their entire campaign with no warning.

**Root cause (full evidence chain in `## D295` M-148):** slot CRCs are computed by `fileGenerateCRC` (`src/game/crc.c`) off a *local constant seed* through `randomGetNextFrom` — so each stored CRC is a fingerprint of the PRNG implementation that wrote it. D284 (`0de99b4d`, port-side `dsll32/dsrl32` semantics fix) changed the PRNG output without changing any persisted state, so every pre-fix CRC now mismatches. The D284 commit's "savegames are unaffected" claim is corrected in `## D284`.

**Scope of any migration (verified, not assumed):**
- Only the **5 slots** (file bytes 32–607) carry user data; each needs its two CRC words recomputed with the *new* PRNG over slot bytes [8..96).
- The block-0 `smallSave` header check (`file2.c:512-535`) needs **no** migration: `SAVEFLAGS_SET(FOLDER3, SAVESLOT1, BOND_CONNERY, FALSE)` = 0x42 and any in-use save has a different header byte (user's artifact: 0x57), so it takes the "customised file" branch and is factory-reset on every load by design (N64-faithful). It is a pristine-cart seal, not progress.

**Fix plan (signed off in principle; reviewed 2026-09-16 and landed as M-150):** `port/src/legacycrc.c` — an isolated, clearly-dated port file carrying the *old* (deliberately-wrong) PRNG + CRC math, called from the eeprom shim's read path: if a slot fails the new-CRC check but validates under the legacy PRNG, re-stamp `chksum1/chksum2` with the new-PRNG values before handing the region to the game. Zero game-code changes; rule-2-clean (port layer satisfies a hardware-format dependency). The old PRNG must stay in-tree until no pre-D284 saves are expected in the wild — the file header must say so loudly. Reference implementation: `tools_pc/d295_crc.py` (bit-exact against compiled C for both PRNGs).

**Alternatives rejected:** dual-CRC acceptance inside `fileValidateSaves` (game-code change, rule 2); "loud release note only" (ships known total data loss — not acceptable for a release).

- **M-150 (fix landed + verified):** independent review of the draft passed with no corrections — reviewer diffed `geLegacyRandomGetNextFrom` line-by-line against `git show 0de99b4d^:port/src/random.c` (bit-exact, operation for operation), and separately confirmed the `save_data` layout, the hook site in `geEepromRW`'s read branch, that `geEepromPatchAllCheats` is genuinely read-time-only (never persists — so the persist-before-patch ordering claim holds), the one-past-the-end boundary pattern (same as `fileValidateSaves` itself, file2.c:544), and that fresh zero slots fail *both* CRC checks and fall through untouched. Applied: new `port/src/legacycrc.c` (isolated, loud dated header explaining why a deliberately-wrong PRNG lives in the tree and when it may be deleted) + a hook in `port/src/libultra.c` `geEepromRW` read branch — fires only on `block == 4 && nbytes == sizeof(ge_save_slot)*5`, runs **before** `geEepromPatchAllCheats` so only pristine+migrated bytes are ever persisted, persists once via `s_eeprom` + `geEepromStore()` with an INFO log. No CMakeLists change (`SRC_PORT` is `GLOB_RECURSE`); zero game-file edits. Verification on `release/v0.3.0` HEAD (ntsc-final): **(1)** user's original #87 artifact → `D297-migrated 5`, all five slots OK, no crash; stored CRCs now exactly the new-PRNG values (`tools_pc/d295_crc.py`: "new PRNG matches all 5 stored CRCs: True"); relaunch → **no** migration (idempotent), still all OK. **(2)** native post-fix save (CRCs pre-stamped via `d295_crc.py`) → zero migrations, all five OK. **(3a)** corrupted slot (one byte flipped inside slot 0's CRC region) → only 4 migrated; the corrupt slot fails both checks, is left alone, and takes the game's own `BAD -> RESET` wipe path as designed. **(3b)** fresh zeroed eep → no migration, clean boot. Then 21/21-level `tools_pc/level_sweep.sh` PASS. `data/ge007.eep` restored to the original artifact and hash-verified **at report time** (md5 `76e18aa4…`; per the porting-notes §E gotcha, after the sweep, not before). Operational note: `fileValidateSaves` runs from `init_menu00_legalscreen` (`front.c:1450`) — the legal screen appears ~36 s / frame ~1800 into an unattended boot, so verification runs must be ≥ 60 s to observe it.

**Status:** **FIXED (M-150)** — migration shim landed and verified; release-blocker cleared. Crash-side companion D295 is FIXED (M-149).

## D299 — Game.SkipIntro crashed selecting any save slot except one (found + fixed this session, 2026-09-17)

**Symptom (user, live repro):** with `Game.SkipIntro=1` (D216), booting straight to file-select and selecting any of the 4 file slots except one crashed the game (`EXCEPTION: 0xc0000005`, fault addr `0x10`). Reproduced on both a clean `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release` rebuild and the normal `RelWithDebInfo` dev build, and with a completely fresh (no `data/ge007.eep`) save — ruling out stale/incompatible save data. With `SkipIntro=0` (normal intro/legal-screen boot), all 4 slots worked with no crash.

**Root cause:** `fileValidateSaves()` (`file2.c:499`) — the only place `saves[]` is populated from EEPROM (`joyGamePakLongRead`, CRC-validated/repaired) — is called exclusively from `init_menu00_legalscreen()` (`front.c:1450`), which only runs when the front-end state machine passes through `MENU_LEGAL_SCREEN`. `Game.SkipIntro`'s shortcut (`src/game/lv.c:417-430`, `#ifdef PORT`) jumps straight to `MENU_FILE_SELECT`, skipping the legal screen entirely, so `fileValidateSaves()` never ran — `saves[SAVESLOTMAX]` (`file2.c:29`, a plain zero-initialized global) stayed all-zero instead of loading real save data. `fileGetSaveForFoldernum()` (`file2.c:434`) then legitimately returned `NULL` for every folder except whichever one a zeroed `save_data` happens to decode its folder field as. File-select's `fileGetIsCheatUnlocked()` (`file2.c:397`) dereferences its `save` argument with no `NULL` guard (unlike sibling call sites, e.g. `file2.c:1190`, which do check) — crashing for every other folder.

**Fix (`src/game/lv.c`, `#ifdef PORT` block, D216's own shortcut):** call `fileValidateSaves()` from the `SkipIntro` shortcut, so `saves[]` gets populated exactly as the skipped legal screen would have done. Zero game-logic change — reuses the existing decomp-verbatim function; rule-2-clean (port-layer completeness fix for a port-only feature, not a `src/game` behavior change). Left `fileGetIsCheatUnlocked`'s missing `NULL` guard alone since the actual bug is the port shortcut not fully replicating the skipped screen's side effects, not a missing defensive check in game code.

**Verified:** build-clean (`ninja`, both `RelWithDebInfo` and `Release`); live user re-test with `SkipIntro=1` restored — intro correctly skipped, all 4 file slots selectable with no crash.

**Generalisable lesson (added to `porting-notes.md`):** a port-only "skip to state X" shortcut must replicate every side effect the skipped screens perform, not just the terminal menu-state flags — `SkipIntro`'s original comment claimed to fully reuse "the game's own post-intro route," but missed the legal screen's one-time `fileValidateSaves()` call.

**Status:** **FIXED** — verified live this session. Not yet run through a full 21-level sweep (docs-only + one `#ifdef PORT` line touching front-end boot, not level code) or committed.

## D300 — Hipfire look non-uniform (GitHub #89): direct camera write replaces the N64 stick-curve routing (WI-1, `docs/dev/GEPD-INPUT-PLAN.md`)

**Symptom (issue #89):** hipfire mouse-look feels non-uniform — slow mouse motion is "almost unrecognised," fast motion saturates quickly, overall bang-bang rather than smooth.

**Root cause (diagnosed in the plan, confirmed by code reading):** hipfire converted mouse px into an *analog stick value* (`sx += (int)(hipEdx * hipSens * MOUSE_TURN_GAIN)`, `port/src/input.c`), which the game then runs through its own N64-era natural-turn response — a quadratic-ish curve with a soft floor that saturates at full 315°/s by ~13 px/poll (D238). Consequences: small stick values from slow motion square off to near-zero turn rate; fast motion saturates almost immediately, narrowing the usable band; `(int)` truncation adds a quantized dead zone. Aim mode (D194's `aimGepdCompute`) never had this problem because it already writes `vv_theta`/`vv_verta` directly, bypassing the stick curve entirely — hipfire was the one leftover N64-stick-shaped path.

**Fix (`port/src/input.c`, port-only, no `src/game` touch):** new `hipDirectCompute()`, structurally mirroring `aimGepdCompute()` and GEPD's own hipfire branch (`reference/mouse-injector/games/goldeneye.c`: `camx += XPOS/10 * (SENS/40) * (fov/basefov)`). Converts this poll's dt-scaled, already-invert/Y-scale-adjusted px directly to degrees (`px * 0.1 * (MouseTurnSpeed/100) * (MouseSensitivity/100) * (fovy/GEPD_BASE_FOV)`) and adds straight to `g_CurrentPlayer->vv_theta`/`vv_verta` (pitch clamped ±90°, matching the aim-mode convention). At default `MouseTurnSpeed=50`/`MouseSensitivity=100` this reduces to GEPD's implied px/10 baseline scaled by the existing 50% fine-trim — same "MouseSensitivity multiplies everything" convention D238 established.

**Safety gates (per the plan's GEPD-parity requirement):** GEPD gates injection on `camera==4||0 && menupage==11 && !dead && !watch && !pause`. Aim mode never needed explicit dead/watch/pause checks because it only runs while RMB is held, which a player can't do through those states in practice; hipfire look is always live, so it needs the check explicitly or it would fight the game's own camera control during a death cam or cutscene. `menupage==11` is already covered by the existing `menuMode`/`current_menu` gate (hipfire's branch is only reached when `!menuMode`). Added explicit reads of `g_CurrentPlayer->bonddead`, `->outside_watch_menu`, `->pause_state` (decomp-canonical fields, `src/game/bondview.h:465/672/705`) — read-only, no logic change, function returns 0 (falls back to the legacy stick path) if any gate is closed.

**Escape hatch:** `Input.MouseDirectLook` (default 1) — `0` reverts to the pre-existing `MOUSE_TURN_GAIN` stick path unchanged. Keyboard-driven turn (arrows) is unaffected either way (only mouse px is rerouted).

**Not done this pass (deferred per the plan's phasing):** WI-2 (raw-input-by-default), WI-3 (sensitivity-knob consolidation), tank-specific direct write (GEPD's separate `0x80036484` tank-rotation global — `g_TankOrientationAngleRad`, `bondview.h:2529`/`bondview.c:269`, per a background mapping pass this session; not wired up — tanks are rare in single-player, phase 2 per the plan).

**Verified:** compiles clean (`ninja`, `port/src/input.c` — no new warnings); full link succeeds; a 1200+-frame bare `-level_33` smoke boot (`GE_D243M=1`, unrelated to this change but running concurrently) completed with zero exceptions/crash signatures, confirming the build is otherwise healthy with this change in it. `GE_INPUTLOG` logs `hipdirect d=... cam=...` lines for the linearity check the plan's Verification section calls for.

Two unrelated side effects noted (mouse now active during the pre-control intro flying cutscene; no mission-complete screen after Dam) were explicitly deferred by the user for separate investigation — not a regression in this fix itself.

**M-190 (2026-09-18, D243 camera-tracking review session): closed the first deferred side effect above — the missing gate was in this feature's own safety-gate list, not a new bug.** The "mouse now active during the pre-control intro flying cutscene" report, surfaced but deferred at ship time, reproduced again during a live review of the Dam abseil cutscene ("camera angles do not follow bond... on the intro fly in camera... you're not supposed to be able [to move the mouse]... same as the intro flyover cam"). ## D301 — `fileGetIsCheatUnlocked()` NULL-deref, unguarded on every call site, not just the D299/SkipIntro one (GitHub #87)

**Symptom (GitHub #87, two independent reports):** (1) fresh save → unlock a cheat (paintball, Dam) → backing out to the profile/file-select screen, or relaunching, crashes (`0xc0000005`, `FAULT ADDR: 0000000000000000`); deleting the save "fixes" it until the next cheat unlock. (2) normal campaign progress through Jungle → Control on 00 Agent (with worsening audio-sync/skipping reported starting around Jungle/Streets, likely unrelated — not folded into this finding), exit level, exit game, relaunch → crash after the intro, before the main menu. **Both crash logs have the identical PC (`00000001400797c1`) and identical `FAULT ADDR: 0000000000000000`**, strong evidence of one shared crash site rather than two coincidental bugs.

**Root cause:** `fileGetIsCheatUnlocked(save_data *save, s32 cheat)` (`src/game/file2.c:391-402`) dereferences `save` with no NULL check:

```c
bits = save->unlocked_cheats_1 | save->unlocked_cheats_3 << 0x18 | ...
```

It's called with `fileGetSaveForFoldernum(selected_folder_num)` passed straight through, unguarded, from several sites: `front.c:1067-1124` (the mode-select screen's per-level cheat-availability checks — the code path that runs every time the mode-select/cheat menu renders) and `file.c:59` (briefing cheat check). `fileGetSaveForFoldernum()` returns NULL whenever no slot in `saves[]` currently matches the requested folder — which real N64 hardware invariants prevent for the *active* folder, but which the PC port can hit whenever that folder's slot fails `fileValidateSaves()`'s CRC check, or was never populated for the active folder in the first place.

**Relationship to D299:** D299 fixed *one* route into this same unguarded function — `Game.SkipIntro` skipping `fileValidateSaves()` entirely, leaving `saves[]` all-zero. That fix (`src/game/lv.c`, `#ifdef PORT`) only calls `fileValidateSaves()` on the SkipIntro boot path; it does **not** guard `fileGetIsCheatUnlocked()` itself. Neither #87 report mentions SkipIntro, so they're reaching the same crash through a different, not-yet-fully-root-caused route (most likely a real save slot failing CRC validation after a cheat-unlock write, or a folder/slot mismatch on a fresh profile) — the *mechanism* (unguarded NULL deref) is now understood and closed regardless of *why* the lookup fails.

**Fix (`src/game/file2.c`, `#ifdef PORT`, unreachable on real N64 hardware so no decomp/byte-match impact):**

```c
#ifdef PORT
    if (save == NULL)
    {
        return FALSE;
    }
#endif
```

Returns "cheat not unlocked" — the same safe default other cheat-state paths already produce — instead of crashing. Closes the NULL-deref class at its single choke point rather than patching each call site.

**Verified this session:** build green (`ninja`, clean incremental link); a `-level_09` smoke boot ran 1000+ frames crash-free with the fix in place; **confirmed the guard doesn't mask a working code path** by temporarily reverting it, rebuilding, and re-running the same smoke test (still crash-free either way — see caveat below). **Not yet reproduced live:** attempted to force the NULL-`save` condition headlessly via `GE_STARTMENU=6` (jumps straight to `MENU_MODE_SELECT`, skipping `fileValidateSaves()` the same way SkipIntro does) — this did **not** crash even on the pre-fix build, meaning `saves[]`'s all-zero decode coincidentally satisfies `fileGetSaveForFoldernum(0)` for that particular repro (the same "works for one folder" coincidence D299's own write-up describes), so this specific synthetic repro doesn't exercise the actual NULL path either reporter hit. **This fix has not been confirmed against the exact reported repro** — it closes a real, confirmed-unguarded crash vector of the identical shape (NULL-deref in this exact function, matching both crash logs' fault signature), but the precise trigger for *why* the lookup fails in the #87 reports remains unconfirmed. A live re-test from either reporter (or a `GE_SAVELOG=1` capture at crash time) would confirm whether this was the whole story or one of two contributing bugs.

**Status:** FIXED locally on `release/v0.3.0` (not yet pushed) — build-verified, crash-free smoke test; live confirmation against the actual #87 repro still owed.

**M-183/M-185 (2026-09-17, this session):** Added playspeed and endframe clamp workarounds for D243's Bond position/animation issue. Both were originally env-gated on GE_D243M — a gate M-187 found to be wrong (the clamps never fired for real players); they are now gated on `gameScriptedCameraActive()` alone and active by default. **M-186 (2026-09-17, later recovery session) — the M-183/M-185 diagnosis above is WRONG; correcting the record.** A follow-up agent acted on "struct layout corruption from pointer widening" and converted `Model`'s 7 pointer fields to u32 slots + accessor macros, rewriting ~200 call sites with blind `sed` across 12 files — this broke the build (macro name collisions with unrelated structs' same-named fields, malformed chained-access substitutions) and was **reverted this session** (changes stashed, not committed: `git stash` "D243 broken sed attempt (superseded)"). The diagnosis itself doesn't hold up: a `Model*` accessed normally is always self-consistent post-compilation; this codebase's actual pointer-widening bug class only bites when something *puns/overlays* a Model onto raw hardcoded-offset bytes (§A, `porting-notes.md`), and all three known instances of that for models (D100 Bond's own inline model, D102 weapon model, D140 watch model) are already fixed with real inline storage. No unfixed punning gap exists for Bond's world model. **The real, already-established lead is above this entry, in M-169 through M-178** — the 3rd `chrlvPerformAnimationForActor` scripted restart (`chraction.c:605`) triggers the rapid `animframe` advancement; M-178's own stated next step (diff that call's caller-side state writes, `chraction.c:615-627`, against a normal `modelTickAnim` loop-wrap) was never carried out and is the correct place to resume. See `docs/HANDOFF.md` for the fuller writeup, including a new unconfirmed candidate (`modelSetAnimation`/`modelSetAnimation2` never reset `playspeed`/`unkb0`/`unkb4`/`unkac`/`animrate`, only `modelSetAnimPlaySpeed` does) that needs a live `GE_D243M` capture to check, and a reminder not to lose D243 CONSOLIDATED NEXT STEPS item 5's model-pointer-reuse caveat as an alternative explanation for the "playspeed already corrupted before `modelSetAnimPlaySpeed` was even called" observation.

### M-187 (2026-09-18, same recovery session): 25-minute parallel triage sweep of `docs/dev/BUG-TRIAGE-REPORT.md`'s open P0/P1 items — 5 read-only investigations, no fixes applied. **v0.3.0 priority set by user this session: D252 and the D243/D173/D292 family are release-blocking; D286/D287/D296 are explicitly deprioritized (old reports).**

Should look better than the existing untested `GE_D245_FIXEDSHIFT` opt-in at the boundary while avoiding its always-coarser quantization elsewhere. Needs the same live A/B (baseline / fixed-k / hysteresis) that `GE_D245_FIXEDSHIFT` itself has never gotten. ### M-189 (2026-09-18, same session): ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED — live-confirmed by the user; D243/D173/D292's animation/positioning symptom is resolved

**The user's own live capture (`GE_D243M=1`, full Dam→abseil playthrough) delivered exactly the data M-187/M-188 asked for, and it refuted the `unkb0`-blend-state hypothesis outright — every `D243M: animrestart` line for Bond's cutscene chr (`chr=5037`) showed `unkb0=0.000` at every one of the 4 scripted restarts.** But the same lines carried the real signature: `unkac=6.283`/`12.566` (exact multiples of 2π — a rotation-angle value, not a legitimate animation blend factor) and `animrate=-3111.625` — which is bit-identical (to print precision) to this same chr's own `pos.z` at that moment (`-3111.6`, matching the exact Z value M-160/M-162's captures cycled through repeatedly). Cross-referencing the immediately preceding `D243M: setanimplayspeed`/`CREATE` lines for the same `model=` pointer made the mechanism undeniable: at model-creation time, `playspeed=-14647.539`/`animrate=-2082.015` (read as stale/garbage before being overwritten) were bit-identical to that exact model's own `prop->pos.y`/`pos.z` (`-14647.5`/`-2082.0`).

**Root cause: a hardcoded 32-bit struct-size literal, stale after 64-bit pointer widening — the actual mechanical bug behind the whole family, distinct from (and more precise than) M-186's "no unfixed punning gap" finding, which only checked ordinary named-field `Model*` access, not this buffer-layout site.** `bondview2.c`'s player third-person body model (used by the `CHR_BOND_CINEMA` cutscene path, the exact model this whole investigation has been chasing) is carved out of a raw scratch buffer with manually-computed offsets: `model = (Model *)(weaponbuf0 + cursor); cursor = ALIGN64_V3(cursor + 0xfb);` (`bondview2.c:598-599`, right after the identical, correctly-written idiom for `ModelFileHeader` one line up: `cursor = ALIGN64_V3(cursor + sizeof(ModelFileHeader) + 0x3f)`, line 591). Decoded: `0xfb == 0xbc + 0x3f` — i.e. this literal IS `sizeof(Model) + 0x3f` for N64's 32-bit `Model` (188 bytes), just pre-computed as a constant instead of written with `sizeof()` like its neighbor. **Confirmed empirically, not just by inspection:** a standalone compile against the real build's exact flags/includes (`scratch/sizeof_model.c`, same defines as `compile_commands.json`'s `bondview2.c` entry) measured `sizeof(Model) == 232` (`0xe8`) on 64-bit PC — pointer-widened fields (`attachedto`, `attachedto_objinst`, `anim`, `anim2`, plus alignment) grew the struct by 44 bytes past the 32-bit original. The stale `0xfb` literal under-reserves by exactly that much, so the very next thing placed in the buffer — the animation-node data array, `animdata = (u32 *)(weaponbuf0 + cursor)` — starts **inside** the tail of the just-allocated `Model`, overlapping precisely `playspeed`/`animrate`/`unkac`/`unkb0`/`unkb4` (`bondtypes.h:1643-1650`, the struct's last 5 real fields before `anim_translation_scale`). Every subsequent write to that overlapping animation-data region corrupts those fields with arbitrary content, and the model's own uninitialized/garbage state before first use reads back as whatever happened to be sitting in adjacent memory (here, the model's own `pos`) — exactly matching every anomalous value captured across M-160 through M-188.

**This qualifies as the project's standard ABI/pointer-width narrow exception (AGENTS.md rule 2), not a game-logic change:** semantics-preserving, mechanical, and the fix simply completes the pattern the surrounding code already uses. **Fix applied (`#ifdef PORT`, `bondview2.c:598-609`):** replaced the stale `ALIGN64_V3(cursor + 0xfb)` with `ALIGN64_V3(cursor + sizeof(Model) + 0x3f)` — the real `sizeof(Model)` computed at compile time, matching the `ModelFileHeader` idiom one line above exactly. The `#else` branch (N64/original literal) is preserved unmodified for non-PORT builds.

**Live-verified by the user, full Dam→abseil playthrough, normal launch (no env vars): "Yep fixed and the animations seem to play right."** This closes the actual animation-corruption mechanism for D243/D173/D292's shared family (see D173/D292's own entries — same `Model`-carving-buffer class is worth checking there too, not yet done). Build clean, `tools_pc/verify.sh dam` PASS. M-183/M-185's clamps (now correctly gated per M-187) remain in the tree as a defense-in-depth stopgap — harmless now that the actual corruption source is fixed, since `playspeed`/`endframe` should no longer go out of range in the first place.

**Remaining open item for this family (not a regression, a distinct piece of work): the Dam end-cutscene camera should now correctly track Bond, but this needs a dedicated review, not just an assumption.** M-170's `field_488.pos` freeze-and-rebaseline-on-teleport-epoch (`bondview2.c:10599-10629`, unconditional, not env-gated) was built as a workaround for camera shake that we now know was itself downstream of this exact M-189 corruption (a corrupted/cycling render-skeleton position feeding the camera's look-at filter). With the real root cause fixed, `field_488.pos` should already be receiving correct, non-cycling data every tick — which may make M-170's freeze either redundant or, worse, actively wrong: freezing between teleports could now be suppressing *legitimate* per-shot camera tracking of Bond's real (correct) motion that the freeze was never designed to distinguish from the old corruption. **Next step:** live-review the Dam abseil cutscene with fresh eyes on whether the camera visibly tracks Bond through each of the 3 scripted shots (per the user's own N64 memory: "stands on the edge and then jumps... camera tracks him as he descends," M-169's note) — if it does, no further work needed; if the camera looks static/wrong-angle for any shot, M-170's freeze is the first thing to loosen or remove now that it's very possibly no longer needed.

### M-190 (2026-09-18, same session): live camera-tracking review confirmed M-189's prediction — M-170's freeze replaced with a filter re-seed; a second, unrelated mouse-lock bug found and fixed in the same pass

**User's live review confirmed the M-189 tail's prediction exactly: "the camera angles do not follow bond and dont fully match n64."** M-170's freeze (`bondview2.c:10599-10629`) was skipping every `field_488.pos` write during `CAMERAMODE_POSEND` except the one tick a teleport epoch changed — correct behavior when the input was corrupted garbage (pre-M-189), actively wrong now that it's legitimate per-tick motion, since freezing it means the look-at target never moves within a shot.

**Fix:** replaced the freeze with a write-every-tick-plus-instant-reseed scheme. `field_488.pos` is now written unconditionally every tick (restoring real per-tick tracking of Bond's motion within a shot). Separately, on the exact tick a teleport epoch changes (a real shot-change, same signal M-170 used), the look-at filter's leaky-integrator accumulator (`field_3B8`, consumed by the unmodified decomp function `bondviewUpdatePlayerCollisionPositionFields`, `bondview2.c:4910-4924`) is re-seeded directly to the new position's *pre-scale* value (`pos / FACTOR_2`, since `field_3C4/8/C = field_3B8 * FACTOR_2` is the filter's actual output) instead of being left to converge over ~20 ticks (M-143's original shake mechanism, confirmed PC-only vs N64 in M-144). `field_3C4/8/C` (what the camera's look-at code actually reads) are also set directly so the correct value is live even before the next filter tick runs. Entirely `#ifdef PORT`, port-layer only — the decomp filter function itself is untouched, this only seeds its accumulator field from the outside at a legitimate, decomp-recognized "reposition" event.

**Second, unrelated bug found and fixed in the same review pass: mouse-look was never gated during scripted/no-control camera states, letting the player freely move the view during the Dam intro flyover and the abseil-jump cutscene (both meant to be camera-locked).** Root cause: `port/src/input.c`'s `hipDirectCompute()` (the default-active WI-1 direct mouse-to-`vv_theta`/`vv_verta` write path, `mouseDirectLook=1`) had its own doc comment explicitly stating "a frozen or scripted-camera state (POSEND/INTRO cutscenes, death cam, pause) must be checked explicitly or this would fight the game's own camera control during those states" — but the actual gate list (`mouseDirectLook`/`mouseGrabbed`/`bonddead`/`outside_watch_menu`/`pause_state`) never implemented that documented check. `bondviewFrozenMoveBond` (`bondview2.c:7947`) already correctly zeroes stick input during these camera modes, but that gate lives entirely inside the stick-based `MoveBond`-vs-`bondviewFrozenMoveBond` dispatch (`bondview2.c:8268`) — `hipDirectCompute` writes `p->vv_theta`/`vv_verta` directly, bypassing that dispatch and the game's own camera-lock logic entirely. **Fix:** added the missing check, calling the same scripted-camera test D243's clamps already use. Renamed `d243mCutsceneActive()` → `gameScriptedCameraActive()` (`bondview2.c`) since the function was never D243-specific and is now used by two unrelated call sites (`model.c`'s clamps, `port/src/input.c`'s new gate) — behavior-identical rename, all three call sites updated.

Build clean (`./build-pc.sh ntsc-final`), `tools_pc/verify.sh dam` PASS. **User confirmed both fixes live, full Dam intro-flyover + abseil-jump + abseil-descent playthrough: "ok yeah looks good."**
