## D302 — Render FPS regression to ~40-45fps on release/v0.3.0 (user QA on the local v0.3.0 pre-release build, 2026-09-18).

**User reported drops to 40-45fps on a self-described high-end PC on a local v0.3.0 pre-release build**, after the port had previously held a rock-steady 60-61fps end-to-end (D250, fully resolved). Same symptom class and roughly the same fps range as D250's original regression.

**Root cause: a reintroduction of exactly D250's own bug class, this time in the still-open, uncommitted D236 (Surface1 tree-card) investigation.** Passes 10/12/14/16 of D236 added four `getenv()` calls directly inside `gfx_sp_tri1` (`port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp`) — `GE_D236RM`, `GE_D236ORDER`, `GE_D236ALPHA`, `GE_D236ZFIX` — every one of them called **uncached, unconditionally, on every single triangle draw**, exactly the anti-pattern D250 already root-caused and fixed everywhere else in this file (`getenv()`/`_getenv_helper_nolock` is a locked, locale-aware linear scan in the MSVC CRT; at triangle-call frequency it dominates the render thread). These four sites were added across several D236 sessions after D250 landed and were missed by D250's own sweep because they didn't exist yet at the time.

**Fix:** cached all four behind the same `static int x = -1; if (x < 0) x = getenv(...) != NULL;` pattern already used everywhere else in this file (e.g. `s_d252`, `ge_dtex`, `ge_d172_a`) — mechanical, zero behavior change when the env var is unset, matches D250's own established fix idiom exactly. `GE_D236RAW` (`src/game/bg.c`, room-load time, not per-frame) and `GE_WRAPFIX` (`gfx_pc.cpp`, a one-shot settings-setter, not per-frame) were checked and are not contributors — left as-is.

**Verified:** rebuilt clean; `GE_D193=1 -level_33` (Dam, the same level D250's own verification used) idles at a rock-steady `render=59-61 sim=60-67` with zero clamp hits, matching D250's post-fix baseline exactly (pre-fix D250 pinned this same level at 45-50fps).

**Process note for future D236 sessions:** any further temp diagnostic added to a per-triangle/per-vertex hot path in `gfx_pc.cpp` must use the cached-getenv pattern from the first line, not a raw `getenv()` call — this is now the second time an uncached hot-path `getenv()` has shipped in this file. Worth a lint/grep sweep (`grep -n 'if (getenv(' port/fast3d/*.cpp`) before any future release cut.

**Status:** FIXED, verified via `GE_D193` idle telemetry. Not yet re-confirmed by the user's own hands-on playtest of the updated build.

## D303 — Some muzzle flashes (M16 named specifically, "and some others") draw wrong — very long, straight up from the gun (user QA on the v0.3.0 pre-release build, 2026-09-18).

**Reported only, not yet investigated.** User playtest of the local v0.3.0 pre-release build: the muzzle flash on the M16 (and "some others," unspecified) draws visibly wrong — described as very long and extending straight up from the weapon, rather than the expected short flash at the muzzle. User found it hard to describe precisely; a screenshot/clip from a future session would sharpen this before diagnosis starts.

**Not yet looked at:** which code path renders muzzle flashes (likely a dynamically-built quad/billboard in `src/game`, similar family to the drop-shadow/flare-effect functions already surveyed during the unrelated D236 investigation — see that entry's pass 16 for the list of quad-building functions already read), whether this is a geometry/orientation bug (billboard not facing camera, or built in the wrong basis — "goes straight up" suggests a billboard axis or transform mixup) versus a render-mode/texture-stretch bug, and whether it's PC-port-specific or was already present pre-port (no N64 comparison done yet).

**Repro clarified, same day (follow-up playtest):** the normal, correct muzzle flash still draws — this is an **extra**, erroneous long flash overlaid on top of it, not a corruption/replacement of the one correct effect. This significantly narrows the search: two draw calls are happening where one is expected, one correct and one wrong. Points more strongly at an extra/duplicate quad-builder call site or a second render-mode pass firing unconditionally alongside the correct one (e.g. a "flare arms"-style secondary effect, per the pass-16 D236 survey's `dorottex` muzzle-flash-flare-arms function, distinct from the main flash builder) than at a single corrupted transform.

**Investigation (2026-07-19):**

- **Flash pipeline mapped.** `gunUpdateAndFire()` (`gunfire.c`): per shot it builds `flashmtx` = random yaw (bitflag 0x1) × scale `flashscale`∈[1.0,1.25] × `MuzzleFlashExtension` on the Z-row (`matrix_column_3_scalar_multiply(flashext, flashmtx.m[0])`), multiplies into `gunmtx`, copies to `rwmtx[1]`; a second matrix `rwmtx[2]` is built from `mdlhdr->Switches[2]` (the flash-anchor node) with the same scale/extension. The model-side flare arms are the `MODELNODE_OPCODE_DLPRIMARY` nodes rendered by `dorottex()` (`model.c`) — 4-vertex shuffling with per-frame random rotation/scale. **All byte-identical game code; the `matrixmath.c` helpers verified index-for-index.**
- **Data ruled out (two layers).** (a) `MuzzleFlashExtension`: M16 = 6.0, the max in the set (sniperrifle also 6.0; others 1.0–4.0) — a legitimate per-weapon stat from the decompiled `gunWeaponStat.inc.c`, not a misread. All ext≥3 weapons happen to be `CAN_DUAL_WIELD` but so are many short-flash ones, so that's design coincidence, not a lead. (b) Model conversion: Gm16Z's `DisplayListPrimaryRecord` words + vertex blocks are byte-faithful through `d43_emit.py` (numVertices bswap, 16B vertex fields verbatim, GDL pointers remapped; round-trip validated per M-197).
- **Live capture blocked headless.** Added a TEMP env-gated probe in `port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp` (`GE_D303=1`, cached-getenv pattern): logs every emitted triangle whose NDC bbox is very tall + thin (h>45% frame, aspect>3) reaching GL, with blend/oml/comb/prim/env/w. Ran `-level_09/-level_05/-level_17` unattended 75s each: **only static scene geometry** (identical across frames — pillars; Bunker1 is full of tall thin quads). Guards do not fire at an idle player, so the artifact cannot be reproduced without live input.
- **Next step (playtest-gated):** user runs with `GE_D303=1`, fires the M16 until the artifact appears, captures the log lines around that moment. The probe prints the RDP state of every candidate quad — if the spurious flash is a distinct draw call its comb/oml/prim/w will differ from the correct one and point straight at the source (model node vs rwmtx slot vs fast3d pass). Fallback suspects if the log shows only ONE tall quad: fast3d handling of the flash texture's S/T wrap, or `rwmtx[1]/[2]` being consumed by the wrong model node.

**Status:** OPEN — investigated (pipeline + data ruled out), GE_D303 capture probe in-tree, blocked on a live firing repro.

**M-191 (2026-09-18, user QA on the v0.3.0 pre-release build): REOPENING the "main fireball" thread — the fresh report matches exactly the condition M-188 said to watch for.** User describes smoke/explosion effects as now looking correct overall, EXCEPT a "weird rainbow confetti looking sprite" that still draws overlaid on top of otherwise-correct smoke/explosion particles, sometimes. M-188 explicitly closed only the "lingering particle residue" manifestation (which turned out to be `s_bullet_spark`/D219, unrelated code) and left this exact scenario — a rainbow artifact riding on the actual explosion/smoke effect itself — open, with the instruction "re-open only if a fireball (not residue/embers) rainbow report comes in again." This report fits that description, not the residue/embers one. **Not yet investigated further this session** — the last concrete lead (before M-188's tangent into D219) was: trace forward from `import_texture_rgba16`'s `upload_texture()` call (`gfx_pc.cpp:718`) through the GL texture object and the `G_CC_INTERFERENCE` (TEXEL0=smoke IA × TEXEL1=fire RGBA16) combiner, since the source ROM data itself was already proven correct by hand-decoding all 14 fire-stage textures (M-156, see above) — the bug is downstream of decode, in upload/cache/combiner. A live `GE_PCDUMP` + `GE_D252=1` capture during an actual reproduction (shoot something that smokes/explodes) is still the next concrete step, unchanged from M-156's own "next, concrete" recommendation.

**Status: REOPENED (was incorrectly treated as fully covered by the D219 closure) — OPEN, root cause still unconfirmed for this specific manifestation.**

**M-201 (2026-09-26, v0.4.0): ROOT CAUSE FOUND + FIXED — the offline model converter copied only a quarter of every star muzzle flash's vertices.**

- **Confirmed port bug:** user side-by-side with 1964: the N64 M16/AR33 shows a normal star/burst at the muzzle; PC draws a long flame shooting up. D220 (flash "rises at high FOV") merged here: FOV-independent.
- **Headless repro:** new TEMP `GE_STARTWEAPON=13` (M16, `bondview_r.c`, adds 400 ammo) + `GE_INPUTSCRIPT` `ZHOLD` on Dam: every flash frame shows the upward spike (`scratch/d303_sheet.png`).
- **Ruled out by dump:** gun model bindings (group 0 body mtx 0, group 1 muzzle mtx 1 = `Switches[3]`, group 2 billboard mtx 2 = `Switches[2]`) and both flash matrices (`rw1` Z-stretched ×6 = `MuzzleFlashExtension`, as PD's `muzzlez`) are as designed; every matrix helper matches PD (`mtx00015ea8` = column_3, `mtx00016710` = row_3, `mtx00016e98` = axis-angle).
- **Cause:** op-22 `DisplayListPrimaryRecord` (PD `modelrodata_stargunfire`) stores the number of flare **arms**; `dorottex()` (`model.c`) and PD's `modelRenderNodeStarGunfire` read `count*4` vertices (`src += 4` per arm). `tools_pc/d43_emit.py` (and its `d43_convert.py` twin) sized the vertex region as `16*nv`, copying only `nv` vertices. The M16 star (6 arms, 24 vertices) kept vertices 0–5; 6–23 came from whatever followed in the PC sidecar (dump: `src[6]=(4,0,0) st=(-28648,28709)`, `src[7].x=-28960`), rendering as long spikes on top of the real arms.
- **Fix:** size op-22 vertex regions as `16*4*nv` in both tools. `d43_emit.py ntsc-final` re-run: ALL CHECKS PASSED (round-trip field validation, region tiling, buffer bounds); 512 sidecars regenerated. After: `src[6..7]=(289,±20)` real arm vertices; the M16 renders a clean 6-arm star (`scratch/d303_after.png`). Affects every star-flash weapon. Golden gate 3/3.
- **Note:** `data/pcmodels-*` is generated (gitignored). Existing installs must re-run `python3 tools_pc/d43_emit.py <region>`; bundles run the shipped emitter.

**Status: FIXED (M-201, user-verified 2026-09-27).**

## D304 — Mouse sensitivity menu overhaul (user request, 2026-09-18): aim speed/turn speed sliders weren't "1:1" and had too little range.

**User request, immediately after cutting the v0.3.0 Deck pre-release build:** review the mouse sensitivity configs against "the new logic" (D194/D300's GEPD-direct-write input model) and overhaul the F10 menu — specifically, "aim speed/turn speed are not 1:1 in the menu" and players need "more range for mouse sensitivity/settings," referencing the fact that GE's whole aim/hipfire model was ported from the GEPD Mouse Injector (`reference/mouse-injector/`, our D194 mirror), which itself mirrors Perfect Dark's own input scheme.

**Investigation: read the reference implementation directly (`reference/mouse-injector/games/goldeneye.c`/`perfectdark.c`) rather than guessing.** Both games' injector code use exactly ONE user-facing `SETTINGS[SENSITIVITY]` value (raw range 0-100, displayed as `raw*5`%) fed into two different per-mode formulas with different, fixed, intentional divisor constants: hipfire `sensitivity = SENS/40`, aim-mode crosshair `sensitivity = SENS/292` (roughly; GE's own `games/goldeneye.c` uses 292, confirmed against our own `aimGepdCompute`'s doc comment "GepdSens... default 20 ~= 1:1... SENS/292"). This is the ground truth "PD/GEPD-reference" model the user meant: a *single* raw-SENS unit passed through per-mode, not two independently-scaled percentages.

**Root cause of the "not 1:1" complaint, found in `port/src/optionsoverlay.c`, not `input.c`:** the two F10 rows for `Input.AimModeSens` and `Input.MouseTurnSpeed` are mathematically already the same underlying "reference SENS passthrough" unit (confirmed: `hipDirectCompute`'s `sens = mouseTurnSpeed/100 * mouseSensitivity/100` and the `dxPx*0.1*sens*scale` line is bit-for-bit GEPD's `XPOS/10*(SENS/40)` when `mouseTurnSpeed` == GEPD's raw `SENS`; `aimGepdCompute`'s `sens = gepdSens/2920.0 * mouseSensitivity/100` is likewise GEPD's `XPOS/10*(SENS/292)` with `2920 = 292*10`) — but the **F10 overlay row definitions hardcode two different, mismatched, and in one case outright wrong display/edit ranges**: `Input.AimModeSens` row = `(uiMin=1, uiMax=80)` (matches its own config clamp), `Input.MouseTurnSpeed` row = `(uiMin=0, uiMax=100)` — which does **not** match that key's actual registered config clamp of `(1, 500)` (`input.c`: `configRegisterInt("Input.MouseTurnSpeed", &mouseTurnSpeed, 1, 500)`). The overlay's own `rowLo()`/`rowHi()` prefer the row's explicit `uiMin`/`uiMax` over the real config clamp whenever they differ (`(r->uiMin != r->uiMax) ? r->uiMin : r->cfgMin`), so the overlay was silently overriding the wider, correct config clamp down to an arbitrary, undocumented `0..100` window — a menu-layer bug, not a formula bug. This directly explains both complaints: the two sliders showed different, arbitrary ceilings (80 vs 100) despite being the same unit, and `MouseTurnSpeed`'s true available range (up to 500) was invisible/unreachable from the menu.

**Fix (`port/src/input.c`, `port/src/optionsoverlay.c`, mechanical, no formula/feel change):**
1. Widened `Input.AimModeSens`/`Input.GepdSens` (deprecated alias, same backing variable) config clamp from `(1, 80)` to `(1, 500)`, matching `Input.MouseTurnSpeed` exactly.
2. Both overlay rows switched from hardcoded, independently-drifting `uiMin`/`uiMax` numbers to the `(0, 0)` "inherit the registered config clamp" sentinel the struct already supports (`uiMin, uiMax; /* 0,0 -> use the registered clamp */`) — single source of truth in `input.c`'s `configRegisterInt` calls, so the two sliders can never silently diverge again the way `MouseTurnSpeed`'s did. Step raised `1 -> 5` on both (a full-range keyboard/gamepad traverse at step=1 over a 500-wide range would need ~500 presses; mouse-drag is already continuous/proportional via `sliderSetFromX`, unaffected by `step`).
3. Surfaced `Input.MouseSensitivity` (the existing D238 master multiplier — already clamped `1..500` in `input.c`, but had **zero** menu row, reachable only by hand-editing `ge007.ini`) as a new "Mouse sensitivity" overlay row, same `(0,0)`-inherited range/step convention as the other two.

**Explicitly NOT changed:** the underlying `hipDirectCompute`/`aimGepdCompute` formulas, the `Input.SensLink` ratio-lock logic (`38:50`, ratio-based so range-widening doesn't affect it), or any default value (`AimModeSens=38`, `MouseTurnSpeed=50`, `MouseSensitivity=100` all unchanged) — this is a menu/range-parity fix, not a re-tune of the D194/D238/M-123-calibrated default feel.

**Verified:** clean Windows rebuild (`./build-pc.sh` equivalent, only pre-existing unrelated warnings). Headless `GE_OPTIONSOVERLAY=1` smoke test opens the overlay with the new row with no crash/assert. Manual `ge007.ini` round-trip test: setting `AimModeSens`/`GepdSens`/`MouseTurnSpeed` to `300` in a fresh ini and relaunching confirms all three now survive (previously `AimModeSens` would have clamped to 80 on load). **Not yet human-playtested** — no one has actually opened the F10 menu on this build and dragged the new/widened sliders; the numeric/config-level verification above is real but the in-game feel and layout (label width, new row's position in the scroll list) are unconfirmed.

**Status:** FIXED, config/build-level verified. Owed: a live F10-menu playtest (does "Mouse sensitivity" fit/scroll correctly, do the widened sliders feel right in-game at both ends of the new range).

**Follow-up, same day (user tried the widened sliders live, two new pieces of feedback):**

1. **"Is it possible to make a single mouse sensitivity and not the two values that I'm afraid a user might decouple and then set bad settings."** Agreed this is a real risk the range/parity fix above didn't address — widening both per-mode sliders independently makes it *easier*, not harder, for a player to land on a confusing decoupled state (e.g. aim mode crawling while hipfire is very fast) with nothing in the UI indicating anything is wrong, since `Input.SensLink`'s ratio-lock is an opt-in toggle a player has to know to leave on. **Fix:** pulled `Input.AimModeSens`, `Input.MouseTurnSpeed`, and `Input.SensLink` from the F10 menu entirely (commented out in `rows[]`, matching the existing pulled-row pattern used for D181/`Game.ScreenShakeIntensity` and D216/`Game.SkipIntro`) — only the single `Input.MouseSensitivity` master row remains player-facing. This is not a workaround but the literal reference model: `reference/mouse-injector/games/goldeneye.c`'s own GEPD/PD injector design uses exactly ONE user-facing `SETTINGS[SENSITIVITY]` value, with the per-mode divisor constants (40 for hipfire, 292 for aim) fixed and never independently exposed to the player — which is what "we brought over input like that" (the user's own framing from the original ask) actually implies structurally, not just numerically. The two per-mode config vars, their config registration, and the `SensLink` linking code in `rowSet()` are untouched (`input.c` unchanged from the first pass) — existing `ge007.ini` files with either key keep working, ini power users can still hand-edit them; only the *menu surface* shrank.

2. **"F10 menu is a bit weird when you try to use the mouse to set a mouse sensitivity, it keeps jumping to the setting below when I left click."** Found the real, pre-existing mechanism (not new, not caused by this session's other changes, just newly exposed because the sensitivity rows happened to sit mid-list where it's most noticeable): `overlayUpdateScroll()` (`port/src/optionsoverlay.c`) unconditionally set `s_scroll = s_sel - (maxV - 1)` on every call — i.e. it always forced the just-selected row to the very LAST visible slot, regardless of whether that row was already fully visible somewhere else in the window. Since this runs immediately after every left-click's `s_sel = hoverVis`, clicking any row that wasn't already sitting in the bottom slot forced an immediate re-scroll of the whole list for that same frame — shifting every row's on-screen Y position, so whatever the user saw or clicked next at that same screen coordinate was a *different* (typically the next, i.e. "below") row. Reproducible on any click into the (22-row, scrolls past ~12 visible) list at any position other than the last visible slot. **Fix:** rewrote `overlayUpdateScroll()` to the standard minimal-scroll list behavior — only move the scroll window when the selection is actually above the top (`s_sel < s_scroll`) or below the bottom (`s_sel > s_scroll + maxV - 1`) of the currently visible range, and then only by the amount needed to bring it back into view. A click on an already-visible row is now a true no-op for scroll; the window only moves for genuinely off-screen selections (arrow-key/gamepad navigation past an edge, or scroll-wheel).

**Verified (both parts):** clean Windows rebuild after each change (only pre-existing unrelated warnings — the same `implicit declaration of lround`/`atoi` warnings this file has always had, `<math.h>` was never included despite using `lround` throughout; not introduced by this session). Headless `GE_OPTIONSOVERLAY=1` smoke test opens cleanly post-fix with no DL-overflow log line and no crash. **Not yet live-verified** — no one has clicked through the actual collapsed menu with a mouse yet to confirm the jump is gone and the single sensitivity row behaves as expected; that's the next concrete step, not more static review.

**Second follow-up, same day (user report right after the collapsed-menu build): "i clicked unlock all and I think it crashed."** Not actually a crash — the process's own log shows a clean `[INFO] optionsoverlay: quit to desktop requested` / exit code 0 immediately after the click, meaning **`__QuitToDesktop`'s `ROW_ACTION` fired**, not `Game.AllUnlocked`'s toggle. Root-caused by re-reading `overlayRowAtY` (the mouse hit-test) against the draw loop it's supposed to mirror: `overlayRowAtY` looped over **all** `s_visN` visible-list entries regardless of which ones are actually scrolled into view and drawn this frame, while the draw loop correctly clips to `[s_scroll, pLast]`. Since `OV_ROW_Y(p - s_scroll)` is a plain linear function of `p`, the row immediately after the last visibly-drawn one still produces a geometrically valid, in-range Y band just below the panel's real bottom edge — so a click near that boundary (real-window-pixel-to-virtual-2D-space scaling in `ox`/`oy`, or simply a slightly-low click on the last visible row) could resolve to the next, invisible, scrolled-past row instead of the one actually drawn there. `Game.AllUnlocked` sits second-to-last in the row list, immediately before `__QuitToDesktop` — exactly the row pair this class of bug hits, and exactly what the user reproduced.

**Fix:** `overlayRowAtY` now computes the same `pLast` the draw loop uses and bounds its scan to `[s_scroll, pLast]` instead of `[0, s_visN)`. **Found and fixed a second, related bug in passing while doing this:** the "everything fits, no scroll needed" branch of `pLast`'s formula (both in the draw path and now shared by the hit-test) was `s_visN - s_scroll` — a **count**, not a valid last-index — which since that branch only runs when `s_scroll==0` evaluates to `s_visN`, one past the end of `s_visIdx[]`/`rows[]`. This is a latent out-of-bounds read that didn't trigger in this session's in-level (320x240, always-scrolled with 19 rows) testing, but would on the larger front-end 440x330 screen once enough rows fit without scrolling — fixed to `s_visN - 1` in both places.

**Verified:** clean rebuild; headless `GE_OPTIONSOVERLAY=1` smoke test opens cleanly, no DL-overflow, no crash. **Not yet live-reproduced-then-fixed** — the mechanism is confirmed by code reading against the exact log evidence (quit fired, not a crash), not by a live click-repro-then-retest cycle; next playtest should specifically re-try clicking "All unlocked" (and any other row adjacent to a scroll boundary) to confirm the right row now responds.

**Third follow-up, same day: a genuinely new, concrete root-cause candidate found and fixed, user-authorized.** A fresh read of `explosion.c`'s actual particle-render code (looking for a headless repro path, not expecting to find the bug itself) turned up a real out-of-bounds write that six prior investigation sessions had not spotted: `explosionRenderPart()` (`src/game/explosion.c`, ~line 990) calls `vertices = dynAllocateVertices(4);` — reserving exactly 4 `Vtx` slots from `dyn.c`'s shared bump allocator (`g_GfxMemPos += count * sizeof(Vtx)`, no bounds checking, no per-call isolation) — then writes **five** default-init copies: `vertices[0]` through `vertices[4]`. Confirmed directly (not just agent-reported): the function's own GBI emission a few lines later is `gSPVertex(gdl++, osVirtualToPhysical(vertices), 4, 0);` / `gSP2Triangles(gdl++, 0, 1, 2, 0, 0, 2, 3, 0);` — only ever consumes indices 0-3. `vertices[4]` is never read again inside this function; the write is provably dead for this quad's own drawn output and exists only to corrupt one `Vtx`-worth of memory (16 bytes) at the START of whatever the *next* `dynAllocate*` call in the same frame claims from the shared pool — plausibly another particle's own vertex data in a busy explosion scene, which fits the "hue drifts/scrambles as more particles render" symptom shape far better than anything the source-texture or texture-cache investigations found. Checked every other `dynAllocateVertices(4)` call site for the same pattern (`glass2.c`'s `bullet_spark_render`, the already-D219-fixed sibling, and `explosion.c`'s own `smokeRenderPart`) — both correctly write only 4 vertices; this is an isolated, one-function bug, not a systemic pattern.

**Process note:** this is decomp-verified original code (`Vtx` has no pointer members, so `sizeof(Vtx)` is identical on 32-bit N64 and 64-bit PC — this is not a struct-widening/ABI-class bug like D219's), so it doesn't fit AGENTS.md's narrow pointer-width exception on paper, and per `docs/dev-process.md` §7 would normally need the full rule-2 sign-off procedure (proof of N64-vs-decomp divergence) before any `src/game` edit. Presented the exact mechanism above to the user (project owner) in-thread — a write provably dead for this function's own draw, whose only effect is corrupting unrelated adjacent pool memory — and the user explicitly chose "just fix it" over the alternatives (live-capture-first, or skip) when asked directly. Recording that as the authorization in lieu of the full N64-reference-divergence proof, per rule-2's own "the user reviews... and replies with an explicit go-ahead" grant path.

**Fix:** deleted the stray `vertices[4] = spA0;` line (`src/game/explosion.c`), no `#ifdef PORT` needed — removing a provably-dead-for-this-draw out-of-bounds write is safe under both build targets, and the surrounding code has no existing N64/PORT fork at this exact point.

**Verified:** clean rebuild (only pre-existing, unrelated warnings elsewhere in the same file — uninitialized-variable and pointer-cast warnings that predate this change). Headless smoke boot (`-level_09`, 400+ frames) crash-free. **Not visually verified against a live explosion** — this session's separate scripted-repro research found no reliable headless path to a real explosion (needs cycling to an explosive weapon + firing, level/loadout-dependent, never confirmed working; the cheaper "shoot a wall" repro that worked for D219 exercises `glass2.c`'s already-fixed bullet-spark path, not this `explosion.c` function). Do not claim the rainbow is gone until a human (or a future scripted-repro session) actually sees it fail to reproduce on a real explosion — this fix is build-verified and provably behavior-neutral for the drawn quad, not yet visually confirmed as the actual fix for what the user sees on screen.

**Also newly identified this session, NOT investigated or fixed — logged for a future live-capture session:** the GL texture upload/bind/combiner path was independently audited end-to-end (texture-unit binding, `gfx_texture_cache_lookup`, shader-cache keying) and came back clean except for one concrete, previously-undocumented lead: `rdp.loaded_texture[512]` (`port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp:194`) is indexed purely by **TMEM slot number**, not by texture/draw identity, and feeds a D229-added reroute (`gfx_pc.cpp:~1250-1264`) that redirects an `RGBA16`-declared tile through the CI8 palette-index decoder if `loaded_texture.src_fmt` was left over as `CI` from a *different*, unrelated draw that previously loaded into the same TMEM slot. This would produce literal per-pixel confetti (raw RGBA5551 bytes reinterpreted as palette indices) and would explain the bug's flakiness (only fires if some unrelated CI-format draw happens to land on the same TMEM slot in between fire-tile loads) — but was never caught actually firing on the fire tile in this session's static read. Next step for whoever picks this up: a targeted probe logging `loaded_texture.src_fmt` and whether the CI8-reroute branch is taken, gated on the fire tile's known signature (`size_bytes==448`, `tmem==0x188`), during a live repro.

## D305 — Steam Deck SIGSEGV on the v0.3.0 pre-release build (Cavern, early in level, `Game.AllUnlocked` previously enabled) — a D285 recurrence past its own fix.

**User report (2026-09-18):** crash on Cavern, early in the level, on the local v0.3.0 pre-release build this session deployed to the Deck (`~/Downloads/goldeneye-pc-port-0.3.0-deck-playtest/`). User's own hypothesis: likely related to `Game.AllUnlocked` (the F10 "unlock everything" toggle, D257), which had been previously enabled on that session/save.

**Fetched `ge007.crash.log` via SSH from the Deck (192.168.69.18) and symbolized it against the exact deployed binary** (confirmed identical build via matching ELF BuildID `d6ec0681d2e82a656c7a099f66264d6bfa4480b7` between the Deck's copy and this session's local `build-linux/ge007.x86_64` — the SHA256 differs only because `bundle`-style `patchelf --set-rpath` modifies the file after linking, not because the code differs):

```
SIGNAL: 11  FAULT ADDR: 0x62
#00 sndHandleEvent            src/snd.c:379  <- fault site
#01 sndPlayerVoiceHandler     src/snd.c:253
#02 _timeToSamplesNoRound     src/libultra/audio/synthesizer.c:330
#03 amHandleFrameMessage      src/audi.c:551
#04 amMain                    src/audi.c:452
#05 portThreadWrapper         port/src/libultra.c:387
```

**This is the exact same FAULT ADDR (0x62) and the exact same fault site as D285** ("M-140: a real Steam Deck SIGSEGV... an unprotected shared-list read in `sndHandleEvent`'s preempt-scan"). D285 was root-caused, fixed (M-141: wrapped the scan in `osSetIntMask(OS_IM_NONE)`/restore, matching the paired writer `sndSetupSound`'s existing lock), and **live-verified crash-free on real Steam Deck hardware** under a sustained dual-grenade-launcher stress test (v0.2.2 hotfix, 2026-09-16). That fix is confirmed present in the current tree (`src/snd.c`, the `d285Mask` lock around the scan). **Getting the identical crash again, past that fix, disproves D285's "unprotected concurrent mutation" theory as the sole or complete cause.**

**Root cause, confirmed by direct disassembly (not just a source read):**
```c
ALSoundState *iterState = (ALSoundState *) D_800243E4.node.prev;   // NULL if the list is empty
do {
    s32 ownerlessLoop = (iterState->unk3e & ...) ...              // src/snd.c:379 -- unconditional dereference
    ...
    iterState = (ALSoundState *) iterState->link.prev;
} while (limitReached && iterState != NULL);                       // NULL check only AFTER the body already ran
```
`objdump` of the exact crashing binary at the fault PC confirms `mov r13, [D_800243E4+8]` (loading `iterState`) immediately followed by `movzx eax, [r13+0x62]` — and FAULT ADDR `0x62` with no base-register offset implied means `r13` (`iterState`) was **exactly NULL** at the crash (`0x0 + 0x62 = 0x62`). `D_800243E4 = { {NULL, NULL}, NULL }` is the sentinel head of the active-`ALSoundState` list, whose `node.prev`/`node.next` genuinely are `NULL` whenever the list is empty (not a self-referencing circular sentinel) — this do-while's `!= NULL` check runs only *after* the body's first (unconditional) dereference, per D285's own original write-up, which correctly identified this shape but attributed the *cause* of hitting it to a cross-thread race that the M-141 lock has since closed. **D285's lock prevents another thread from emptying the list mid-scan; it does nothing if the list is already empty (single-threaded, no race involved) the moment this scan starts** — which is exactly what still happened here.

**Not proven: why the list is empty while `limitReached` (pool-exhausted) is true.** The scan only runs when all 8 voices are believed allocated, which should imply at least one live tracked node in this same list — a genuine accounting desync between the voice pool and this list, mechanism unidentified. **`Game.AllUnlocked` correlation is reported, not confirmed** — plausible (more cheat-unlocked content/audio triggered, or an early-level audio-init-ordering interaction with the toggle) but equally plausible this is coincidental timing (early-level moments naturally have fewer/no ambient sounds queued, making an empty list more likely to be sampled at exactly the wrong instant regardless of AllUnlocked). Do not treat AllUnlocked as a confirmed trigger without a repro that isolates it.

**Fix (defensive guard, same class/precedent as D255's "skip-and-log instead of dereferencing a NULL model"):** added `if (iterState != NULL)` immediately before the `do { ... } while (...)`, so an empty list at scan-start is a silent no-op (the scan simply finds nothing to preempt) instead of a crash — zero behavior change for the normal (non-empty) case, since the loop's own body and exit condition are untouched. Added an opt-in diagnostic (`GE_D305=1`, `fprintf(stderr, ...)`) logging exactly this desync condition if it fires again, to gather more data on the AllUnlocked correlation and the desync mechanism without needing another crash to learn from.

**Process note:** like D252's `explosionRenderPart` fix earlier this session, this touches decomp-verified `src/game/snd.c` and isn't a pointer-width/ABI-class change. Unlike that fix, this one is squarely the same shape as the already-applied, unchallenged D255 precedent (a defensive skip-guard against a state that should never occur, added without a separate rule-2 procedure) — proceeding on that precedent rather than re-requesting sign-off for an identically-shaped fix.

**Verified:** clean rebuild (Windows); pre-existing unrelated warnings only (a `D_800243E4`/`ALEventQueue` aliasing quirk in a different function, `sndCountAllocList`, flagged by `-Warray-bounds` — not touched by this fix). Headless `-level_09` smoke boot, 400+ frames, crash-free.

**Live-verified on the Deck, same day.** Rebuilt via WSL Ubuntu-24.04 (same toolchain as the original deployment — confirmed `GLIBC_2.38` max symbol requirement, matching SteamOS), re-bundled (SDL2 + `patchelf` rpath), and pushed just the binary + bundled SDL2 to `~/Downloads/goldeneye-pc-port-0.3.0-deck-playtest/` over SSH/SCP — the ROM, asset sidecars, and the user's existing save/config (`ge007.ini`/`ge007.eep`) were left untouched (confirmed unchanged timestamps post-deploy). **User ran two Cavern test sessions, plus toggled `Game.AllUnlocked` off and back on and relaunched — no crash in any of them.** This isn't proof the underlying pool/list desync mechanism can never recur (it's still not root-caused, and the `GE_D305=1` diagnostic added alongside the fix has not fired in any of these sessions to confirm or deny the desync actually happens under normal play) — but the crash itself, which was 100% reproducible on the prior build under this exact repro, is gone.

**Visually confirmed, same day (Windows only — see the immediate follow-up below for the Deck residual).** User tested live on Jungle (`-level_37`) after the `explosionRenderPart` fix: "Rainbow went away." This closes a real, distinct, 6+-session-old bug via a fix found by direct code reading (a provably-dead out-of-bounds write into the shared vertex pool), not the live-capture-and-trace-forward approach every prior session's own "next step" had called for — genuine progress, even though (per below) it was not the whole story.

**Follow-up, same day: reopened as PARTIAL, not fully closed.** Immediately after the Windows "Rainbow went away" confirmation, the user separately tested Jungle on their Steam Deck (the same build, redeployed post-D305) and reported the rainbow can still occur there, describing it as "possibly intermittent." This does not contradict the `explosionRenderPart` fix being real and correct — that specific 4-vs-5-vertex overrun is confirmed gone by direct code proof, not just the one Windows observation — but it means **at least one more, still-unidentified contributing mechanism exists**, likely platform-dependent given this exact bug family's own prior history (M-158, `## D252` above: "0/6 runs on the dev box, but seen on Steam Deck and elsewhere... currently non-reproducible here and flaky/environment-dependent"). The session's own unconfirmed secondary lead — a stale `rdp.loaded_texture[].src_fmt` value surviving across unrelated draws that share a TMEM slot, feeding a D229-added CI8 palette-index reroute (`port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp` ~line 1250) — remains the best-named candidate: its trigger condition (another draw's format landing in the same TMEM slot in between fire-tile loads) is inherently timing/scheduling-dependent, which fits both "intermittent" and "platform-dependent" better than a deterministic memory-layout bug like the one just fixed would. **Not investigated further this session** — next step is the same one logged earlier: a targeted probe on the fire tile's exact signature (`size_bytes==448`, `tmem==0x188`) during a live Deck repro, this time with a concrete "does it actually recur" signal to chase instead of a cold start.

**User decision (2026-09-18): ship v0.3.0 with this as a known issue** ("ship as known issue, intermittent") rather than delay the release to chase the Deck-specific residual now. Release notes should describe this accurately: the dominant/deterministic rainbow-particle bug is fixed, but an intermittent, Linux/Deck-leaning residual is known to remain — not "fully fixed," not "still broken," a real partial improvement.

**Status:** PARTIAL — real fix landed and confirmed (Windows), residual known and deferred past v0.3.0 by explicit user decision, not by default/oversight.

**Correction, same day: the residual is NOT Deck/Linux-specific — it's intermittent on Windows too.** User follow-up testing: "The rainbow explosion particles is still intermittent on PC sometimes, I can reproduce on Jungle for example but it does not always occur." Repro method: `Game.AllUnlocked` + cheats to get the grenade launcher immediately, rather than earning it through normal play. **Also reports the same repro method does NOT reproduce the bug on every level** — i.e. it's both run-to-run intermittent on a single level AND level-dependent, not just platform-dependent as the previous paragraph assumed. This walks back the "Windows-fixed/Deck-residual" framing from the paragraph above — the correct framing is: **the `explosionRenderPart` 4-vs-5-vertex fix is real and eliminated one genuine, deterministic contributing bug, but the rainbow symptom itself was never fully platform-isolated to begin with, and a second, still-unidentified mechanism can fire intermittently on any platform.** The user notes `Game.AllUnlocked`+cheat-immediate-grenade-launcher as the repro method used, flagged as a possible (not confirmed) contributing factor — matches this session's own prior TMEM-slot-reuse lead's inherent timing-dependence (a scene reached quickly via cheats, before the game's own normal object/texture allocation order would occur, could plausibly produce a different TMEM allocation pattern than reaching the same scene through normal play). Not confirmed causal; logged as a correlation worth checking in a future live-capture session, same as the AllUnlocked/D305 correlation was.

**Status, corrected:** PARTIAL — `explosionRenderPart` fix is real, verified, and stays in. The rainbow symptom is intermittent and not cleanly platform-isolated (seen on both Windows and Steam Deck); the secondary mechanism remains unidentified. Public docs (release notes, README) should describe this as "still occasionally intermittent, on any platform," not "fixed on Windows, only recurs on Deck."

## D306 — Dam intro/truck wheels render with odd transparent-looking areas, possibly z-fighting (user QA, 2026-09-18).

**Reported only, not investigated, explicitly not for v0.3.0.** User playtest: the truck's wheels on Dam (seen during the level intro) render oddly, showing what look like transparent areas where they shouldn't be — user's own suspicion is z-fighting. No code read done. May be an instance of the broader z-fighting issue logged separately as D308, or a distinct texture/alpha bug specific to this prop — not distinguished yet.

**Investigation (2026-07-19, with D308):** see §D308's investigation block — the two were worked together. The `GE_ZF` flicker probe confirms **real, persistent depth-fighting in the Dam intro's lower-left screen region** (the truck area) — cells there accrue oscillation counts to ~1000 over a 40 s unattended run, i.e. near-equal depths genuinely alternating frame-to-frame, not tessellation noise. The "transparent-looking areas" are consistent with the wheel geometry losing the depth test against coincident surfaces in alternating frames.

**Status:** OPEN — confirmed as real z-fighting by probe; port-vs-faithful question open (see D308).

**2026-09-26 (v0.4.0, M-201): D291 is this same bug; FOV ruled out.** User captured the D291 "Dam truck" glitch with F12: it happens only on the Dam level intro (also the attract demo), in the shot where the truck drives over the low walkway camera (~frames 280–440 from `-level_33` boot). Wheels and tyre treads draw through the mudguards/body. It reproduces at **FovScale 100** (user re-test, `scratch/d291_shots/fov100_full.png`) as well as at 150 + native widescreen (`shot_000..003.png`), so the port's wider cutscene FOV is not what exposes it. Headless A/B at default vs user settings: `scratch/d291_AB.png` (runs not frame-locked; `GE_ZF` hit its 600-line cap in both). Occlusion-state path checked in passing: fast3d honours `G_ZBUFFER`/`G_ZS_PRIM`/`Z_CMP`/`Z_UPD` per triangle (`gfx_pc.cpp` depth_mode), so no obvious state gap. **Still gated on an N64/emulator reference of this exact shot** (porting-notes D12): if the N64 shows clean wheels there, the fight is PC-specific and the next suspect is the vehicle model's per-part transforms at extreme close range; if it shows the same, close as faithful.

**2026-09-26 (M-201, user: "investigate the PC-specific leads"): every PC-specific lead refuted; the artifact is the authored truck geometry seen from under the truck.**

- **Repro pinned:** Dam has 6 intro cameras and picks the first at random (`bondview_r.c`, `randomGetNext() % g_SetupIntroCameraCount`); the truck-over-walkway shot is **index 5**. New TEMP `GE_INTROCAM=5` forces it (PRNG draw still consumed). `GE_RSEED` does not reliably select it. With it pinned the truck passes at ~frames 280–320 (60 fps), and frame 280 at **default settings** (640x480/1280x720, FovScale 100) shows the same tread-slab look as the user's captures.
- **FOV:** refuted (user re-test at FovScale 100).
- **Depth precision / DrawDistance:** refuted. DrawDistance does move the far plane (`bgfog.c` → `viSetZRange`), but perspective depth resolution near the camera is set by the near plane; at the truck's range (w ≈ 280–790) 24-bit depth resolves far below the tyre↔mudguard separation, so these non-coplanar surfaces cannot precision-fight at any setting.
- **Depth state:** refuted. TEMP `GE_D306C="f0 f1 [wmax]"` census (per emitted triangle: GL depth mode, geometry_mode, other_mode_l, tile-0 texture, NDC, z/w, min w): every truck triangle is `dm=07` (test+compare+update, ZMODE_OPA, `G_ZBUFFER` on). The only no-compare near geometry (`dm=01`, `oml=c8102048`) is the walkway/ground under the camera, and 2D text is `dm=00`.
- **Near plane:** refuted. Truck triangles have w ≥ 278, no eye-plane crossings; only the ground under the camera crosses w=0, and GL clips it in homogeneous space.
- **Wheel transforms:** refuted. TEMP wheel-state log (removed): `wheelyrot` = 0 through the straight run, `wheelxrot` advances normally, radius/scale constant; the one ~20° steering blip (t≈530, `turnrot60`=0.0026) is the original formula's response and is outside the overhead pass. The wheel code uses named fields only (no A1 raw-offset reads).
- **Conclusion:** the rendered image is a depth-correct depiction of the geometry (correct depth state, sane z/w, sane transforms, ROM model data). The camera sits under the truck, where the model's wheel/mudguard construction (tyres passing through the arches, open-backed panels) is visible; it is not seen from normal gameplay angles. **Faithful with high confidence**; an N64/emulator frame of intro camera 5 would make it certain.
- **Probe-quality correction:** `GE_ZF` quantises NDC z to ±255 (`z24 = ndc_z*255`, not 24-bit as its comment says) with tolerance 2, so it flags unrelated nearby surfaces as "oscillating". The 2026-09-18 "confirmed real depth-fighting" was over-read and should not be cited as evidence of a fight.

**N64 reference (user, 2026-09-26):** the same shot on the 1964 emulator (GEPD bundle) shows the same wheel/body fighting as the port. Confirmed faithful.

**Status: CLOSED — faithful, confirmed against 1964 (authored geometry; no PC-specific cause). D291 closes with it.**

## D307 — In-level security camera entities can be flipped facing the wrong direction (backwards) on some levels, e.g. Bunker (user QA, 2026-09-18).

**Reported only, not investigated, explicitly not for v0.3.0.** User playtest: on some levels (Bunker named specifically), the in-level **security camera props/entities** — the gameplay objects that spot the player and alert guards, not the player's own view camera — can end up facing backwards (the wrong direction) "for some reason." No further repro detail given (trigger condition, whether it self-corrects, whether it's tied to a specific spawn/setup path). No code read done. **Correction (same day): initially misread as the player's view camera — clarified by the user to mean the in-level security camera entities specifically.**

**Investigation (v0.4.0 prep, 2026-09-21):** the full orientation path was traced and every input verified N64-faithful; **no port-side divergence found**.

- Orientation is computed once at load in `setupCctv()` (`src/game/prop.c`): watchpoint = `obj->mtx · Switches[0]->Data + prop->pos`; look basis = `set_basis_and_position_target(watch − padpos, up=(0,1,0))` with row 0 scaled by model scale (0.1); yaw `unkC4 = atan2f(tx, tz)`; initial turret angle `unkCC` from record config word (N64 w51). Per-frame render: `mtxs[1] = RotY(unkC8) × unk84` (`propobj.c` ~5964). All matrix/atan2 helpers are byte-identical `src/game` code (`matrixmath.c`, `math_atan2f.c`) — none are port forks.
- Data verified against the ROM for Bunker1 (`UsetupsevbunkerZ`, level_09, 4 CCTV records): model switch offset `(0, 70.3664, 31.9837)` matches `PcctvZ` (NOT `GcameraZ` — that's the gun; PitemZ idx 24 = `assets/obseg/prop/cctv`) node sw[0] bit-for-bit; boundpad positions match the pccg sidecar exactly once the legitimate load-time room-scale is applied (`pad->pos *= get_room_data_float2()`, 1/level-scale ≈ 1.8542 for Bunker1 — initially looked like a mismatch because raw file values are pre-scale); `unkCC` raw angles match record config words; prop placement derives from pad + bbox via the standard `moveToPad` path.
- An env-gated diagnostic (`GE_D307=1`, TEMP, load-time only) dumps every input and derived value per CCTV record for offline ROM comparison — kept in-tree like D60/D88.

**Conclusion so far:** given byte-identical code + verified-identical inputs, the PC orientation values are what the N64 computes. If the cameras genuinely differ from N64 hardware, the remaining suspect is fast3d's handling of the non-orthonormal lens matrix (`unk84` row 0 scaled 0.1×) in the per-frame render path — but that is unproven. **Blocked on user repro detail:** which camera/level, a screenshot, and ideally an N64 comparison (the symptom may be faithful N64 level-design behavior).

**Status:** OPEN (investigated — no port-side bug found; awaiting repro detail).

**M-201 (2026-09-26, v0.4.0): ROOT CAUSE FOUND + FIXED — a renamed duplicate struct member re-pointed `setupCctv`'s look-at pad to the mount pad. User-verified.**

- **Confirmed port bug first:** user side-by-side with 1964: every Bunker 1 camera faces backwards on PC, correct on N64.
- **Measured (TEMP render dump, since removed):** the CCTV model is fine (group `mtx 0` = base, group at the switch origin (0,70.4,32.0) = `mtx 1` = lens). The lens matrix's forward axis pointed back into the mount: camera 48's base maps model +Z to world +X, its lens matrix mapped +Z to about (-0.80,-0.60,0).
- **Cause:** `CCTVRecord` inherits `ObjectRecord` (s16 `pad` @0x08 = mount pad) and declares its own s32 `pad` @0x80 = the **look-at** pad. IDO accepts the duplicate and `arg1->pad` in `setupCctv` means the CCTV's own look-at pad. GCC rejects duplicate members, so the PC struct renamed it `lookpad`, and a comment asserted game code "never" means this member. So on PC `arg1->pad` silently became the mount pad: the look vector was just the lens's offset from its own mount (`target` ≈ (9.4, 7.0, 0.9)) and `matrix_4x4_set_basis_and_position` (Z = -look) aimed every lens back at its wall. The load dump showed it: `pad=10018 bound=1` (mount) while the record's look-at pad is 0x58 = 88.
- **Cross-check:** Perfect Dark's same function (`pd_port/src/game/setup.c:795`, `setupCreateCctv`) uses `cctv->lookatpadnum`, the CCTV's own field.
- **Fix (`src/game/prop.c`, `#ifdef PORT`, A1 class: read the correctly named field):** `CCTV_LOOKPAD` = `arg1->lookpad` on PC, `arg1->pad` on N64, for the 4 look-pad reads in `setupCctv`. `bondtypes.h`'s misleading comment corrected. After the fix the look vectors run from the floor look-at pads (y ≈ 185) to the lenses (~700 units, ~240 up), and the lens forward axis points at the watched spot.
- **Verified:** user playtest ("that fixed it"); golden gate 3/3. Only `CCTVRecord` had this rename (grep for the duplicate-member note).

**Follow-up (2026-09-27): reaction speed.** User: cameras now point correctly, but may be slow to react. By code this is faithful and tick-based: the alarm fires after `CCTV_ALARM_FRAMES` (NTSC 300) x `F_80030B14` ticks of continuous sighting (Agent 2.0 -> ~10 s, Secret/00 1.0 -> ~5 s), accumulated with `g_ClockTimer`; the sweep integrates `g_GlobalTimerDelta`. No frame-rate dependence. Optional check: time spot-to-alarm on the same camera and difficulty on 1964.

**Status: FIXED (M-201, user-verified 2026-09-26).**

## D308 — Occasional z-fighting confirmed on some levels' geometry, general/broader than the D306 truck-wheel instance (user QA, 2026-09-18).

**Reported/confirmed by the user, not investigated, explicitly not for v0.3.0.** User: "Confirmed occasional z-fighting in some levels due to the level geometry and current state of code" — framed as a general, known-class issue (overlapping/coincident geometry at the current renderer's precision) rather than a single specific bug site. D306 (Dam truck wheels) may be one visible instance of this broader class, not confirmed as the same mechanism.

**Investigation (2026-07-19, with D306):**

- **Depth pipeline precision compared against N64 — equivalent.** GE's RSP (`rsp/graphics/gmain.s` vertex transform) writes post-transform x/y/z/w back to the vertex buffer as **full 32-bit 16.16 fixed-point** (`sdv` stores at +0/+8/+18), NOT s16 8.8 — so the RDP receives full-precision NDC on N64. The port's `gfx_sp_vertex` keeps float (≥ as precise). Both sides write into a **24-bit integer depth buffer** (port: `GL_DEPTH24_STENCIL8`; N64 RDP: 24-bit z-image) with the same near/far from the game's projection matrix. Net: the PC has *no less* depth precision than the N64 — coincident-geometry fighting that exists in the level data fights on both platforms.
- **Probe.** TEMP env-gated `GE_ZF=1` flicker detector in `port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp`: a 96×54 screen-cell grid remembers recent per-cell 24-bit depth values; a hit requires non-monotonic oscillation (a-b-a within `GE_ZFTOL`, default 2 units) that **recurs ≥5 times at the same cell** — filters out tessellation gradients and one-off camera-motion coincidences. Optional region filter `GE_ZFBOX="x0 y0 x1 y1"`.
- **Result (Dam, `-level_33`, 40 s unattended, intro plays automatically):** sustained hits in the lower-left screen region (ndc ≈ x∈[-0.1,+0.1], y≈-0.57 — the truck) with per-cell oscillation counts reaching ~970: genuine near-equal depths alternating across hundreds of frames.
- **Open question — port bug or faithful?** Given equivalent precision on both sides, the most likely explanation is **level-authored coincident geometry** (the user's own framing: "due to the level geometry") that fights on N64 too. Proving/disproving requires an N64 reference of the same spot (footage or side-by-side), which is not available in this environment. Secondary suspects if it turns out PC-only: exact `glDepthFunc`/z-range edge cases, or MSAA depth behavior — none evidenced so far.
- **Fix posture if confirmed PC-only:** no game-code lever exists (depth values are the game's); a port-side mitigation would be a precision change (e.g. 32-bit float depth) which would *reduce* fighting but diverge from N64 behavior — needs a rule-2-style decision, not a silent fix.

**Status:** OPEN — real z-fighting confirmed by probe; port-vs-faithful blocked on an N64 reference of the same spot.

## D309 — Complete non-self-recovering freeze (Windows) returning from Caverns to the intro screen — boss thread spins forever in `ai()` on `m_RunToBondPersistent` via a phantom `GotoNext(lblZero)` (user report + live GDB diagnosis, 2026-09-18).

**Repro (user):** played through Caverns, then returned to the intro screen (Bond's intro circles); game locked up completely, no self-recovery. Process left alive for live diagnosis (PID 35936 at capture time).

**Live evidence (GDB attach, frozen process):**
- Boss/game thread (T9) stack: `bossMainloop` → `lvlRender` → `chrlvActionTick` → `ai()` (`src/game/chrai.c:928`) → `chraiGoToLabel(AIList=m_RunToBondPersistent, Offset=133 [mid-scan], LabelNum=0)` → `chraiitemsize`. Main thread idle in the SDL event pump. Stacks: `scratch/freeze_caverns_stacks.txt`.
- The AI list's live memory was dumped (`x/160bzx m_RunToBondPersistent`, `scratch/freeze_ailist_dump.txt`) and compared byte-for-byte against the compiled object (`objcopy` of `chraidata.c.obj` `.data`): **IDENTICAL** — no runtime corruption, and since the decomp is byte-matched to ROM, no data-side explanation. ABI/pointer-width drift was also ruled out structurally: every AI record type is `#pragma pack(1)` small-int (no pointer fields), so `chraiitemsize`'s `sizeof`s match N64 widths exactly.

**Root-cause chain (all verified against source + live bytes):**
1. `m_RunToBondPersistent` (`src/game/chraidata.c:551`) begins `Label(lblRun)` / `TRYRunToBond(lblRunning)` / `PRINT("no go!\n")` / `DO(lblRunning)` … The decompiled `PRINT` macro (`src/aicommands2.h:4913`) expands to **only the one command byte** — no string is stored in the stream.
2. `chraiitemsize()`'s `AI_PRINT` case (`src/game/chrai.c:682`) sizes the record by scanning forward until a NUL byte. With no embedded string, it runs 18 bytes past the PRINT at offset +4 (through eight real records) to the first NUL at +21 (inside an `IFMychrflagsHas` record).
3. Execution resumes at +22 = bytes `00 00`, which decode as `AI_GotoNext` with `GOTOLABEL=0` (`lblZero`). A full named decode of the list (decoder: `scratch/decode_ailist.c`, command table: `scratch/ai_cmd_vals.txt`) confirms the stream is otherwise perfectly coherent — `Label(40=lblRun)`, `TRYRunToBond(27=lblRunning)`, `PRINT`, `Label(27)`+`Yield`, … all matching the source exactly — and that **no `Label(0)` exists anywhere in the list**.
4. `chraiGoToLabel` scans forward from +22 for label 0, reaches `AI_EndList`, and returns 0 — the decomp's own comment: "restart ai list PC if next label not found - causes infinite loop outside of debug" (`src/game/chrai.c:753`).
5. `ai()` sets `Offset=0` and its `for(;;)` restarts: `TRYRunToBond` fails **immediately without yielding** (`chrGoToBond` false → plain fall-through, `src/game/chrai.c:1534`) → PRINT → 18-byte mis-skip → phantom `GotoNext(0)` → scan → 0 → repeat. Tight infinite loop inside a single `ai()` call — matches the observed stack exactly.

**Why PC and not N64:** code and data are ground truth, so given this state the N64 would spin identically — this is a **latent original bug** requiring a guard on this list to tick AI while Bond is unreachable ("guard can't reach bond"). The repro (level teardown back to the intro screen) is exactly such a window: on PC the boss thread still ticks a guard whose level/Bond state is already invalid, and the state never recovers so the spin is permanent. Same freeze class as D287 (Windows, non-self-recovering) / D286 (Deck). Not yet established *why* the N64 scheduler never presents this state (teardown ordering / single-threaded timing) — that's the open question for any fix.

**Fix bucket:** NOT an ABI/layout exception (no pointer-width involvement at all). The decomp's code+data are faithful; the divergence is in *when* the state occurs, i.e. PC teardown/scheduling. A port-side fix (ensure guards stop ticking AI before/while Bond+level state goes invalid on level exit) is the natural home and needs its own investigation of the teardown ordering (`gesched.c` / boss-thread vs level-unload race). Any `src/game` edit would require rule-2 sign-off.

**Status:** **FIXED via D310 — user-playtest-confirmed 2026-09-18** (Caverns→intro transition clean; the spin record `PRINT("no go!")`@+4 itself was observed in the post-fix probe log stepping `size=1 global=1` and resuming at `Label(27)` as intended). The teardown-ordering open question (why PC presents the unreachable-Bond state) remains documented but is now harmless — reaching that state no longer spins.

## D173/D292 — user confirmation, 2026-09-18: mostly fixed as a side effect of D243's root cause.

**User playtest, same day as the D243/D173/D292 draft-wording correction above (which had said the shared mechanism was "identified but not confirmed" for these two):** "Yeah the Bond floating/animations - 9/10 times he's in the right place now, if he's off it's only by a small amount, no more floating in midair or glitching out spinning like before."

This confirms the M-160/M-164/M-165 hypothesis (`## D173`'s own consolidated-next-steps section) — that D173/D292/D243 share one "third-person world model transform/lifecycle" mechanism, specifically `chrUpdateAnim` reading a stale/mismatched animation's root motion back into the puppet's logical position after a transition (teleport/spawn/death) that didn't also update the animation state — was correct, even though it was never separately code-traced and confirmed for D173/D292 the way it was for D243 (D243's own fix was the hardcoded 32-bit `sizeof(Model)` struct-size literal corrupting animation-timing fields; the M-160 write-up's own caveat was exactly that this general mechanism might explain D173/D292 too, without a live capture to prove it — this user confirmation is that proof, by outcome).

**Not "fully fixed"** — user is explicit that a small positional-offset residual remains ~1/10 of the time, and that no separate investigation/fix was made for D173/D292's own code path specifically (D243's fix in `bondview2.c`'s cutscene body-model buffer layout was the actual change; D173/D292 improving alongside it is the side-effect being confirmed here, not a targeted fix). Worth noting for a future session: since D173/D292 were never traced to their own exact call site, if the residual offset ever becomes a live complaint again, whoever picks it up should not assume it's the same code path as D243's fix — that fix touched one specific buffer-layout call site (Bond's cutscene body model), and D173's own M-172/M-173 measurements were taken on the *level-start intro puppet*, a different code path (`solo_char_load`/`bondviewSetCameraMode`'s `CAMERAMODE_SWIRL` branch, per D173's own M-175 finding) that was never itself touched by the D243 fix — the improvement is a side effect of shared underlying mechanics, not the same call site being patched twice.

**Status:** MOSTLY FIXED (D173 and D292 both), user-confirmed live, small residual offset remains and is not investigated further. Public docs (release notes, README) should describe this as "the Bond positioning/floating issue is now mostly resolved, small residual placement drift only, no more full floating or spin-glitching" rather than "separate, unconfirmed, still open."

## D310 — RULE-2-SIGNOFF: `chraiitemsize()` mis-sizes 1-byte `AI_PRINT` records (NUL-scans forward), corrupting AI execution for any list containing an active PRINT — fixes D309's freeze mechanism and the Caverns standing-still guards (signed off + implemented, 2026-09-18).

**Status:** **RULE-2-SIGNOFF / FIXED — user-playtest-confirmed (2026-09-18).** All three checks passed live in Caverns: standing-still guards resume, Trevelyan follows his path, Caverns→intro no longer freezes. `src/game` behavior change under `#ifdef PORT`; N64 build untouched.

**Post-fix probe log (clean session, 989 lines):** global-list PRINTs (`m_RunToBondPersistent`, chr=4/24/72) all step `size=1 global=1` — including the D309 spin record itself (`off=4 "no go!" landcmd=0x02`=Label, resumed correctly) and the standing-still record (`off=167 "wait" landcmd=0x95`=UnsetMyFlags2), each hit exactly once (no per-tick re-execution). Local-list PRINTs (Trevelyan chr=88, fake-GUARD driver chr=254) all keep NUL-scan sizing (`size=4/7 global=0`) with valid landing commands. Zero `LABEL-NOT-FOUND`, zero D156 fires, zero watchdog freezes.

**The defect.** The `PRINT()` macro (`src/aicommands2.h:4913`) emits exactly **one command byte** into the built AI list — its string argument is discarded at list-build time. But `chraiitemsize()`'s `case AI_PRINT:` (`src/game/chrai.c:682`, original) sized the record by scanning forward to the next NUL byte, so stepping on a PRINT always skips ~20 bytes into whatever records follow and resumes at an arbitrary byte pattern. Only 4 PRINTs exist in all of `src/game/chraidata.c`; two are commented out (`m_DeadAI:74`, `m_StandardGuard:136`) and **both active ones are in `m_RunToBondPersistent`** — so exactly one AI list in the game is affected.

**Two observed symptoms, one landmine (both live-verified 2026-09-18 with `GE_D309` probes, gdb symbol confirmation):**
1. **D309's complete freeze** (Caverns→intro): `PRINT("no go!\n")` @+4 mis-lands at +22 = `00 00` = phantom `AI_GotoNext(0)`; no `Label(0)` exists → `chraiGoToLabel` returns 0 ("causes infinite loop outside of debug", `chrai.c:753`) → PC restarts at 0 → same path → tight spin inside one `ai()` call. (Full mechanism in `## D309`.)
2. **Standing-still guards** (user report, Caverns 00 Agent: one after the first elevator, one after the next door — "fidgeting but staying still", still react to shots): guard completes its 1-second dash window → `Stop()` + `PRINT("wait\n")` @+167 mis-lands at +189, where arg bytes of a later record decode as `Label(88)` then `0x04` = **`AI_EndList`**. `ai()` at EndList `return`s **without saving the offset** (`chrai.c:988`, "same as yield except without pushing offset past it") → the identical path re-executes every tick → `Stop` re-issued forever; the source's intended follow-up (UnsetMyFlags2 / random check / MyTimerStart / sit-rep DO-LOOP / `GotoFirst(lblRun)` resume) is swallowed by the mis-skip. Damage still interrupts because shot/death changes `actiontype` outside the AI list. Live probe lines: `D309: PRINT chr=3/4 list=<m_RunToBondPersistent> off=167 size=22 landcmd=0x02` repeating every tick; `gdb info symbol` confirmed the list pointer is `m_RunToBondPersistent`.

**Sign-off request as stated (per `docs/dev-process.md` §7):**
1. *Change:* `src/game/chrai.c`, `chraiitemsize()`, `case AI_PRINT:` — replace the NUL-scan with `return 1;` (the record's true on-disk size), under `#ifdef PORT`; the `#else` arm is byte-identical to the original decomp.
2. *Proof of divergence:* mechanism verified live (gdb symbol + per-tick probe lines above, exact offsets/sizes/landing bytes). Intended-behavior references: (a) the list source itself — PRINT sits between two real commands and is a no-op by construction; (b) user's direct N64 experience — guards do not stand frozen in Caverns on real hardware (same standard as M-144's user comparison that settled D243). Honest caveat recorded at request time: the ROM *code* would mis-skip on N64 too if reached — this is a latent original defect, and the fix restores the list author's intent rather than provable N64 behavior.
3. *Why not `port/`:* no N64 hardware dependency to shim — the sizer function's own logic operating on game data is the defect; nothing upstream (ABI/layout §A1 suspects, port-layer) is involved. *Why not the ABI exception:* nothing pointer-width-driven; the 32-bit original has identical code and data.
4. *Same-engine precedent:* Perfect Dark removed `PRINT` from the AI language entirely and **reassigned slot 0xAD** to a real command (`aiChrCopyProperties`, `pd_port/src/game/chraicommands.c:8159`) — Rare themselves retired this broken record class in the next title on the same engine.

**Grant (2026-09-18, in-thread):** "I want to proceed with your implementation plan here to fix this bug." (User's reply to the full §7 write-up; asked only whether a fresh session was needed — answered no, granted in this session.)

**Resulting diff v1 (REGRESSED, superseded):** `chraiitemsize()` `case AI_PRINT:` → `return 1;` under `#ifdef PORT`. Fixed the guards, but live testing then broke **Caverns' Trevelyan (chr=88)**: ran in circles with glitched animations. Memory dump of his list (`0x701cca30`, a level-LOCAL list from `g_CurrentSetup.ailists`) shows local lists **embed a NUL-terminated string after the PRINT byte** — live bytes `AD 44 0A 00` (PRINT + "D\n"), `AD 57 0A 00`, `AD 34 0A 00` at offsets 50/288/302 — so the NUL-scan is CORRECT for local lists; the uniform 1-byte size landed mid-string (garbage commands + a `LABEL-NOT-FOUND` spin, off=403 label=0, probe-capped). Only the macro-built GLOBAL lists (`g_GlobalAILists`, chraidata.c) discard their PRINT strings.

**Resulting diff v2 (current):** `chraiitemsize()` left byte-identical to the decomp. New PORT-only `d310ItemSize(AIList, offset, isGlobalAIList)` returns 1 for a PRINT only when `chraiGetAIListID()` confirms the list is global; otherwise falls through to the original NUL-scan. Applied at both record-walk sites: `ai()`'s AI_PRINT step and `chraiGoToLabel`'s label scan (a backward `GotoFirst` crossing a global PRINT would mis-scan even with v1's sizer, since the scan also steps records). Lists found in neither table (teardown) default to the original NUL-scan. Verification: full-list decode of `m_RunToBondPersistent` with 1-byte global PRINTs (`scratch/decode_printfix.c`) walks +0→EndList@223 with every record valid, and the post-`"wait"` sequence matches `chraidata.c:666+` line-for-line (`UnsetMyFlags2(4)`, `IFNewRandomGreaterThan(160)`, `SetMyFlags2(4)`, `MyTimerStart`, sit-rep block, `GotoFirst(lblRun)`); post-`"no go!"` resumes at `Label(27)+Yield` as in source.

**Scope note (§7 drift check):** v1's sign-off scope ("exactly one AI list affected") was wrong in one respect — PRINT records also exist in level-local lists, but with a different shape (embedded string), where the original NUL-scan is already correct. v2's *behavioral* change is still confined to global-list PRINTs: `m_RunToBondPersistent`'s two records. Local-list behavior is byte-identical to the original decomp — Trevelyan reverts to his pre-fix (working) pathing. Drift disclosed to user in-thread when the regression was reported; same sign-off intent (fix global PRINT sizing, no other behavior change).

**Cross-refs:** D309 (this fix neutralizes its spin mechanism — the teardown-ordering open question in D309's "why PC and not N64" remains, but reaching that state is now harmless); GE_D309 probes (`chrai.c` `ai()`/`chraiGoToLabel`, `chraction.c` `chrGoToBond`) remain as diagnostic tools.

**Perf gauge (2026-09-19, release review — M-192 item 6):** v2's up-front `chraiGetAIListID()` call in `chraiGoToLabel` (added so the sizer knows global-vs-local) runs on EVERY label jump; originally that lookup ran only in the rare EndList-not-found branch. Cost per call: ≤ (level-local lists + ~20-entry `g_GlobalAILists`) pointer comparisons ≈ tens of ns. Worst case for a heavy level (Train/Archives, ~50 active guards each executing 1–2 goto-family records per tick): ~1000 calls/tick × ~40 comparisons ≈ 40 µs/tick — under 0.3% of a 16.7 ms frame, and two orders of magnitude below the D250 `getenv` anti-pattern (which was per-TRIANGLE, tens of thousands of calls per frame). **No change warranted; re-measure only if an AI-heavy level shows a regression.**

## D311 — Complete freeze in `modelSetAnimFrame2WithChrStuff` root-motion loop: D156 guard hole — poisoned `framea` (`model->animframe1`) passes through the frameb-only clamp and saturates to a ~3.1e9-iteration spin (Caverns, live GDB diagnosis, 2026-09-18).

**Reported:** user playtest of the D310 v2 build in Caverns — "it's frozen" shortly after launch (watchdog: no frame rendered for 8014 ms at frames=8424; ~2.3 min into the session).

**Live evidence (GDB attach, PID 46948, mainThread):**
- Stack: `sincosf` ← `modelSetAnimFrame2WithChrStuff` (`model.c:3349`, anim-merge branch) ← `modelTickAnim` ← `bheadUpdate` ← `bondviewMoveAnimationTick` ← `MoveBond` — the **player's own** model anim tick. Zero `D309:` probe lines in the log → no AI-list involvement; this is a different bug from D309/D310.
- Locals at the spin site: `curframe = -966612173`, `endframe = 2147483647` (INT_MAX) → ~3.1e9 loop iterations; `pos34 = (-6.7e30, ?, 2.9e32)` — root-motion accumulator already blown up; `model->animframe1 = -1.6708e+31`; `model->endframe = 17` (the anim has 17 frames); `speed = 0.22` (normal), but `newspeed = -3.2e7`, `oldspeed = -1.75e18`, `timespeed = 0`, `unkb0 = 0`; `anim2 != NULL` with healthy frame2 (18.8→20.9).
- The existing D156 guard **had fired** earlier in the same session (`[D156] bad anim frame guarded: frame=-1.6708e+31 animframe1=-1.6708e+31 ... oldspeed=-1.75136e+18 timespeed=0 unkb0=0`) — i.e. `animframe1` was already poisoned *before* the guarded tick, and the guard's fallback (`frame = model->animframe1`) plus the callee's frameb-only clamp (`if bad frameb: frameb = framea`) passed the poison straight through.

**Mechanism (the guard hole):** D156's guard in `modelSetAnimFrame2WithChrStuff` validates only `frameb`. With `framea = frameb = -1.67e31`, `floorFloatToInt` saturates the two near-equal huge floats to far-apart ints (`curframe = -966612173`, `endframe = INT_MAX`), so the `while(1)` root-motion loop walks ~3.1e9 frames — each doing a joint transform + bitstream decode + `sincosf` — i.e. a permanent hang. The N64 never presents this state (fixed timestep, bounded speeds); the poison is PC-side upstream corruption of the model speed/frame fields (see open question).

**Fix (landed, `#ifdef PORT`, same file/pattern as the accepted D156 guards — port-side defensive clamp against non-finite state, no game-logic change):**
1. `modelSetAnimFrame2WithChrStuff`: validate **both** `framea` and `frameb` against ±1e6; a bad one snaps to the other if that is valid, else 0. Both-bad → both 0 → loop does ~0 iterations; the in-loop `animframe1` rewrite (`model.c:3447`) then heals stored state on subsequent ticks.
2. `modelTickAnim`: heal `model->animframe1`/`animframe2` (snap to 0) **before** the bad-frame fallback reads them, so the poison source itself is cleared instead of being re-derived every tick.

**Open question (deeper root cause, NOT fixed):** what wrote `-1.75e18` into `oldspeed` / poisoned `animframe1` in the first place? `oldspeed = model->speed` at transition start (`model.c:2975`) means `speed` was already garbage upstream; `timespeed = 0` and `unkb0 = 0` at the guarded tick are suspicious division denominators (D156's original note flagged `/ unkb0` and `/ timespeed` as guarded `> 0` but not against tiny values). Also, the model's persistent root-motion header (`header->unk34/unk24`) is poisoned to ~1e30–1e32 in this instance, so **Bond's rendered model may be displaced even after the freeze is prevented** — a level reload clears it. Needs its own investigation (dump speed-field write sites during the triggering transition) before any further fix.

**M-194 (v0.4.0 Phase 1, 2026-09-21): upstream poison source — static pass + choke-point instrumentation.** Every write of `model->speed` funnels through exactly two functions: `modelSetAnimSpeed` (startframe≤0 path) and `modelSetAnimation2`. Both now log a `D311: … ANOMALY` line when the incoming value OR the already-resident `model->speed` is non-finite or |v|>1e4 (`#ifdef PORT`, unconditional-on-fire like the D156 guards — silent in healthy play). The line captures in/resident/startframe/oldspeed/newspeed/timespeed + model pointer, so the next occurrence pins the exact injecting call. Static pass over the computed-speed callers: `sub_GAME_7F06FE90` (the `t = speed + 2·φ/arg2` divider) is only ever called with arg2=16.0f — its denominator is safe, though a garbage `animframe1` would poison its numerator; `bheadAdjustAnimation` divides by the *static* `g_BondMoveAnimationSetup[].speedMultiplier` table (bondhead.c:19) — safe constants, but its `speed` parameter is the player's live movement speed, so an upstream velocity-field corruption would flow straight into `model->speed`; the old→new lerp at model.c:3654/3663 only circulates already-poised values (no new garbage). Live repro (Caverns, ~2 min in) remains the trigger; the probe turns that occurrence into a one-line diagnosis.

**Status:** GUARDED (freeze class neutralized; upstream poison source OPEN — M-194 probe armed). **RULE-2-SIGNOFF (2026-09-19, release review — M-192 item 2):** user approved retention as the stability-maximizing option; classified as a defensive guard against non-finite state in the same class as the accepted D156 guards — it fires only on poison values that indicate an already-broken state and snaps to a valid frame rather than altering any legitimate animation. Previously disclosed in-thread as a D156-guard extension following the already-accepted D156 precedent in this same file; revert is still two small blocks. Cross-refs: D156 (original guard + Facility outro hang), D309/D310 (ruled out for this freeze — no AI involvement).

**2026-09-24 — likely root cause found in D336.** D311's own static pass named `bheadAdjustAnimation` as the one path where a corrupted value reaches `model->speed`. D336 showed that path computing Bond's head-bob start frame from a never-written alias field (`field_5C0` = N64 `model.animframe1`), i.e. uninitialised player-struct bytes, whose garbage depends on memory layout (room-pool size, previous level). That matches D311's intermittent `oldspeed=-1.75e18`-at-transition signature. After the D336 fix: headless Caverns (`-level_39`, user settings incl. the 2× room pool `ma=512000`, scripted movement/turning, ~80 s) gave **0 D156 guards, 0 D311 anomaly lines, no crash**. **Close after one live Caverns combat session (~2 min) stays D156/D311-silent.**

**2026-09-25 playtest (user, Windows, one ~46-min session Silo → Caverns, `GE_D322=1 GE_D204=1`, build `7baf4900`):** Caverns combat ~2 min, plus Silo onwards: zero `D311: … ANOMALY` lines (the probe logs via `osSyncPrintf` into the same log, and D318W lines from the same path prove it is live). Combined with D336 (upstream poison source) this closes D311. Guard stays (Rule-2 sign-off 2026-09-19).

## D312 — Throwable items (mines, grenades, etc.) can clip through walls in certain spots (user report, v0.3.0 pre-release playtest, 2026-09-18) — FIXED: `bgBuildRoomVtxBounds` mis-reads the G_VTX vertex count on PC (Gfx_le `dma.par` bit-layout shift), collapsing whole batches of wall geometry out of the collision query (diagnosed + fixed, 2026-09-18).

**Reported:** user's last-minute v0.3.0 playtest: thrown/placed throwable items — mines, grenades, "etc." — can pass through wall geometry in certain spots rather than colliding with it. Spot-dependent ("certain spots"), not universal.

**Diagnosis (2026-09-18, env-gated probes `GE_D312`/`GE_D312V`, Runaway spawn-area wall):**
- Fidelity confirmed first: the N64 original does NOT clip — this is a port-side divergence (user confirmation + the pipeline below being structurally identical to the working door/window path).
- Both D312 (projectiles) and D313 (bullets) funnel into `bgTestBulletHitBackground` (`propobj.c handles_projectile_motion` bg loop; `chrprop.c` fire path). Doors/windows use the separate, working `bgTestHitOnObj` path — matching the user's "works on doors/windows" symptom exactly.
- Probe run 1: queries during a mine flight DO reach the room (room 14) and even register HITs — but only on floor triangles far ahead of the mine; the wall's triangles are never tested. The per-batch AABB pre-test in `bgTestBulletHitBackground` rejects the batches that own the wall.
- Probe run 2 (`D312B` batch-table dump): room 14 has 37 vertex batches; most have degenerate 1-unit bounds (single vertex), while a few (e.g. the floor batches) have correct extents. The pre-test therefore only ever admits the correctly-bounded batches.
- Probe run 3 (`D312V` per-triangle world-box dump, mirroring `bgTestRayIntersectionInRoom`'s index recovery): the wall geometry EXISTS and is at the right place — batch 35 owns a vertical wall at z=-647 spanning x 510..560, y -59..-23; the mine's fixed-point trajectory crosses it dead-center. So the geometry is fine; only the bounds table is wrong.
- Root cause: `bgBuildRoomVtxBounds` (bg.c) computes the G_VTX vertex count as `((gdl[cmdindex].dma.par >> 4) & 0xf) + 1`. On N64, `Gfx.dma.par` IS the params byte `((n-1)<<4 | v0)`, so that is correct there. The PC shim's `Gfx_le` packs word0 as `(cmd<<24)|(par_byte<<16)|len`, and its `Gdma_le.par` bitfield spans bits 0–23 — i.e. `(par_byte<<16 | len)` — so `(dma.par>>4)&0xf` actually reads the low nibble of `len>>4` (= `n & 0xf`). For n ≤ 15 the builder still reads the whole block (+1 vertex, harmless); for **n = 16** (the most common authored size) it collapses to `numvertices = 1`, and the batch's bounds shrink to a single vertex. The per-batch AABB pre-test then rejects that batch for nearly every ray, so its triangles are never intersected: projectiles pass through those walls (D312) and bullets register no impact on them (D313). Batches with n ≤ 15 keep correct bounds — hence "certain spots", not universal. This is the §A1 struct-layout-driven misread class (raw field alias into a union arm whose bit layout changed in the port shim), same pattern as D154/M-30.

**Fix:** `src/game/bg.c` `bgBuildRoomVtxBounds`, under `#ifdef PORT`: recover the params byte from bits 16–23 of `words.w0` — `numvertices = (((u32)gdl[cmdindex].words.w0 >> 20) & 0xf) + 1;` — restoring the N64 semantics (the `(n-1)` field). N64 path untouched. Verified by repro: with the fix, the mine-flight queries pre-pass and win batch 35, HITs land exactly on the wall plane (hit z = -647.0 in fixed-point), and `handles_projectile_motion` reports `result=0` (collision) instead of pass-through; pistol shots at the same wall now produce impact decal positions on the wall plane.

**Status:** FIXED (v0.3.1). Cross-ref: D313 (same root cause, merged diagnosis), D154/M-30 (same §A1 pattern in this file).

So the impact system works; its trigger is surface-dependent.

**Diagnosis:** merged into D312 — see that entry for the full trace. The bullet path (`chrprop.c` fire → `bgTestBulletHitBackground`) shares the same broken per-batch bounds table: batches whose G_VTX block holds exactly 16 vertices get single-point bounds, fail the AABB pre-test, and their wall triangles are never ray-tested — so no hit is registered and no impact effect spawns. Doors/windows use the separate `bgTestHitOnObj` path (unaffected), which is why impacts worked there. The "surface-dependent" appearance was actually batch-size-dependent.

**Fix:** same one-line change as D312 (`src/game/bg.c` `bgBuildRoomVtxBounds`, `#ifdef PORT`). Verified: pistol shots at the previously-failing Runaway wall now register hits on the wall plane and spawn impacts.
